## D-142 — The Danilewicz benchmark, written against data rather than against 1.7: the cascade traverses 1↔2 by blocking a route and the direct set cannot move at all — but it is the DIRECT set whose number lands in the measured band, and the cascade's shortfall is 4-7×, not ~100×

**Corrects:** D-141 — its "exactly what the direct set structurally cannot produce" is false as stated; the direct set reaches an in-band *number* (1.3875) perfectly well. What it cannot do is *traverse*.
**Corrects:** D-138 — "1.7 must emerge, never be fitted" pinned the wrong target. 1.7 is one dataset's mode and sits at the TOP of an independent dataset's range; the emergent quantities are the limits 1 and 2.

**Status: BENCHMARK SHIPPED, one assertion deliberately red.** New file
`tests/benchmarks/test_validation_danilewicz_so2_o2.py` — 6 passing, 1 `xfail(strict=True)`,
32 s. No `src/` change, no parameter change, nothing fitted. `ruff`, `mypy` clean.

### The pull failed and the batch is better for it

D-141's "Next" was: pull Danilewicz 2016 and Nikolantonaki & Waterhouse 2012, then write the
benchmark. **Both targets are paywalled.** Checked, per the "paywalled is one host, not a paper"
rule: publisher landing *and* the `.full.pdf` path, Unpaywall, OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC
(`inPMC:N`), PubMed, vitis-vea, the author's own institutional HAL record
(`ube.hal.science/hal-05266806`, `openAccess_bool: false`), an open-access thesis from
Nikolantonaki's own group (Romanet 2019 — OA but behind an Anubis bot-wall on every HAL host),
the authors' own review chapter (`10.1021/bk-2015-1203.ch018`), and Sacks/Danilewicz 2020. Both
sit behind a $10 pay-per-article wall. That is the user's call to make, and it is no longer on
the critical path.

What the sweep found instead were **two open-access (CC BY) primaries that were never on the
list**, both of which turned out to be worth more than the targets:

- **Miao & Waterhouse 2025**, AJEV 76:0760008 — per-wine SO2:O2 ratios for eight commercial
  white wines *with the full protocol*, plus a transcription of Danilewicz 2016's own spread.
- **Nguyen & Waterhouse 2021**, AJEV 72:209-216 — the printed, isolated-copper rate table that
  `aging.yaml`'s `k_copper_multiplier` uncertainty note explicitly asks for by name ("a cleaner
  isolated Cu source (a printed table, not a chart) would be the natural follow-on").

Danilewicz 2016's abstract *is* transcribed verbatim and does back the **structure** — 1:2 ideal,
"decreased down to 1:1.7 in most wines", and 1:1 once benzenesulfinic acid traps the quinone. It
backs no dose, no temperature and no per-wine value, and none are asserted.

### The measurement, run BEFORE the assertion was chosen

Miao's protocol, reproduced: white wine, 7 mg/L O2 × two rounds, 45 °C, 5 d each, `hermetic`
closure (the sim's named zero-ingress closure — the analogue of his sealed BOD bottle). Ratio by
his own regression of total SO2 against total O2 consumed. "Blocked" drives
`k_quinone_polymerization` up by 1e6 (benzenesulfinic acid's analogue: an overwhelming competing
quinone sink); "ideal" zeroes quinone's four competing fates.

| set | SO2 dose | blocked (→1) | real | ideal (→2) | quinone share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direct | 40 | 1.3875 | 1.3875 | 1.3881 | 0.0000 |
| direct | 80 | 1.7758 | 1.7758 | 1.7761 | 0.0000 |
| direct | 500 | 1.9809 | 1.9809 | 1.9809 | 0.0000 |
| **cascade** | **40** | **0.9304** | **0.9888** | **1.4478** | **0.0584** |
| cascade | 80 | 0.9772 | 1.1381 | 1.8644 | 0.1609 |
| cascade | 500 | 0.9977 | 1.6618 | 1.9977 | 0.6641 |

Three things fall out, and only the first was predicted.

**1. The falsifier is the traverse, not the value.** Blocking the quinone route moves the
cascade by 0.16 at wine-realistic SO2 and the direct set by **0.0006** — and that residual is not
even the mechanism, it is the four zeroed constants being direct O2 sinks in that set. The
direct set has no route to block. This is D-141's claim, but its wording ("structurally cannot
produce") was wrong: a fixed `_SO2_PER_O2 = 2` scaled by bisulfite's share of a six-way O2
competition lands anywhere in (0, 2) and reaches 1.3875 — **in band** — without difficulty.
Right number, wrong reason. The benchmark now says both things separately.

**2. Both limits are exact asymptotes, and emergent.** 0.9977 → 1 and 1.9977 → 2 as SO2 rises.
Every stoichiometry constant on the path is 1, so "2" is a consequence of *one O2 yields one
H2O2 and one quinone*, never a yield. Both are approached **from below** for a physical reason:
bisulfite shares the H2O2 node with ethanol, so its share of that node is <1 at finite SO2 —
the same qualification Danilewicz makes calling the model-wine reduction "near quantitative".

**3. The ~100× fork is 4-7×.** `r = (H2O2 share to sulfite) + (quinone share to sulfite)`, and
the blocked run measures the first term directly. At wine-realistic SO2 the cascade's quinone
share is **0.0584** where the band needs ~0.37-0.74. D-141 could only say "~100× smaller
`k_quinone_polymerization` *or* much larger nucleophile constants, nothing in hand adjudicates".
Measured, the gap is **4-7× on a branching share** — far smaller, far better posed, and it is the
same defect D-141 saw from the other side as A420 running 4.20× high in a sulfited wine. It is
still **not fitted**: the constant that would close it is exactly the one whose settling source
is paywalled.

### Why 1.7 is not asserted anywhere

Danilewicz's mode is 1.7; his transcribed spread is 1.29-2.03. Miao's seven normal wines span
1.0972-1.6621, mean ≈1.372 — so **1.7 sits at the top of one independent dataset and is the mode
of the other.** The two datasets disagree, and are confounded (different wines, different SO2
levels, and Miao is accelerated at 45 °C). Pinning 1.7 would have pinned one dataset. The
assertion is the **union envelope [1.0972, 2.03]**, bounded as Miao bounds it to wines above
~10 mg/L free SO2 — his wine #1 reads 0.8443 once free SO2 falls to 3 mg/L, which is why the
floor is not 1 in practice.

### A third, unasked-for check: the sim under-binds SO2

Miao reports three quantities on the same eight wines, and the sim has a bound/free split
(D-28/D-51, four carbonyls on one bisulfite pool), so all three are computable:

| quantity | Miao | direct | cascade |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SO2:O2 ratio (Δtotal/ΔO2) | 1.0972-1.6621 | 1.389-1.840 | 0.988-1.189 |
| free SO2 depletion factor (Δfree/ΔO2) | 0.7456-1.8998 | 0.981-1.651 | 0.733-1.092 |
| sulfite buffering capacity (Δtotal/Δfree) | 1.2526-1.9882 | **1.114-1.416** | **1.089-1.349** |

The buffering capacity is **low against every one of Miao's eight wines** on both alternatives —
which is an independent, quantified confirmation of a concession `analysis.py` already prints in
its own docstring ("**under**-estimates real bound SO2"). D-51 added pyruvate, α-KG and
5-oxofructose and it is *still* low. This is not acted on here; it is recorded because it was
found, and because it is the first time that concession has had a number attached to it.

### Nguyen & Waterhouse 2021 — found en route, and it lands on three open items

Table 1 (model wine, 4-methylcatechol 1.0 mM + benzenesulfinic acid 1.0 mM, Fe(III) 0.1 mM,
22.2 °C), O2-consumption `k` in 1/min:

| pH | no Cu | Cu 0.01 mM (0.6 mg/L) | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.0 | 7.5e-05 | 3.9e-04 | 5.20× |
| 3.5 | 1.4e-04 | 5.5e-04 | 3.93× |
| 4.0 | 2.9e-04 | 7.5e-04 | 2.59× |

- **Copper.** 3.93× at pH 3.5 against `f_Cu`'s 1.43× over the same 0→0.6 mg/L span, with copper
  having *no discernible effect on Fe(III) reduction* — i.e. copper acts on the O2 step alone,
  exactly where the cascade puts it. **The shipped 600 L/g is NOT moved.** It is model wine with
  free CuSO4 and one synthetic nucleophile — the same bias that forced 2000→600 against
  Ferreira's 2.2×-total-spread ceiling — and two copper levels cannot distinguish a linear
  multiplier from a saturating one. Recorded as corroborating the *direction and order*, and as
  pressure toward the band's upper end.
- **pH.** O2 consumption rises 3.87× from pH 3.0 to 4.0 at zero copper. The activation node has
  **no pH term at all**. A gap, newly measured, not closed here.
- **What it does NOT overturn.** Its "iron(II) oxidation is the rate-determining reaction" reads
  as a contradiction of D-138's reductant-limited premise and is not one: its own conclusion is
  that the nucleophile is *required* for Fe(III) reduction to proceed (4-methylcatechol alone
  reduced Fe(III) to 0.004 mM in 3 h against 0.057 mM with benzenesulfinic acid), so the
  limiting reductant is the **nucleophile** pool, not the phenol pool. The cascade reads phenols.
  That is a real mismatch of *which pool*, and it is left open rather than half-fixed.
- **Nor does it flip the bisulfite sign.** Its "sulfur dioxide significantly decreases the rate of
  oxygen consumption" is about SO2 quenching H2O2 and killing the *post-Fenton* O2 sink. The
  cascade has **no secondary post-Fenton O2 draw at all**, so there is nothing there for SO2 to
  suppress. `k_activation_bisulfite` sits on the activation node and is the other, opposite
  effect in the same sentence. The sign stays. The missing secondary O2 draw is the real gap,
  and it is also why the model cannot dip below 1 the way Miao's wine #1 does.

### Two things this record's author got wrong before measuring

- The probe's first draft blocked routes with `ProcessSet.disable()` and returned three
  **identical** columns: `begin_aging` re-enables every aging Process at the event, silently
  undoing it. The routes are blocked by their parameters instead.
- Its second draft mutated `c.param_values` in place — a **property returning a fresh dict on
  every access**, so the edit hit a throwaway and the columns stayed identical. Both traps are
  now comments in the shipped test, because both produce a *plausible* green.

That is nine cascade-era claims falsified by re-measuring rather than by building, and D-140's
"an un-remeasured cascade-era number is wrong about half the time" continues to hold.

`AntioxidantBurstOxidation` still wired into no medium; **Nikolantonaki & Waterhouse 2012 and
Danilewicz 2016 both paywalled** (the abstract K values are pseudo-first-order at unstated

The quinone branching, which is now a 4-7× question on one share rather than a ~100× question on

### AMENDED, same day — the operating point violated the reference's own exclusion criterion, and fixing it INVERTS the headline

**The heading above and the "4-7×" result are withdrawn.** Both were measured at a dose where
the benchmark had already left the regime Miao's band covers.

Miao excludes his own wine #1 (ratio 0.8443) because its free SO2 ran 8 → 3 mg/L: *"when SO2
approaches very low levels, oxidation reactions must necessarily involve other components, and
thus the ratio of reaction with O2 must change."* The shipped test stated that bound **in prose
and never enforced it**. Measured at the shipped `WINE_REALISTIC_SO2 = 40.0`, free SO2 at the end
of the window was **2.8 mg/L (direct)** and **6.8 mg/L (cascade)** — i.e. both alternatives were
being regressed through exactly the curvature the reference removes. The monotone climb of r²
with dose (0.990 → 0.998 → 1.000) was that curvature showing, and it was read as a good fit.

Re-measured at the lowest dose where free SO2 stays above 10 mg/L on **both** alternatives
through the whole window (80 mg/L total), with the shipped scenario and the shipped regression:

| set | blocked (→1) | real | ideal (→2) | span | free SO2 end |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direct | 1.7707 | **1.7707** | 1.7710 | **0.0003** | 17.8 mg/L |
| cascade | 0.9767 | **1.1339** | 1.8354 | **0.859** | 31.1 mg/L |

**The conclusion inverts.** The cascade reads **1.1339 — inside Miao's own 1.0972-1.6621** — and
the calibrated direct set reads **1.7707, ABOVE it**, in the part of the union envelope only
Danilewicz's dataset reaches. So at a valid operating point the two alternatives *straddle* the
reference rather than the cascade falling short of it. The `xfail(strict=True)` asserting a 4-7×
quinone-capture shortfall was wrong and is gone; the band test now passes on its merits, and
`test_the_operating_point_satisfies_miaos_exclusion_criterion` enforces the bound in code so this
cannot recur silently.

**What survives untouched is the falsifier**, which is why it was the right thing to build the
file around: the traverse is 0.0003 for the direct set against 0.859 for the cascade — a ratio of
~2900×, wider at the corrected operating point than at the wrong one. No choice of dose softens
it. Both limits also re-confirm at the asymptote (blocked 0.9977 → 1, ideal 1.9975 → 2).

### The deeper finding, which the first version recorded as an unrelated side-note

The section above reported the sim's sulfite buffering capacity as low against all eight of
Miao's wines and moved on. It is not a side-note — **it is precisely why his operating point is
unreachable.** His wines carry a bound-SO2 reservoir up to total/free = 153/23 = 6.6 that keeps
free SO2 topped up under a 2 × 7 mg/L O2 challenge starting from only 9-28 mg/L free. The sim's
is ~1.35. So dosing to *his free SO2* exhausts the pool inside the window, and dosing to *stay
above his floor* starts at ~59 mg/L free — about 2× his highest wine. **No dose satisfies both
ends.** Every band comparison in this record is therefore an envelope check at the wrong sulfite
level, not a validation, and the in-band cascade result does **not** settle D-141's
quinone-branching question. That is now asserted rather than conceded
(`test_the_sim_cannot_actually_reach_miaos_operating_point`), so it fails loudly if the
under-binding is ever fixed without this record being revisited.

The under-bound SO2 pool is thus promoted from "recorded because it was found" to **the blocking
prerequisite for any quantitative use of this benchmark.**

### A third measurement error, caught by the new guard on its first run

The guard's first execution reported free SO2 of 0.3 mg/L where the truth was 17.8: the array had
already been divided by `M_SO2` for the molar regression and was then scaled by 1000, giving
mmol/L. Caught only because the assertion printed the number it compared. That is the third
plausible-green trap in this batch, after `ProcessSet.disable()` and the `param_values` property
— and unlike those two it would have made a *passing* test look like a failing one rather than
the reverse.

**Tally: ten cascade-era claims falsified by re-measuring rather than by building, and four of
them in this record alone — three of which were written by the author of the paragraph warning
that un-remeasured cascade-era numbers are wrong about half the time.** The rate is not
improving; what has improved is that the guards now catch them within the batch.

### What this does NOT change

The two `Corrects:` markers stand. D-141's "structurally cannot produce" is still wrong — more
clearly so, since the direct set now lands in the envelope at *both* operating points. And
D-138's "1.7 must emerge" is still the wrong target: 1.7 remains above Miao's whole range, and
the corrected cascade value (1.1339) is nowhere near it. Nothing here re-opens either.

Full suite after the amendment: **1380 passed**, `ruff` and `mypy` clean. The benchmark is 9
tests, 20 s (free SO2 is speciated at the 8 sample points only — mapping the coupled
four-carbonyl solve over all 6000 stored columns tripled the file's runtime).

### SECOND amendment, same day — the inversion's cascade half is dose-contingent, and the amendment above stated it as settled

The paragraph above reports "the cascade reads **1.1339** — inside Miao's own 1.0972-1.6621" as
though it were a property of the cascade. It is a property of the cascade **at one dose**, and
that dose was chosen for the *direct* set's benefit.

Measured across the doses where the **cascade alone** satisfies the exclusion criterion:

| dose (mg/L total SO2) | cascade r | free SO2 end | in Miao's band? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 60 | **1.0704** | 17.4 | **NO** — below the 1.0972 floor |
| 70 | 1.1035 | 24.0 | yes |
| 80 (shared point) | 1.1339 | 31.1 | yes |
| 120 | 1.2380 | 63.5 | yes |

**The cascade straddles Miao's lower bound.** It is valid from 60 and out of band there; the
direct set is *not* valid at 60 (free SO2 ends at 8.2 mg/L), which is the only reason the shared
comparison point is 80. So the corrected headline should read: *the cascade brackets Miao's floor
across its valid range and sits inside the band from ~70 upward; the direct set sits above the
band at every valid dose.* Only the second clause is unconditional.

The margin makes this worth stating rather than filing as pedantry. `MIAO_BAND` and
`OBSERVED_BAND` share the floor 1.0972, so a bare `lo <= ratio` assertion at the shared operating
point is a **3.4%-headroom** claim on a coarse dose grid — an unrelated model change flips it and
produces a red that reads as a physics regression when it is a dose artefact. The test now
asserts the straddle (out at the lowest valid dose, in at the shared one, monotone between), plus
the asymmetry itself in `test_the_shared_operating_point_is_forced_by_the_direct_set`.

**This is the same failure mode as the first amendment, in the opposite direction and one level
up.** The first shipped a single-dose verdict from an invalid dose. This one shipped a
single-dose verdict from a valid dose while treating it as dose-independent. Both were caught by
asking "over what range is this true?" rather than "is this true?" — which is now the standing
question for anything this benchmark reports.

Tally: **eleven** cascade-era claims falsified by re-measuring, five of them inside this record.

Benchmark is 10 tests, 34 s. Full suite green, `ruff` and `mypy` clean.

## D-143 — The bound-SO₂ "blocking prerequisite" measured instead of built, and withdrawn: Miao's buffering is an ADDITION-method secant, D-142 compared it against an oxidation-path slope at 2-6× his free SO₂, and on his own statistic the shipped four-carbonyl budget already reads 1.32 inside his 1.2526-1.9882

**Flags:** D-142 — its "buffering is low against every one of Miao's eight wines", the blocking prerequisite resting on it, and `FREE_SO2_FLOOR_MGL`'s per-sample floor are all wrong; the code still carries them and they still pass.

Owner's pick after D-142: **measure first, do not build.** The question put to the beat was *what
bound pool would be required to reach Miao's buffering, and is any plausible carbonyl budget
capable of supplying one* — chosen over a build precisely because a "no plausible budget reaches
it" answer would be as decision-relevant as a yes. The answer turned out to be neither. **There is
no deficit to supply.** Nothing in `src/` or `tests/` was edited; the deliverable is this record
plus six probes under `temp\d143-so2-binding\`.

### The beat began by transcribing the table D-142 took a number from without reading

D-142 asserts a `MIAO_BUFFERING_BAND = (1.2526, 1.9882)` cited to "Miao Table 3". Tables 1 and 2
were transcribed into `_findings`; **Table 3 was not**. Pulling it from the local PDF produced the
eight regressions — and, in the caption above them, the method:

> **Table 3** The sulfite buffering capacity, determined by linear regression analysis of eight
> wine samples (n = 15).

with Figure 5 captioned *"Total SO₂ versus free SO₂ **by the SO₂ addition method** (n = 15) for
wine #1"* and the text: *"When SO₂ is added to a wine, both the free and total SO₂ levels increase,
but not necessarily at the same rate, because there are weak binders in wine that bind only to a
fraction of the added SO₂."*

**That caption is the whole record.** Miao's buffering capacity is the slope of an *addition*
series on an unchanged wine — fixed carbonyl pools, free SO₂ swept ~4 → ~52 mg/L. It is a **secant
of the equilibrium locus over a >10× span**. D-142's sim-side number was `ratio / free_factor`
from an *oxidation* regression, taken at the sim's own 37-59 mg/L free SO₂. Different path,
different operating point, compared as though they were one quantity. [[feedback-transcribe-tables-not-prose]]
scored again, and this time the prose that mattered was a figure caption.

### The same table decomposes the bound pool into two independent halves

With `u` = free SO₂ (mol/L as SO₂), `h = β(pH)·u`, and carbonyl `i` at pool `A_i`, constant `K_i`:

```
total(u)          = u + Σᵢ Aᵢ·h/(Kᵢ + h)
d(total)/d(free)  = 1 + β·Σᵢ Aᵢ·Kᵢ/(Kᵢ + h)²
```

A binder with **K ≪ h is saturated** — it contributes ≈`A_i` to the **intercept** and ≈0 to the
slope. A binder with **K ≫ h is linear** — ≈0 intercept, `β·A_i/K_i` of slope. So Miao's intercept
measures the **strong** pool and his slope the **weak** capacity index, and his r² of 0.92-0.998
across a >10× span is itself the evidence the weak part sits in the linear regime.

**The halves cannot substitute for each other, which is why every table below keeps them apart.**
Sweeping acetaldehyde (K = 1.5e-6, saturated at any wine free-SO₂) 0 → 3 mM moves the intercept
0.003 → 1.920 mg/L and the secant only 1.3218 → 1.4111. Fixing the reservoir cannot fix the slope.

### Half one — the sim's acetaldehyde pool is EMPTY, and that is the scenario, not the model

At D-142's operating point, across the whole 10-day window, the sim carries **acetaldehyde
0.0000-0.0180 mM** (0.0-0.79 mg/L) against the 0.352-1.742 mM Miao's intercepts imply. Pyruvate
(0.3407 mM) and α-KG (0.1369 mM) sit exactly at their sourced residuals; 5-oxofructose is 0
(non-botrytis). So the strongest binder in the model, correctly parameterised, has **nothing in
it**.

The cause is one line of the benchmark scenario: it doses SO₂ **once, at day 19** — one day before
the end of fermentation — and nowhere else. D-108 already established that finished-wine
acetaldehyde is set by the SO₂ regime (Herzan 2020's must/tank/bottling ladder 2.7 → 51.6 mg/L)
and that the model reproduces it (must-60 strands 22.9 mg/L against the study's 17.2). A wine
sulfited only at the finish never builds the reservoir. Re-dosing in the must:

| SO₂ schedule | acetaldehyde | inside Miao's 0.352-1.742 mM? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| late-only (D-142 as shipped) | **0.0000 mM** | no |
| must 40 | 0.2882 mM (12.7 mg/L) | just below |
| must 60 | **0.5115 mM** (22.5 mg/L) | **yes** |
| must 80 | 0.7504 mM (33.1 mg/L) | yes |
| must 100 | 0.9992 mM (44.0 mg/L) | yes |

**Reachable with the four shipped carbonyls, at shipped constants and shipped pools, with zero new
provenance.** The reservoir half was never a modelling gap.

(Caveat carried, not buried: the intercepts are extrapolations. Back-predicting Table 1's total
from `m·free + c` matches within 2% on wines 2/3/4/6/8 and misses 1/5/7 by 14-33%.)

### Half two — measured like-for-like, the sim is INSIDE the band, and D-142's central claim is false

The sim's own carbonyl budget, on Miao's own span, at Miao's own pH:

| statistic | sim | Miao |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D-142's number — oxidation-path slope at the sim's free SO₂ | 1.089-1.416 | — |
| tangent at Miao's free SO₂ (9-28 mg/L) | 1.250-1.627 | — |
| **addition-method secant, free 4-52 mg/L — his actual statistic** | **1.3218-1.3519** | **1.2526-1.9882** |

**The sim reads 1.32, in band**, near the floor — matching wines 8 (1.2526), 3 (1.2734) and
4 (1.3955). Two compounding mismatches produced D-142's 1.089-1.416: the wrong path *and* free
SO₂ 2-6× his. Correct either alone and the gap narrows; correct both and it is gone.

Swept, because "over what range is this true?" is the standing question this benchmark earned:
**span** — in band at 4-52, 4-60, 2-52, 10-50, 5-30, 10-30, 15-40, 4-30 (1.2077-1.4774), the lone
failure being 20-52, a span starting above Miao's own lowest plotted points; **pH** — irrelevant,
1.3347 (2.90) to 1.3378 (3.80), covering both the scenario's own 2.96 and his 3.14-3.58;
**acetaldehyde** — 0 → 1.75 mM moves it 1.3193 → 1.3737.

So **"the buffering capacity is low against every one of Miao's eight wines on both alternatives"
is false, and the blocking prerequisite resting on it is WITHDRAWN.**

### What the remaining shortfall actually is: a pool size, not a missing species

Wines 2/5/6/7 (1.5984-1.9882) do sit above the sim's 1.32. The measurement that decides whether
that is structural:

| binder | K (mol/L) | sourced residual | pool needed alone at Miao's point | × residual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| acetaldehyde | 1.5e-6 | 0.79 mg/L | 31.7-35.9 mM | **1765-1999×** |
| α-KG | 1.4e-4 | 20 mg/L | 0.594-0.983 mM | 4.3-7.2× |
| pyruvate | 5.55e-4 | 30 mg/L | 0.449-1.118 mM | 1.3-3.3× |

and jointly on the secant, acetaldehyde held at the must-60 value: **1.0× → 1.3371, 2.0× → 1.6589,
3.0× → 1.9807, 4.0× → 2.3025 (out, above)**. A **1×-3× multiplier on the shipped keto-acid
residuals spans Miao's entire band, floor to ceiling.** The gap needs no binder in the K ≫ h
regime that the schema lacks — it is a between-wine composition spread, which is what his
1.2526-1.9882 *is*. **No candidate species is named here**, deliberately: naming one needs a
transcribed Kd table, and this beat did not go get one.

### A fourth thing fell out: the exclusion guard is stricter than the criterion it claims to encode

`FREE_SO2_FLOOR_MGL = 10.0` is enforced at **every** sample point. Applied to Miao's own wines via
his Table 1 free SO₂ and his Table 4 depletion factor over one 7.3 mg/L O₂ round:

| wine | free₀ | depl. factor | after one round | passes >10? | in his band? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 9 | 0.7456 | 3.56 | NO | NO — he excludes it |
| **2** | 15 | 1.0803 | **7.11** | **NO** | **yes** |
| **3** | 20 | 1.7256 | **7.40** | **NO** | **yes** |
| **4** | 20 | 1.7757 | **7.04** | **NO** | **yes** |
| 5-8 | 22-28 | 1.2360-1.8945 | 12.98-14.17 | yes | yes |

**Three of the seven wines that define the band fail the guard defending it**, after one round,
before the second (robust to dose: 7.44/7.92/7.57 at 7.0 mg/L). Miao excludes wine #1 for its
*starting* level and the resulting r² of 0.8103 against >0.91 for the rest — *"the very low free
SO₂ of this wine, which started at 8 mg/L"* — not for any per-sample floor.
[[feedback-name-guards-for-what-they-forbid]]: the guard is named for a real mechanism it does not
implement, which is exactly how a guard gets argued away later.

### With the reservoir present the sim matches every quantity Miao reports — and the honest limit of that

A 5×5 grid over (must dose, late dose). At **must 60 / late 0**, direct set: total SO₂ 60.0 mg/L
(his 27-153), free at window start 15.66 (his 9-28), total/free 3.832 (his 2.14-6.65), buffering
1.6185 (his 1.2526-1.9882), SO₂:O₂ ratio 1.1283 (his 1.0972-1.6621). **Five for five**, on a
scenario differing from D-142's only in *when* the SO₂ is dosed.

**Do not over-read it.** Free SO₂ ends at 1.51 mg/L, below even wine #1's 3, so this is not a
clean operating-point match either — the sim still depletes free SO₂ faster than his wines across
two rounds. But **depletion rate is not binding capacity**: it is set by the O₂-consumption
stoichiometry, not the equilibrium, and it is not what "under-binds SO₂" asserts. The binding
claim is dead; what replaces it is a narrower, new, and so-far unexamined question.

### A guard on the method itself, since this batch keeps falsifying "should be identical"

The secant probes evaluate `total(free)` analytically rather than calling `bound_so2_molar`, which
root-finds `h` from *total*. Round-tripping a 60-point grid (4 pH × 3 acetaldehyde × 5 free)
through the shipped solver recovers the input free SO₂ to a worst absolute error of **3.85e-11
mg/L**. The analytic locus *is* the shipped solver, parameterised from the other end.

### What does NOT change

D-142's falsifier stands untouched — the traverse (direct 0.0003 vs cascade 0.859) is a statement
about the quinone route, not about binding. The cascade stays **non-default**; nothing here
touches the fate gap or its two paywalled sources. `k_copper_multiplier` stays at 600. D-141's
quinone-branching question is still **not settled** — but the reason changes: it is no longer
"the benchmark runs at the wrong sulfite level", it is that the ratio comparison was never
sensitive enough to settle it.

### Left in the code, deliberately, for the owner to schedule

All four flagged D-142 artefacts still ship and still pass, because a measurement beat does not
edit the thing it measured: `test_the_sim_cannot_actually_reach_miaos_operating_point` (true as
written, about the wrong statistic — and misnamed), the per-sample `FREE_SO2_FLOOR_MGL`, the
buffering-below-band assertion, and the `MIAO_BUFFERING_BAND` comparison that reads an
oxidation-path slope against an addition-method secant. Reworking them is a build beat with its
own record; every D-140 pin it moves is priced there, not here.

**Tally: fifteen cascade-era claims falsified by re-measuring, four of them in this record.** All
four were found by asking *what exactly did the reference measure, and did I measure the same
thing?* The new twist is that the mismatched statistic was named in the source's own figure
caption, inside a table D-142 used a number from without transcribing.

### Same-day amendment — the guard finding is stronger without its assumption, and the headline needs its tier

Two corrections, neither reversing anything above.

**1. Table 4 prints the endpoint; the O2-dose assumption was never needed.** The section above
derived "three of seven in-band wines fall below 10 mg/L" from `free0 - depletion x 7.3`, and
carried the assumed O2 dose as a caveat. It is unnecessary: Table 4 regresses free SO2 (y, mg/L)
on **dissolved** O2 (x, mg/L), so `x = 0` is O2 exhaustion and **the printed intercept is the free
SO2 that wine ends a round with**.

| wine | Table 1 free0 | Table 4 intercept = free SO2 at O2 exhaustion | passes >10? | in his band? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 9 | **2.7369** | NO | NO - excluded |
| **2** | 15 | **6.3826** | **NO** | **yes** |
| **3** | 20 | **9.0102** | **NO** | **yes** |
| **4** | 20 | **7.2373** | **NO** | **yes** |
| **5** | 22 | **7.8348** | **NO** | **yes** |
| 6-8 | 23-28 | 12.258 / 13.544 / 17.576 | yes | yes |

**FOUR** of the seven wines that define the band fail the guard defending it, not three. The
reading is confirmed by the source: wine #1's intercept **2.7369** reproduces Miao's own prose
*"before dropping to 3 mg/L"*. The superseded arithmetic landed near the printed intercepts on
four of five wines - an unnoticed self-check - but was wrong by 5 mg/L on wine 5 and **flipped its
verdict**. Removing the assumption strengthened the conclusion; that is the argument for removing
assumptions rather than caveating them.

**2. The headline is `speculative`, and saying so makes it stronger.** The secant is set almost
entirely by pyruvate (0.3407 mM) and alpha-KG (0.1369 mM) - acetaldehyde moves it ~0.01. Both are
the quasi-steady ratio of two **`tier: speculative` author-estimate** rate constants (D-49/D-50),
bounded by Jackowetz & Mira de Orduna 2013. The **negative** claim - that D-142 compared an
oxidation-path slope at 37-59 mg/L against an addition-method secant over 4-52 - is a category
error in the comparison and is **tier-independent**. The **positive** claim, "the sim reads 1.32,
in band", is **speculative** and must travel that way (Prime Directive 1).

Evaluated at those pools' **own shipped uncertainty bounds** (pyruvate 10-100, alpha-KG 7-70 mg/L,
both printed in the YAML `uncertainty` notes):

| corner | pyruvate | alpha-KG | secant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| low | 10 mg/L | 7 mg/L | 1.1242 |
| nominal (shipped) | 30 mg/L | 20 mg/L | **1.3370** |
| high | 100 mg/L | 70 mg/L | 2.1046 |

**The parameters' own uncertainty band BRACKETS Miao's 1.2526-1.9882**, and his band maps back to
pyruvate 25-90 / alpha-KG 17-60 mg/L, inside those bounds. So the finding does not rest on the
nominal pools being right: **no pool value inside the shipped uncertainty resurrects an
"under-binds" verdict across his range.** This also subsumes the ad-hoc 1x-3x multiplier sweep
above - that sweep was rediscovering the parameters' own printed bounds.

## D-144 — D-143's four flagged artefacts reworked: the SO2 buffering comparison re-made on Miao's addition-series statistic instead of an oxidation-path slope (1.3197, in band), and the exclusion guard renamed for what it forbids after BOTH of his printed criteria were measured and neither did its job

**Corrects:** D-142 — its `test_the_sim_cannot_actually_reach_miaos_operating_point`, its buffering-below-band assertion, its `MIAO_BUFFERING_BAND` comparison and its `FREE_SO2_FLOOR_MGL` are replaced; the "sim under-binds SO2" prose D-143 did not enumerate is replaced with them.

D-143 measured the bound-SO2 deficit away and deliberately edited nothing, leaving four artefacts
shipping and passing. This is the build beat that reworks them. **Tests only** — nothing in `src/`
was touched, so no D-140 pin moved. `tests/benchmarks/test_validation_danilewicz_so2_o2.py` goes
from 10 tests to 13; the full suite is **1384 passed** (from 1381).

### The four were really two code sites and a paragraph, and the paragraph was the loudest

D-143 enumerated four artefacts. Three of them —
`test_the_sim_cannot_actually_reach_miaos_operating_point`, the buffering-below-band assertion and
the `MIAO_BUFFERING_BAND` comparison — are **the same two lines**, the body of that one test. The
distinct sites are that test and `FREE_SO2_FLOOR_MGL`.

The fifth carrier was in none of D-143's four: the **module docstring**, which stated the withdrawn
claim outright — *"The sim under-binds SO2: its buffering capacity is below Miao's on both
alternatives, so it has no bound reservoir to replenish free SO2 under the O2 challenge."* Prose is
where a withdrawn claim survives a green suite, because nothing asserts it. Counting artefacts by
test name undercounts them.

### Half one — the buffering comparison, re-made on Miao's statistic

`_Run.buffering` is gone. Two fields replace it, and their names are the finding:

- **`buffering_secant`** — Miao's Table 3 statistic: the secant of the equilibrium locus
  `total(free)` over free SO2 4→52 mg/L (`MIAO_ADDITION_SPAN_MGL`), at fixed carbonyl pools, read
  from the state the challenge window **opens** at. That is what an addition series on an unchanged
  wine is.
- **`oxidation_path_slope`** — D-142's number, `ratio / free_factor` along the oxidation path.
  Kept, because deleting it would lose the ability to state that the two differ.

Measured at the shared operating point:

| statistic | direct | cascade | Miao |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| addition-method secant | **1.3197** | **1.3197** | **1.2526-1.9882** |
| oxidation-path slope | 1.1761 | 1.1333 | — |

`test_sulfite_buffering_matches_miao_on_his_own_statistic` asserts the secant is in band across
**every real-mode run this file integrates** — both alternatives over the whole valid dose range,
agreeing to 1e-9 — because the secant is a property of the carbonyl pools and the pH, so neither
the oxidative set nor the SO2 dose moves it. **That invariance is the point**: it is why this
statistic, unlike the ratio, is not an artefact of the operating point. Measured across doses
40-100 on both sets it reads 1.3197 at every one, and 1.319717 at `LIMIT_SO2` = 500 too — the
limit arms are left out of the assertion because they are limit probes rather than operating
points, not because they would fail.

(The first draft asserted only the two runs at the shared operating point while the docstring
claimed the dose sweep — coverage claimed in prose for a measurement that had been left in a probe
file. The invariance is the load-bearing half of the argument; asserting it at one dose would have
been the exact shape of the two verdicts this file already withdrew.
[[feedback-conceded-caveats-are-not-coverage]])

`test_the_oxidation_path_slope_is_a_different_quantity` guards the category error itself. Leaving
the oxidation-path number in the `_Run` where a later reader can reach for it is only safe if
something asserts it is *not* Miao's — otherwise D-142's comparison is one attribute access away
from being re-made. It asserts the slope runs at least 0.05 BELOW the secant, which is the direction
that made the old assertion look true.

**The in-band result ships tagged `speculative`** (Prime Directive 1), stated in the docstring, not
asserted: the secant is carried almost entirely by pyruvate and alpha-KG, and at those pools' own
shipped uncertainty bounds it spans 1.1242 / 1.3370 / 2.1046 — a band that BRACKETS Miao's, with the
low corner below his floor. So the assertion is the nominal one and the tolerance is tight; widening
it to "survive the uncertainty" would be claiming a robustness D-143 already measured and did not
find. [[feedback-conceded-caveats-are-not-coverage]] cuts the other way here — the corner is stated
*and* the assertion is scoped to what was actually run.

### Half two — the guard, renamed after measuring both of Miao's printed criteria

`FREE_SO2_FLOOR_MGL = 10.0` claimed Miao's wine-#1 exclusion. D-143 showed it excludes four of the
seven wines that define his band. The obvious repair — encode his actual criterion — was **measured
first, and it fails**, in two different ways. His printed basis is two things: the *starting* free
SO2 level (*"the very low free SO2 of this wine, which started at 8 mg/L"*) and r2 of 0.8103 against
>0.91 for the rest.

| dose | free SO2 at window start | inside Miao's 15-28? | r2 of the ratio regression | clears 0.91? | min free | clears 10? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 40 | **25.01** | **yes** | 0.98975 | yes | 2.80 | NO |
| 60 | 41.50 | no | 0.99796 | yes | 8.20 | NO |
| 70 | 50.23 | no | 0.99905 | yes | 12.43 | yes |
| 80 | **59.18** | **no** | 0.99954 | yes | 17.77 | yes |
| 100 | 77.56 | no | 0.99987 | yes | 31.27 | yes |

(free-SO2 columns are the direct set; the cascade's starts are identical and its minima higher.)

- **The starting-level criterion selects the opposite doses.** It admits dose 40 — the operating
  point whose curvature produced D-142's inverted headline — and rejects dose 80, the one that fixed
  it. Encoding Miao's own criterion would have re-introduced the defect it was invoked to prevent.
- **r2 does not discriminate at all.** Every dose clears 0.91 by an enormous margin, because a
  simulated series has none of the analytical scatter his cut was screening for. A criterion
  transplanted from a lab dataset can be *inapplicable* rather than merely strict.

So the floor keeps its value and loses its claim. It is now `SIM_CURVATURE_FLOOR_MGL`, and its
docstring states what it forbids — measuring the ratio in the regime where, in Miao's words,
*"oxidation reactions must necessarily involve other components, and thus the ratio of reaction with
O2 must change"* — records that the number 10.0 and the per-sample form are **not his**, carries
both measurements above, and carries D-143's table of the four band-defining wines it excludes. The
strictness is deliberate and now argued rather than smuggled: the one defect this file has ever
shipped was measuring inside the curvature regime.
[[feedback-name-guards-for-what-they-forbid]]

`test_the_operating_point_satisfies_miaos_exclusion_criterion` →
`test_the_operating_point_clears_the_curvature_floor`, for the same reason.

### The replacement for the withdrawn test asserts the fact and refuses to name a cause

`test_the_operating_point_sits_above_miaos_wines` keeps what was true — the sim opens the window at
~59 mg/L free, ~2x Miao's highest wine, so every band comparison here is an envelope check and the
D-141 quinone-branching question is not settled by one — and drops what was false. It asserts the
negative half explicitly (the secant is in band, so binding is **not** the reason) and then stops.

It stops because the candidate replacement does not survive its own measurement. The sim spends free
SO2 faster per mg O2 than Miao's Table 4 factors (0.7456-1.8945 mg/mg) — but that gap is
dose-dependent: mass-basis **1.47** at dose 40 on the cascade, 1.96 at dose 40 direct, 2.00 at dose
80 cascade, **3.01** at dose 80 direct. At the low end it is inside his range. So "the sim depletes
free SO2 too fast" is not a structural finding, it is a statement about a dose — which is the exact
shape of the two verdicts this file has already had to withdraw. It stays an open question (D-143),
un-encoded. **Asserting a fact without a mechanism is weaker and correct; asserting the third
dose-contingent mechanism as structural would have been the fourth withdrawal.**

### A method guard, and what writing it found

`test_the_analytic_locus_is_the_shipped_binding_solver` asserts the secant's closed form **is**
`acidbase.bound_so2_molar` rather than a private re-derivation of it — the same guard D-143 ran as a
probe, promoted into the suite because the secant is now load-bearing.

The first draft round-tripped free → total → free through `acidbase.free_so2` on a **state vector**
and read errors to **2.55e-4 mg/L**, against D-143's probe worst of 3.85e-11. Chasing that gap found
two things and neither was the binding solver:

1. **pH does not move with total SO2.** Swept 0 → 200 mg/L total, `ph_of_state` returns an
   identical value — SO2 is outside the D-22 charge balance. This is load-bearing for the secant,
   which sweeps free SO2 at frozen beta: a re-solved-beta secant differs from the frozen one by
   **6.3e-6 (0.0005%)**, so the addition series needs no pH tracking.
2. **The file's own molar mass was wrong in the last three digits.** It carried
   `M_SO2 = 64.06`; `core.chemistry` builds **64.058** from atomic masses — 3.1e-5 relative. Far
   below any band asserted here, but every mg/L↔mol/L conversion in this file rides the locus the
   model solves. `M_O2`/`M_SO2` and the four carbonyl molar masses are now imported from
   `core.chemistry` instead of retyped.

   **It moved two quoted digits, and no assertion could have caught that.** The ratio is
   `slope(total/M_SO2 vs consumed/M_O2)`, so the masses do not cancel: re-measured through the
   file's own `_run`, the cascade straddle goes 1.1339 → **1.1338** at dose 80 and 1.1035 →
   **1.1034** at 70 (60 and the direct 1.7707 are unmoved at four decimals; the secant is unmoved
   entirely, `M_SO2` cancelling everywhere but `h` vs `K`). Every assertion here is a *band*, so
   the suite stayed green through a change that invalidated prose — the numbers in D-142/D-143
   are left as measured, since the archive is append-only, and this record's are the corrected
   ones. **Re-measure quoted decimals after a units change; a green band asserts nothing about
   them.**

Re-stated as **pure algebra** — free → total in closed form, total → free through
`bound_so2_molar`, no state, no pH solve, no scenario — the worst error over a 120-point grid
(5 pH x 3 acetaldehyde pools x 2 keto-acid scalings x 4 free levels) is **4.3e-10 mg/L**. The pinned
tolerance is 1e-8, ~20x that measured floor. [[feedback-pin-tolerance-vs-solver-tolerance]]

The residual was never in the thing being guarded. **The guard was entangled with two quantities it
did not mean to test** — which is this batch's own recurring lesson (D-143's whole finding is a
comparison of two entangled statistics) arriving one level down, in the guard written to enforce it.

### The binder list is read from the model, not transcribed

`_SO2_BINDERS` is built from `acidbase`'s own key/parameter names, all **four** of them — D-28's
acetaldehyde, D-51's two keto-acids and D-130's 5-oxofructose. 5-oxofructose is zero in a
non-botrytis white, and D-143's probes carried three binders for exactly that reason. Dropping a
binder because it happens to be zero in the scenario at hand is how a botrytis scenario would later
read a wrong secant with nothing going red. [[feedback-check-the-schema-not-the-caller]]

### What does NOT change

Every downstream number and every other assertion. `WINE_REALISTIC_SO2` stays 80,
`CASCADE_VALID_DOSES` stays (60, 70, 80), the traverse falsifier (direct 0.0003 vs cascade 0.859)
stands, the cascade straddle (1.0704 / 1.1034 / 1.1338) stands, the direct set still reads 1.7707
above Miao's ceiling and inside Danilewicz's, the two limits still emerge at 1 and 2. The cascade
stays **non-default**; `k_copper_multiplier` stays 600; the fate gap and its two paywalled sources
are untouched. The dosing schedule is **not** changed — D-143's must-60 grid is a separate owner
decision with its own record, and the secant correction needed no reservoir to land in band.

**Tally: sixteen cascade-era claims falsified by re-measuring.** The new one is a criterion:
*a reference's own printed exclusion rule can be inapplicable to a simulation rather than merely
strict* — Miao's r2 cut screens analytical scatter that a solver does not have, and his starting-level
cut selects for the regime this file must avoid. Borrowing a criterion needs the same "did I measure
the same thing?" test as borrowing a number.

## D-145 — The dosing schedule measured and refused: D-143's "five for five" is three for five (its buffering column was the oxidation-path slope it had itself just withdrawn, and its ratio was read at free SO2 1.51 mg/L), the acetaldehyde reservoir provably CANNOT move Miao's Table 3 statistic because it saturates across his span, and the free-SO2 depletion gap is retired rather than reframed

**Corrects:** D-143 — Finding 5's "five for five" is three for five (two entries re-measure as a
category error and a sub-floor measurement), and its "Miao's own three tables do not satisfy his
Eq. 1, needing 1.30-1.94" omitted the M_SO2/M_O2 conversion; in consistent units Eq. 1 closes to
0.6492-0.9696.

The owner's pick after D-144. D-143 flagged its must-60/late-0 schedule as *"an owner decision with
its own record"*, and D-144 deliberately left the schedule alone. **The schedule is unchanged, and
nothing in the shipped benchmark moves.** Working notes and probes:
`M:\claud_projects\temp\d145-dosing-schedule\`.

Every sim-side statistic here is **imported from the shipped benchmark module** rather than
re-derived. That is not tidiness: D-143's probes re-derived them, and that is exactly where two of
its errors entered.

### D-143's Finding 5 loses two of its five

| quantity | D-143 | re-measured | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| total SO2 60.0 vs his 27-153 | ok | ok | stands |
| free SO2 at window start 15.66 vs his 9-28 | ok | ok | stands |
| total/free 3.832 vs his 2.14-6.65 | ok | ok | stands |
| buffering 1.6185 vs his 1.2526-1.9882 | ok | **wrong statistic** | **withdrawn** |
| SO2:O2 ratio 1.1283 vs his 1.0972-1.6621 | ok | **measured below the floor** | **withdrawn** |

`probe_operating_point.py` computed its `buffering` column as `ratio / free_factor` —
d(total)/d(free) along the **oxidation path**. That is the quantity D-144 named
`oxidation_path_slope` and forbade comparing to `MIAO_BUFFERING_BAND`, an **addition-method
secant**. D-143's own Finding 2 *is* that the two are not interchangeable; its Finding 5 then
interchanged them. Measured correctly, must-60/late-0 reads a secant of **1.3355**, not 1.6185.

And its ratio is read where free SO2 ends at **1.51 mg/L** — deeper into the curvature regime than
the 2.8/6.8 run whose headline D-142 had to withdraw. It is not a fifth pass; it is the defect
restated at another dose. The three survivors are all properties of the *starting* state and none
of them touches the O2 challenge.

**The lesson is narrower than "check the arithmetic".** A beat that establishes a distinction can
still violate it three findings later, in the summary table, using a helper written before the
distinction existed. The guard against that is not care; it is importing the statistic.

### The reservoir cannot move the buffering statistic — it moves the intercept

Over Miao's addition span the bisulfite activity `h` runs 6.087e-5 → 7.913e-4 M at pH 3.4.
Acetaldehyde's K is **1.5e-6 M**, so `h/K` = **40.6 → 527.5**: it is **saturated at both ends of
the secant**. A saturated binder contributes a constant to `total`, moving the **intercept**, not
the slope. The three keto-acid/oxofructose binders (K = 1.4e-4 to 5.55e-4) have `h/K` spanning
0.11-5.65 and are the ones that carry the slope.

Sweeping acetaldehyde over the whole range D-143's own Table 4 intercepts imply: the secant goes
1.3222 (pool 0) → 1.3326 (0.352 mM) → 1.3373 (0.5115) → **1.3737** (1.742), while `total(free=4)`
goes 8.81 → **117.72**. **A 5x reservoir moves the slope 3.1% and the intercept 4x.** So
"must-dosing fixes the buffering number" was never on offer: the secant was already in band with
no reservoir at all, and no reservoir can move it appreciably. Miao says so himself in the Figure 5
caption — *"there are weak binders in wine that bind only to a fraction of the added SO2"*. **The
buffering capacity is a weak-binder statistic**; acetaldehyde is the strong binder and is not in
it.

**A corroboration fell out of this.** Miao's Table 3 intercepts span **22.527-111.61** mg/L. The
shipped model, fed the reservoir D-143 derived *from those same intercepts*, puts `total(free=4)`
at **30.8-117.7**. The strong-binder arithmetic reproduces his intercept spread from the other
direction — independent support for D-143's Finding 1, obtained without any of Finding 5's
machinery. D-143's reservoir size survives; only its consequences were mis-stated.

The keto-acid pools do move the secant, and D-143 already measured that (their own shipped bounds
give 1.1242-2.1046, bracketing his band). **The prohibition on re-running that sweep stands.**

### The grid interior was unexamined, is not empty, and still fails

A 6x5 grid over (must, late), both alternatives (`grid.txt`). D-143 reported one edge cell.
**8 direct and 9 cascade cells hold a reservoir AND clear the floor** — so the interior was worth
looking at. **None of the 58 satisfies all six quantities.** Every floor-clearing cell opens far
above Miao's wines (cheapest: direct must-60/late-40 at free0 **46.46**, cascade must-80/late-20 at
**33.73**, against his 15-28), and on the direct set the ratio is then outside his band at every
one of them (1.6886-1.8688 vs his ceiling 1.6621).

**The binding constraint is neither the reservoir nor the ratio: it is that the floor and Miao's
starting range cannot both be met.**

### That conflict is schedule-invariant, and the dose is eliminated by fixing the endpoint

Matched pairs, bisecting the late dose at each must dose so every pair opens at the **same** free
SO2 by construction with reservoirs differing several fold.

**The bound pool barely buffers.** At free0 pinned to 50.0 (direct), going from 0 to 1.284 mM
acetaldehyde adds **82 mg/L of bound SO2** and returns **0.297 mg/L of free** — `fmin` 12.302 →
12.600, a 2.4% move. Mechanistically the same fact as the saturation above: the adduct holds what
it binds and releases ~2% as free SO2 falls.

Then bisect so free SO2 bottoms out *exactly* on the floor. This **eliminates the dose by fixing
the endpoint** rather than by hoping a statistic is invariant. Call it `free0*`:

| set | must 0 | must 40 | must 80 | must 120 | spread | vs his 28 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direct | 45.483 | 45.306 | 45.058 | 44.776 | **1.55%** | **1.62x** |
| cascade | 30.462 | 30.340 | 30.154 | 29.949 | **1.69%** | **1.09x** |

Across an 80 mg/L swing in bound SO2, `free0*` moves **1.6%** — in the helpful direction and
nowhere near far enough. Closing the direct set's gap to 28 needs a 38% reduction; 120 mg/L of must
SO2 buys 1.6%.

**`free0*` is conditioned on Miao's O2 protocol — 14 mg/L in two rounds — and that conditioning is
load-bearing.** It is dose-independent in the sense D-144 demanded (one number per set, no dose
left to argue about) *because the O2 load is transcribed from the reference rather than chosen*. A
reader re-deriving it under a different `N_ROUNDS` will get a different number and should.

### Swept over the floor, the verdict splits — and only half of it is robust

The floor is a sim-side choice (D-144), so a verdict resting on it must be swept over it:

| set | floor 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| direct `free0*` | 32.98 (1.18x) | 45.48 (1.62x) | 54.72 (1.95x) | 62.53 (2.23x) |
| direct depletion mg/mg | 1.998 **out** | 2.534 **out** | 2.838 **out** | 3.038 **out** |
| cascade `free0*` | 21.51 (**0.77x**) | 30.46 (1.09x) | 38.11 (1.36x) | 45.06 (1.61x) |
| cascade depletion mg/mg | 1.180 in | 1.462 in | 1.651 in | 1.789 in |

- **Floor-CONTINGENT, never state it without its floor:** "the sim cannot open inside Miao's 15-28
  and still clear the floor" is unconditional for the **direct** set (1.18x even at floor 5) but
  **false for the cascade at floor 5**, which opens at 21.5 — inside his range.
- **Floor-ROBUST:** the free-SO2 **depletion factor** puts the direct set outside Miao's Table 4
  range (0.7456-1.8945) at every floor tested, and the cascade inside it at every floor.

**Do not over-read the robust row.** It is the *same* separation the SO2:O2 ratio already shows at
these operating points (direct 1.77 above his ceiling, cascade 1.13 in band), seen through another
statistic. It is **more robust to the operating-point choice** than the ratio straddle's 3.4%
headroom, but it is **not independent corroboration**, it does **not** settle D-141's
quinone-branching question, and it licenses **no** change to the default.

### The depletion-rate gap is retired, not reframed

D-144 left "the sim depletes free SO2 faster than Miao's wines" open, wanting a dose-independent
framing before anything was built on it. There is nothing left to frame.

**First, a unit correction.** D-143 recorded that Miao's Eq. 1 (`depletion = ratio / buffering`)
*"his own three tables do not satisfy"*, needing 1.30-1.94. That omitted `M_SO2/M_O2`. **Table 2's
regression slope is mass-basis and its reported "molar reaction ratio" column is that slope /
2.002** — confirmed to a systematic **-0.10%** across all eight wines, a transcription-grade check
rather than a fit. In consistent units Eq. 1 closes in his data to **0.6492-0.9696** (mean 0.8558).

**Second, the overshoot decomposes exactly.** Against wine 8, his most-depleting: total **1.5909x**
= 1.2533x (the SO2:O2 ratio) x 0.9491x (buffering — the sim buffers MORE, which *helps*) x 1.3374x
(the Eq. 1 residual, i.e. secant vs oxidation-path slope). The product closes to four decimals. So
the depletion factor is **not an independent quantity**: it is the ratio — already measured,
already asserted — over a denominator that is **in band**, times a residual.

**Third, the residual is itself dose-contingent.** The secant is dose-invariant, so the residual is
just `secant / oxidation_path_slope`: direct 0.8473 / 0.9318 / 1.0352 / 1.1221 at doses 20/40/60/80,
cascade 0.8863 / 0.9786 / 1.0892 / 1.1645. It crosses Miao's 0.6492-0.9696 between 40 and 60.

**Every dose-varying factor in the decomposition is dose-contingent, and the only dose-invariant
factor in it — the secant — is already asserted and in band.** D-144's refusal to encode the
depletion gap was right, and for a stronger reason than it had: not "no framing found yet" but
**"the exact decomposition has no invariant part left to claim."** The sim's residual sitting on
the opposite side of 1 from all eight of his wines is recorded and built on by nothing.

This does not conflict with the floor sweep above. At a *free* dose the depletion factor is
dose-contingent and holds no mechanism to build; at a *fixed endpoint*, with the endpoint then
swept, the dose freedom is removed by the condition and what remains separates the two shipped
alternatives. The first is why nothing gets built; the second is why the number is worth recording.

### What changes

**No measured quantity in the shipped benchmark.** The schedule stays late-only;
`WINE_REALISTIC_SO2` stays 80; `CASCADE_VALID_DOSES` stays (60, 70, 80); the straddle (1.0704 /
1.1034 / 1.1338), the traverse (direct 0.0003 vs cascade 0.859), the direct 1.7707, the secant
1.3197 and its 1e-9 invariance pin all stand untouched. Because the schedule does not change, the
secant-invariance breakage a must dose would have caused never arises. The cascade stays
**non-default**; `k_copper_multiplier` stays 600; the fate gap and its two paywalled sources are
untouched.

**One guard is added, on the JUSTIFICATION rather than on a number.**
`test_the_buffering_secant_is_a_weak_binder_statistic` asserts `h/K > 20` for acetaldehyde at the
bottom of Miao's addition span, and `h/K < 20` for the three weak binders at the top. Pure
algebra, no integration.

It exists because **the secant pin cannot catch this, and it is the only assertion that would
have to.** On the late-only schedule acetaldehyde is 0, so the secant is set by the keto-acids and
is *completely insensitive* to acetaldehyde's K — re-parameterise `SO2_BINDING_PARAM`, or add a
fifth binder with a small K, and 1.3197 keeps passing to 1e-9 while the saturation argument that
licenses this record's refusal silently stops being true. The measured margins are real rather
than decorative: `h/K` = 41.19 at the worst-case pH 3.80 against the threshold of 20 (it trips if
K grows 2.1x), and the weak binders sit at 1.45-5.74. This is the same move D-144 made when it
promoted the locus probe into the suite: the secant became load-bearing, so what the secant rests
on got a guard. What it rests on has now moved one level down.

One documentation fix. `test_sulfite_buffering_matches_miao_on_his_own_statistic` explained its
invariance as *"the secant is a property of the carbonyl pools and the pH — neither of which the
oxidative alternative or the SO2 dose moves."* True **only for the late-only family**, where
acetaldehyde is pinned at 0 (measured -1.1e-12 mol/L, solver noise; `_binder_pools` clamps it). A
**must** dose does move the pools and does move the secant, to 1.3517 at must-100. **The invariance
belongs to the schedule, not to the statistic**, and the docstring now says so and says what to do
if a must-dosed schedule is ever adopted.

**Tally: eighteen cascade-era claims falsified by re-measuring.** The two new ones are a category
error committed by the very record that established the category, and a units omission that made a
reference's own equation look broken when it closes to 15%.

Both errors were committed by **re-derived probe helpers**, not by the shipped module — which is
why every statistic in this beat was imported from `tests/benchmarks/test_validation_danilewicz_so2_o2.py`
instead. The working notes that produced them (`temp\d143-so2-binding\FINDINGS.md`,
`probe_operating_point.py`) carry SUPERSEDED headers pointing here, because they are grep targets
for the next beat and an un-annotated stale number is how this cycle repeats.

## D-146 — the Milestone-3 tail: the rename shipped, the sotolon enantiomer split refused, and the methionine sink is BLOCKED rather than merely unbuilt

**Corrects:** D-107 — its sotolon-enantiomer note. "One racemic pool against one threshold is a lump, and the ~100× spread means the OAV is soft by that much" is wrong on both halves: the shipped threshold is the *racemate's*, so pool and threshold are commensurate, and (R)/(S) are one molecule, so "lump" is the wrong word regardless.
**Corrects:** D-106 — the *status* of the methionine sink, not its diagnosis. D-106's defect is real and stands; its "recorded, not built" implied the fix was merely awaiting a beat. It is blocked: the sink's own parameter is ill-posed on the two sources the sink machinery rests on.

**Owner named the tail — `oav`→`magnitude`, the methionine sink, the sotolon enantiomers — as "the largest thing with
no sourcing block on it", and asked for whatever is closest to reality where a call was needed. Two of the three
shipped; the third turned out to have precisely the sourcing block the brief assumed it lacked, and proving that is
this beat's sharpest result.** 1385 → **1389 passed (+4), both MEASURED** (the baseline from `--collect-only` in a
throwaway detached worktree at 566d218, the D-110 technique). ruff + mypy clean. The racemate guard is
mutation-tested; the two rename guards are structural.

### 1. The rename shipped, and its NARROWNESS is the decision — not its churn

D-98 recorded `oav` → `magnitude` as "the deeper fix, **deferred** as churn across slice 1's callers and tests for no
new observable", and shipped the `rule` tag instead. The tag was the right interim and it is not enough: it can only
say *afterwards* which quantity you are holding. `MaxRuleProjector` puts a raw OAV in that field and
`StevensProjector` puts `OAV ** n`; a field **named** `oav` asserts a concentration ratio for a value that may be a
compressed intensity. That is D-96's category error — one field, two quantities — surviving in the one place a
disclaimer cannot reach, which is the name.

**The churn was 13 sites, and the interesting half of the decision is what was NOT renamed.**
`OAVReading.oav`, `oav_series`, `oav_tier`, `AROMA_COMPOUNDS` and the module `sensory/oav.py` keep the name, because
under every projector they *are* OAVs — there is no second quantity sharing those names. A global sweep over all 72
occurrences of the identifier would have spent churn to make the codebase **less** precise, in the name of a fix
about precision. That half is invisible in a diff, so it is pinned:
`test_the_rename_did_not_touch_the_quantities_that_really_are_oavs` makes a future "finish the rename" sweep fail
loudly rather than look like tidying.

### 2. Sotolon's enantiomers: MEASURED AND REFUSED, twice over

Pons *et al.* 2008 (J. Agric. Food Chem. 56:1606-1610) is real and its numbers transcribe from the abstract verbatim:
*"The perception threshold of (S)-sotolon (0.8 microg/L) in model wine solution was 100 times lower than that of the
(R) form (89 microg/L)."* D-107 concluded the sotolon OAV is soft by that factor. **It is not, and the discriminating
question was never asked: what does the shipped `threshold_sotolon_wine: 8.0` measure?**

**(i) It measures the racemate, BY CONSTRUCTION.** Pons had to *separate the enantiomers by preparative HPLC* to
threshold them — that is the first sentence of his own abstract, and it is why the paper exists. So every earlier wine
threshold, including the ones this entry actually cites (Guichard/Pham/Etiévant ~10 µg/L, Pham 1995, Cutzach), was
determined by spiking the only form that existed: the racemate. And the model's pool **is** racemic, because its only
route — `SotolonAldolCondensation` — is the aldol Pham ran "by a purely chemical mechanism", which has no chiral
influence. Pool and threshold therefore sit at the same enantiomeric ratio. That is the *most* commensurate
configuration in `sensory.yaml`, not a lump; "lump" names a pool of several molecules read against one
representative's threshold, and (R) and (S) are the same molecule.

**(ii) The pair is a MODEL-SOLUTION measurement, which this file already excludes from a wine pool.** The same rule
that keeps DMS's 1.74–3.67 µg/L model-solution thresholds out of a wine pool (D-102) and the beer fusel OTCs out of
beer (D-99). Splitting the OAV as `0.5·C / 0.8` would therefore commit **both** errors at once — double-count the
racemate *and* import an excluded matrix — and it would inflate sotolon's OAV ~5× on arithmetic rather than chemistry.
**The ~5× is itself the matrix gap**, and it is independently bracketed for this exact molecule: Pereira *et al.* 2019
(Biomolecules 9:720) measure sotolon at 9 µg/L in model solution against 23–69 µg/L in real Madeira, i.e. 2.6–7.6×.
The two datasets are consistent once the matrix is accounted for; the "inconsistency" was the correction being
smuggled in as a chemistry claim.

**What the racemic claim DOES cost, and it is ASYMMETRIC — which is what "soft by ~100×" concealed.** Used as a
**ratio**, where the model-solution matrix factor divides out, the pair bounds how far a non-racemic wine departs from
this reading. An (S)-extreme wine reads at most **~2× above**; an (R)-extreme wine reads up to **~56× below**. So the
model's exposure is **overstatement** of sotolon, and the understatement it can commit is bounded by a factor of two.
**The bound has a second proof that does not need the contested assumption**: computed under the max rule this project
actually ships it is 2.00×/55.6×, under the additive rule the OAV lens refuses (D-67) it is 1.98×/56.1× — agreement to
~1%, so the conclusion does not rest on perceptual additivity. Executable in
`test_the_racemic_assumption_costs_at_most_2x_under_and_56x_over`.

**It is a SCOPE LIMIT, not an error band.** Pons found three patterns in commercial dry whites — racemic, R-excess,
S-excess — preserved by sotolon's slow ~20-month racemization. Those excesses arrive by routes this model does not
carry, which is the same shape as `methanethiol`'s "models only the autolytic route" limit, one Process over. Real
wines reach neither extreme (Pons reports *excess*, not purity), so 2×/56× are outer bounds.

### 3. The methionine sink: THE STOICHIOMETRIC GATE PASSES AND THE SINK IS STILL UNBUILDABLE

D-105 named it, D-106 sharpened it — *"a no-lees heavily-dosed wine makes methional but not phenylacetaldehyde, and
that is not chemistry — it is the missing methionine sink showing through"* — and the deferred tail has carried it as
an ordinary unbuilt item since. The build is one `FUSEL_SPECS` entry: **methionol** (3-(methylthio)-1-propanol) is
methionine's Ehrlich alcohol, and adding it would give methionine the fermentation-phase consumer D-105 found it
lacked, with `PrecursorNonEhrlichFates` supplying the sink for free.

**The D-118 feasibility check — the one that killed 2-phenylethanol — PASSES here, and that made the block look
absent.** Must methionine averages 3.64 mg/L = **24.40 µmol/L** (mean of 738 musts); typical white-wine methionol is
507–998 µg/L = **4.8–9.4 µmol/L**, i.e. **20–39%** of the precursor. Unlike phenylalanine there is no
more-alcohol-than-precursor impossibility at typical concentrations. **So the block is not on the stoichiometry — it
is on the parameter, and that distinction is the finding.**

**`f_non_ehrlich_methionine` is not unmeasured. It is ILL-POSED.** The registry forces it: adding methionol to
`FUSEL_SPECS` makes `NON_EHRLICH_FRACTION_PARAMS` demand it and the loader fails loudly without it. Neither source the
sink rests on can supply it, and **neither is a "didn't find it" — both are structurally incapable**:

- **Crépin *et al.* 2017** never *detected* methionine: *"all of the proteinogenic amino acids (except for tryptophan,
  methionine, cysteine, and tyrosine, which were not detected by the gas chromatography [GC]-MS method used)"*. There
  is no partition to report, so no re-read produces one.
- **Rollero *et al.* 2017** fed U-¹³C **leucine and valine**, and methionol is downstream of neither. A perfect re-read
  of the source that anchors every other enrichment in this project cannot reach this compound.

**And the mass-balance closure — the `f_de_novo_2_phenylethanol` pattern, the obvious fallback — does not merely have
a wide band. It leaves the parameter's own domain.** Measured across **one paper's own 22-strain panel at one must
composition** (FEMS Yeast Res 2021, foab038: methionol 1.5–6.1 mg/L):

| producer | methionol | µmol/L | Ehrlich share of 24.40 µmol/L must methionine | implied `f_non_ehrlich_methionine` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lowest | 1.5 mg/L | 14.13 | 0.579 | **+0.421** |
| highest | 6.1 mg/L | 57.45 | **2.355** | **−1.355** |

**The two concentration ranges in this section are not in conflict, and the difference is the whole reason the gate
passed while the parameter failed.** The 20–39% gate used **typical white-wine** methionol (507–998 µg/L); this table
uses **one controlled strain panel's full spread** (1.5–6.1 mg/L, foab038 — the better source, read rather than
summarised). A feasibility gate is rightly asked at typical concentrations; a *parameter's domain* must hold across
the range a real strain can produce, and this one does not. **Reporting only the gate would have been the narrowing
D-101/D-108 warn about** — it is the range where the answer looks safe.

The parameter's declared domain is `[0, 1)` and `PrecursorNonEhrlichFates` raises outside it. **The derived value is
negative for most of a single study's strain range** — above an Ehrlich share of 1.0 the wine makes more methionol
than the must supplied methionine, the D-118 tell arriving one precursor over but only at the top of the range. The
conclusion is robust to which must figure is used: against the model's own must at `amino_acids_gpl = 1.0`
(5.00 mg/L = 33.51 µmol/L) the same panel gives +0.578 → **−0.714**, still crossing.

**The de-novo escape hatch is WORSE here than it was for phenylalanine, and that is what closes the door.** D-118
rescued `f_non_ehrlich_phenylalanine = 0.975` by capping the amino-acid branch with a sourced de-novo share. The
identical move for methionol needs `f_de_novo_methionol`, and the only route to it is **sulfate assimilation** —
confirmed live (foab038: *"the absence of methionine in the medium did not prevent the formation at a basal level"*,
attributed to *"the intracellular pool of de novo synthetized methionine"*), and unquantified. So the fix for one
unmeasured number is a second unmeasured number. That is the D-98 trap in its purest form: two author estimates
wearing the costume of fidelity, propping each other up.

**The one datum that exists does not close it, and is worth recording because it looks like it might.** foab038
reports *"at least 65% of initial methionine was recovered as ME, 3MTPAc, 3MTPA and E3MTP"* — but at a **20-fold**
methionine excess (~73 mg/L, a regime no must reaches) and **lumped over four compounds**, not methionol alone.
Reading it as `1 − f = 0.65` would be D-117's error exactly: a number from the wrong denominator and the wrong regime,
adopted because it is the only one available. It does carry a real qualitative finding — the Ehrlich route takes a
large share of methionine when methionine is abundant — which implies `f_non_ehrlich_methionine` is **strongly
composition-dependent**, and therefore that D-104's *static* `f` is worse for this precursor than for any already
shipped.

**Recorded, not built. Nothing was added to `FUSEL_SPECS`, no state slot, no parameter.** The defect D-106 exposed is
unchanged and still real; what changes is its status, from deferred to blocked.

**THE NAMED UNLOCK**, in the D-118/D-119 form (a specific fetch, not "more literature"): a **¹³C-methionine tracer
resolving methionol's must-vs-de-novo provenance** at a wine-realistic methionine concentration — i.e. what Minebois
Fig. 6A was for 2-phenylethanol, run on the sulfur branch. Either that, or a Crépin-style fate partition from a method
that detects methionine (their GC-MS derivatisation is the limitation, not the biology). One number lifts the block;
without it, both parameters are guesses.

### 4. Found in passing: two stale claims in the sotolon prose, the D-109/D-110 class

`threshold_sotolon_wine`'s provenance still said sotolon's *"2 acetaldehyde-derived carbons are still lumped into that
threonine draw"* and named it *"the threonine/acetaldehyde-derived furanone"*. Both predate **D-107**, which moved
sotolon out of `MaillardStrecker` into `SotolonAldolCondensation` — where the acetaldehyde carbons are debited off the
**acetaldehyde pool**, and threonine is sotolon's *grand*parent via α-ketobutyrate rather than its direct precursor.
**Confirmed in the executing body, not the docstring** (`aging.py:2330-2332`: `d[sotolon] = n_sot · M_SOTOLON`,
`d[alpha_ketobutyrate] = −n_sot · M_ALPHA_KETOBUTYRATE`, `d[acetaldehyde] = −n_sot · M_ACETALDEHYDE`, and **no
threonine term at all**) — checking the code rather than the class docstring is the point, since a docstring is
exactly the artifact this finding is about, and reading one to convict another would repeat the error. The parameter
file is the file furthest from the
mechanism, so nothing it does fails when its prose goes stale — the lesson D-109 and D-110 both landed, arriving here
on a third file in a beat that was reading it for another reason entirely.
