## D-147 — the D-133 burst wired at last, into an opt-in third oxidative set: constraint 1 holds end-to-end, constraint 2 fails structurally, and under the default closure the "self-exhausting sink" is a permanent ~37% tax

**Corrects:** D-133 — three things. Its Process shipped wired into **no medium at all** while its own docstring claimed the wine medium; its load-bearing "fast, self-exhausting sink" shape is a property of Ferreira's saturation protocol, not of the sink; and its D-45 seed argument *inverts* where no consumer exists.
**Flags:** D-138 — its proposed cascade-frame resolution ("a transient modifier on the activation node") assumes a transient. Under the default closure the burst is measured as permanent, so that shape is not available; the cascade-side placement stays UNDETERMINED, and there is deliberately no `cascade_burst`.

**Owner picked this off a four-way list as the highest-information buildable item, and it was: what looked like dead
code turned out to be a live defect, a calibration that had never been run, and a shape claim that is true only where
it was measured.** 1389 → **1418 passed (+29)**. ruff + mypy clean. All 31 D-140 pins **unmoved and un-re-derived** —
which is not a happy accident but the reason for the placement. Measurements:
`M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d147-burst-wiring\` (`FINDINGS.md` + three scripts, none of which edit source).

### 1. What was actually wrong, and why "dead code" undersells it

D-140 recorded that `AntioxidantBurstOxidation` is *"defined, exported, unit-tested and listed in
`compile._AGING_GATED_PROCESSES` — and appears in no medium's `process_factories`"*, so the `begin_aging` enable loop
skips it silently (it guards `name in process_set`, the same guard that makes the tuple beer-safe). That is true and
was the entry point. It is not the whole defect.

**The `burst_antioxidant` slot is seeded 3.3e-3 g/L in every wine and drawn by nothing.** Over a 2 y run of the
default build the pool's `ptp` is **`0.0` exactly** — a constant, never-consumed antioxidant emitted in every output
column for the life of the wine. And the reasoning that put it there is the reasoning that condemns it: D-133 seeded
non-zero on D-45's *"absent does not mean 0"*, because *"a 0 default would silently assert every wine's
Ferreira-measured day-1 O₂-burst is zero."* **Without a consumer that argument inverts.** The missing Process already
asserts the burst never happens — the seed cannot un-assert it — so all the non-zero seed adds is the further claim
that an antioxidant is present and is *never spent*. Strictly worse than 0, and unlike a quiet modelling choice it is
visible to any consumer of the output. `[[feedback-rejected-values-must-be-unreachable]]`, one layer up from a
sampled field: an unreachable *consumer* leaves a reachable *value* asserting something nobody chose.

Third instance of the D-109/D-110/D-146 stale-prose pattern, and the most consequential yet, because this one was in
the *executing* class rather than a parameter file: `aging.py`'s docstring said the pool *"is wired into the wine
medium only"*. It was false from the day D-133 shipped.

### 2. D-133's two joint constraints, run end-to-end for the first time — one holds, one fails

D-140's sentence is the brief: *"D-133's calibration was never exercised end-to-end."* The two constraints **jointly**
pin `k_burst_oxidation` (1.6 L/(g·h)) and `burst_antioxidant_initial` (3.3e-3 g/L) **separately**, so they had to be
run separately, and at **D-133's own operating point** — a fresh 8 mg/L O₂ charge, hermetic (a one-shot pool, as
Ferreira's was), 20 °C — because judging a calibration outside its own stated condition is the D-142 error. Both SO₂
arms were run, since Ferreira reports *both* his rates SO₂-independent.

**Constraint 1 — the ~1.0 mg/L/day day-1 excess: HOLDS.** Read as D-133's target names it, i.e. this Process's *own*
draw: `y_burst_per_o2 = 1.0 g/g`, so the pool's drop **is** the O₂ that went through this route. That gives
**0.929 mg/L/day with SO₂ and 0.949 without** at the instantaneous reading — −5 to −7% off target, comfortably inside
`k_burst_oxidation`'s declared 0.5–5.0× band, and faithful to the isolated unit test's 1.014. **The net-total
difference between the arms is the wrong quantity** (0.637/0.751), because it nets off the ~0.10 mg/L the siblings
back off by as they lose share — a distinction worth recording, since the smaller number reads as a failure and is not.

**Constraint 2 — the pool ~95% spent within one ~10-day saturation cycle: FAILS, and structurally.** With SO₂ the pool
is at **41.8% left at 10 d** and **plateaus at 39.2%**; without SO₂, 22.4% at 10 d and 7.8% at 60 d. Neither reaches
95% spent, ever. The reason is arithmetic, not tuning: spending the pool takes **3.3 mg/L of O₂ through this route
alone**, and the burst is one of six sinks competing for a shared 8 mg/L charge, winning ~35% of it. **It cannot
self-exhaust within one cycle by construction.** With SO₂ the plateau is hard — 7.9996 of the 8.0 mg/L charge is gone
by 60 d — so the pool stops **because the oxygen ran out first**, and no amount of extra *time* rescues it.

**So the PRODUCT `k_burst_oxidation · burst_antioxidant_initial` is constrained and the SPLIT between them is not**,
because constraint 2 was the only thing that pinned the split. That is the precise status of two shipped parameters.

### 3. The green test that hid it, and what it was really testing

`test_burst_pool_exhausts_within_first_saturation_cycle` certifies constraint 2, and passes. It sets **`o2 = 0.5
g/L` — 500 mg/L, ~62× air saturation**, against the ~8 mg/L a saturated wine actually holds, and says why: *"o2 not
limiting… so the burst pool's decay is not confounded by O2 itself running out."*

**O₂ running out is not a confound. It is the binding constraint.** Removing the competition removes the constraint's
entire content, and what remains — an isolated first-order decay against an infinite oxidant — is a restatement of the
rate law, not a test of the timescale. This is `[[feedback-rejected-values-must-be-unreachable]]` in test form and the
D-145 class exactly: a green assertion at an operating point the model can never reach. **Relabelled, not deleted** —
its rate-law and non-negativity content is genuine and worth keeping; only its claim to certify D-133's timescale is
withdrawn, with a pointer to where that claim is now measured at a reachable charge.

The lesson generalises past this test, and is why it is recorded rather than quietly fixed: **a constraint that only
binds in competition cannot be validated on an isolated Process.** D-133 solved both constraints in single-Process
arithmetic where the burst got all the O₂ it needed, then tested them the same way. The joint solve was internally
consistent and end-to-end wrong, and nothing in the suite could tell.

### 4. Under the default closure the shape does not merely weaken — it inverts

The corked bottle is not a smaller version of Ferreira's experiment. There is **no bolus at all**: `o2` at
`begin_aging` is 0.0 and the cork trickles it in at `closure_otr = 1.19e-7 g/L/h`, a **constant** source. Total supply
is therefore identical with and without the burst — **the burst never consumes more O₂, it only steals share**, which
is D-136's supply limitation landing again.

| | |
|---|---|
| O₂ standing level, default build | 1.44e-5 g/L = 0.0144 mg/L — **~550×** below D-133's calibration point |
| O₂ the cork delivers in 2 y | 1.19e-7 × 17532 h = **2.09 mg/L** |
| the pool's O₂ capacity | **3.3 mg/L — 1.6× more than the bottle ever receives in two years** |
| time to spend it **even at 100% capture** | **≥3.2 y** |
| at the measured ~35% share | **~8.5 y, and rising as the share decays** |
| pool actually spent over 2 y | **22.3%** |

**The self-exhausting shape is a property of Ferreira's protocol, not of the sink.** He delivers ~8 mg/L *per 10-day
cycle*; a natural cork delivers 2.09 mg/L *per two years* — **~1400× apart in flux**. Under the default closure the
sink's share of `Σk` never decays, so it is not a burst at all but a **permanent tax**, and the trajectory says so
plainly: the suppression **grows monotonically to a plateau** where a genuine transient would peak and fade.

| slot | aging+1d | aging+7d | aging+30d | 1 y | 2 y |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `o2` | −5.8% | −24.7% | −34.9% | **−37.2%** | **−37.4%** |
| `A420` | −3.9% | −17.7% | −29.4% | **−35.8%** | **−36.4%** |
| `acetaldehyde` | −4.0% | −18.1% | −30.5% | — | — |
| `so2_total` | +0.0001% | +0.009% | +0.11% | **+2.2%** | **+4.7%** |

`o2` quasi-steady-states at `closure_otr / Σᵢkᵢ`, so a 37% drop means the burst holds **37% of `Σk`, permanently**;
every downstream oxidative fate is scaled by ~0.63 for the life of the wine and SO₂ survives correspondingly longer.
**The noise floor was measured before any of this was called a movement** (baseline re-integrated at rtol 1e-8 on a
2× denser grid): ~1.7e-8 for `o2`, ~1.0e-8 for `so2_total`, ~6.6e-7 for `A420`, and the baseline reproduces D-140's
pins to **3e-11 – 7e-9**. Every figure above is five to eight orders of magnitude above its own floor
(`[[feedback-pin-tolerance-vs-solver-tolerance]]` — a pin asserted at 1e-4 while BDF runs at 1e-6 proves nothing
until the floor is taken).

### 5. Ferreira's OWN statistic does not discriminate — and says something else instead

§2 validated against D-133's *arithmetic intermediate* (`2.7 × 0.58 − 0.58 ≈ 1.0`). What the source reports is a
**ratio**: 12/15 wines' initial rate ≥ 2.7× the average. That is the statistic to run — D-144's "Miao's own statistic"
landing a second time. Ferreira's prose fixes **neither** the initial-rate window nor the averaging window, so both
were swept rather than chosen, and the question asked was whether the criterion discriminates at all.

| initial window | base +SO₂ | burst +SO₂ | base −SO₂ | burst −SO₂ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 d | **3.141** ✓ | **4.127** ✓ | 1.871 ✗ | **2.970** ✓ |
| 0.5 d | **2.997** ✓ | **3.860** ✓ | 1.832 ✗ | **2.826** ✓ |
| 1 d | **2.743** ✓ | **3.414** ✓ | 1.757 ✗ | 2.577 ✗ |
| 2 d | 2.336 ✗ | **2.758** ✓ | 1.624 ✗ | 2.192 ✗ |
| 3 d | 2.026 ✗ | 2.300 ✗ | 1.509 ✗ | 1.908 ✗ |

**The verdict flips with the window and with SO₂, and no source fixes either — a borrowed criterion that is
INAPPLICABLE, not strict**, which is D-144's finding restated on a different paper. Two things it does say:

1. **With SO₂ the model already meets 2.7× with no burst wired** (2.74 at 1 d, 3.14 at 0.25 d), and wiring the burst
   pushes it *past* the threshold rather than toward it. Mechanically expected: every direct sink is bilinear in
   `[o2]`, and `SulfiteOxidation` is itself a fast self-exhausting sink, so a one-shot charge decaying under six sinks
   manufactures fast-initial-then-declining **for free**. On this arm D-133 added a pool, a state slot and three
   parameters to reproduce a shape the existing sinks already produced.
2. **Without SO₂ the base model misses at every window** (1.87 → 1.51) and the burst moves it toward Ferreira's band
   at every window, meeting 2.7× at ≤0.5 d. Here it is doing real work.

**The strongest point in the burst's favour is the one D-133 invoked to justify it, and it survives.** Ferreira reports
both rates SO₂-*independent*. The shipped model's fast-initial shape is strongly SO₂-*manufactured* — ratio spread
between the SO₂ arms 1.678/1.561/1.343 at 0.25/1/3 d — and the burst **narrows** it to 1.390/1.325/1.205 at every
window without closing it. Recorded because a record carrying only the failures would be the narrowing D-101/D-108
warn about.

**Caveat, stated rather than resolved:** the 2.7× is D-133's **paraphrase** of Ferreira. Using it against D-133's own
conclusion is an internal-consistency argument and legitimate without re-pulling — but it is a paraphrase, and the
Danilewicz rule binds: pull the source before this backs a `source:` field.

### 6. What shipped: a third oxidative set, and a seed that follows its consumer

**`oxidative="direct_burst"`** — the direct six plus the burst, a **superset of `direct`**, not a third mechanism. The
D-141 cascade treatment, for the same kind of reason: reachable, isolable and tested, never default. `MEDIA` and
`MEDIA_CASCADE_OXIDATIVE` gain a sibling `MEDIA_BURST_OXIDATIVE`, and `get_medium`'s two-way ternary becomes a
`_MEDIA_REGISTRIES` lookup with an import-time assertion that every set in `_OXIDATIVE_SETS` has a built registry —
otherwise a new alternative silently falls back to the old one, which is the failure mode the replacement design
exists to prevent.

**Why not default.** Making it default re-derives all 31 D-140 pins *and* re-opens the direct arm of the Danilewicz
benchmark — where the traverse falsifier and the unconditional 1.7707 ratio live — on the strength of a joint
calibration whose second half fails. "Re-derived as a consequence of a decision" and "re-fitted to whatever the code
now produces" are hard to tell apart in a record, and constraint 2's failure makes the first hard to argue. **Under
this placement the Danilewicz question is moot, and that is stated so the next reader does not re-derive it.**

**Why no `cascade_burst`.** D-138 ruled the burst's cascade node *"UNDETERMINED — do not force a node"*: it was fitted
to a day-1 O₂ **flux**, and re-homed as an H₂O₂/quinone consumer the O₂ spike vanishes, since only the activation node
consumes O₂ in that frame. That ruling stands. Its suggested resolution — *"a transient modifier on the activation
node"* — is what §4 flags: it presumes a transient, and under the default closure there isn't one.

**The seed follows the consumer.** `_resolve_burst_antioxidant_seed` applies D-133's sourced fallback under
`direct_burst` and seeds **0.0** otherwise, because the D-45 argument is sound exactly where a consumer exists.
Dosing `burst_antioxidant_gpl` into a build that cannot draw it **raises** rather than seeding an inert number — the
`hops`-without-a-bitterness-model precedent one block up in `compile_scenario`. The builder cannot see the condition
(it does not know the oxidative selection), so the resolution lives at the compile seam that does, with both halves
cross-referenced.

### 7. Guards, named for what they forbid

Beyond membership, isolability (an explicitly-zeroed pool reproduces the direct trajectory **bitwise**, not
approximately) and the measured pins on both sets, two guards exist to stop this beat being undone by prose:

- **`test_the_burst_is_not_a_transient_under_a_cork`** — forbids re-describing the burst as self-exhausting under the
  default closure. It asserts the pool is **70–85% remaining at 2 y** and that `o2` is still *rising* toward its
  suppressed steady state at 30 d. Asserting "the pool depletes" would have passed at 22%-in-two-years and read as
  confirmation of the claim the measurement refutes — `[[feedback-name-guards-for-what-they-forbid]]`.
- **`test_the_pool_cannot_self_exhaust_within_one_saturation_cycle_at_a_real_o2_charge`** — pins the 41.8% / 39.2%
  plateau at a **reachable** 8 mg/L charge, so the 500 mg/L operating point can never again be mistaken for evidence.
  Its failure message says that self-exhaustion appearing here would be a finding for the record, not a test to update.

### 8. The prohibition, and the named unlock

**Do NOT re-solve the split to rescue constraint 2.** It is tempting and it is well-posed-looking: constraint 1 pins
the product, so a smaller `burst_antioxidant_initial` with a proportionally larger `k_burst_oxidation` keeps the day-1
rate identical while becoming genuinely self-exhausting. **It is a second unmeasured number propping up the first** —
the trap D-146 refused for `f_de_novo_methionol`, arriving on a different axis one decision later. It would also not
fix what it appears to fix: the share is set by `k·[burst]`, so a corked bottle still starts at −37% and decays over
years rather than days.

**THE NAMED UNLOCK**, in the D-118/D-119 form (a specific fetch, not "more literature"): **Ferreira 2015's per-cycle
O₂ consumption curves** — the raw traces across saturations 1→5, not the reported average rates — which give the
pool's actual decay and pin `burst_antioxidant_initial` independently of `k_burst_oxidation`. One dataset lifts the
block; without it, any value for the split is a guess wearing a joint solve's costume.

### Next

- **The burst is now REACHABLE, not unbuilt and not refused** — `oxidative="direct_burst"`. Do not re-propose wiring
  it into the default without the §8 unlock, and do not re-open it as dead code: the comparison `media.py` used to
  draw against it ("wired into no medium at all") is retired, because nothing in the package answers to that now.
- **The `_OXIDATIVE_SETS` axis is now three-valued and asymmetric by design** — `direct`/`cascade` are mutually
  exclusive mechanisms, `direct_burst` extends `direct`. A fourth entry needs a registry in `_MEDIA_REGISTRIES` or the
  import-time assertion fires.
- The deferred tail, unchanged by this beat: growth-linked excretion (D-49 option B); Pham's pH + ethanol terms; the
  methionine sink (**BLOCKED**, D-146); a peptide pool; variety-specific DMSp; a sourced yeast-autolysate spectrum;
  re-anchoring `f_methional`; masking (blocked on `cos-alpha`); the D-55 Brett-phenol prose.
- Unchanged and still load-bearing: the quinone branching (D-145), closure O₂ ingress, acetaldehyde in maturation.
  D-139's own leftovers — the Brett/quench over-draw (§2.4) and the copper re-fit against D-134 (§2.5) — are still
  open, and are now the largest un-blocked items on the oxidative axis.

### Amendment — the isolability guard was vacuous, and constraint 1 is stronger than §2 stated

Found in review, immediately after the record above shipped. Appended rather than edited in place.

**1. `test_an_empty_burst_pool_reproduces_the_direct_trajectory_exactly` asserted nothing.** §7
claims isolability is checked *"bitwise, not approximately"*. It was written as
`np.array_equal(direct.y[-1], empty.y[-1])` — and `trajectory.y` is `(n_states, n_times)`, so
`y[-1]` is not the final state vector but **the last slot's time series**. The last wine slot is
`quinone`, which is identically `0.0` under both sets (already pinned by
`test_quinone_is_identically_zero_under_the_direct_set`). The assertion compared zeros to zeros and
would have passed on *any* divergence whatsoever.

**This is the defect class this record spends four sections indicting, committed inside the test
that certifies its central isolability claim** — a green assertion whose framing deletes its own
content, one file over from §3's 500 mg/L operating point. That it happened here, in the same beat,
is the strongest available evidence that the pattern is not a property of D-133's author but of the
move: an assertion is written to express a belief, and the shape that expresses it is not checked
against the shape that tests it.

**Fixed by comparing the whole `(n_states, n_times)` array**, plus a shape assertion so a silent
broadcast cannot restore the hole. **The claim survives: equality holds bitwise across all 94 slots
and 800 grid points.** That is the expected result and worth stating as mechanism rather than luck —
the `burst <= 0` guard returns `schema.zeros()`, adding exact zeros perturbs no RHS value, so BDF
selects identical steps. Had it *not* held bitwise, that would have been a finding about the solver
path, not a licence to fall back to `allclose`. §7's sentence is now true.

**2. §2's "0.929 / 0.949 at the instantaneous reading" is mislabelled, and the correction favours
D-133.** Those two figures are **0.25-day means**, the shortest window the sweep measured — already
declining, since the charge depletes from the first hour. The genuinely instantaneous rate at
D-133's stated point is `k_burst_oxidation · [o2] · [burst_antioxidant]` = `1.6 × 0.008 × 0.0033`
= 4.224e-5 g/L/h = **1.0138 mg/L/day**, against a ~1.0 target — and it reproduces the isolated unit
test's 1.014 exactly, as it must, being the same expression at the same state.

So **constraint 1 holds more tightly than the record states**: ~+1.4% instantaneous rather than
−5 to −7%, with the decline to 0.93/0.95 over the first six hours being real competition for a
depleting charge rather than calibration error. Nothing else in the record moves — the split is
still unpinned, because constraint 1 pins only the *product* however precisely it is read, and it is
constraint 2 that failed. §8's prohibition stands unchanged.

**3. `_MEDIA_REGISTRIES`' consistency check was an `assert`**, which `python -O` strips. Converted
to a `raise`: a check that disappears under a flag is not one. Its job is also narrower than first
written — `get_medium` would raise a bare `KeyError` for an unbuilt set anyway, so what this buys is
failing at *import* with both key lists named, not preventing a silent fallback to the default.
The comment now says that instead of the stronger claim.

Suite still **1418 passed**; ruff + mypy clean. No pin moved, in either direction.

## D-148 — D-139 §2.4 closed by measurement: the Brett/POF over-draw cannot fire, because SUMMING is not the mechanism — one drawer over-draws at a zero-order corner and two are indistinguishable from one inside the band, so no shared depletion gate is built

**Corrects:** D-138 — constraint 3's "`ProcessSet` sums, so both draw simultaneously and **can over-draw it** … needs a shared depletion gate" is wrong on both halves at every in-band parameter: summing is not the mechanism, and no gate is needed.
**Corrects:** D-139 — its §2.4 names the over-draw as **Brett/quench**, and D-141 then declined to build any quench draw. The live pair is Brett/POF, which is why D-141, D-143 and D-147 each re-listed §2.4 as open *after* L9 was discharged.

**Status: MEASURED + GUARDED, nothing built.** Two tests in `tests/test_brett.py` (§22), no new
Process, no new parameter, no RHS change. Suite **1420 passed** (was 1418); ruff + mypy clean.
Receipts: `M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d148-overdraw\` (`probe.py`, `probe2.py`, `falsify.py`).

### What §2.4 actually still asked, after D-141

D-138 constraint 3 bound two draws together: `brett.py`'s decarboxylase and "the Gislason radical
quench". D-141's **D2 = off-ledger** discharged the second — the cascade reads `hydroxycinnamics`
as one of `_PHENOLIC_REDUCTANT_POOLS` inside `activation_rate` and **never writes it**. So the
quench half of §2.4 has no referent in the code and cannot be tested. What survived is the pair
D-138's own sentence also named: **`BrettDecarboxylation` vs `YeastPOFDecarboxylation`**, both
drawing **`hydroxycinnamics` *and* `ferulic_acid`**, both routed through the same
`_decarboxylation_branch`. Three later records carried "§2.4" forward without saying which of the
two pairs remained, which is the whole reason it read as untouched work rather than a narrowed
question.

**The competition is reachable, not hypothetical.** `_BRETT_PROCESSES` and `_POF_PROCESSES` are
separate tuples on orthogonal gates (`brett_pitch_gpl` vs `pof_positive`, pinned by
`test_pof_gate_is_independent_of_the_brett_pitch`), so a POF+ must with a Brett co-inoculation runs
both. `test_pof_carbon_closes` already ran that configuration — and called `assert_nonnegative` on
the **POF-only** arm while leaving the combined arm, the one D-138 was about, unasserted.

### The measurement, and the claim it refutes

Corner chosen to maximise the summed draw: every decarboxylase rate at its band **high**, every
precursor half-saturation at its band **low**, 10/6 mg/L precursors (bottom of the ~10–200 mg/L
must range, so the pools reach the Monod roll-off while both draws are still at full strength),
Brett **co-inoculated** at 50 g/L so peak fermentative flux and peak `X_brett` coincide. Worst
(most negative) value over the whole 40 d trajectory, g/L:

| arm | drawers | `hydroxycinnamics` min | `ferulic_acid` min |
|---|---|---|---|
| nominal parameters | 2 | **+7.90e-04** (never nears 0) | +7.52e-04 |
| band corner | **2** | **−5.24e-11** | **−5.65e-11** |
| band corner, Brett only | 1 | −4.83e-11 | −5.29e-11 |
| band corner, POF only | 1 | −3.47e-11 | −6.48e-11 |
| K → 1e-12, rates ×100 | 2 | −2.37e-04 (frozen) | −1.04e-04 |
| K → 1e-12, rates ×100, Brett only | **1** | **−4.25e-06 (frozen)** | −1.86e-07 |
| K → 1e-12, rates ×100, POF only | **1** | **−4.05e-05 (frozen)** | −3.82e-05 |

**Two readings, and the second is the finding.** In-band, the worst excursion anywhere is
**−3.13e-10 g/L** (on `ferulic_acid`, at a 0.3 g/L Brett dose) — three orders of magnitude inside
`assert_nonnegative`'s own 1e-9 solver-noise floor, and it recovers. Out of band, where it does
bite, **a single drawer over-draws on its own**: POF alone reaches −4.05e-5 with no Brett present
at all. So the pool is not over-drawn *because two Processes sum*. D-138 attributed the hazard to
`ProcessSet`'s summing contract, and that attribution is wrong.

**The mechanism is zero-order-ness, and it is a property of one draw, not of two.** Every write to
these pools goes through `_decarboxylation_branch`, whose Monod is taken in **the pool it draws**:
`r = k · activity · [P]/(K + [P])`. As `[P] → 0` that is first-order in `[P]`, so
`d[P]/dt = −[P]·g(t, [P])` with `g` bounded, and the exact solution decays toward zero without
crossing it. A **sum** of such draws is still of that form — bounded `g` plus bounded `g` — which
is why adding POF to Brett changes the in-band excursion by 4e-12 g/L. It breaks only when `K → 0`
drives the Monod to 1 and the draw becomes constant in `[P]`, at which point the pool reaches zero
in finite time and the crossing is real. `K_hydroxycinnamic`'s band **low** is 1.0e-4 mol/L; the
excursion does not leave the noise floor until ~1e-6, and the guard's corner sits **10^8x** above
where the premise fails.

**The rate structure gives the ODE claim; the corner run gives the solver claim.** Neither alone
is the argument — BDF at `rtol=1e-6` is what actually integrates this, and only a run can speak
for it.

### Why the codebase's own shared-gate precedent argues AGAINST building one

D-138 asked for "a shared depletion gate" by analogy to `amino_acid_pools.depletion_gate`, whose
docstring is explicit: *"the guard that stops any draw from driving a pool negative."* Read at its
eight call sites (`aging.py` x3, `amino_acids.py`, `brett.py`, `byproducts.py`, `keto_acids.py`,
`malolactic.py` x2, `mercaptans.py`, `oxidative_cascade.py`), it is **not** cross-Process
coordination and imposes no ordering: each consumer calls it independently, and what it buys is
per-draw first-orderness in the drawn pool. The amino-acid pools needed it because their consumers
— Strecker, mercaptans, keto acids, byproducts, the two bacterial growths — had **no precursor
Monod of their own**. `_decarboxylation_branch` already has one, for both pools, in both
Processes. The precedent, applied honestly, is already satisfied.

So **no gate is built.** A shared gate here would be a second unmeasured coupling propping up a
non-problem — the move D-147 §8 prohibits on the burst axis, arriving one decision later on this
one.

### The real defect this uncovered, which is unreachable rather than absent

`_decarboxylation_branch` returns `(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)` at `precursor_gpl <= 0.0`, so a pool that
undershoots has **no draw left to push it back**: it is frozen negative for the rest of the run.
Measured directly — every zero-order arm above ends at its minimum, not above it (the `frozen`
column of `probe2.py`). And `conservation.py` weights **both** pools unclamped
(`carbon_mass_fraction("p_coumaric_acid")` at line 303, `("ferulic_acid")` at 313), so a frozen
negative would enter the carbon ledger as negative carbon rather than being absorbed.

Recorded, **not fixed**: reaching it needs a draw that is zero-order in the pool it draws, and the
`touches` contract plus `ProcessSet(strict=True)` mean no such draw can appear without failing the
second guard below. Fixing it speculatively would mean choosing a recovery rule for a state the
model cannot enter.

### The numbers out of band are step-control artefacts and must not be read as calibrated

Three signatures, all in `probe.py`/`probe2.py`:

- **Solver-dependent.** At `K → 0`, rates x100: BDF **−6.57e-05**, LSODA −8.40e-10, Radau
  −2.21e-09. Same ODE, same parameters, five orders of magnitude apart.
- **Non-monotone in K.** Sweeping `K_hydroxycinnamic` at rates x100: 5e-4 → −3.30e-10, 1e-4 →
  −4.45e-08, 1e-5 → −4.95e-07, 1e-6 → −2.65e-06, **1e-8 → −2.19e-10**, 1e-12 → −1.06e-03. A
  physical over-draw would not recover by 4 orders at 1e-8 and then lose it again at 1e-12.
- **Anti-correlated with the draw rate in-band.** A 0.3 g/L Brett dose gives a *worse* excursion
  (−1.86e-10) than 50 g/L (−5.24e-11). Whatever sets the in-band number, it is not how hard the
  pool is being drawn.

The table is therefore evidence about **which regime crosses zero**, not a measurement of by how
much.

### The two guards, named for what they forbid

- **`test_the_summed_decarboxylase_draw_cannot_drive_either_precursor_negative`** — the band
  corner, asserting the **minimum over the whole trajectory** on *both* pools at the 1e-9 floor.
  Not an endpoint check: both pools legitimately end at ~0 (fully converted), so an endpoint
  assertion could not tell "converted" from "over-drawn and frozen", which is the only failure
  available. It reads `series()` by name rather than `y[-1]` — the **D-147 amendment's** defect,
  in the same codebase, where `y[-1]` is the last slot's time series and not the final state. It
  also asserts **both** Processes are active, so the guard cannot silently degrade into the weaker
  one-drawer test, and asserts the corner actually bites (`series[-1] < 1% of series[0]`). Its
  failure message says a negative here is a finding for the record, not a test to relax.
- **`test_only_the_two_decarboxylases_may_draw_the_shared_precursors`** — the drawer inventory is
  **closed**: exactly `{brett_decarboxylation, yeast_pof_decarboxylation}` declare either pool in
  `touches`, checked under all three `oxidative` settings (`direct`/`cascade`/`direct_burst`) so
  the cascade's read-not-write status is pinned rather than assumed. It does **not** certify that
  a future drawer would be Monod-gated; it makes adding one loud. Said that way in the docstring,
  because the stronger claim is the one it cannot support.

**Both proven red-able** (`falsify.py`), which is the part a green pair cannot demonstrate about
itself: guard 1 fires at −2.368e-04 under a zero-order corner, fires again when the competition is
degraded to one drawer, and guard 2 fires when a third writer appears.

### Scope, stated rather than conceded

The corner is the worst case for **draw magnitude** — the rate is monotone increasing in each `k`
and decreasing in each `K`, so the band interior cannot draw harder. It is **not** provably the
worst case for **solver undershoot**: the K sweep above shows undershoot is not monotone in the
same parameters, and the 0.3 g/L Brett arm is 6× worse than the 50 g/L one. The guard therefore
runs **both** in-band Brett doses measured above rather than only the one that maximises the draw
— picking by draw magnitude would have guarded the *better*-behaved of the two, on a rationale
this record's own data undercuts. The rest of the band interior is covered by the structural
argument, not by the run.

## D-149 — D-139 §2.5 closed by measurement: the copper re-fit performed at last, and the "printed table arguing it should go UP" turns out to re-derive the value D-134 already rejected — 2092 L/g, over the same budget

**Corrects:** D-143 — its forward-pointer, repeated verbatim by D-148, reads Nguyen & Waterhouse 2021 as "a printed table arguing `k_copper_multiplier` should go **up**". Converted into the parameter it lands at 2092 L/g and fails the identical acceptance test that forced 2000 → 600. It is corroboration, not pressure.
**Corrects:** D-142 — "The activation node has **no pH term at all**" is wrong as written: `k_activation_bisulfite · hso3` carries an indirect pH route through `free_bisulfite`. Measured, it is worth 1.036× against Nguyen's 3.87×, so D-142's *gap* is real and its *claim* was not.

**Status: MEASURED + GUARDED, nothing built.** No parameter moved, in either direction. Nine tests
in `tests/test_oxidative_cascade_guards.py` (§Guard 4), two provenance/docstring corrections, no
new Process, no new parameter, no RHS change. Suite **1429 passed** (was 1420); ruff + mypy clean.
Receipts: `M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d149-copper-refit\` (`probe.py` … `probe4.py`,
`falsify.py`, their `.json` outputs).

### What §2.5 actually asked, and whether its trigger had fired

D-138 constraint 4: "**Moving** copper off `PhenolicBrowning` invalidates D-134's calibration…
re-deriving it against the dataset that produced it is a **re-fit, not a validation**." Read
literally that is contingent, and the contingency looked unfired — `aging.py:1548` still multiplies
`k_browning_eff` by `f_copper` exactly as D-134 fitted it, so the default wiring is untouched.

It *had* fired, one layer down. D-141 re-used the same constant at `oxidative_cascade.py:239`,
where it multiplies the **whole** activation node, and that file's own docstring concedes the debt
in its own words: "**This changes what the constant multiplies** … so it is a re-fit rather than a
validation." So the debt is real and **cascade-scoped** — which is why it could sit for four
decisions without a single test going red. Three records (D-142, D-147, D-148) re-listed §2.5 as
open without saying which structure owed what.

### The frame error: the check that set 600 was never run in the frame that binds

`aging.yaml`'s uncertainty note derives the value from Ferreira 2015's ceiling — the **total**
between-wine O₂-consumption spread from every compositional factor combined is "never > factor
2.2", so copper alone must not over-spend it — and then evaluates it as `f_Cu` **in isolation**:
"central 600 => f(0.168)=0.95 / f(0.679)=1.25, ~1.32×". That is a ratio of the *multiplier*.
Ferreira's 2.2× is a spread in *measured total rate*. Validate-in-the-frame-that-binds says those
are not the same statistic, and whether they differ depends entirely on what share of total uptake
copper multiplies.

Measured at the instant of an 8 mg/L dose on a typical red (`probe2.py`), per Process, g/L/h
converted to mg/L/day — and the copper-responsive set **detected** by zeroing the multiplier
rather than asserted:

| set | SO₂ | the O₂ drawers, largest first | Cu-multiplied share |
|---|---|---|---|
| direct | 0 | **phenolic_browning 0.513** · anthocyanin_fading 0.288 · oxidative_acetaldehyde 0.038 · strecker 0.0002 | **61.1%** |
| direct | 60 | sulfite_oxidation 1.479 · **phenolic_browning 0.513** · anthocyanin_fading 0.288 · oxidative_acetaldehyde 0.038 | **22.1%** |
| cascade | 0 | **oxygen_activation 0.549** | **100.0%** |
| cascade | 60 | **oxygen_activation 1.947** | **100.0%** |
| direct_burst | 0 | antioxidant_burst 1.012 · **phenolic_browning 0.513** · anthocyanin_fading 0.288 · … | **27.7%** |
| direct_burst | 60 | sulfite_oxidation 1.479 · antioxidant_burst 1.012 · **phenolic_browning 0.513** · … | **15.4%** |

**And the isolated check turns out to be the cascade's exact number.** With `R = C·f(Cu) + U`, the
total-uptake ratio is `1 + s·(f_hi/f_lo − 1)` for copper-multiplied share `s` — so at `s = 1` the
two frames coincide. Measured against `f_Cu`'s isolated 1.3245×:

| set | SO₂ 0 | SO₂ 60 |
|---|---|---|
| cascade | **1.3244×** | 1.3242× |
| direct | 1.1983× | 1.0717× |
| direct_burst | 1.0898× | 1.0499× |

The identity reproduces every measured ratio to four decimals, which is what licenses reading `s`
off the run rather than off the wiring. So D-134's note was **not** evaluated in the wrong frame in
any way that matters: for the cascade it is exactly right, and for the two direct sets it is a
strict **upper bound**. Across the whole declared band — 200 / 600 / 1500 L/g — every point clears
Ferreira's ceiling under every wiring, worst case 1.8889× (cascade at the band high, which is the
1.89× the note already computed). **The re-fit is a no-op against the constraint that set the
value.** Nothing moves.

### The re-fit actually performed, against the table three records pointed at

D-142 found Nguyen & Waterhouse 2021 (AJEV 72:209-216) and D-143 recorded it as "a printed table
arguing `k_copper_multiplier` should go **up**"; D-148 repeated that as the live risk of this beat.
Nobody had converted the table into the parameter.

Table 3.1 was **re-verified against the primary** rather than trusted from this archive's own
secondary copy: the full text is held locally (Nguyen's UC Davis dissertation; the paper is that
chapter verbatim), its OCR column alignment is scrambled, and the transcription is confirmed by
every `(k1+k2)/2` entry reproducing from its own printed `k1`,`k2`. D-142's O₂ column is exact.
Model wine, 4-methylcatechol 1.0 mM + benzenesulfinic acid 1.0 mM, Fe(III) 0.1 mM, 22.2 °C:

| pH | no Cu | Cu 0.01 mM (0.6355 mg/L) | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.0 | 7.5e-05 | 3.9e-04 | 5.20× |
| 3.5 | 1.4e-04 | 5.5e-04 | **3.93×** |
| 4.0 | 2.9e-04 | 7.5e-04 | 2.59× |

Solving `f(0.6355 mg/L)/f(0) = 3.9286` for the mean-centered multiplier gives **k = 2092.1 L/g**
(round-trip verified: it reproduces 3.9286×). Then run through D-134's *own* acceptance test:

| k | cascade | direct | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 600 (shipped) | 1.324× | 1.198× | ok |
| 1500 (band high) | 1.889× | 1.524× | ok |
| **2092 (Nguyen)** | **2.324×** | 1.759× | **OVER the 2.2× ceiling** |

**2092 is within 5% of the 2000 L/g raw digitization D-134 already rejected, and it fails the same
test in the same way.** The printed table does not argue the value should go up; it independently
re-derives the number that was already refused, from a different experiment. What a printed table
buys over a chart is the removal of digitization uncertainty — and digitization was never the
binding objection. The binding objections were free CuSO₄ in model wine against "most copper is
under complex forms in wine", and a single-exposure kinetic regime nearer Ferreira's steep
*initial*-rate copper sensitivity than the *steady* rate this term is scoped to. Both survive
intact, and two copper levels still cannot distinguish a linear multiplier from the saturating one
the paper's own mechanism predicts. **600 stays. The band stays.**

**The failure is cascade-only, and that is constraint 4 landing rather than a caveat.** At 2092 the
direct sets sit at 1.76× and 1.33× — inside the ceiling, because copper multiplies only 61% and 28%
of their uptake. The identical constant is over budget in one structure and not in another. That is
precisely why "re-deriving it against the dataset that produced it is a re-fit, not a validation",
and it is now a measured statement rather than an argued one.

### Two things measured on the way, both of which change a claim on the record

**1. The 10-day window average is saturation-compressed, and reading a share off it would have
been wrong.** The first probe used Ferreira's own cycle length. Its arms consume 55–96% of the
8 mg/L charge inside the window, so the mean rate is pinned near the `dose/window` ceiling of
0.8 mg/L/day and the Cu-hi/Cu-lo ratio is squeezed toward 1 by **substrate exhaustion**: the
sulfited direct arm reads 1.021× on the window against 1.072× instantaneous. Attributing that to
structure would have understated copper's share by ~3.4×. The shipped numbers are therefore the
instantaneous draw at the dose, cross-checked against a 0.25-day window (≤2.6% of the charge
consumed) that reproduces them to <0.4%.

**2. D-142's "the activation node has no pH term at all" is wrong, and the correction does not
rescue the gap.** `activation_rate` includes `k_activation_bisulfite · hso3`, and `free_bisulfite`
is pH-dependent, so an indirect route exists whenever SO₂ is present. Measured at fixed copper,
pH 3.0 → 4.0:

| set | SO₂ 0 | SO₂ 60 |
|---|---|---|
| cascade | 1.0000× | 1.0363× |
| direct | 1.0000× | 1.0319× |

So: **exactly** no pH dependence unsulfited (both sets), and 3.6% sulfited, against the 3.87× (287%)
Nguyen measures at zero copper. The route exists and is ~80× too weak to be the dependence he
measured, and it vanishes entirely in the arm his measurement was taken in. D-142's conclusion —
a real, unclosed gap — is unaffected; only its reason was overstated.

### A disconnect found while checking who reads `copper`, recorded and NOT fixed

`_verb_add_copper` (D-44/D-45) writes `h2s` and `methanethiol` and **never** the `copper` state
slot D-134 added. The model has two coppers that never meet: fining a wine cannot change its
oxidation rate, though residual copper from fining is the commonest way real wine's copper level
rises. The verb's docstring already said "residual copper … is untracked"; what was not said is
that this now has a *rate* consequence, not merely a bookkeeping one. Fixing it means choosing a
residual-copper fraction and nothing sources one, so it is recorded and left — the D-148 precedent
for a defect whose fix would be a guess.

### The two guards, named for what they forbid

- **`test_copper_may_not_over_spend_ferreiras_between_wine_spread`** — total O₂ uptake across
  Ferreira's own 15-wine copper range (0.168–0.679 mg/L) may not spread further than his 2.2×
  ceiling for every factor combined. Run under **all three** oxidative sets and at **both** the
  shipped value and the band's declared high edge, with the high edge **read from the
  `ParameterSet`** so widening the band moves the guard instead of leaving it pinned to a number the
  band no longer contains. Unsulfited, deliberately: that is the worst case for the direct sets,
  whose copper-free `sulfite_oxidation` otherwise dilutes copper's share 61% → 22%, so guarding the
  sulfited arm would guard the better-behaved one.
- **`test_only_the_declared_o2_draw_responds_to_the_copper_multiplier`** — the responder inventory
  is closed, per set: `{phenolic_browning}` under direct/direct_burst, `{oxygen_activation}` under
  cascade. Measured by zeroing the multiplier and collecting the draws that move, so a Process that
  reached copper by an undeclared route still appears. It does **not** certify that any set's share
  is correct — the sibling guard bounds that — and says so, because the stronger claim is the one it
  cannot support.

**Both proven red-able** (`falsify.py`), on the real hazard rather than a synthetic one: guard 1
fires at 2.324× when `k` is set to Nguyen's implied 2092 — the exact move the standing prohibition
forbids — and, on the same arm, stays **green** in both direct sets, so it is sensitive to the
structure and not merely to the number. Guard 2 fires in all three sets when a second copper-scaled
O₂ draw is planted (planted as an *added* term, since the cascade has exactly one O₂ drawer and it
is the declared one — a plant needing a second existing drawer could not run in the set that most
needs covering).

### Scope, stated rather than conceded

The shares are measured **at the instant of a fresh 8 mg/L charge on a young red**, which is
Ferreira's operating point and therefore the frame his 2.2× ceiling lives in. They are not the
5-year cumulative split: D-137 measured SO₂ taking ~90% of a whole 5-year budget under a cork,
where the mix — and so copper's leverage — is different. A ceiling derived from saturation-cycle
data is guarded where that data was taken, and the guard says so by running the same protocol.

The measurement also does not establish that 600 is *right*. It establishes that the one
constraint which produced it still holds across the whole band under all three wirings, and that
the newest independent source does not relieve it. The value remains an order-of-magnitude,
budget-constrained calibration device, exactly as its provenance says.

### Amendment — Ferreira's ceiling never bound in the wiring D-134 shipped into, and the probe wine had no acids

Found in review immediately after the record above shipped, and appended rather than edited in
place (the D-147 precedent). Receipts: `probe5.py`, `probe2.py` re-run.

**1. The Scope section's "the one constraint which produced it still holds across the whole band
under all three wirings" is true, and says much less than it sounds.** It holds because it is
*slack*, not because it is satisfied at the margin. Run at the value D-134 actually rejected:

| k | direct SO₂ 0 | direct SO₂ 60 | cascade SO₂ 0 | cascade SO₂ 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 600 (shipped) | 1.198× | 1.070× | 1.324× | 1.324× |
| **2000 (rejected)** | **1.721× ok** | **1.247× ok** | **2.252× OVER** | **2.251× OVER** |

The cascade crosses 2.2× at **k = 1927 L/g**. The direct set does not cross it anywhere in the
range this beat measured — not at 2000, not at Nguyen's 2092 (1.759×).

**So Ferreira's ceiling did not adjudicate the rejection of 2000.** D-134's stated arithmetic —
"the raw slope alone gave copper-alone a 2.24× rate ratio … assigning the entire multi-factor
budget to copper alone over-spends it" — is `f_Cu` in **isolation**, which this record has just
shown is the *cascade's* statistic. The cascade did not exist for another seven decisions. In the
only structure that existed at D-134, copper multiplied 61% of unsulfited uptake and 2000 L/g
lands comfortably inside the budget it was said to over-spend.

**This does not move 600, and the record's own reasoning is why.** The two objections §"the re-fit
actually performed" names as binding against Nguyen — free CuSO₄ in model wine against "most copper
is under complex forms in wine", and single-exposure kinetics nearer Ferreira's steep *initial*-rate
sensitivity than the *steady* rate this term is scoped to — are properties of the **source**, not of
the wiring, and they applied to Danilewicz's Figure 4 exactly as they apply to Nguyen's Table 3.1.
They survive this amendment untouched. What changes is which argument is load-bearing: the budget
check is a **backstop that the cascade makes real**, not the thing that picked the number.

Stated because the failure mode is silent. A future source arguing 1200 L/g would clear the ceiling
in every wiring and the guard would stay green — correctly, since a guard that fires on everything
forbids nothing. Whoever weighs that source must know the ceiling is not the adjudicator and that
the model-wine objections are, or they will read a green suite as an endorsement.

**2. The probe and guard wine declared no titratable acidity, and solved to pH 2.924.**
`tartaric_gpl` and `malic_gpl` both default to 0.0 and neither was set — the same omission that made
the pH sweep in `probe3.py` throw "below the acid load's intrinsic pH" and get patched there alone.
pH 2.924 is outside any real red's 3.4–3.8, and `free_bisulfite` — hence the whole **sulfited**
column of the share table — is a function of pH. Fixed in both (tartaric 6.0 g/L, malic 3.0 g/L,
`initial_ph` 3.5) and re-taken:

- **The unsulfited arms are byte-identical**: 0.83964 / 0.54948 / 1.85177 mg/L/day and spreads

  §"pH" argued structurally — with no SO₂ there is no pH-dependent term anywhere in the O₂ draw —
  and it is why the guards' assertions do not move.
- **The sulfited column does move, in the direction that strengthens the guard's design choice.**
  `sulfite_oxidation` rises 1.479 → 1.544 mg/L/day (more HSO₃⁻ at the higher pH), so copper's share

**The record above therefore carries the PRE-FIX sulfited column** (the archive is append-only, so
it is superseded here rather than edited). The corrected sulfited rows in full:

| set | SO₂ 60, the O₂ drawers | Cu share | total spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| direct | sulfite_oxidation 1.544 (64.8%) · **phenolic_browning 0.513 (21.5%)** · anthocyanin_fading 0.288 (12.1%) · oxidative_acetaldehyde 0.038 (1.6%) | **21.5%** | 1.0698× |
| direct_burst | sulfite_oxidation 1.543 (45.5%) · antioxidant_burst 1.012 (29.8%) · **phenolic_browning 0.513 (15.1%)** · anthocyanin_fading 0.288 (8.5%) | **15.1%** | 1.0490× |

Over a real span (Carrascón 2018's own 8 reds, pH 3.26–3.61) the model delivers **1.0060×** sulfited and exactly **1.0000×** unsulfited, against real wine's 1.16×. The gap is real and the frame was too wide.

change, no YAML change. Suite **1436 passed** (was 1429); ruff + mypy clean.

`sim.py`, `falsify.py`, their `.json` outputs).

### The beat as it was handed over, and what the first conversion found

D-149's Next: *"The activation node's **missing pH term** is now measured rather than asserted:
1.036× available against 3.87× wanted, and 1.0000× in the unsulfited arm where Nguyen took the
reading. That is a bigger, cleaner gap than D-142's wording implied, and it is the natural next
oxidative beat."* D-142 had recorded the same gap; neither converted Nguyen's pH column into a
rate law, which is what this beat does first.

Nguyen & Waterhouse 2021 (AJEV 72:209-216) Table 3.1 — the same table D-149 converted the copper
column of, whose transcription was verified there against the primary:

| pH | k, no Cu (1/min) | k, Cu 0.01 mM | copper ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.0 | 7.5e-05 | 3.9e-04 | 5.200× |
| 3.5 | 1.4e-04 | 5.5e-04 | **3.929×** |
| 4.0 | 2.9e-04 | 7.5e-04 | 2.586× |
| **pH ratio 3.0→4.0** | **3.867×** | **1.923×** | |

Log-linear, the zero-copper column gives **0.5873 decades/pH** (3.867×/unit, max residual 3.5%)
and the copper column **0.2840** (1.923×/unit, 1.1%).

### Leg 1 — the only mechanism the corpus supplies over-predicts by 2.6×

*Concepts in Wine Chemistry* (held locally): *"The pH controls the phenol-phenolate equilibrium
which sets the phenolate concentration available to undergo an oxidation reaction. The equilibrium
pKa's between phenols and phenolates are in the order of 9–10 … at the higher pH range (4.0) the
concentration is still about 10 times higher than at the lower pH range (3.0)."* At pH ≪ pKa the
phenolate fraction is ~10^(pH − pKa), so the mechanism predicts **10× per pH unit** on the term it
multiplies. Nguyen's model wine has 4-methylcatechol as its **only** reductant, so the
phenol-driven share is ~1 and the prediction is ~10× **total**. Measured: 3.867×.

Fitted as `k = a + b·10^(pH−3)` on the pH 3.0 and 3.5 points, with pH 4.0 held out as a genuine
out-of-sample prediction:

| column | floor `a` | phenolate `b` | pH-4.0 prediction error | pH-flat share at pH 3.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no Cu | 4.494e-05 | 3.006e-05 | **+19.2%** | **59.9%** |
| Cu 0.01 mM | 3.160e-04 | 7.400e-05 | **+40.8%** | 81.0% |

For 10×/unit to land on 3.867×, **68.1% of the rate in a catechol-only model wine would have to
come from something pH-flat.** Nguyen's system has nothing else to supply it. So a built term
would be a **fitted exponent with no mechanism** — and not one exponent but two, 0.587 at zero
copper and 0.284 at 0.01 mM.

### Leg 2 — the table is not separable, and adding `f_pH` re-opens the copper value D-149 closed

This is the structural leg. The architecture's rate modifiers are **multiplicative and
independent** (D-10), so `f_pH · f_Cu` asserts that the copper ratio is the same at every pH.
Nguyen's table:

| | copper ratio |
|---|---|
| pH 3.0 | 5.200× |
| pH 3.5 | 3.929× |
| pH 4.0 | 2.586× |
| **swing across one pH unit** | **2.011×**  (a separable `f(pH)·g(Cu)` requires 1.000×) |

Symmetrically the pH ratio is 3.867× at Cu 0 and 1.923× at Cu 0.01 mM — the same 2.011×, because
it is the same interaction read down the other axis.

D-149 converted the **pH 3.5 row** into `k_copper_multiplier` and got 2092 L/g, over Ferreira's
ceiling, and refused it. The other two rows convert to:

| row used | implied `k_copper_multiplier` |
|---|---|
| pH 3.0 | 2425 L/g |
| pH 3.5 | 2092 L/g  (the value D-149 refused) |
| pH 4.0 | 1511 L/g |

**Which row you stand on moves the copper parameter by 1.6×.** A pH term makes that choice
load-bearing where today it is not, so it does not merely sit beside `f_Cu` — it re-opens the
calibration D-149 closed. That is D-138 constraint 4 ("a constant fitted to one structure does not
survive being moved to another") landing for the **fourth** time, and the first time it has landed
on a structure that does not exist yet.

### Leg 3 — the headline: every steep slope is an INITIAL-rate slope, and this node carries the steady rate

Carrascón, Vallverdú-Queralt, Meudec, Sommerer, Fernandez-Zurbano & Ferreira (2018), *Food
Chemistry* 249:172-179, held locally as a primary — eight commercial Spanish reds on the **same**
repeated-air-saturation protocol Ferreira 2015 used, i.e. the protocol D-132/D-133 are anchored
on. Table 1 gives pH; Table 2 gives each wine's **initial** and **average** OCR. So one dataset
supplies both the span and the spread, which is the frame error D-149 exists to catch.

Transcription check first, on the one statistic the paper prints against this pairing (Table 3,
r(pH, initial OCR) = 0.689): recomputed **0.6876**, Δ 0.0014. It is shipped as a test.

| statistic | OLS slope | per pH unit |
|---|---|---|
| **initial** OCR | +0.6613 decades/pH | **4.585×** |
| **average (steady)** OCR | +0.2093 decades/pH | **1.619×** |

And the three published pH slopes sort cleanly by which statistic they are:

| source | medium | statistic | per pH unit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carrascón 2018 | **real red wine** | initial OCR | 4.585× |
| Nguyen 2021 (Cu 0) | model wine | pseudo-1st-order k, single exposure | **3.867×** |
| Fernández-Pérez et al. 2022 (PMC9266014) | grape-extract reconstitution | `R_max` | ~2.6× |
| Carrascón 2018 | **real red wine** | **average (steady) OCR** | **1.619×** |

`k_activation_floor/phenolic/bisulfite` and `k_browning_eff` are calibrated to the **steady** rate
(D-132: Ferreira's constant cycles-2-to-5 rate). `burst_antioxidant` / `k_burst_oxidation` is the
**day-1 initial** rate (D-133). **Nguyen's 3.867× sits inside the initial-rate cluster and 2.4×
above the steady one.**

D-134's uncertainty note argued exactly this against the *copper* column — *"Danilewicz's
single-exposure kinetics may sit closer to Ferreira's steep INITIAL-rate copper sensitivity than
the STEADY rate this term is scoped to"* — and D-149 repeated it as one of the two objections that
survived. **It was an argument. It is now a measurement, on a different axis and from a different
dataset.** And it inverts the target: D-142 and D-149 both pointed the pH term at the activation
node, and the sources point it at the burst.

The 2022 Taguchi study is recorded as **direction and order only**, deliberately. Its L16 design
is genuinely orthogonal — pH 3.3/3.9 crossed against Fe, Cu, Mn, ethanol and acetaldehyde, with
pH, Fe and Mn significant and **Cu not** — which is the one thing no other source here has. But
its 6.5 → 11.6 hPa/h comes from **prose describing a figure**; a second fetch confirmed the paper
carries no level-means table. Its medium is a dealcoholized grape-extract reconstitution with
dosed metal chlorides, and `R_max` is a maximum rate on a single saturation. It corroborates the
pattern; it sources nothing.

### Leg 4 — the one affordable number is measured in the wrong frame to build from

The real-wine steady slope, 0.2093 decades/pH, **is** affordable: injected in the sim it costs at
most 1.167× under any wiring, inside every budget. It is still not buildable:

- **pH is perfectly collinear with variety** in that dataset — all four low-pH wines are Garnacha
  (3.26–3.32), all four high-pH are Tempranillo (3.51–3.61). r = 0.608 on the average rate, n = 8;
  the paper's own verdict on the *initial*-rate correlation it does report is "non-significant".
- **It is a between-wine correlational slope; a sim pH term is a within-wine causal knob.**
  Comparing a Garnacha to a Tempranillo is not the experiment of raising one wine's pH by 0.35.
  Validate-in-the-frame-that-binds points *against* building here, not for it.

So the slope is an **upper bound on pH's own contribution across those wines**, not an isolation
of it.

### The gap, re-measured in the frame that binds

D-149's numbers were taken over pH 3.0 → 4.0. No real red spans a pH unit. Re-run over Carrascón's
own 3.26 → 3.61:

| set | SO₂ 0 | SO₂ 30 mg/L |
|---|---|---|
| direct | 1.0000× | 1.0060× |
| cascade | 1.0000× | 1.0074× |
| direct_burst | 1.0000× | 1.0036× |

against real wine's **1.158×** over the same span (Carrascón steady-rate OLS) and Nguyen's
**1.511×**. The whole between-wine steady-rate spread those 8 wines showed, from every factor
combined, is 1.420×.

**Two findings on the way, both about the sweep rather than the chemistry.**

1. **`initial_ph` anchors t = 0, not the aging pH, and there is no way to set one.** It back-solves
   a strong-cation charge with Byp = 0 (D-18), and byproducts then pull pH down through the
   ferment: `initial_ph` 3.26 / 3.61 arrive at the O₂ dose as **3.2084 / 3.5135**, a span of
   0.3052 rather than 0.35. Ratios between two runs of one sweep are unaffected, which is why the
   guard is written as a ratio — but nothing in the archive states this, and any future pH work
   that tries to *set* an aging pH will not be able to.
2. **The injected share reads slightly over 100% in the cascade** (measured 102.0% / 105.3%
   sulfited, `sim.py`). D-149's identity `total = 1 + s·(f_hi/f_lo − 1)` assumes one multiplied
   route; here the injected multiplier stacks with the **existing** indirect pH route
   (`k_activation_bisulfite · hso3` through pH-dependent `free_bisulfite`), so total uptake moves
   slightly more than the multiplier alone accounts for. It is that second route, not an artefact.

### The guard, named for what it forbids

- **`test_ph_may_not_out_spend_the_between_wine_steady_rate_spread`** — pH alone may not move
  total O₂ uptake, across Carrascón's own 8-red pH span, further than every compositional factor
  combined moved the **steady** rate across those same wines. Six arms: all three oxidative sets ×
  unsulfited and 30 mg/L SO₂. Both arms are kept: unsulfited is the worst case for the direct sets
  (a multiplier at the `f_Cu` slot reaches 62.4% of unsulfited uptake against 37.1% sulfited), and
  the sulfited arm is the only one where the model has **any** pH response at all today.
- **`test_the_carrascon_transcription_reproduces_its_papers_printed_correlation`** — the eight
  wines are the only thing setting the span *and* the bound, so the transcription is checked
  against the paper's own printed r = 0.689 rather than trusted. Both the span and the spread are
  **derived** from that table, never hardcoded, so correcting a wine moves the guard with it —
  the same design as D-149 reading the copper band's high edge off the `ParameterSet`.

**The bound is an OBSERVED spread, not a claimed ceiling, and the guard docstring says so.**
Ferreira's 2.2× is a stated maximum over 15 wines ("never > factor 2.2"); Carrascón's 1.420× is
merely what 8 wines happened to show. It is the right comparator because it comes from the same
wines as the span, and it is the weaker claim. D-149's amendment 1 is the reason this is spelled
out: a green guard is not an endorsement.

**All four falsification arms verified** (`falsify.py`), on the real hazard:

| arm | cascade | direct | direct_burst |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (shipped) | 1.0000× / 1.0074× green | 1.0000× / 1.0060× green | 1.0000× / 1.0036× green |
| **planted at Nguyen's 0.5873** | **1.6048× / 1.6163× RED** | 1.3778× / 1.2236× green | 1.1745× / 1.1338× green |

The second row is the arm that matters: **the same constant is red in one structure and green in
two others**, so the guard is sensitive to what the multiplier reaches and not merely to its size
— which is what made D-149's Guard 1 credible and is the same failure shape copper had. (The plant
keys on nominal `initial_ph`, so it applies the exponent over 0.35 units where a term reading
`ph_of_state` would apply it over the solved 0.3052 — `sim.py` measures that version at 1.5104× /
1.5213×, red in the cascade and green in both direct sets exactly the same way.) Arm 3: the
transcription guard reads 0.6876 as transcribed and **0.5935 — red — on a single changed digit**.

### Scope, stated rather than conceded

This refuses a pH term **on the activation node / `k_browning_eff`**, which is where D-142 and
D-149 asked for one. It does **not** refuse one on `burst_antioxidant`, which is where the sources
put the steep slope — that is left open below rather than settled here, because D-133's pool is
wired opt-in (D-147) and its own provenance already records it as implicitly carrying untracked
between-wine variance, so whether a pH term there would double-count is a question this beat did
not measure.

Nor does it establish that the model's ~1.006× is right. It is not: real wine's steady rate rises
~1.62× per pH unit and the model delivers ~1.006× of it. The under-response is recorded as an open
gap and deliberately **not** guarded, because guarding it would require a within-wine pH rate law
and no source supplies one.

### The beat, and why it was the cheap one

D-150's amendment named it precisely: Carrasco-Quiroz 2022 is *"the **only** copper-orthogonal
design in this record's evidence set,"* its L16 independently found pH significant and **Cu not**,
and its **Table 2 is condition-by-condition raw data**. Recovered, it would give a pH slope with
copper orthogonalised — *"a cheaper unlock than the within-wine pH series,"* bearing on **leg 2**
rather than leg 3, and therefore not on its own licensing a term. All of that turned out true.

Carrasco-Quiroz, Martínez-Gil, Nevares, Martínez-Martínez, Sánchez-Gómez & del Alamo-Sanza (2022),
*Foods* 11(13):1961, doi 10.3390/foods11131961, PMC9266014. Table 1 (the L16(2^15) design) was
transcribed **independently from two hosts** — the PMC HTML and the EuropePMC full-text XML — and
they agree cell for cell. Table 2 gives 11 kinetic parameters × 16 conditions × 3 grape-extract
wines (GEw-A/B/C), as mean ± SD over five replicates.

### Leg 0 — the design is genuinely orthogonal, and the interaction is unaliased

This is the precondition for everything else, and it is now a test rather than the paper's word.
All six factors are balanced 8/8; all fifteen pairwise sign-column dot products are **0**; and —
the load-bearing one — the **pH×Cu interaction column is orthogonal to every one of the six
studied main effects**. So the interaction estimated below is not some other factor's main effect
wearing a disguise, which is exactly the objection that could be raised against Nguyen.

### The transcription, checked against the two things the paper prints

**(1) The prose figure D-150 refused to source from, re-derived from the table.** The paper says
`R_max` rises *"from 6.5 to 11.6 hPa/h"* with pH. Computed as pH level means over all 48 rows:
**6.475 → 11.546**.

The low level lands exactly. The high level is **0.47% short**, and that is recorded rather than
rounded away — the D-150 amendment is about precisely this. No defensible aggregation reaches
11.6: arithmetic gives 11.546, geometric 10.116, mean-of-per-GEw-means 11.546. The residual is
consistent with Table 2 being printed to one decimal place; it is not consistent with the prose
reporting a different statistic. **The prose was reporting the pH main effect**, and the table
reproduces it — which is what converts this source from "direction and order only" into a table.

**(2) A categorical verdict across all six factors.** The paper reports *"pH, Fe²⁺ and Mn²⁺ being
the significant conditions"* (ANOVA/LSD, p < 0.05). An ANOVA over the transcription reproduces it
**exactly** — pH 34.9, Fe 18.3, Mn 13.6 significant; Cu 0.23, EtOH 0.63, AcH 0.14 not — against
F(1,38) crit 4.098. Reproducing a six-way categorical verdict is much stronger evidence about a
table than any single number.

**Two honest limits on that second check, both measured.**

- **The error term is not the paper's.** Table 2 prints means of five replicates, so the replicate
  variance is unrecoverable; the residual used here is that of the 48 condition×GEw means and
  absorbs every unmodelled interaction. It is a *conservative* term for the effects it fits, but
  **no p-value below is the paper's own.** What survives is "my ANOVA on my transcription
  reproduces the paper's categorical verdict" — a transcription check, which is all it is used for.
- **Its resolution is coarse, and was measured rather than conceded.** The verdict's margins are
  wide, so the smallest single-cell error it catches is **43%**; a one-digit slip does not fire it,
  and neither does a GEw block permutation or a halved condition-11 row. A factor-aligned column
  distortion *is* caught. Those two columns feed nothing else — the load-bearing `R_max` column has
  its own check, and that one **is** single-digit sensitive (33.0 → 3.0 fires it).

### The finding — leg 2 corroborated in a design Nguyen's objection cannot touch

D-150 leg 2 is the structural leg: rate modifiers are multiplicative and independent (D-10), so
`f_pH · f_Cu` asserts the copper ratio is identical at every pH, and Nguyen's Table 3.1 swings
**2.011×** across one pH unit. The standing objection to that leg was that Nguyen doses copper into
the same wells the pH is set in, so the interaction could be a non-orthogonality artefact.

It is not. On `R_max`, over the 3.3→3.9 span:

| | pH 3.3 | pH 3.9 | pH ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cu 0.1 mg/L | 6.008 | 14.142 | **2.354×** |
| Cu 0.8 mg/L | 6.942 | 8.950 | **1.289×** |
| **swing** | | | **1.826×**  (separable requires 1.000×) |

F(1,38) = **5.95, p = 0.0195** on the error term above. Same **direction** as Nguyen — pH's effect
is weaker at high copper — and a comparable **magnitude**, 1.826× over 0.6 pH units against his
2.011× over a full unit. Two media, two designs, one conclusion.

**It is not an outlier artefact.** Condition 12 is the one `R_max` outlier (33.0 / 30.7 / 6.4) and
it sits in the pH-3.9/Cu-0.1 cell, i.e. in the cell that drives the swing. Dropping it makes the
interaction **stronger**, not weaker: F = **9.27**, p = **0.0044**. The outlier was inflating the
error term, not manufacturing the effect.

### Leg 3 gets a third dataset, weakly

Per pH unit, this design gives **2.622×** on `R_max` (2.237× geometric). Two things follow.

First, **this reproduces D-150's own "~2.6×" for this source** — the row its table attributed to
"Fernández-Pérez et al. 2022 (PMC9266014)" and its amendment reassigned to Carrasco-Quiroz. That
number was taken from prose describing Figure 2; it is now derived from Table 2 and it lands in
the same place. The figure prose was reporting the pH main effect, and it was reporting it
correctly.

Second, `R_max` is a **maximum** rate on a single saturation, so it belongs to the initial-rate
class in D-150 leg 3's sorting, and 2.622× sits below Nguyen's 3.867× and Carrascón's real-wine
initial 4.585× while still exceeding every steady-rate figure in the corpus. The ordering holds.
But it is corroboration only, not a second measurement of leg 3: the sharp initial-vs-steady pair
available here (2.622× vs the duration statistic's 2.113×) is far weaker than Carrascón's 4.585×
vs 1.619×, and — for the reason given below — the two members of this pair are not two readings of
one rate curve.

### What this does NOT do — stated here because it is the thing most likely to be misread

A derived quantity, `ΔO₉₀₋₁₀ / Δt_O₉₀₋₁₀`, has units of hPa/h and looks like an average rate; on it
the pH×Cu interaction is **not** significant (F = 0.47). **That does not retire leg 2 for the
activation node, and it is not a partial unblock.** It is a limit on how far this dataset reaches:

- **It is a duration statistic wearing rate units.** Across all 48 rows the numerator spans 1.49×
  (CV 0.074) while the denominator spans 4.79× (CV 0.398), and the quotient correlates with
  `1/Δt` at **r = 0.988**. It measures how long one saturation takes to decay, not a rate the
  archive's nodes carry — which is why Fe lights up on it (F = 18.3) and vanishes on `R_max`
  (F = 0.017). Changing which physical quantity is measured is not the same as moving along one
  rate curve.
- **It is the wrong frame regardless.** `k_activation_*` / `k_browning_eff` are calibrated to
  Ferreira's **repeated-saturation** cycles-2-to-5 rate in **real wine** (D-132). This is a single
  saturation in a **dealcoholized grape-extract reconstitution** with dosed metal chlorides.
  Validate-in-the-frame-that-binds points against reading a separability verdict off it.

**And leg 1 is untouched, and got worse.** D-150 refused a term partly because it would be *"a
fitted exponent with no mechanism — and not one exponent but two."* The corpus now carries
**four**: 0.587 (Nguyen, Cu 0), 0.284 (Nguyen, Cu 0.01 mM), and 2.62×/2.24× per unit here on a
third medium. Nothing in this beat supplies a mechanism, and D-150's opening prohibition stands
undisturbed.

### The copper null — flagged, deliberately not acted on

Copper's own main effect in this design is **F = 0.23** on the duration statistic and **F = 2.87**
on `R_max` — and on `R_max` it points the *wrong way*, 0.789× (more copper, lower max rate).
Dropping condition 12 takes it to F = 0.199. The levels are 0.1 and 0.8 mg/L, which **bracket
Ferreira's 0.168–0.679 range** that `k_copper_multiplier` is bounded against (D-149 Guard 4).

This is the first copper-orthogonal reading the archive has on copper's own size, and it points
opposite to D-134 and D-149, which both argued about whether to raise the constant. It is **not**
acted on here, for three reasons: it is a **null**, not a bound, and the paper reports it as
non-significant rather than bounded; the medium is a reconstitution with dosed CuCl₂, not wine;
and moving a shipped constant on the strength of one null in a non-wine medium would be D-149's
own mistake run in reverse. Hence `**Flags:**` — identified, code unchanged.

### The guards, named for what they forbid

- **`test_the_carrasco_quiroz_l16_design_is_orthogonal_and_ph_x_cu_is_unaliased`** — forbids

- **`test_..._reproduces_its_papers_printed_significance_verdict`** — the six-way categorical

Everything is **derived from the transcribed tables, never hardcoded**, so correcting a cell moves
the guards with it — the D-149/D-150 design.

**All arms verified red-able on the real hazard** (`falsify.py`), which is the point D-149's

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| baseline (all four, as shipped) | green |

The planted-separable arm is the one that matters: it removes *only* the interaction, leaving
