### Amendment (same day) — the ordering screen's RECALL was unmeasured, and measuring it moved the count up

§3's counts were produced by a resolution rule that **silently dropped claims**. For each
ordering word the harness walked `ALL_NAMES` sorted longest-first and `break`ed on the first
sibling found in the window — so **when a window named two parameters, the longer string won
regardless of which one the sentence was about**, and the other claim was never emitted, never
evaluated and never counted.

**It fired on a row §3 hand-killed as a false positive.** `oak.yaml`'s ellagitannin note reads
*"… E_a_ethanol_oxidation / E_a_strecker) and DELIBERATELY well above the weak diffusion
`E_a_oak_extraction` …"*. `E_a_ethanol_oxidation` (21 chars) beat `E_a_oak_extraction` (18), so
the harness emitted the wrong pair, the hand-reading correctly discarded it — and **D-168 §3's
own ordering 2 vanished without appearing in any denominator**. That is
`feedback-count-and-print-your-skips` committed by this record against this record's own
harness, one beat after D-168 did the same thing with its regex.

**Fixed and re-measured.** Every sibling in a window is now emitted (a shorter name that is a
substring of a longer hit is still folded, and that rule is stated rather than assumed), and the
count of multi-name windows — the previously unmeasured denominator — is printed:

| | §3 as published | amended |
|---|---|---|
| distinct candidate claims | 49 | **69** |
| evaluable at a joint band edge | 24 | **36** |
| windows naming MORE THAN ONE sibling | **not measured** | **21** |

**Recall control, now in the harness.** D-168 §3's three hand-transcribed orderings are the
known-true set; all three are recovered **with the correct sibling**
(`E_a_maillard_strecker > E_a_browning`, `E_a_ellagitannin_oxidation > E_a_oak_extraction`,
beer `E_a_esters > dH_ester_volatil`). A screen that cannot re-find the claims a previous record
read by hand has unmeasured recall, and its counts are lower bounds — which is what §3's were.

**Twelve rows are new. Two matter, and one of them is not benign.**

* **`E_a_ellagitannin_oxidation > E_a_oak_extraction`** — D-168 §3's ordering 2, the one that
  *inverted* there. Post-D-168 (oak's high edge 35k → 25k) it **HOLDS**: joint-edge margin
  **+5,000 J/mol**, breach 0.0000 %, and both members are drawn together in wine + aging and
  beer + aging. A seventh instance of the shape, currently satisfied — and a clean confirmation
  that D-168's narrowing did what it claimed.
* **`ethanol_tolerance_mlf < ethanol_tolerance`** — *"Set to ~14 % ABV (110 g/L), BELOW the yeast
  `ethanol_tolerance` (142 g/L) — O. oeni is less ethanol-tolerant than the yeast"*, a sourced
  biological direction. Nominal margin +32 g/L; **joint-edge margin −5 g/L**; breach **0.0362 %**
  over 2×10⁶ draws; **LIVE** (both drawn in wine + MLF, wine + MLF + Brett, wine + aging), and
  **unguarded**. A new live instance, on an axis §3 never reached.
* **`wine_generic::E_a_fusels`'s note is FALSE AT THE SHIPPED NOMINALS** — not at a band edge.
  It read *"all > `E_a_uptake` (55,100); below `E_a_esters` as the ester/fusel ratio rises with
  T"*. That is **beer's** ordering (beer `E_a_esters` = 200,000) shipped in the **wine** file:
  wine's `E_a_esters` is **55,100**, set `== E_a_uptake` by D-21 so run-integrated synthesis is
  ~T-independent, and this 70,000 sits **14,900 J/mol ABOVE** it. The wine ester/fusel ratio
  therefore FALLS with T — which is the *deliberate* wine design (liquid esters fall with T
  through the stripping sink). This is the **fourth carrier** of the wine-`E_a_esters` confusion
  D-168 §4 killed in three others, and the only one that survived because no screen had ever
  emitted the pair. **Note corrected; no number moved.**
* The remaining new rows are the same ellagitannin window's *"matching the oxidative siblings"*
  read as *"above"* them — false positives of the kind §3 already documents.

**§3's headline is corrected.** "Five live instances, not four" was a lower bound stated as a
census — the shape D-163 §7 got wrong and D-167 corrected, arriving here from the recall side
rather than the field side. The measured position:

* **7 invariants found**, of which **1 HOLDS** (ellagitannin/oak, +5,000), **1 TOUCHES at zero**
  (`E_a_decarb`, now guarded), and **5 BREACH and are unguarded** — `y_acetaldehyde_per_tannin`
  34.22 %, `k_death_brett` 23.09 %, `y_methanethiol` 19.36 %, `y_a420_per_maillard_melanoidin`
  16.37 %, `ethanol_tolerance_mlf` 0.0362 % — plus D-118's guarded pair.
* Recall is now measured **against D-168's three** and against nothing else. **Seven is still a
  lower bound**: a screen keyed on ordering words cannot find an ordering stated without one.
  Any future count off `orderings.py` must say which control it was validated against.

Also settled, from the same review: `.claude/hooks/check_memory_size.py` was verified to *bite*
rather than merely exit 0 — fed a deliberately 9-line block it reports both the block and the
300-line backstop, and reports clean on the shipped file. An exit code with no output is not

## D-171 — The beat was "guard the five ordering breaches" and not one of them can be guarded where it breaches: every joint-edge margin is negative, so the D-170 guard shape needs a band edge moved and no citation licenses that — but proving the five are unguarded took four rounds, because rounds 1 and 2 each attributed a RED to the archive that belonged to something else, and the pair whose consequence guard NAMES the ordering does not fire when the ordering is fully inverted

**Corrects:** D-170 — "five live instances" was again a lower bound stated as a count; three recall holes hide two more pairs, one of them the sharpest instance in the archive (55.20 % breach), and D-170's own §3 verdicts for those five said "note correction" without the mutation evidence that would license the claim.
**Flags:** D-74, D-137 — `k_browning_base`/`k_ethanol_oxidation` are documented as a PARTITION of a fixed 5.0e-4 (one degree of freedom) but ship as two independent draws, and `k_activation_floor` is documented as that same sum yet ships as a third. Identified, measured, NOT repaired — the code still carries the old behaviour.

### 1. The beat is not achievable as named, and that is the result

D-170 closed with `test_the_decarb_reduction_ordering_survives_both_bands`, which guards a
sourced ordering *where the sampler reads it*:

```python
assert decarb.uncertainty.low >= reduction.uncertainty.high   # -> 60,000 >= 60,000
```

That assertion exists there because the margin is **non-negative** — the two edges meet
exactly. Copying the shape onto the five breaches is impossible: **every one of their
margins is negative**, i.e. `low >= high` is *false today*. Shipping it would require first
narrowing a band, and nine of the ten parameters involved are `author estimate` /
`speculative`. The pre-registration committed the constraint in advance — *an `author
estimate` cannot license a band narrowing* — because narrowing a band so the author's own
prose comes true is tuning the band to the test, the mirror image of the error the archive
already forbids. **Zero edges moved.** The inversions remain live and unguardable until a
citation arrives that moves an edge on its own authority.

What shipped instead is nominal-scoped coverage that says, in each docstring, the breach
rate it does **not** forbid. A guard silent about its own scope gets read as covering the
breach — which is exactly the false assurance D-170 §5 documented, and this beat exists to
close it, not to manufacture another instance of it.

### 2. Recall, again: 5 -> 7, from three holes the amendment named but did not instantiate

D-170's amendment wrote that "a screen keyed on ordering words cannot find an ordering
stated without one" and stopped there. Instantiated (`recall_holes.py`):

* **SYMBOL, NOT WORD.** `k_browning_base`'s note states its claim as the expression
  `k_browning_base > k_ethanol_oxidation` inside *"The load-bearing claim is the ORDERING"*.
  `ABOVE`/`BELOW` are English words; the screen never emitted it. This is the **highest
  breach rate in the archive, 55.20 %**, and it was invisible for want of a `>`.
* **THE AMBIGUOUS-PARSE QUARANTINE WAS NEVER REVISITED.** The screen rightly refuses to let
  a regex resolve *"held ABOVE X … below Y"* and quarantines the pair; the hand-read pass
  never went back for it. It holds `E_a_fusels` vs `E_a_uptake` — and `E_a_pof`'s, which is
  stated **band-scoped in so many words** (*"across the full parameter range, not just at
  the point estimate"*).
* **A DIRECTION WORD CAN INVERT ON THE QUANTITY.** *"steeper than"* is an `ABOVE` synonym,
  but a retention fraction that decays steeper is numerically **smaller**.

Denominator stated (`feedback-count-and-print-your-skips`): 36 evaluable rows, of which 21
carried a published adjudication and **15 did not — all 15 adjudicated here**, including
eight INVERTS rows §3 never named. Two new false-positive classes appear: *"below"* as a
**file position** (*"the byproduct diversion below (decision D-16)"*), and *"below"* whose
referent is a **threshold, not the sibling** (*"Below the floor the rate is zero"*).

### 3. Four rounds, because the first three REDs were not about the ordering

This is the transferable part. Each round's design was falsified by the next, always the
same way: **a RED was credited to the mechanism under test when it belonged to something
else.**

* **Round 1 — a schema rejection wearing a finding's colour.** The arm was "move the
  nominal across the ordering". For three arms the crossing point lies *outside the
  parameter's own band*, and `Parameter` enforces `low <= value <= high`, so the store
  refused to load and the suite failed at **collection**. Worst: **arm 7 was the KNOWN-RED
  CONTROL.** It returned RED, "matching its prediction", having never executed
  `test_aging.py:1459`. A control that confirms itself through the wrong mechanism is worse
  than none — it certifies a harness that was never tested.
  `feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms` generalises: verifying the RESTORE is
  not enough, the **APPLY must be verified to produce a loadable tree**.
* **Round 2 — magnitude wearing the ordering's colour.** Fixed with a per-arm pre-flight
  load (schema rejection now reports INVALID, never RED) and in-band crossings where *both*
  members move onto their own edges. Three arms went RED. But doubling a yield, cutting
  `ethanol_tolerance` 15 %, or moving an activation energy 14 % perturbs plenty that has
  nothing to do with which side of a sibling the value lands on.
* **Round 3 — keep the perturbation, drop the flip.** Each RED re-run against an
  ordering-*preserving* move of the same size; for the two-parameter crossings, each half
  alone (each half leaves the ordering intact, only together do they cross). Result:
  **every round-2 RED reproduced under a baseline.** `y_acetaldehyde_per_tannin` 0.06->0.12
  and 0.06->0.03 fire the *identical two* trajectory pins; 5's three MLF failures reproduce
  under the mlf-side half with **identical assertion values** (`2.3545520666619044`).
* **Round 4 — assert granularity, because a node can have more than one cause.**
  `test_integrated_wine_aroma_temperature_directions` carries four asserts with three
  causes. Node-level subtraction would have deleted it as "magnitude" and hidden a real
  guard. It did not hide one — it revealed the opposite, §4 below.

Also measured: `-x` makes a red arm *slower* under xdist (394 s vs a green arm's 232 s),
since each worker finishes its in-flight test before teardown. Round 2 dropped it, which is
also what made "which test fired" answerable at all.

### 4. The sharpest finding: a guard that names the ordering and does not fire on it

`test_kinetics_byproducts.py::test_integrated_wine_aroma_temperature_directions` calls
itself *"THE load-bearing regression guard for the per-pool E_a ordering (D-19 -> D-21)"*,
and line 691 asserts the consequence `cold[fusels] < warm[fusels]`, commented *"FUSELS rise
with T (E_a_fusels > E_a_uptake)"*.

Set the pair to their worst joint draw — `E_a_fusels` 60,000 against `E_a_uptake` 63,000,
the ordering **fully inverted**, exactly the −3,000 J/mol the bands permit — and **line 691
passes**. The asserts that do fire (line 711's flat-total, varela2004's dryness window)
reproduce **bitwise-identically** when `E_a_uptake` moves alone with the ordering intact,
and the fusel-side half alone is entirely green.

This is worse than an absent guard. An absent guard is found by a census; a guard whose
**sensitivity threshold sits above the breach its own bands permit** reads as coverage,
names the right mechanism in its own comment, and would have survived any review that read
it rather than ran it. `feedback-name-guards-for-what-they-forbid` has been about
mis*labelled* guards; this is a correctly-labelled guard that is nonetheless insensitive at
the reachable magnitude — a distinct failure mode, and one only mutation at the true joint
edge can find.

### 5. The seven, adjudicated on evidence

| pair | breach | verdict | shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `k_browning_base > k_ethanol_oxidation` | **55.20 %** | nominal GUARDED (`test_aging.py`), band half UNGUARDED — a pure band move (high 8.0e-4 -> 2.9e-4, nominal untouched) leaves 1518 passing | scope stated in that test |
| `y_acetaldehyde_per_tannin < …_anthocyanin` | 34.21 % | unasserted at ANY scope; both round-2 REDs are magnitude pins | nominal guard |
| `k_death_brett < k_death_mlf` | 23.05 % | unasserted at ANY scope (nominal crossed, 1518 passed) | nominal guard |
| `y_methanethiol < y_h2s_autolysis` | 19.39 % | unasserted at ANY scope | **deliberately none** |
| `y_a420_per_maillard_melanoidin > y_a420_per_melanoidin` | 16.41 % | unasserted at ANY scope | nominal guard |
| `ethanol_tolerance_mlf < ethanol_tolerance` | 0.036 % | unasserted; all REDs reproduce from the mlf-side half alone | nominal guard |
| `E_a_fusels > E_a_uptake` (wine, beer) | 0.0051 %, 0.0021 % | guard exists, names it, **does not fire** (§4) | nominal guard, both media |

The ship/don't-ship line is **whether the note declares the DIRECTION sourced**, not whether
the ordering exists. `k_death_brett` (*"DIRECTION is sourced …; the magnitude is the
speculative modelling choice"*), `y_a420_per_maillard_melanoidin` (Hodge 1953),
`E_a_fusels` (*"the sourced, load-bearing constraint"*), `ethanol_tolerance_mlf`
(Ribereau-Gayon; G-Alegria 2004) and the ethyl-bridge stoichiometry (Timberlake & Bridle
1976) all qualify. **`y_methanethiol` does not**: its ordering rests on *"reduction skews to
H2S"*, and no source in its provenance fixes that branch ratio — the citations are biomass
methionine content and sensory thresholds. Asserting it would pin author prose as if it were
sourced, the same error as narrowing a band to make prose come true. It ships **unguarded,
with the reason recorded as a test** that fails if either parameter ever acquires such a
source.

One caveat the tannin guard cannot discharge and says so: the one-bridge-per-PAIR argument
is **molar**, while both yields are **mass** ratios over lumped pools with, in their own
notes, *"no clean molar mass"* — which is precisely the uncertainty those bands carry.

### 6. The two flags — identified, measured, not repaired

* **`k_ethanol_oxidation`'s band contradicts its own stated construction rule.** The note
  says *"Banded ~0.2-0.6x the total"* of 5.0e-4, licensing [1.0e-4, 3.0e-4]. The shipped
  band is [4.0e-5, 8.0e-4] = **0.08–1.6x**, and a 1.6× *share* of a total is not a share.
  Two consequences need no edge move to state: (a) even the note-licensed 3.0e-4 still
  exceeds `k_browning_base`'s low 2.0e-4, so the ordering breaches at the joint edge **either
  way** (margin −1.0e-4); (b) the rule's own 0.6× exceeds 0.5, so **the rule admits the
  inversion of the "SMALLER share" claim the same note calls load-bearing**. Its sibling's
  band ([2.0e-4, 4.0e-4] = 0.4–0.8×) *does* obey its own rule — the defect is one-sided.
  This is the only instance of the seven where the narrowing question is decidable **from
  the note** rather than from provenance tier, and it is still not taken unilaterally:
  narrowing a shipped band changes a sampling surface.
* **One degree of freedom, three independent draws.** `k_browning_base` +
  `k_ethanol_oxidation` are documented as a partition of a fixed 5.0e-4, and
  `k_activation_floor` as that same sum. All three are sampled independently; the two shares
  sum over **[2.4e-4, 1.2e-3]** against the 5.0e-4 that `test_aging.py` asserts at a single
  point with `pytest.approx` — `feedback-pin-tolerance-vs-solver-tolerance` waiting to
  happen.

### 7. Limits of this record

* **Nominal guards do not close the breaches**, and nothing here should be read as if they
  did. Seven live inversions remain, four of them above 15 % of joint draws.
* The `_inverts` companion assert in each new test **records that the bands still overlap**.
  It is not a claim that they should — it fails loudly if an edge moves, so promoting a pair
  to the joint-edge assertion is a deliberate act.
* **Two orderings remain non-live rather than resolved** (D-159 applies): `E_a_pof <
  E_a_uptake` HOLDS but `E_a_pof` reaches no sampler in the seven scenarios tried, and
  `spirit_soak_retention < oak_fill_retention` INVERTS (0.2973 %) but barrel-fill history is
  never exercised. "No scenario tried" is not "structurally undrawable".
* The note corrections quote the orderings they correct, so the D-170 §2 non-idempotence
  applies: **a re-run of the text screen will re-flag these repaired notes.** Any future
  count must diff membership against the pre-repair tree, not compare totals. **The
  pre-repair tree is commit `3c45216`** — `git show 3c45216:src/fermentation/parameters/data/<f>`
  reconstructs it, which is the only place it survives (the screen itself lives under
  `M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d171-ordering-guards\`, outside the repo). Naming the
  baseline is what makes that diff runnable later instead of merely recommended.

Suite **1524 passed** (1518 + 6), `ruff` and `mypy` clean. Nine notes corrected, one test
docstring scoped, six guards added, **no number moved**.

## D-172 — The "one degree of freedom, three independent draws" flag is a claim about the FILES and not about any ensemble: no run ever draws all three, but two are live in every aged arm, and the pair the cascade draws is a TOTAL against its own SHARE — repaired by reparameterising rather than by coupling the sampler, which drops the archive's highest ordering-breach rate from 55.20 % to 12.54 % with no edge moved

**Corrects:** D-171 — its §6 "one degree of freedom, three independent draws" is true of the parameter files and false of every ensemble: the maximum co-drawn in one run is two, and under the cascade the live pair is the total against one of its own shares, not share against share.
**Flags:** D-141 — `k_activation_floor`'s high edge 1.0e-3 has no account; it is carried over unchanged into `k_o2_depletion_total` because moving it is the owner's call, not mine.
**Flags:** D-74 — `E_a_ethanol_oxidation` and `E_a_browning` are two entries with identical value AND identical band, drawn independently, while `E_a_browning`'s note claims the partition is exact "at every T"; the amendment below measures it. The rate constants are repaired here; the activation energies carry the same defect and still ship.

Owner's direction was **"B then A"**: fix the partition first so that `k_ethanol_oxidation`'s
band question falls out as a consequence rather than as an independent sampling-surface move.
It did — but as a **dissolution**, not a repair, which §7 states in those terms.

### 1. What is actually drawn, which took three corrections to establish

D-171 §6 flagged three constants documented as one number: `k_ethanol_oxidation` +
`k_browning_base` as a partition of a fixed 5.0e-4, and `k_activation_floor` as that same
sum. Whether they are drawn *together* is a sampler question, and the answer is no:

| arm | eth | brn | floor | live pair |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wine/beer aged, `direct` (default) | MOVES | MOVES | — | share vs share |
| wine/beer aged, `direct_burst` | MOVES | MOVES | — | share vs share |
| wine/beer aged, `cascade`, no SO2 | *inert* | — | MOVES | none |
| wine/beer aged, `cascade`, +50 mg/L SO2 | MOVES | — | MOVES | **TOTAL vs its own SHARE** |

**Max co-drawn in any single run: two of three.** The `reads` predicate declares
`k_ethanol_oxidation` under the cascade, but D-166's rule bites — declared `reads` is an
upper bound. There it is only the H2O2 ethanol branch weight in
`w_eth / (w_eth + k_so2_oxidation·[HSO3-])`; at zero free bisulfite that is `w/w == 1` and
the constant cancels out of the trajectory bitwise.

**Three corrections were needed to get this table, and each is the failure mode a note in
`.claude/memory` already names.**

1. The first run returned INERT for all three constants in all three sets. The positive
   control (`mu_max`, which MOVES) showed why: the scenario had **no closure and no
   `add_oxygen`**, so `o2` was identically 0 for the whole run and every O2-rate constant was
   inert *correctly and uninformatively*. `feedback-a-null-result-needs-a-positive-control`,
   landing for the second time after D-166.
2. With O2 supplied, the cascade read INERT on `k_ethanol_oxidation` — and that was reported,
   in the first draft of this record's own pre-registration, as a structural fact. It is not:
   it is held open by an absent SO2 dose. `feedback-a-margin-is-a-claim-about-what-holds-it-
   open`. The sulfited arm is what caught it.
3. The pairing the cascade draws is **worse** than the one D-171 flagged, not a milder
   version of it: `k_ethanol_oxidation`'s high 8.0e-4 is **8× `k_activation_floor`'s low**
   1.0e-4, so a member could draw one route's share at eight times the total it is a share of.

### 2. Why the repair is a reparameterisation and not a sampler hook

The obvious fix — a post-draw hook deriving `k_browning_base := 5.0e-4 − k_ethanol_oxidation`
— **cannot ship at all**: ethanol's own shipped high, 8.0e-4, drives browning negative. It
also inverts the owner's chosen order, since it would need A done first to be well-posed.

The shipped form is the in-Process-composite idiom `k_browning_eff` already uses one level up:

    k_ethanol_oxidation  ==  k_o2_depletion_total *      f_ethanol_o2_share
    k_browning_base      ==  k_o2_depletion_total * (1 - f_ethanol_o2_share)
    k_activation_floor   ==  k_o2_depletion_total

**Two products, never a subtraction, for an arithmetic reason measured before anything was
designed around it:** `5.0e-4*0.4 == 2.0e-4` and `5.0e-4*0.6 == 3.0e-4` are both exact in
float64, while `5.0e-4 - 2.0e-4` is `3.0000000000000003e-4`. That exactness is what makes the
"no number moved" claim bitwise rather than approximate.

**The first draft of this record justified that choice with a consequence it had not run —
and the consequence is false.** It said the subtraction form "would red every
`np.array_equal` isolability pin". §9 arm A measured it: the subtraction form leaves **361
tests GREEN**. The isolability pins each compare two runs that both use whichever formula is
in the file, so a one-ULP shift moves them together and they stay self-consistent. The
exactness only shows up against the values the *pre-repair tree* produced, and nothing in the
suite compared against those. `feedback-conceded-caveats-are-not-coverage`, in its other
direction: a stated mechanism is not a measured one.

Three YAML entries retired, two shipped, one new pure helper
(`core/kinetics/o2_partition.py::o2_depletion_shares`) that both oxidative sets call.

### 3. The headline, pre-registered before the campaign

| | breach rate of "browning is the DOMINANT share" |
|---|---|
| pre-repair, two independent bands | **55.2332 %** (D-171 reported 55.20 %) |
| post-repair, one total × one fraction | **12.5398 %** |
| pre-registered analytic prediction | **12.5000 %** |

`|measured − predicted| = 0.04 pp` — a **HIT**, at n = 2,000,000, seed 20260810. The claim
is now exactly `f_ethanol_o2_share < 0.5`, so the breach rate is the triangular tail
`0.1²/(0.4·0.2)` on ONE band. **No edge was moved to achieve it.**

The sum those notes documented as fixed at 5.0e-4 was, pre-repair, off by more than 1e-6 on
**99.54 %** of draws.

### 4. The ordering is still NOT closed, and the guard says so where the breach is

12.5 % is not 0 %. The band's own construction rule — `"~0.2-0.6x the total"`, quoted
verbatim from the two retired entries, which stated the same rule from opposite ends and
agree exactly — licenses 0.6, and 0.6 > 0.5. Closing the ordering needs that high edge
narrowed to 0.5 on the strength of the author's own prose, which is the narrowing D-171
refused seven times. **Left open on purpose.** `test_aging.py`'s guard asserts the ordering
at the nominal *and* asserts `high > 0.5`, so the test fails loudly if that edge is ever
quietly moved to make the prose come true.

### 5. The half-life text was RIGHT when written and went stale — the opposite of D-170

D-170 found two notes whose bands were wrong *when written*. This is the other shape.

`k_ethanol_oxidation`'s note said the sum gives `"half-life ln2/k ~ 350-7000 h"`, and
`k_activation_floor`'s repeated it. That text is arithmetically exact for **[1.0e-4,
2.0e-3]** (346.6 h and 6931.5 h) — which is precisely the band D-71 shipped for this
parameter, at the same value 5.0e-4, as the sole always-on sink before D-74 partitioned it
(commit `e1105ae`). D-74 moved the band to [4.0e-5, 8.0e-4] and **left the sentence**, where
it has since described the sum rather than the entry. D-141 copied the sentence again, onto a
third band.

So the total's high edge has **three disagreeing claimants and the shipped one has no
account**:

| candidate | high | account |
|---|---|---|
| `k_activation_floor` as shipped (**carried over**) | 1.0e-3 | **none** — a clean decade, and not what its own note claims to inherit |
| its own note's "inherits the band of the total it un-partitions" | 1.2e-3 | the arithmetic sum of two independent bands — i.e. the artefact being repaired |
| D-71's shipped band, whose half-life prose still survives verbatim | **2.0e-3** | **PRINTED**, and previously shipped |

The low edge 1.0e-4 is agreed by all three. D-172 **moves no declared edge** and writes the
three accounts into `k_o2_depletion_total`'s own note. Adopting 2.0e-3 would be a restoration
with printed provenance rather than a new number, and it is the owner's call.

### 6. The price, which is not zero and is not a defect

The two shares no longer carry their own bands — they inherit the total's (r = 10):

| | retired band | reach after |
|---|---|---|
| ethanol share | [4.0e-5, 8.0e-4] | [2.3e-5, 5.9e-4], median 3.23e-4 → **2.05e-4** |
| browning share | [2.0e-4, 4.0e-4] | [4.3e-5, 7.9e-4] — low ×0.21, high ×1.98 |

The browning share in particular now reaches five times below its retired low. That is what
"one degree of freedom" costs, and no edge was moved to cause it. The ethanol share's median
falling to within 2 % of its nominal is a side effect of the fraction being symmetric where
its retired band was strongly right-skewed — *not* an identity (the D-165 trap), but not an
improvement anyone asked for either.

### 7. Two things this record must not be read as claiming

* **The sum anchor is now an IDENTITY, which makes the assert VACUOUS, not stronger.**
  `total·f + total·(1-f) ≡ total` holds by construction. D-171's version of that assert held
  at one point of a two-dimensional band; the repair did not strengthen it, it removed its
  content. The falsifiable residue moved entirely into `f < 0.5`. The test says so in its own
  comment. (Measured, since it was an open question at pre-registration: the identity is
  **mathematical, not bitwise** — exact on 89.80 % of draws, max residual 2.2e-19.)
* **A did not complete; it DISSOLVED.** `k_ethanol_oxidation` no longer exists as a sampled
  object, so its band has no edge left to narrow and D-171 §6's first flag is **moot**, not
  repaired. D-168's beer margin dissolved the same way. Reporting this as "the band question
  is fixed" would be a different and false claim.

### 9. The guards were mutation-tested BEFORE they were written

`feedback-mutate-the-premise-before-building-the-guard`. Three arms, each a one-line edit to
`o2_depletion_shares`, run against the shipped suite *first* and against the new
`tests/test_o2_partition.py` *after*:

| arm | shipped suite (361 tests) | with the new guards |
|---|---|---|
| **A** browning := `total - total*f` (1-ULP shift) | **GREEN** | **RED** — `assert 0.00030000000000000003 == 0.0003` |
| **B** shares swapped (the control) | **RED** | **RED** |
| **C** `f` hard-coded to 0.4 (drops the parameter) | **GREEN** | **RED** — `assert brn_hi < eth_hi` |

Two of three GREEN, so the guard is **licensed** rather than decoration — the D-155/D-156
test, passed on the D-156 side. Arm B is the arm designed to be RED, which is what makes the
restore verifiable (`feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms`); the file was
compared byte-for-byte against its original after every arm.

Arm C is the sharper of the two greens: `f_ethanol_o2_share` can be deleted as a *parameter*,
keeping only its nominal, and 361 tests do not notice. That is the same shape as D-166's
"`reads` reach is an upper bound" — a name can be declared, drawn, and still not be load-
bearing for anything the suite checks.

### 8. Limits

* The co-draw table is **per scenario tried**, and the scenarios are named. D-159 applies:
  "no scenario tried" is not "structurally undrawable".
* **No count assert broke.** The D-156/D-157 surface counts (247 distinct varying names, and
  the rest) are recorded in *prose* in `test_drawability_surface.py`, not asserted, so
  retiring three parameters and adding two turned nothing red. Pre-registration P5 predicted
  those files would go RED; they did not, and the reason is that the counts were never pins.
  That is a live gap in the surface guards, found by accident, and it is not fixed here.
* **P2 (bitwise) is a HIT**: all nine nominal arms — {wine, wine+SO2, beer} x {direct,
  cascade, direct_burst} — are bitwise identical between `413c809` and this tree, over a
  400-point grid on every state slot. The comparison carries its own control: both same-shape
  sibling arms differ from each other *within* one tree, so "all identical" is not the diff
  silently comparing a file with itself.

`f·f_E / (f·f_E + (1−f)·f_B)` against a nominal 0.400:

| T | worst low | worst high | spread |
|---|---|---|---|

### 1. Control A — does the mechanism claim reproduce on THIS tree?

§6 attributed the reachability to the TOTAL alone: standing `o2` is `otr / Σk`, and after D-172
`Σk = total·f + total·(1−f) ≡ total`, so `f_ethanol_o2_share` cancels. If that is right, forcing

with both retired constants at their own lows (`413c809`, Σk = 4.0e-5 + 2.0e-4 = 2.4e-4).

| tree | arm | `o2.max()` | headroom |
|---|---|---|---|
| `413c809` | both retired lows (Σk = 2.4e-4) | 4.2732e-3 | 1.87x |
| this | `k_o2_depletion_total` = 2.4e-4 | **4.2657e-3** | 1.88x |

It reproduces to **0.18 %** — not bitwise, and the residual is real rather than solver noise: the

Three separate PRINTED claimants agreed on 1.0e-4: `k_activation_floor`'s shipped low, D-71's
original shipped low, and the 7000 h end of the retired half-life text. D-172 §5 was right that this

### 5. The guard, and what its RED names

`tests/test_closure_ingress.py::test_the_low_edge_of_the_o2_total_cannot_draw_a_supersaturated_wine`.
It does **not** copy D-154's recompute-the-bound idiom: `otr/Σk` is the CEILING, and §6 spent a
section establishing that a ceiling above saturation does not mean `o2` gets there — an algebraic
guard would re-commit that conflation in code. It integrates instead.

* the edge is **read from the compile seam**, never restated, so re-lowering the YAML fails here;
* **monotonicity** `at_low > at_nominal > at_high` is asserted, which makes "the low edge is the
  worst case" run rather than assumed — and doubles as the anti-self-confirmation control, since an
  override that silently failed to apply returns three equal numbers and fails the ordering
  (`feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms`);
* the nominal arm is the **paired GREEN control** (`< sat/3`);
* the cascade arm covers the other shipped set.

**Mutated before it was trusted.** Reverting the YAML low to 1.0e-4 kills **exactly one test** — this
one — and the RED prints the edge and the value it drew: `low edge 1.00e-04 draws o2.max() =
9.676e-03 g/L`. The other 36 tests in the file, *including* the nominal-level saturation test that
motivated the whole thread, stay GREEN. That is the attribution discipline of
`feedback-pair-the-red-with-an-ordering-preserving-baseline`: the RED names the cause, and a
same-file baseline shows the mutation did not just break the scenario.

One scenario family (the D-136 five-year bottle-aging arm), one state slot, one medium. The 12-parameter

### 8. Amendment (same day) — the headline margin counts a member this record itself calls not-a-sink, and the guard's monotonicity arm forbade the safe direction

Two defects, both in what shipped an hour earlier, both caught by review rather than by the suite.

**(a) The heading's 1.14x is a THREE-SURFACE figure, not the sink joint.** §2's corner includes
`T_ref` at 298.15 — and §2 itself parenthesises `T_ref` as "not a sink constant", §3 puts
`closure_otr` in a separate class for the same reason, and the harness printed the split. So the
headline asserts the tighter number while the body explains why that member does not belong in it.
The cascade's 1.04x in §3 carries the same contamination and was never run the other way. Measured
here, sink constants only (11 parameters, `T_ref` held out):

| set | corner + shipped low 1.0e-4 | corner + D-173 low 2.4e-4 |
|---|---|---|
| direct, sinks only | 1.1117e-2 (0.72x) | 5.0409e-3 (**1.59x**) |
| direct, sinks + `T_ref` | 1.4165e-2 (0.56x) | 7.0230e-3 (1.14x) |
| cascade, sinks only | 1.1487e-2 (0.70x) | 5.6640e-3 (**1.41x**) |
| cascade, sinks + `T_ref` | 1.4002e-2 (0.57x) | 7.7287e-3 (1.04x) |

**The sink-joint margin is 1.59x (direct) and 1.41x (cascade).** 1.14x / 1.04x are three-surface
figures and should be quoted only with `T_ref` named. Every arm at the shipped low is above
saturation and every arm at 2.4e-4 is below it, so the *conclusion* is unchanged in all four rows —
it is the number in the heading that is over-tight. The heading is left as written (append-only);
read it as the three-surface figure it is.

**(b) The guard forbade the safe direction.** §5's monotonicity arm was `at_low > at_nominal >
at_high`. Raising the low edge *toward* the nominal — a change that makes the physics safer —
collapses that ordering and turns the guard RED for it. A guard that fires on the safe direction is
one the next reader argues away, which is `feedback-name-guards-for-what-they-forbid` landing on a
guard written in the same commit that cites the lesson. Fixed by taking the middle arm at the band's
**geometric centre** `sqrt(lo*hi)`, strictly interior for any band the schema admits, and by moving
the paired GREEN control onto the *high* arm (`at_high < sat/3`), whose direction is also safe. Both
mutation arms re-run: low edge raised to 5.0e-4 → **GREEN**; low edge re-lowered to 1.0e-4 → **RED**,
still naming the edge and the value. The nominal arm is dropped, so the guard now costs four
integrations rather than five.

Neither defect was reachable by the suite: (a) is prose and (b) only fires on a mutation nobody had
run — the mutation discipline covers *removing* the protection, and this was the arm that
*strengthens* it.

| 1.2e-3 | `k_activation_floor`'s claim to inherit "the band of the total it un-partitions" | the arithmetic sum of two independent bands — the artefact D-172 repaired |
| **2.0e-3** | D-71's shipped band for exactly this parameter, `[1.0e-4, 2.0e-3]` at commit `e1105ae` | **printed, and previously shipped** |

The first row is the finding. 1.0e-3's only recorded rationale was structural — it made a clean
decade with 1.0e-4 — and **D-173 deleted the number it was round against**. The rationale
dissolved in the same commit that wrote "the high edge is untouched and still has no account",
and the note said so accurately ("a clean decade with the OLD low") without anyone noticing that
this had stopped being a description of anything. So the shipped edge was not merely unaccounted
for; its one account had been *invalidated by the previous record*.

2.0e-3 is also D-71's own rendering of the sentence that is **still live in this entry's `source`
field** — "a saturating O2 charge is scavenged over weeks-to-months at cellar temperature" —
which D-71 wrote out as "half-life ln2/k ~ 350-7000 h (~2 weeks to ~10 months)", arithmetically
exact for its band (346.6 h, 6931.5 h). The shipped 1.0e-3 renders that same sentence's fast end
as 4.1 weeks. **This is not the "weeks vs months" word-argument it could be mistaken for**: the
point is that one sentence has two renderings in this archive, one of them printed and shipped,
and the edge that survived is neither.

### 2. The null D-173 conceded, now run — with a positive control and a 200x sweep

`feedback-conceded-caveats-are-not-coverage`. Every arm forces `k_o2_depletion_total` and holds
everything else nominal; the wine arm is D-173's own five-year `synthetic_supremecorq` bottle,
the beer arm is D-139's 8 mg/L packaging dose over 120 d. Both oxidative sets, 32 integrations.

| `k_total` | wine `o2.max()` (direct) | × sat | beer consumed | acetaldehyde (wine) | A420 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1.0e-4** (retired low, **positive control**) | **9.6756e-3** | **1.21 — ABOVE SAT** | 1.770 mg/L | 0.0170 | 0.1925 |
| 2.4e-4 (shipped low) | 4.2657e-3 | 0.53 | 3.609 | 0.0217 | 0.2459 |
| 5.0e-4 (nominal) | 2.0498e-3 | 0.26 | 5.706 | 0.0240 | 0.2722 |
| 1.0e-3 (old high) | 1.0249e-3 | 0.13 | 7.337 | 0.0256 | 0.2904 |
| **2.0e-3 (adopted)** | **5.1262e-4** | **0.064** | 7.932 | 0.0271 | 0.3078 |
| 1.0e-2 | 1.0259e-4 | 0.013 | 7.931 | 0.0313 | 0.3550 |
| **1.0e-1 (200x nominal)** | 1.0264e-5 | 0.001 | 7.335 | 0.0360 | 0.4091 |

The control reproduces D-173's 9.6756e-3 **exactly**, so the null is a measurement and not a
silence (`feedback-a-null-result-needs-a-positive-control`). Across the whole sweep `o2.max()`
tracks `1/k` to four figures, `o2` never goes below -2.4e-12 (solver residue on an exhausted
pool, 3e-10 of the dose), beer's consumption only rises toward its dose, and acetaldehyde and
A420 rise monotonically and stay in range. **There is no high-side channel to an impossible
state at 200x the nominal**, let alone at 4x. The cascade set was swept identically and agrees
to three figures on `o2.max()` at every point.

### 3. The price — which exists, is on a different surface, and is the thing D-173 §4 missed

Raising the always-on total does not only lower standing o2: it takes a larger share of the same
O2 away from every substrate-gated sink. The one external-facing quantity that reads that
competition is the SO2:O2 reaction ratio the Danilewicz/Miao benchmark measures. **Both
directions were pre-registered before the arm ran**, per set, and the harness was gated on
reproducing the benchmark file's own printed numbers first (1.7707 direct / 1.1338 cascade /
traverse 0.8586 — all three reproduced).

| `k_total` | DIRECT ratio | in Miao (1.0972-1.6621) | CASCADE ratio | in Miao |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nominal 5.0e-4 | 1.7707 | **no — above it** | 1.1338 | yes |
| 1.0e-3 (old high) | 1.6590 | yes | 1.1100 | yes |
| **2.0e-3 (adopted)** | **1.4829** | **yes** | **1.0655** | **no — below the floor** |
| 1.0e-2 | 0.8579 | no | 0.8177 | no |

* **P1 HIT.** Predicted "1.32 ≤ direct < 1.77, inside the union band"; measured 1.4829. The
  starvation mechanism is real and lives mostly in the direct set, where the total competes
  head-on with `SulfiteOxidation`.
* **P2 MISS.** Predicted `|Δcascade| < 0.05`; measured **0.0683**. The direction was right (the
  cascade is 4.2x less sensitive, because there the total is the *activation* rate rather than a
  competitor at the H2O2/quinone nodes) and the threshold was wrong. The miss matters: it is
  exactly the 0.018 that carries the cascade below Miao's floor, and a record that had stopped at
  "insensitive, as predicted" would have shipped without noticing.
* **Neither is a licence, in either direction.** Agreement with one dataset's spread is what a
  band is *for*, and the benchmark file already records the cascade straddling that same floor on
  a **dose** change with no edge moved (1.0704 at 60, 1.1338 at 80, ~3.4 % headroom). A ratio
  below 1 is not unphysical either — Miao's own wine #1 reads 0.8443. So the cascade leaving the
  envelope at the edge is a **cost recorded**, not a refusal, and it is on a surface the shipped
  tests never run: they run at the nominal, which no edge move touches.
* The benchmark's own falsifiable content survives the move: the blocked→ideal traverse reads
  0.8586 at the nominal and **0.8296** at the new edge, still over its 0.4 floor and still ~4600x
  the direct set's residual.

### 4. What licenses the move, and the symmetry that must be said out loud

Documentary, and only documentary: 2.0e-3 is the sole candidate with a printed, previously
shipped account, and the alternative's account was invalidated by D-173. Two supporting facts
that are **not** the ground: the null in §2 (which removes an objection, not a reason), and the
direct set's agreement improving in §3 — the pre-registration ruled that out in advance, because
choosing an edge to land inside a benchmark band is fitting, which that benchmark file forbids in
its own words ("1.7 must emerge, never be fitted"). Widening is also the conservative direction on
a `speculative` band, and is **not** the class D-171 refused seven times — every one of those was
a narrowing.

**The half-adoption is symmetric and deliberate.** D-173 took the **low** of `k_activation_floor`'s
two-edge inherit-claim and rejected its high. D-174 takes the **high** of D-71's two-edge claim
whose **low** the same archive rejected on a measurement. Two two-edge claims, one edge taken
from each, neither kept whole — so the shipped `[2.4e-4, 2.0e-3]` **matches no printed band
anywhere**, and that is a consequence of deciding each edge on its own ground rather than an
oversight. Unstated, "picked the widest band on offer" is the objection that sticks; it is stated
here and in the YAML note.

### 5. The guard, and the measurement that licenses it

**The suite does not notice this edge in either direction.** Full run at the old 1.0e-3: 1532
passed. Full run at 2.0e-3, before any test was written: **1532 passed**. A doubling of a sampled
band's high edge, on the one band whose *other* edge D-173 had to move because it could draw an
impossible state, and nothing goes red — D-163's finding landing where it costs the most, and the
D-155/D-156 licence for what follows.

Two tests ship in `tests/test_o2_partition.py`, and they are **two tests rather than two asserts
on purpose**: in one function the first failure masks the second, and the two arms that matter
differ only in the second.

* `test_the_o2_totals_band_edges_are_pinned_to_the_accounts_that_set_them` — the low is
  **recomputed** from the retired shares' own lows (`4.0e-5 + 2.0e-4 == 2.4e-4`, exact in
  float64), the high is a **transcription** of D-71's printed high with nothing to recompute it
  from. It forbids **silence**, not a direction: the RED says moving it is allowed and moving it
  quietly is not (`feedback-name-guards-for-what-they-forbid`).
* `test_the_notes_half_life_span_is_the_shipped_edges_rendered` — the note's printed span is
  recomputed from the shipped edges (`347-2888 h`). This is the defect this axis has actually
  suffered: D-74 moved the band and left D-71's sentence describing the old one, D-141 copied that
  sentence onto a third band, and D-172 §5 caught it four records later.

Mutation arms, each a YAML edit, restored byte-for-byte with the SHA-256 verified after every one
(`feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms`):

| arm | pin | span | D-173's closure guard |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A0** file unchanged (the designed-GREEN control) | GREEN | GREEN | GREEN (46 passed) |
| **A1** high back to 1.0e-3, note left alone | **RED** | **RED** | GREEN |
| **A2** high back to 1.0e-3 **and its sentence moved with it** | **RED** | **GREEN** | GREEN |
| **B** low back to 1.0e-4 (harness-is-live control) | **RED** | **RED** | **RED** |

A2 is the ordering-preserving baseline at test granularity: a *consistent* re-sourcing reds only
the pin, which is what makes the pair diagnostic rather than redundant
(`feedback-pair-the-red-with-an-ordering-preserving-baseline`). B shows the arms are not
self-confirming — the same edit reaches a guard in another file.

### 6. Bookkeeping

* `hi/lo` goes 4.17 → **8.33**, still under D-165's `r >= 10` threshold, so that census's 338 live

### 7. Limits

* **One documentary ground, and it is contestable.** Nothing measured forces this edge — that is
  now established rather than assumed, and it cuts both ways: a future record with a real O2-uptake
  dataset for stored wine should overwrite both edges, not argue with these accounts.
* The §3 price is measured at **one dose (80 mg/L SO2), one protocol, one medium**, and at the
  band edge rather than over the band. No frequency claim: a triangular sampler puts vanishing
  density at an endpoint.
* **The beer arm's own control breaks at the far end of the sweep, benignly.** At `k >= 1.0e-2`
  the "dose landed" reading (taken 1 h after the dose, `rel=1e-3`) sees a pool that has already
  started draining, which is why consumption *falls* at 1.0e-1 in §2's table. It is a statement
  about the 1-hour sampling offset, not about the dose — and at the adopted 2.0e-3 the 1-hour
  depletion is 0.2 %, which would sit just outside that same tolerance if any test ever ran that
  arm at a band edge. None does.
* `closure_otr`'s band is still not sampled (D-136, flagged at D-173) and `T_ref` is still the
  member that must be named when the joint-corner margins are quoted (D-173 amendment). Neither
  moved here.

### 8. Amendment (same day) — the headline finding was read off a paraphrase, and the `Corrects` marker convicted a parenthetical of a claim it does not make

Three defects in what shipped an hour earlier, all found by review rather than by the suite. The
first strengthens the licence, the second withdraws a back-edge from the correction map, and the
third is this record's own defect class landing on a file it had just measured.

**(a) §1's account of 1.0e-3 came from D-173's note, not from D-141 — and the primary source says
something stronger.** §1 wrote that "1.0e-3's only recorded rationale was a clean decade with
1.0e-4". That phrase is D-172's and D-173's *description* of an edge they both call unaccounted;
it is not what D-141 recorded. Read at the source (`git show a96ebf1:...aging.yaml`), the entry
that introduced this edge states **two** accounts for its band and **neither of them is 1.0e-3**:

> `uncertainty: { low: 1.0e-4, high: 1.0e-3, note: "... Inherits the band of the total it
> un-partitions: k_ethanol_oxidation (4.0e-5..8.0e-4) plus k_browning_base together anchor a
> total O2 half-life ln2/k ~ 350-7000 h (~2 weeks to ~10 months) ..." }`

The inherit-claim computes **1.2e-3**. The half-life sentence — carried verbatim from D-71 —
renders **[1.0e-4, 2.0e-3]**. So D-141 shipped a high edge that contradicts both of the accounts
in its own note, and one of those accounts is the number D-174 restored. The correct statement is
therefore not "its rationale dissolved at D-173" but **"it never had one, and the note it shipped
under printed 2.0e-3"**. §4's licence stands and is stronger than it was written;
`feedback-verify-latest-state-not-breadcrumbs` — a load-bearing claim was taken from a downstream
paraphrase, and the paraphrase was mild rather than wrong.

**(b) `Corrects: D-173` is withdrawn.** D-173 §4 reads: "nothing measured forces it (raising it
only *lowers* standing o2), so D-172's owner's-call … stands open." In its own context the
parenthetical is the **direction on the o2 slot** — the subject of the two sections immediately
above it — and it is the *reason* nothing forces the edge, not an assertion that no other surface
moves. §2 of this record **confirms** that conclusion at 200×; §3 measures a different surface it
did not cover. Convicting it of exclusivity would be D-172's amendment repeating itself, where a
docstring was convicted of a nominal-only claim and then shipped unchanged. A wrong back-edge is
worse than a missing one, because "check the index row before trusting a record you jumped to" is
this archive's navigation contract. The marker is removed and the relationship is an **extension**:
D-174 runs the null D-173 conceded and sweeps a surface D-173 did not. The heading's "true and
incomplete" already said so; the marker did not. (The commit message for the parent commit says
"'only' was wrong" — that is over-strong for the same reason and is superseded here.)

**(c) The benchmark file's own headroom claim is now held open by a band edge, and it was left
saying otherwise.** `test_validation_danilewicz_so2_o2.py` states the cascade sits inside Miao's
band "with ~3.4% headroom". §3 measured a draw at this record's new high edge taking it to 1.0655
— outside — and the file was left asserting the clean version. That is D-170's "verified at a
point, sampled over a band" shape, and this commit is its cause. Repaired in the file: a paragraph
naming `k_o2_depletion_total`'s high as what spends that headroom, both sets' figures, and the
scope (edge draws, not shipped results — every test there runs at the nominal).

**(d) Run labels, for the matched pair in §5.** "1532 passed at 1.0e-3" is HEAD before this beat
(`df9b119`, D-173's own figure); "1532 passed at 2.0e-3" was taken today on the edited tree before
any test was written. Same tree, one YAML edit apart — a legitimate pair, but the rows are from
two different runs and `feedback-a-majority-is-not-a-direction` asks that they say so.

## D-175 — "Banded so it never monopolizes the O2" was computed with both rate constants at their nominals and only the pool varied, and over the two bands the sampler can actually reach the oak sink takes 4.58 % to 88.40 % of the aging-phase budget — so the banding named as the reason it could not monopolize is what makes it possible

**Corrects:** D-78 — its "banded to take roughly a third-to-half of the O2 ... banded so protection is PARTIAL" is the nominal arm, not what the banding produces.
**Flags:** D-137 — `k_so2_oxidation`'s note quotes "~2.9e-3 /h against a typical red" as the always-on denominator; measured here, that is a **t=0** value and the five-year window median is ~4.3e-4 /h. Identified, not repaired: it is another parameter's note and deciding what it should say needs its own measurement.

Owner's direction was **the ellagitannin joint**, picked from four unblocked options.

### 1. The claim, and the four places it lived

`oak.yaml`'s `k_ellagitannin_oxidation` note: "at a 50-100 mg/L ellagitannin charge the
pseudo-first-order O2 rate k*[ellag] ~ 2.5e-4-5e-4 /h is ~0.5-1x the always-on total, so
ellagitannin takes roughly a third-to-half of the O2 — a MAJOR, VISIBLE, but PARTIAL protection
**(banded so it never monopolizes the O2)**." Restated in the same file's oak-axis comment block,
in the D-78 spine comment, in `EllagitanninOxidation`'s docstring, and in `provenance.notes`.

D-174 flagged this note for naming the two parameters D-172 retired, and restated the ratio
"across the total's band" as `0.125-2.08x`. **That restatement is not corrected here and no
`Corrects: D-174` marker ships**: it scopes itself to the total's band in its own words, so
convicting it of claiming the joint would be D-174's own amendment (b) repeating itself, where a
parenthetical was convicted of a claim it did not make. The relationship is an **extension**.

### 2. The static pass, pre-registered before any integration ran

`feedback-pre-register-the-cheap-prediction`, written to `PREREGISTERED.md` first.
`R = k_ellag * (oak_gpl * yield) / k_total`, share of a fixed budget `R/(1+R)`, at `T_ref` where
both Arrhenius factors are 1.

**The nominal reproduces the note's own arithmetic to the digit**: over the pool span the note
itself names (0.05-0.10 g/L) with both rate constants at nominal, R = 0.500-1.000 and the share is
33.3-50.0 % — its "~0.5-1x" and "roughly a third-to-half". So the reading of the note is a
**positive control**, not an interpretation, and what follows changes its scope rather than its sum.

### 3. The correction that landed mid-campaign: two bands, not three

The pre-registration treated the ratio as a joint over three sampled bands.
`oak_yield_ellagitannin_light` is **drawn but unreachable** — `add_oak` bakes
`oak_gpl * yield * fill_scale` into the event at compile time — and **D-159 already pins exactly
this** (`test_forcing_an_oak_yield_band_into_the_sample_cannot_move_the_run`, on the vanillin
sibling). The first run reproduced that pinned fact as a harness bug: all three arms ran at the
same 0.1000 g/L ceiling. So the ratio rides on **two reachable bands and one unbanded scenario
input**, and the ensemble surface and the scenario surface must be reported apart — reporting them
together would be the D-162 muddle.

### 4. Measured: per-Process O2 draws off the shipped `ProcessSet`

Five-year `synthetic_supremecorq` bottle, `add_oak(4.0, "light")` at `begin_aging`, aging-phase
window only, `p.derivatives(...)` at 4000 `t_eval` points trapezoid-integrated — **not** a
re-derived rate law (D-145). DIRECT set, `T_ref`.

| surface | low corner | nominal | high corner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ensemble** (two bands, dose 4 g/L) | **4.58 %** | **48.62 %** | **88.40 %** |
| scenario dose (1.28 / 11.2 g/L) | 1.51 % | — | 95.53 % |
| red wine (tannin 2.0 + anthocyanin 0.3) | 3.88 % | 41.13 % | 80.38 % (84.23 % at `k_browning_phenolic` low) |
| + 60 mg/L SO2 | — | 33.72 % | 60.37 % |

The static pass predicted every arm within **1.6 percentage points**, always slightly high, and the
reason is the pre-registered P5: the pool sits at **96-99.8 %** of its ceiling, so the
ceiling-based R is a tight upper bound. That survives stress — tripling the burn to
`y_ellag_per_o2 = 6.0` pulls the pool to 89 % of its ceiling and moves the share **0.8 points**.

**Scorecard: P2 hit (0.4862), P4 hit (0.0458), P5 hit, P3 MISS.** P3 predicted > 0.90 at the high
corner and surface 1 gave 0.8840. **The miss is the pre-registration's own defect**: the threshold
was written for the three-band corner of §3, whose third band cannot reach a run. Had D-159 been
applied before the threshold was written it would have read "> 0.85". Recorded rather than
rewritten — a pre-registration whose threshold moves after the run is worth nothing.

### 5. The three scopes the old text did not carry, and a prediction that missed by 2x

* **RED WINE — the phenolic boost does not rescue the claim, and the reason is a second instance of
  this record's own defect class.** The objection was that every arm ran a phenolic-free wine, the
  medium nobody oaks: on a red, D-132's boost lifts the denominator ~6x, R drops to ~0.7 and the
  share should land at **~41 %**, i.e. "never monopolizes" would hold. Measured at the same corner:
  **80.38 %**. The ~41 % is the red **nominal**, and the static formula over-predicts the corner's
  denominator ~7x because the grape phenolic pools **deplete ~95 % across five years** (tannin +
  anthocyanin 2.3 -> 0.1226 g/L window median -> 0.0623 at the end, anthocyanin to exactly 0,
  drawn by the D-79/D-84/D-85 condensation sinks). So `k_browning_eff` runs at **4.35e-4 /h**
  against the **2.83e-3 /h** its t=0 value implies — and the "~2.9e-3 against a typical red" that
  `k_so2_oxidation`'s note quotes is a **t=0 statistic used as though it described the window**.
  That is the flagged item above: the same verified-at-a-point shape, on the sibling note that was
  held up as the model of good practice.
* **CASCADE — no referent, structurally.** The sets are **replacements** (D-141), so under
  `oxidative="cascade"` the `ellagitannin_oxidation` Process is **absent**, not re-wired:
  `quinone_ellagitannin_oxidation` reads the same constant against `quinone`
  (`r_q = k*f(T)*quinone*ellag`) and touches no `o2` at all, leaving `oxygen_activation` the sole
  non-ingress `o2` Process. "A share of the O2" means nothing there. The first draft of this
  record's prose said the Process "does not touch o2 in the cascade set", which is true and misses
  that it is not in the set at all; the guard is written on the **membership**, not the touches.
* **OFF-`T_ref` — three independent `E_a` entries.** `E_a_ellagitannin_oxidation`, `E_a_browning`
  and `E_a_ethanol_oxidation` share the band `[30000, 70000]` as **three entries**, drawn
  independently — the D-172-amendment shape one level up. At 5 C, same k corner: **94.63 %** at the
  max-R `E_a` corner and **75.64 %** at the min-R corner, against 88.09 % at nominal `E_a`. Any
  span the note prints is a `T_ref` span and now says so.

**Supply limitation is why shares and not rates are the readout.** Every arm consumes ~4.4e-2 g/L
against a fixed 4.514e-2 g/L closure ingress. Raising `k_browning_eff` 6x does not multiply
browning's draw 6x — it takes a larger share of the **same** budget (D-136).

### 6. Zero edges moved, and what did not license anything

`k_ellagitannin_oxidation`'s source is `author estimate`, which cannot license a narrowing (D-171,
refused seven times). The band is untouched, the value is untouched, and the deliverable is a
restatement plus a guard. The measurement is **not** an argument for a different edge: it says what
the shipped edges imply, which is what the note was for.

### 7. The guard, the licence for it, and the arms

**The pre-existing suite does not notice this edge.** Full run with `k_ellagitannin_oxidation`'s
high halved 2.0e-2 -> 1.0e-2 and the new file ignored: **1534 passed** — D-163's finding landing
again, and the D-155/D-156 licence for what follows.

`tests/test_ellagitannin_o2_share.py`, three tests. The corner shares are **recomputed** from the

— but the cheap static bound is asserted to bracket them in the supply-limited direction.

| **A0** unchanged (designed-GREEN control) | — | GREEN | GREEN |
| **A1** high 2.0e-2 -> 1.0e-2, note silent | `oak.yaml` | **RED** — `..._recomputed_from_the_shipped_edges` | GREEN |
| **A2** withdrawn claim restored, edges silent | `oak.yaml` | **RED** — `..._monopolize_claim_has_not_returned` | GREEN |

### 8. Bookkeeping — D-174's `Flags: D-172` is discharged

All seven sites naming the retired `k_ethanol_oxidation` / `k_browning_base` pair now name
