## D-184 — The structure map went 127 archive-commits stale, and the convention meant to prevent that is the one that had already failed

**Trigger.** The owner asked whether the memory and docs principles need updating as the project
grows — "keep track of structure and changes, without blowing too much initial token usage." The
question named two things. Measurement found the project tracks *changes* exhaustively and
*structure* barely at all, and that the token worry was aimed at the wrong file.

### 1. What was measured, before proposing anything

* **Session-boot cost is fine and was not the problem.** The surfaces actually loaded every session
  are the two `CLAUDE.md` files and `MEMORY.md`: **26.7 KB ≈ 6.7k tokens**. The 41 KB
  `project-fermentation-sandbox.md` is **not** auto-loaded — its index row *instructs* a read, which
  is a conditional cost, not a boot cost. An earlier draft of this analysis put boot at 17-19k
  tokens by counting it, and that error would have aimed every proposal at the wrong file. The
  advisor caught it by checking what the session reminder actually contains.
* **`ARCHITECTURE.md` last changed 2026-07-25. `DECISIONS.md` took 127 commits after that date.**
  Probing it for things the project memory calls current: **zero** hits for `ACID_STATE`, `quinone`,
  `oxidative`; **one** for "aging", a module holding **24** Processes. Eleven of 22 kinetics modules
  and ten of 19 parameter files were missing from the package map.
* **The plan docs are worse, and are a known live hazard.** `milestone-3-plan.md`'s header log stops
  at **D-118** (D-146 elsewhere) with the project at D-183, still carries an "Active beat: the
  sensory / OAV readout layer" heading for a beat closed at D-95/D-98, and its "Deferred / later
  beats" list keeps offering shipped work. `feedback-verify-latest-state-not-breadcrumbs` already
  records **two** re-proposals sourced from exactly that list.

### 2. The decision

**`ARCHITECTURE.md` is rewritten from measurement and re-scoped to structure alone** — where things
live, what may import what. Why anything is shaped this way stays here, in the archive, which is
what the old document had drifted into duplicating (and duplication is why it rotted: two copies of
a rationale, one of them unmaintained).

Its numbers are **derived, and the file says so**, with a snippet at its foot that re-derives every
one. That snippet was **run before shipping**, which caught a real defect: the first draft ended in
`| paste -sd+ | bc`, and `bc` is not installed on this box. A self-check that does not execute is
worse than none — it reads as verification. Today's derived figures: wine **94** slots / **62**
Processes + 4 modifiers, beer **57** slots / **27** + 3, both moving with
`get_medium(..., oxidative=)`; **79** kinetics implementations; **19** parameter files; **72** test
files.

**The `docs/plans/milestone-*.md` maintenance rule is RETIRED, not re-affirmed.** "Keep the plans
updated as work progresses" was honoured for a while and then silently stopped — and a
half-maintained plan is strictly worse than a frozen one, because its unstruck items read as open
work. All seven plan documents are bannered as frozen historical logs; the milestone-3 banner names
its own log's stopping point and flags the deferred-beats list as the known trap by name.

`CLAUDE.md` now carries the replacement: update `ARCHITECTURE.md` **in the same commit** as any
change to the layer/package layout, the Process registry, the state vector, or the parameter-file
set.

### 3. Bannered in place, not moved to `done/`

The obvious tidy — move the finished plans into `docs/plans/done/` — was **measured and refused**.
Five references to those paths live in this archive, which is append-only, so the move would strand
pointers that cannot be rewritten, plus five more in source docstrings. Banners fix the actual
failure mode (a stale header read as live) at none of that cost. The folder looking tidy was never
the problem; the folder *lying* was.

### 4. The transferable lesson: a doc rots where it duplicates, and suspect the rule before the discipline

Both failures here have one shape. `ARCHITECTURE.md` rotted **in exactly the sections that restated
the archive**; its structural sections (layering, `Process`/`RateModifier`, tiers, units) were still
accurate after four months, because nothing else claimed to own them. The plan docs rotted
**entirely**, because they duplicated the archive by construction.

So the diagnostic is not "is this doc old" but **"does anything else own what it says?"** A document
that is the sole owner of its content stays true for free; one that restates another's decays at the
rate the other advances. And when a doc goes stale, **suspect the maintenance rule before the
discipline** — here the rule was followed, then abandoned, and re-affirming it would have bought
another cycle of the same decay. The fix was to delete the rule and move the obligation to a
surface that owns its content.

### 5. Open, and deliberately not closed here

- **The project memory grew 34 % the day its cap came off, and this is NOT yet acted on.** It sat at
  exactly **300 lines on 8 of 9 commits** on 2026-08-10 — the round-number signature D-169 used to
  diagnose 250. D-177 removed the total cap on 2026-08-11. Same day: 303 → 317 → 335 → 353 → 368 →
  388 → **402**. D-177's argument was that a *reported* number cannot become a target, and that
  still holds — nothing here shows it became one. What it does show is that the argument never
  claimed accumulation would slow, and it did not. D-177 pre-committed to wanting exactly this
  evidence before anyone raises a cap a fifth time; **the owner's call is to hold a week and gather
  more before designing anything**, so no mechanism is proposed here. One day is a point, not a
  trend.
- **`MEMORY.md`'s 320-character row cap is being written to** — longest row exactly **320** on each
  of the last **9** commits, having been 314 for four before that. Before the cap arrived (2026-08-09)
  rows ran to **963** characters, so the cap did real work once. Nine commits is not D-169's
  thirteen, and the cap is two days old. Recorded now so the pre-registration is on the record:
  **when it bites, the answer is not to raise it.**
- **`MEMORY.md`'s index grows one permanent row per lesson** — 6 rows on 2026-07-08, 45 on
  2026-08-11 — and the 45 notes fall into roughly ten recurring families, of which one ("what I
  measured was narrower than what I claimed") holds about 17. Grouping the index by family was
  offered as a **presentation-only** change — no note merged, no slug lost, since merging would
  collide with the standing "never evict an old prohibition" rule — and was not taken up this
  session.

## D-185 — The status memory's growth is in the SETTLED tail, that tail is incompressible, and the affordable fix was granularity rather than eviction

**Trigger.** D-184 §5 left the project memory's post-cap growth as an open item with a stated
plan: wait a week, because one day is a point and not a trend. The owner asked instead to "attack
the main problem." Thirteen commits of evidence had landed by then, so the hold's own condition
was already discharged; this record is what that evidence turned out to say.

### 1. The history, which is the find

`.claude/memory/project-fermentation-sandbox.md` across its 64 commits, counting *entries* (the
hook's own `block_spans`) and the age of the D-record each cites, relative to the newest in the
file at that commit:

| date | lines | entries | newest | entries citing the **last 5 beats** | entries citing **40+ back** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06-23 | 303 | 12 | D-19 | 6 | 0 |
| 2026-07-08 | 550 | 38 | D-59 | 17 | 1 |
| 2026-07-22 | 178 | 19 | D-133 | 6 | 2 |
| 2026-07-28 | 236 | 57 | D-156 | 11 | 12 |
| 2026-08-09 | 250 | 52 | D-165 | 9 | 10 |
| 2026-08-10 | 300 | 64 | D-172 | 16 | 13 |
| 2026-08-11 | 353 | 74 | D-180 | 17 | 18 |
| 2026-08-12 | 406 | 83 | D-184 | 15 | **22** |

**The live frontier is self-limiting.** Entries about the newest five beats have sat between 6
and 17 for two months, through a 3× change in file size. Each beat adds two or three and older
ones stop being recent. Nothing needs to be done to that end.

**The settled tail only grows**: 0 → 1 → 2 → 12 → 13 → 18 → **22**, never down. That is the whole
accumulation, and it is the finished work, not the live work.

**A story that did not survive checking.** The draft of this record said the removed whole-file cap
had been quietly forcing tail retirement, and that D-177 broke an equilibrium. Both halves fail on
the same table. The 550 → 178 line cut in late July is a **distillation event inside the window**,
so the flat 52-58 stretch after it is refill, not a cap-maintained steady state; and entries climbed
**54 → 58 → 61 → 64 straight through** totals pinned at exactly 250 and then exactly 300, which is
the cap being *written to*, exactly as D-169 and D-177 measured. Nothing shipped was wrong. The
accurate statement is narrower: D-177 removed the only pressure of any kind and **nothing replaced
it** — a gap, not an error.

### 2. A prediction that failed, and why it is recorded

Reading the file, `D-128, D-129, D-130 … D-136` appears as nine records on one line, and the
recent beats are visibly verbose. The obvious inference — old entries collapse on their own as they
settle — was **pre-registered and then measured, and it is false.** Mean entry size by age:

| age | 0-5 beats | 6-15 | 16-40 | 41+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean lines | 4.4 | 4.0 | 4.0 | 3.0 |

Essentially flat, and several **8-line entries reach 13-20 beats back**. That one collapsed bullet
was a sample of one, generalised from. What *does* vary is entries per beat — about 3 for recent
beats against 0.15 for old ones — so old material was compressed by **dropping entries**, which is
what the standing "never evict an old prohibition" rule forbids and what the history above shows
happened anyway, in one large event rather than continuously.

### 3. The design that was built on paper and REJECTED

The measurement points at an obvious fix: a budget on the tail, forcing retirement where retirement
is safe. It has the properties every previously-rejected candidate lacked — it can fire (22 today),
it has no round number for the *file* to be written up to, and the pressure never lands on live
work, which was D-169's actual complaint.

It was rejected on **reading the population it would act on**. The 22 entries at 40+ beats back are:
beer `Y_byproduct_sugar`=0 is load-bearing; self-exhaustion is Ferreira's protocol not the sink;
direction is the owner's call; the O2 gate is Fe(II)+O2 with SO2 **inverted in role**; do not rebuild
bottle reduction as thioacetate precursors; the blocker moved, it did not lift. **Every one reads
live.** Age does not measure settledness — and by survivorship the oldest guardrails are the ones
that have already earned their place. A budget there would demand deleting precisely the wrong
entries, and because the population cannot shrink it would fire forever, which the hook's own
docstring rejects in another form ("a guard that forbids nothing is worse than none").

**The tail is incompressible. It is expected to keep growing, and that is correct behaviour.**

### 4. The decision

The file's real defect is not its size but that it is **monolithic in a system that is otherwise
granular**. The 46 lesson notes work: one file each, a one-line description, pulled in on relevance.
The status file never adopted that — 18 subjects on one 406-line page, all 18 read to learn one.

Per-subject prohibitions move to **`.claude/memory/prohibitions/`**, six files, reached **by path
from a ledger** in the core file. The ledger keeps the guarantee: one line per subject naming what
is settled, so *not* opening a file still stops a re-proposal; the file only says why.

The load-bearing detail is that these files get **no `MEMORY.md` row**. An index row is the one
thing that would have made them cost boot tokens, and boot cost was the owner's stated worry. The
arithmetic was run **before** the design was proposed: boot is `8,234 + 8,831 + 10,748 = 27,813 B
≈ 6,950 tokens`, and index rows average 226 chars, so six new rows would be **+4.9 %** and eighteen
**+14.6 %**. Pointing by path is **+0 %**. Core: **406 → 119 lines**; the six files hold 401.

**Nothing was evicted.** The move was performed by script and verified against `HEAD`: of 380
non-blank original lines, exactly **three** are absent afterwards, all three deliberate — the caps
sentence reworded, `D-184` → `D-185`, and the old section heading replaced by the ledger.

**The ledger introduces a failure mode the 406-line version did not have, so it was checked
separately.** A subject whose former heading contributes *no* clause is invisible unless someone
opens its file — worse than being buried in a long page, because the long page at least contained
the words. Screening the 18 former headings against the ledger for a distinctive token each found
**three genuine gaps**: sulfides, closures and fusels/2-PE were named in a list but carried no
prohibition. Fixed by naming them — do not rebuild bottle reduction as thioacetate precursors,
release is temperature-flat, technical cork ships below screwcap, never put 0.963 in a sampled
field — plus the Q10 sweep's non-idempotence, which had the same gap. All ten distinct subjects now
carry at least one clause; **a merged subject file must never leave a former heading wordless.**

The hook (`.claude/hooks/check_memory_size.py`) now gives the detail files **the same
`BLOCK_LINE_CAP`** and reports them **apart from** the three boot surfaces. Same cap because an
uncapped destination beside a capped source is an arbitrage, not a relief valve — the same failure
the column-0 paragraph clause already closes one level in; it is inert on arrival by construction,
since every moved line was already under cap, and binds on what is written next. Reported apart
because folding 401 non-loaded lines into the boot totals would misreport the exact number the
design was chosen to hold flat. Three tests pin all of it.

### 5. Transferable lesson

**When a surface grows, measure which end of it is growing before designing anything.** Here the
two ends behaved oppositely — one self-limiting for two months, the other monotone — and every
whole-file mechanism tried across D-169, D-177 and this record was aimed at their sum, which is why
four of them failed in four different ways. The follow-on is that **age is not a proxy for
finishedness**: the oldest entries survived *because* they keep binding, so any "retire the old
stuff" rule deletes by exactly the wrong key. When a population turns out to be incompressible, the
remaining lever is not eviction but **granularity** — stop loading all of it to use one part.

### 6. What this does NOT do, named so it is not conceded and then treated as covered

It does **not** bound how many records there are; nothing does, and after §3 nothing should. Growth
now lands in a subject file that is read only when that subject is worked on, so the cost is
conditional rather than resident — the rate is unchanged. `MEMORY.md` row **count** stays an open
channel (47 rows, +1 per lesson, 10.7 KB = 38 % of boot); grouping it by family was offered at D-184
and is still not taken up, and it would save zero bytes since the cost there is recall precision,
not scan-ability. The hook still cannot see growth **rate**, so a split that quietly re-inlines
would not fire — only the ledger's "never inline a subject back into this file" forbids it, and that
is prose.

## D-186 — The pH a beverage AGES at becomes an input: `initial_ph` anchors t=0 and the ferment then moves it 0.05–0.10, so a 0.35-unit pH span was arriving at the aging boundary as 0.3045 — closed by a cation-MOVING verb, which is a real cellar operation in both directions rather than a pH dial

**Corrects:** D-150 — its finding 1 ("`initial_ph` anchors t = 0, not the aging pH, and there is no way to set one") recorded a limitation that this record removes; the sentence is now false and the correction map is the only place a reader jumping to D-150 will learn that.

**Trigger.** Nothing was mid-flight after D-185, so the next beat was the owner's call (D-66).
Four unblocked candidates were offered and this one was picked: it needs no external source, it
had been carried as open in roughly eight consecutive records' closing lists, and it gates the
pH-dependent aging work several *blocked* items would want anyway.

Two candidates were dropped during the check that preceded the offer, and both are worth
recording because the reason generalises. The `add_copper`/`copper`-slot disconnect is **not**
merely unsourced — D-149 refused the fix deliberately, on the D-148 precedent for a defect whose
fix would be a guess, so offering it as "unblocked" would have misdescribed a decision as an
absence. And the open-items boilerplate copied forward across ~15 records still names the
withdrawn SO₂ under-binding (D-143) and points at "the natural next oxidative beat" that the very
next record **refused** (D-150's pH term on activation). **The ledger is the authority; the
copy-forward tail is not**, which is exactly the trap the correction map exists for.

### 1. The gap, re-measured rather than quoted — and the numbers have moved since D-150

`initial_ph` back-solves the strong cation with `Byp` = 0 at pitch (D-18). Byproducts then
accumulate against a frozen cation and pull pH down, so the pH the *aging* segment runs at is
never the one the scenario named. Re-taken on today's code, wine, 6 g/L tartaric + 3 g/L malic,
20 d ferment then a 20 d tail, pH sampled just past the breakpoint:

| `initial_ph` | pH at t=0 | pH where aging starts | drift |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.26 | 3.2600 | **3.2075** | −0.0525 |
| 3.61 | 3.6100 | **3.5120** | −0.0980 |

**A 0.3500 span asked for arrives as 0.3045 — 87.0 % of it** — and the shortfall is not a constant
offset that a ratio would divide out: the two arms drift by *different* amounts, 0.0525 against
0.0980, because the arm that starts higher has more dissociated acid to lose.

D-150 measured the same pair at 3.2084 / 3.5135, span 0.3052. Today's 3.2075 / 3.5120, span
0.3045. **The numbers moved because the charge balance grew a dissolved-CO₂ term at D-182**, and
that is the whole argument for re-measuring rather than quoting: a figure copied from a record
written before a mechanism landed is a figure about a model that no longer exists.

### 2. What was built, and why it is a cation-moving verb rather than a pH setter

`set_ph` writes the `cation_charge` slot at a scheduled day so the state sits at the named pH from
that moment. **D-65 deferred exactly this** — "potassium bitartrate / K-tartrate additions
(deacidification via a counter-cation — a different, cation-moving verb)" — as v1 scope, not as a
refusal, so this is deferred work built rather than a new axis.

The name invites the objection that wine has no pH dial, and the answer is that **both directions
are real operations on the same quantity**:

- **raising pH** = deacidification with potassium/calcium carbonate — base in, strong cation up;
- **lowering pH** = cation-exchange resin, which strips K⁺ and acidifies without adding anything.

Lowering pH by *addition* is a different operation and already had a verb (`add_acid`, D-65, which
doses tartaric/malic/lactic onto their own slots and leaves the cation alone). So the model change
— move the cation, touch nothing else — corresponds to a real treatment in either direction. The
measured moves are −5.67e−3 mol/L to reach 3.26 and +1.18e−2 mol/L to reach 3.61, from a wine whose
own pH at that instant was 3.3763.

**The chemistry is a new core function, not a scenario-layer trick.** `acidbase.cation_charge_for_ph`
is the exact inverse of `ph_of_state`, term for term: same acid registry (per-medium, D-179), same
`Byp`-as-succinic pool, same `min(evolved, C_sat(T))` dissolved-CO₂ term (D-182). It exists as a
*state*-level function because the pre-existing `solve_cation_charge` anchors from **scenario
inputs**, where `Byp` and dissolved CO₂ are structurally 0 because nothing has fermented — the two
assumptions that cannot survive being applied part-way through a run. On the measured state they
are 2.8653 g/L and 3.96e−2 mol/L; neither is negligible.

### 3. The one check that cannot happen at compile, and where it surfaces instead

Every other verb validates entirely at compile. The reachable pH range is a property of the
**state** at the moment of the adjustment, so "is this target reachable" cannot be answered until
the event fires. The split shipped: param keys, the (0, 14) bracket, the `cation_charge` slot, and
the presence of the pKa and CO₂-solubility parameters are all compile-time (the `begin_aging`
discipline); the reachability check lives in the mutation.

That is tolerable rather than merely conceded, because `simulate_scheduled` applies mutations
**between segments** — so the error comes out of the event application carrying the verb's label,
with no partial state committed, rather than as a traceback from inside the solver's RHS. It names
the floor, which is `ph_of_state` on the same state with the cation zeroed and is computable
without risk because `solve_ph` is total (D-46). Measured floor on the probe wine: **2.1869**.

### 4. The opt-in gate, whose justification is NOT the same in both media

`set_ph` requires the scenario to have given `initial_ph`, enforced at compile in
`_compile_interventions` (a verb receives only its own `Intervention`, the schema and the
parameters — never `scenario.initial`). **The reason differs per medium and neither reason covers
for the other**, so both are written down:

- **Beer** — structural. Without `initial_ph` every acid slot is 0 (D-179's opt-in), so anchoring
  would write a counter-cation into an *empty* acid load: a charge balance with nothing to counter,
  solving to the top of the bracket. Not a beverage.
- **Wine** — epistemic. The balance is *not* empty: `tartaric`/`malic` are seeded from their own
  scenario keys regardless, and D-182 measured an un-anchored wine at pH 2.92 off `Byp` alone. The
  objection is that re-anchoring a wine whose pH the scenario never supplied would let one
  intervention manufacture the very information D-18's inverse anchoring says must be an input.

### 5. What was verified

- **Round trip, closed form against root-find**, on a fermented state across pH 2.80–4.00: worst
  error **1.75e−11**, four of seven targets exact to the last bit. There is no root-find on the
  cation side, so this is an algebraic identity being checked, not a convergence tolerance.
- **The no-op is a no-op**: asking for the pH the state already has returns the cation already
  there to **1.24e−15** relative. This is the test a one-sided inverse fails — one that silently
  dropped the carbonic term the forward solver reads would still pass every "pH moved the right
  way" assertion.
- **The headline, both arms**: `set_ph` 3.26 and 3.61 arrive at 3.260000 and 3.610000 (errors
  1.7e−9 / 1.4e−9) and the span is **0.350000, 100.0000 % of what was asked** — against the 87.0 %
  the `initial_ph` route delivers. The failing route is measured in the same test as the working
  one, so the comparison is of two mechanisms and not of two protocols.
- **Ledger**: the jump books an external flow like every mutation, and that flow's carbon and
  nitrogen are exactly 0 — `cation_charge` carries weight 0 in `total_carbon` and is absent from
  `total_nitrogen`, being charge rather than matter. The zero is checked *beside* an assertion that
  the cation actually moved, so it cannot pass vacuously. No other slot is touched.
- **No tier moves**: the tier map is identical to the same run without the verb. pH's tier is
  already the PLAUSIBLE-floored pKa tier (D-18) and this writes state, not a parameter.
- **Beer path exercised, not assumed** — the verb reads the medium's own registry, and a beer
  aged at 4.20 arrives at 4.20.
- **Full suite green: 1612 → 1622**, ten new tests, all in `tests/test_interventions.py` beside the
  other verbs. `ruff` and `mypy` clean.

### 6. Scope, stated rather than conceded

- **Cold stabilisation is not this verb.** KHT precipitation removes potassium *and* tartrate;
  only the cation is booked, so the acid slots are untouched. A scenario wanting the tartrate loss
  must schedule that itself.
- **The `CO2` slot is deliberately not written**, though carbonate deacidification evolves gas.
  That slot is the cumulative *evolved* integral and the balance reads `min(evolved, C_sat(T))`
  (D-182), already saturated many times over by the time anyone ages a wine — so writing it would
  move the dissolved term by exactly nothing. Bookkeeping theatre, refused.
- **Beer's finished pH remains a PREDICTION** (D-180). This acts downstream of that prediction, at
  a day the scenario names; it does not turn beer's outcome back into an input.
- **It does not add a pH *rate* dependence anywhere.** It makes the pH an aging study runs at
  controllable; what reads that pH is unchanged. Checked rather than asserted: over the aging tail
  with 60 mg/L SO₂ dosed at the breakpoint, molecular SO₂ runs **0.0014 mg/L at aging pH 3.26
  against 0.0006 at 3.61** — the right direction and a factor of ~2.3, so the controlled pH does
  reach a pH-dependent readout. **The absolute level is very low in this scenario** (a nearly
  fully bound wine), so that is a direction check and explicitly not a magnitude claim.

### 7. Next

- **D-150's aging-pH item is closed. Do not re-open it from the copy-forward open lists**, which
  name it in about eight records and are the same lists still carrying D-143's withdrawn item.
- The pH under-response itself is **untouched and still open**: real wine's steady oxygen-uptake
  rate rises ~1.62× per pH unit and the model delivers ~1.006× of it (D-150). This beat makes that
  gap *measurable at a stated pH* for the first time; it does not narrow it, and the standing
  refusal of a pH term on the activation node (D-150, two independent legs) is unaffected.
- The one place a pH term was left open rather than refused is the **burst axis**
  (`burst_antioxidant`, D-133/D-147), and its first question is unchanged: whether that pool
  already implicitly carries the between-pH variance, which would double-count.
- Unchanged and still open: the `add_copper`/`copper`-slot disconnect (D-149, refused-pending-a-
  source, **not** merely unsourced), the quinone branching (D-145), closure OTR(T) and the
  bottling-burst auto-dose (D-136), acetaldehyde in maturation, and the missing post-Fenton
  secondary O₂ draw (D-142).

### 8. Transferable lesson

**A "there is no way to do X" note is a claim with a shelf life, and it decays differently from a
refusal.** Both were sitting in the same copy-forward list, in the same sentence shape, and they
needed opposite treatment: D-150's limitation was waiting to be built, while D-149's was a decision
that had already been taken and would have been *overturned* by treating it as a gap. The
distinguishing question is not how old the item is or how often it is repeated — it is **whether
the record says nothing sources it, or says it was refused on that basis**. The first is an
opening; the second is a closing that looks identical from the index.

### D-186 amendment — the ensemble surface, and a guard for it that was DESIGNED, falsified and REJECTED because it could not fire

Found in review immediately after the record above shipped, and appended rather than edited in
place (the D-147/D-181 precedent). Receipts: `ensemble_probe.py`, `falsify.py` under
`M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d186-set-ph\`.

**1. The gap in §5: every test ran the nominal path.** `_verb_set_ph` captures the resolved
parameter map at compile and the mutation solves the cation from it, while under an ensemble each
member re-integrates with its **own drawn pKa set** — 21 pH-system parameters vary across members
(`pKa_tartaric_1/2`, `pKa_malic_1/2`, `pKa_carbonic_1`, `H_co2_beverage`, `vant_hoff_co2_solubility`
and the rest). If the two disagreed, the verb's headline claim would silently fail per member and
nothing shipped would have noticed. This is the archive's recurring point-vs-band shape (D-118,
D-154, D-155, D-157, D-180, D-181) arriving on a new surface.

**2. What it actually does, measured — and it is the PRECEDENT, not a new weakness.**
`simulate_ensemble` holds `y0` **and** `events` fixed across members, so the compile-seam anchor is
nominal-only too. Both were measured on the same 24-member ensemble, wine, `initial_ph` 3.55 with
`set_ph` 3.40 at the aging boundary:

| anchor | where | member spread |
|---|---|---|
| `initial_ph` (D-18, pre-existing) | pH at t=0 | **0.1273** |
| `set_ph` (this record) | pH after the event | **0.1292** |

**Ratio 1.015.** The nominal run is exact for both (t=0 error 8.9e−16, post-event 1.6e−9). So the
new anchor is the same class as the one it extends, which is what the sampling prohibition already
predicts — a compile-time value is in no Process's `reads` and is therefore never drawn. The scope
line now sits in the verb docstring, including the instruction **not to "fix" this one anchor
alone**: the two would then disagree about what a member's pH means and the state-level one would
be the odd anchor out.

**3. The guard that was built on paper and REJECTED on falsification.** The obvious pin for §2 is
the ratio itself — "`set_ph`'s off-nominal spread may not exceed `initial_ph`'s by more than 30 %"
— guarding the real hazard, which is a future verb solving from a **different** parameter map than
the run integrates against. It was sized (0.962 at 6 members, 0.988 at 8, 1.015 at 24) and then
falsified before shipping, by planting exactly that defect: the anchor solves from a pKa map shifted
by a constant.

| planted pKa shift | nominal post-event pH | set_ph spread | ratio | verdict at 1.30 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none (shipped) | 3.400000 | 0.1048 | 0.988 | green |
| +0.05 | 3.350988 | 0.1077 | 1.016 | green |
| +0.15 | 3.253431 | 0.1129 | 1.064 | green |
| +0.30 | **3.108756** | 0.1187 | **1.119** | **green** |

**It cannot fire.** A defect that throws the *nominal* anchor 0.29 pH off target moves the ratio by
0.13, nowhere near any threshold that would not also fire on noise. The reason is structural rather
than a bad constant: a constant offset in the anchor's pKa map moves every member by nearly the same
amount, so it lands in the **mean** and barely touches the **spread** — the statistic was measuring
the wrong moment of the distribution. Shipping it would have produced precisely what the memory
hook's own docstring rejects in another form: a guard that forbids nothing and reads as coverage.

**What does detect the planted defect is the nominal error, and that is already pinned** —
`test_the_aging_ph_is_the_one_asked_for_not_the_one_the_ferment_left` asserts the post-event pH to
1e−5 and goes red at every shift in the table. So the correct outcome here was a **measured scope
statement plus no new test**, not a test that would have made the surface look covered.

**4. The transferable half.** Before pinning a spread, check which moment of the distribution the
defect you fear actually moves. A wrong *shared* input shifts the mean and leaves the spread almost
intact, so a spread-ratio guard is blind to exactly the class of bug that motivated it — and blind
in the reassuring direction. The general form: **falsify a guard against the defect it names before
shipping it, and if it stays green, the honest output is the measurement without the guard.**
### D-186 amendment 2 — two overstatements in the record above, both found in review and neither load-bearing

Appended rather than edited in place, per the archive's append-only rule. Both were caught by
re-reading the record against its own receipts — the check §5 describes performing on D-150's
figures, which had not been turned on this record.

**1. "Four of seven targets exact to the last bit" is THREE.** The round-trip errors were
1.75e−11 / 1.19e−11 / 2.80e−13 / 4.44e−16 / 0.00e+00 / 9.46e−14 / 4.44e−16 at pH 2.80 through
4.00. At pH ~3.4 one ulp is ~4.4e−16, so exactly three targets (3.40, 3.60, 4.00) land within one
ulp; 3.80's 9.46e−14 is ~200 ulps — comfortably inside the "worst error 1.75e−11" headline, which
is unaffected, but not "exact". The headline number and every conclusion drawn from it stand; only
the count was wrong. Recorded because this is the archive that refuses D-152's printed "663" in
favour of an exact 662.802522, and a miscounted ulp claim is the same species of error.

**2. "D-65 deferred exactly this" (§2) overstates what D-65 said.** Its deferral names "potassium
bitartrate / K-tartrate **additions**" — the DOSE form, a mass of salt onto the wine. This record
ships the TARGET form: name the pH, back-solve the cation that reaches it. That is the form an
aging study actually needs, because the input a comparison is designed around is the pH itself and
not the grams that get there. So **D-65 anticipated the axis and did not specify the API**, and the
claim that survives an objection is the weaker one. The verb docstring now carries the corrected
version, and so does the memory ledger's subject file.

Neither changes the design, the measurements, or any prohibition. What generalises is small and
familiar: **a record that re-measures someone else's numbers should re-read its own.**

## D-187 — The bottling burst becomes a sourced dose: the closure's own trapped air, which D-136 measured and then left to the author to invent, now arrives from `bottling_burst_<closure>` via a `seal_bottle` verb — and re-reading the second primary found two of D-136's cited numbers swapped between entries

**Corrects:** D-136 — two figures quoted from Oliveira 2013's introduction were transposed between `otr_natural_cork` and `otr_synthetic_nomacorc`, which turned one entry's corroboration into tension and made the other's a wrong quote.

**Owner picked this off a three-way list of unblocked options, and it was the one whose originating
record certified its own data in words**: D-136 §Next says the bottling burst *"could be a sourced
auto-dose ... left out deliberately to keep the D-133 line clean, **not** for lack of data"*. 1622 →
**1693 passed (+71 in `test_closure_ingress.py`, 46 → 71 in that file)**. ruff + mypy clean. No
Process, no state slot, no parameter file added; the aging axis's 31 D-140 pins are untouched and
un-re-derived, because the verb is opt-in and every scenario written before it is bit-identical.
Receipts: `M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d187-bottling-burst\` (both primaries as PDF + extracted
text, `bands.txt`, `values.txt`, `FINDINGS.md`).

### 1. The gap, and why it was the last un-sourced oxygen input on the aging axis

D-136 turned closure oxygen from a dosed stock into a continuous flow, and shipped **only the
steady column** of Lopes et al. 2007's Table I. It said why, and the reasoning was sound: the
first-month rate is 10–150× the steady one, it is a different mechanism (the cork's own compressed
air escaping, not permeation), and a one-off release of a finite charge is what `add_oxygen`
already expresses. So the file drew a line — *"this file is the STEADY permeation, `add_oxygen` is
the bottling burst, and the two do not overlap. An author simulating a freshly bottled wine should
dose BOTH."*

The consequence was that the burst had **no provenance**. Every other quantity on this axis is a
`Parameter` with a source; this one was a number the caller typed. And it is not a small number:
under technical cork the charge is worth **~8.9 years** of that closure's steady ingress, arriving
on day one. A scenario that omitted it was not slightly light on oxygen for a month — it was
missing most of the oxygen its wine would see in a decade.

### 2. What the two primaries actually print, read again rather than remembered

Neither paper was re-fetched from a summary; both were downloaded and read as text (P1 via the
authors' own trade reprint, openly hosted, as at D-136; P2 via the ResearchGate author deposit).

**P1 (Lopes et al. 2007) Table I, first-month column, µL O₂/day:** screwcap `<500` [at moment of
bottling], technical cork 15–40, natural cork 25–45, Nomacorc 30–40, SupremeCorq 35–45.

**P2 (Oliveira et al. 2013) publishes the same first month as an INTEGRAL**, in 593 bottles, three
independent ways: Table 1 caliper means of **0.97 and 1.58 mg/bottle**; a Discussion average of
*"27 to 29% (1.0 mL, or **1.43 mg**)"* of the 4.9–5.2 mg the stopper holds in its own cell lumen;
and a Table 2 all-class month-1 rate of 54.07 µg/day (**1.62 mg** over 30 d).

**The cross-validation is the strongest in this file.** P1's un-subtracted first-month total for
natural cork is 35 µL/day × 30 d = **1.50 mg/bottle**; P2's is **1.43 mg**. Four replicates against
593 bottles, 5% apart, on a quantity neither paper was written to report. The two are commensurable
because both exclude the bottling line: P2 deducts a measured 1.50 mg headspace charge explicitly,
P1 measured fill oxygen at *"less than 9 µg/L"*.

### 3. The arithmetic, and the subtraction that is not a rounding correction

```
burst [µL]  = (P1 first-month rate − THIS FILE'S SHIPPED otr_<closure>) × 30 days
burst [g/L] = burst [µL] × 1.43e-6 g/µL / 0.750 L        (D-136's conversion and 750 mL scope)
```

P1's first-month column is a **total** — the trapped-air release plus the permeation running
underneath it — and `ClosureOxygenIngress` already integrates that permeation. Dosing the column
unmodified would count the steady share twice. That share is **1% for technical cork but 17% for
Nomacorc and 32% for SupremeCorq**, so this is a structural correction, not a tidy-up.

It also has a consequence in the API, and it is the reason for the ordering gate in §4: the
subtraction assumes the steady Process is *switched on* across that first month, which it is not
until `begin_aging`.

**Shipped (g/L, one-off):** hermetic 0.0 · screwcap 9.53e-4 · technical cork 1.56e-3 · SupremeCorq
1.54e-3 · Nomacorc 1.66e-3 · natural cork 1.92e-3.

**Two things the shipped set says that are worth stating explicitly.** First, the four cylindrical
charges land within 1.16–1.44 mg/bottle of each other while the steady rates beside them span ~52×
— but that is **a statement about P1's table, not a measured mechanism**: its first-month ranges
overlap so heavily that they do not separate the closures the way its steady ranges do. The file
says so, and does not claim the near-equality as a finding. Second, **the most permeable closure
has the smallest burst**, because the largest steady rate is subtracted from it — the ordering of
the bursts is not the ordering of the closures, and nothing asserts that it is.

**Screwcap is the one entry that is a bound.** P1 prints `<500` — a ceiling with no floor — so the
entry ships the **ceiling itself**, with `low: 0.0` marked CONSTRUCTED and the note saying in
capitals that it is an upper bound rather than a central estimate. The midpoint of `[0, ceiling]`
was the first draft and was rejected: the source contains one number, and a midpoint invents a
second (the D-102 fabrication shape). It is also the one entry not integrated over 30 days —
footnote [a] pins that cell to the moment of bottling, because a screwcap's charge is headspace air
at sealing, not a compressed stopper decompressing. Read as a rate it would be 15000 µL, ~15× every
other closure's month, and P1's own Figure II contradicts it.

### 4. The verb, and the gate that keeps the subtraction honest

`seal_bottle` is **`add_oxygen`'s dose with the number taken out of the author's hands**. Identical
mutation — one bolus onto `o2`, carbon- and nitrogen-free, no volume change — and a test asserts
that equivalence directly, so the verb cannot quietly grow a second effect. It takes **no params at
all**: a scenario cannot say "seal it with a natural cork but dose 4 mg/L", which would be an
`add_oxygen` wearing a sourced verb's name.

It is the first entry in a second dispatch table, `_SCENARIO_INTERVENTION_VERBS`. Every other verb
is a function of its own `Intervention` alone; this one's *magnitude* comes from `scenario.closure`.
A second table rather than a fourth parameter on all twelve signatures, so the distinction stays
visible rather than becoming a scenario nobody reads.

**Two gates, in `_compile_interventions` because a verb never sees the scenario:** the scenario must
name a `closure` (the dose *is* the closure, and silently dosing zero is the failure `_closure_otr`
already refuses), and the seal must not precede `begin_aging` (§3 — sealing earlier nets off a flux
the run never paid, producing no error and no NaN, just a quietly under-dosed wine).

**A third gate was written and deleted, because it provably could not fire.** It rejected
`seal_bottle` on a medium without the `closure_otr` slot. But `compile_scenario` rejects a `closure`
on such a medium *before* it compiles any intervention (D-136), and a scenario with no closure dies
on the first gate — so no beer scenario can reach it. Deleting it is D-186's lesson applied
prospectively: falsify a guard against the case it names, and if it cannot fire, ship the
interaction as a test instead of the guard. That test now pins both halves.

### 5. The transposition, which only surfaced because a new beat needed the sentence

Re-reading P2's introduction for the burst turned up two numbers D-136 had swapped between entries.
P2's actual text: *"natural cork stoppers reached a mean permeation of **9.33 mg** O₂/stopper/year
... (Godden et al. 2005). ... Synthetic stoppers ... reaching a mean oxygen ingress of **1.60 mg**
O₂ in the first month (Lopes et al. 2005)."* D-136 recorded Godden's natural-cork figure as 1.60
mg/yr and Lopes 2005's synthetic first month as 9.33 mg — each entry got the other's number.

Both live in `notes:` fields, so **no shipped value moves**. What moves is what they support:

- **`otr_natural_cork` loses a corroboration and gains a tension.** D-136 wrote that Godden "runs
  the right way too" at 1.60 mg/yr = 4.4 µg/day, *"HIGHER than the steady 2.5 µg/day because a
  36-month mean still carries the first-month burst"*. At the correct **9.33 mg/yr = 25.6 µg/day**
  that argument fails: burst + steady gives ~2.2 mg over year 1 against Godden's 9.33, so the burst
  cannot absorb the gap. The resolution is **method**, and P1 states it against Godden by name —
  values measured without liquid contact run *"substantially lower than the oxygen transmission
  rates and 1000-fold variation reported by other studies"*, because *"contact with liquid is an
  important factor"*. Godden is excluded on method rather than reconciled on arithmetic, and the
  entry now says so instead of claiming agreement.
- **`otr_synthetic_nomacorc` gains a quantitative cross-check where it had a vague direction.**
  Repaired to 1.60 mg, Lopes 2005's figure for "synthetic stoppers" — a pool of both — falls
  **between** P1's two synthetics (1.50 Nomacorc, 1.72 SupremeCorq), from a different experiment by
  the same group. That is the independent check this beat's synthetic bursts rest on, and it is
  corroboration **repaired into existence**: a reader trusting the old note would have drawn the
  opposite conclusion.

### 6. What was verified

25 new tests, all green, and three of them earn their place by having failed first:

- **The published column, net of steady** — each shipped charge re-derived from P1's printed
  first-month range and this file's shipped OTR, plus the explicit check that
  `burst + steady × 30 d` reproduces P1's total. Both band edges pinned the same way (D-163's
  lesson applied while the band was being written rather than after), with the extra assertion that
  the nominal is the **exact midpoint** — which fails if anyone re-derives an edge against the
  steady *band* instead of its shipped value, mixing two scopes.
- **The second primary must sit inside the band, except where it does not.** P2's 1.43 and 1.58
  mg/bottle fall inside; its **thinner-caliper mean of 0.97 mg falls 3.5% BELOW the low edge**. The
  test pins the near-miss as a bound in both directions rather than averaging it away, and the file
  now records why it is not a disagreement about the same stopper: P2 varied cork-plank caliper,
  which this menu has no axis for.
- **Isolability and inertness** — a hermetic seal is byte-for-byte the run without it, and an
  unsealed scenario compiles to exactly the pre-D-187 event list.
- **The equivalence to `add_oxygen`**, the `no params` refusal, both gates' messages, the deleted
  gate's interaction, and the two-table unknown-verb message.
- **Integrated consequence over five years**: a sealed bottle browns more and holds less SO₂ than
  the same closure unsealed, standing O₂ returns to under 1% of the dose (the charge is spent, not
  stockpiled, so D-136's supply-limited reframe survives a bolus), and carbon still closes.

**Three numbers in prose were wrong in this beat and none of them was a shipped value.** D-136's
transposition is one. The other two were mine, in notes drafted before the tests existed: a "~2.7
years of steady ingress" that is actually **8.9**, and a claim that both of P2's caliper means fall
inside the band when one falls **3.5% outside**. Both were caught within minutes by tests written
against the *published literals* rather than against the shipped value — a test that reads the YAML
it is checking would have agreed with both errors.

### 7. Scope, stated rather than conceded

- **The bolus front-loads the release.** P2 resolves it over time — *"35% of the overall ingress ...
  in the first five days, 59% in the first month, and 78% in the first three months"* — while the
  charge arrives instantaneously at the seal. That is D-136's decision (a decaying pool would
  re-litigate D-133's burst-pool argument), not an unexamined default, and the file says so.
- **The bottling line's own oxygen is deliberately excluded.** P2 measures it at 1.4–1.9 mg per
  375 mL bottle, and it is a property of the LINE, not the closure. Folding a fixed charge into
  every closure would silently dose a line nobody described; it belongs to `add_oxygen`. The one
  exception is the screwcap, where P1 says the charge **is** headspace air.
- **The 750 mL scope and the temperature-flatness are D-136's, unchanged.** A magnum takes the same
  milligrams into twice the wine, and no OTR activation energy is fitted.
- **Under an ensemble these are nominal-only**, like every other parameter in this file: they seed a
  dose at an event rather than being read per RHS step, so `simulate_ensemble` will not propagate
  their bands. Identical in kind to the OTRs (D-136's own ENSEMBLE CAVEAT) and to `set_ph` (D-186).
- **All six entries are `speculative`**, for the OTRs' reason plus one: each is an integral of a
  month-average rate rather than a directly measured charge — natural cork excepted, where P2
  published the integral itself.

### 8. Next

- **OTR(T) remains the blocked half of D-136's Next** and is untouched here: it still needs a source
  reporting one closure at two storage temperatures. Warm-storage predictions stay lower bounds.
- Unchanged and still open: the `add_copper`/`copper`-slot disconnect (D-149, **refused pending a
  source**, not a gap), the quinone branching (D-145, paywalled on two hosts), the missing
  post-Fenton secondary O₂ draw (D-142), acetaldehyde in maturation, and the burst-axis pH question
  (D-150/D-186), whose first step is a measurement of whether `burst_antioxidant` already carries
  the between-pH variance.
- **Closure-driven reduction stays unmodellable** for D-136's reason (it needs D-135's blocked
  de-novo route or an O₂-coupled sulfide term), and **bottle format** is still inexpressible.
- Nothing here re-opens D-136's ordering correction: it is a steady-state claim, and the burst
  ordering runs differently on purpose.

### 9. Transferable lesson

**A `notes:` field is the least-checked storage in the repo, and this beat measured its error rate
at three wrong numbers in one sitting.** A shipped `value` is pinned by a test, re-derived when a
band moves, and re-read whenever a Process changes. The prose around it is pinned by nothing — it
is written once, at the moment of most enthusiasm, and then quoted forward as if it had been
checked. D-136's transposition survived 51 records not because anyone doubted it and lost, but
because **nothing ever reads a note until a later beat needs exactly that sentence** — and when one
finally did, the number it needed was the one that had been swapped.

The practical form: when a new beat leans on a citation already in the file, **re-open the source
rather than the note** — the note is a claim of the same species as the one being built, not
evidence for it. And when writing new notes, the number in the prose deserves the same test as the
number in the field: two of the three errors here were caught only because the tests were written
against the *published* literals, which is the one construction that can disagree with the file it
is checking.

### D-187 amendment — the record's own test counts were wrong in four places, which is the record's own lesson landing on the record

Found in review immediately after D-187 shipped, and appended rather than edited in place (the
D-147/D-181/D-186 precedent). The suite is **green at 1656**, and every count in §opening and §6
above was wrong, in the same direction and for the same reason the lesson describes: they were
prose, written from memory between two runs, and nothing pinned them.

**What was claimed, and what is measured.** The baseline was re-derived from a worktree at the
parent commit (`pytest --collect-only`), not remembered:

| claim | shipped as | measured |
| --- | --- | --- |
| suite before → after | 1622 → **1693** | 1622 → **1656** |
| delta | +71 | **+34** |
| `test_closure_ingress.py` | 46 → 71 | **37 → 71** |
| "25 new tests" (§6) | 25 | **18 test functions**, 34 collected |

The 1693 came from adding the file's *new* count to the suite's *old* total; the "46" was read off
a `-x` run that had stopped early, so it was the new file's count minus the failures, not the old
file's. The "25" counted test functions and then called them tests, where four are parametrized
(4 + 4 + 6 + 6 = 20 collected from 4 functions). **`Suite **1693**` was also wrong in the memory
status line and is corrected there.**

None of it is load-bearing — no shipped value, band, gate or test depends on a count — which is
exactly why nobody would have caught it later. It belongs in the record because the lesson in §9 is
that *a number in prose is unpinned by construction*, and the record making that argument shipped
four unpinned numbers of its own within an hour of writing it. The generalisation is not "be more
careful": it is that **a count is only trustworthy if the message that reports it also produced
it**, and every number above now comes from a command whose output is in the receipts directory.

**One further check, which came out the other way.** The full run *did* find a genuine interaction
this record's §6 did not anticipate: `test_switch_site_census.py` pins the set of wine parameters
whose nominal sits on a band edge, and `bottling_burst_screwcap` joins it — because the entry ships
P1's `<500 µL` ceiling as its value on purpose (§3). It is added to the pinned set with the reason,
not worked around. That is a test outside this beat's domain suite catching a new registry entry,
which is the standing hazard for exactly this kind of addition, and it fired as designed.

**And one claim in a test comment was upgraded from inference to measurement.** The five-year
comparison ends with the sealed arm holding **13.7 %** more standing O₂ than the unsealed one, and
the first draft of that comment *asserted* the cause — the sealed arm spends more SO₂, and SO₂ is
itself an O₂ sink — after inferring it from the sign of a failed assertion. That is the shape of
D-101's wrong mechanism. It is now measured: re-running the **unsealed** arm at a reduced SO₂ dose
lands on the sealed arm's surviving SO₂ *and* on its standing O₂ at the **same** dose, ~54.5 mg/L
(at 55 mg/L the two ratios are 1.016 and 0.979; at 53 mg/L, 0.977 and 1.024). Standing O₂ is
therefore a function of surviving SO₂, and the bolus leaves no trace except through it — D-136's
supply-limited reframe holding under a bolus rather than an exception to it. Receipt:
`d187-bottling-burst/mechanism.txt`.


## D-188 — Herzan's SO₂ ladder, measured: the model collapses a three-stage sulfiting design onto the must stage alone and inverts the maturation column's sign — the O₂ competition owns the sign, a missing post-dryness source owns the size, and nothing is built because the only magnitude anchor is the table under test

**Corrects:** D-108 — two of its statements about the maturation regime are no longer true of the code: *"no maturation-phase source to make more"* and the 0.000 unsulfited floor. Closure oxygen (D-136 steady, D-187 burst) gave the model both, and neither beat named D-108, so no ⚠ ever appeared.

**Owner picked this off a three-way list of unblocked options.** The probe that decided the pitch
ran before the list was written: D-108's blocker was *named* as closure O₂ ingress, and that had
been built 51 records earlier, so the question was whether the beat was "build the source" or
"measure what got built". A sealed sulfited bottle now makes acetaldehyde, so it was the second.
Suite **1656 → 1664** (both from `pytest --collect-only -q`, not arithmetic). ruff + mypy clean.
**No Process, no state slot, no parameter, no YAML entry** — one new benchmark file. Receipts:
`M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d188-herzan-ladder\` (`ladder.py`/`diagnose.py`/`probe2.py` and
their captured output).

### 1. The source, re-opened rather than re-read — and it had two rows the archive never carried

Herzan, Prokes, Baron, Kumsta, Pavlousek & Sochor (2020), *"Study of carbonyl compounds in white
wine production"*, Food Sci. Nutr. 8(11):5850–5859, PMC7684598, open access, full text read. Its
Table 1 grades **seven** SO₂ regimes, notated (must / tank / bottling) in mg/L, on total
acetaldehyde at day 182 from grape processing:

| variant | (0/0/0) | (0/0/35) | (0/30/35) | (0/60/0) | (60/0/35) | (60/30/35) | (60/60/0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| published mg/L | 2.7 | 6.5 | 25.9 | 9.6 | 17.2 | 51.6 | 22.6 |

**D-108 carried five of the seven.** The two it dropped — (0/60/0) and (60/60/0) — are the ones
that drive the tank column at double strength with the bottling column switched off, and they are
what turns "the model is low on the tank column" into "the model has the sign wrong". Re-reading
D-108's note would not have found them; that is [[feedback-re-read-the-source-you-already-mined]]
and D-187's lesson, and it paid twice in two beats.

Two further things the paper says that the note did not. The method *"is based on the hydrolysis
of carbonyl compounds bound to SO₂"*, so the published column is **total** acetaldehyde and is
commensurable with the model's slot rather than with `free_acetaldehyde`. And the tank column is
**not a dose**: *"Samples for measurement were taken once every 14 days. After each determination
of SO₂, its volume in the wine was adjusted to the specified value."* A (x/30/y) wine was topped
back to 30 mg/L **free** SO₂ every fortnight for three months.

### 2. "Maintained" is why the harness integrates in segments

A single `add_so2` at the start of the tank phase is a different treatment from the paper's, and
naming it after the paper's would be the error the file exists to catch. `_run` therefore
integrates fortnight by fortnight and **bisects the shipped binding solver** for the dose that
restores free SO₂ to target *in the state the run has actually reached* — how much total SO₂ a
target free level costs depends on the carbonyl load, which is the quantity under test. Measured,
the difference is real but small on this model (the (0/30/35) endpoint moves 0.096 maintained vs
0.149 dosed once), because the model's free SO₂ barely decays here; on a model with the missing
source it would not be small, which is why the harness is built the honest way now.

`simulate_scheduled` is restarted at every top-up. That is safe for a reason worth writing down:
`ScheduledEvent.reconfigure` mutates the `ProcessSet` **in place**, so a `begin_aging` fired in an
earlier segment stays in force across the restarts; each segment is handed only its own events, so
nothing fires twice.

### 3. The result — and the ratio that would have read well

Model, natural cork, no tank oxygen (`ladder-output.txt`, arm A):

| variant | (0/0/0) | (0/0/35) | (0/30/35) | (0/60/0) | (60/0/35) | (60/30/35) | (60/60/0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| published | 2.7 | 6.5 | 25.9 | 9.6 | 17.2 | 51.6 | 22.6 |
| model | 1.013 | 0.303 | 0.096 | 0.089 | 26.256 | 26.507 | 26.604 |

**The three sulfited-must variants agree with each other to 1.3 %** against a published span of
3×. That is the whole finding: *the model's answer to a three-stage design is a function of the
must stage alone.* Within sulfited must it is flat where the paper spans 17.2 → 51.6; within
unsulfited must it **declines 11×** (1.013 → 0.089) where the paper **rises 10×** (2.7 → 25.9).

**The first draft of this record led with "1.53× high on (60/0/35)", and that number is an
artifact.** A model emitting one constant against three published values spanning 3× is
*guaranteed* one respectable ratio; which of the three it lands on says nothing about the model.
This is D-108's own lesson (v) — the measurement that agrees with you is the one to distrust —
recurring in the beat that re-opens D-108, exactly as D-108 recurred inside D-107.

What survives as a quantitative claim is the **absolute** must-column lift on Herzan's two matched
pairs, where only the must dose differs: published +10.7 and +25.7 mg/L, modelled +25.95 and
+26.41. The direction is right and the size is the right order. The near-equality on the second
pair is the same lottery and the test says so in its docstring rather than banking it.

### 4. The attribution — the sign and the size have different owners

Two candidate causes, and the probe that separates them is scaling `k_so2_oxidation`
(`probe2-output.txt`), on the pair that *is* the tank column, (0/0/35) → (0/30/35):

| `k_so2_oxidation` × | 1 | 0.1 | 0.01 | 0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (0/0/35) | 0.3034 | 0.8216 | 0.9907 | 1.0137 |
| (0/30/35) | 0.0964 | 0.5687 | 0.9546 | 1.0236 |
| direction | DOWN | DOWN | DOWN | **UP** |

- **The sign belongs to O₂ competition.** `SulfiteOxidation` and `OxidativeAcetaldehyde` draw on
  the same dissolved-O₂ pool, and after D-136/D-187 that pool *is* the model's only
  post-fermentation acetaldehyde source. Dosing SO₂ during maturation starves it. Remove the
  competition and the published direction appears — so **the D-47 protection mechanism is present
  and working**, which is not obvious from the shipped run and would have been easy to indict.
- **The size belongs to a missing source.** That flip is 1.0137 → 1.0236, **+1.0 %**, against the
  paper's **+298 %**. Even with the competition entirely removed the model has no post-dryness
  acetaldehyde source at all: *both* terms of `AcetaldehydeProduction` — the D-27 base borrow and
  the D-48 SO₂-induced over-production — ride `fermentative_flux_shape`, which `diagnose-output.txt`
  shows is **exactly 0.000e+00 from day 21 onward**, and viable `X` falls 6.83e-1 → 2.13e-4 by the
  end of tank → 3.63e-7 at day 182. Herzan's stated mechanism for the tank column is precisely that
  regime — *"acetaldehyde formation is a way to protect the yeast from the antiseptic effects of
  SO₂"*, *"the highest concentrations of acetaldehyde occur in the presence of free SO₂ and active
  yeast"* — a young wine on lees, which this model does not have.

**A fix aimed at either half alone cannot move this benchmark**, and that is the sentence the
attribution buys. It also disposes of a confound worth naming: this "white wine" seeds **tannin,
anthocyanin and ethyl_bridge all at 0.000000 g/L**, so the D-80 bridging sinks are inert and
"protection has almost nothing left to protect" is a measurement about this scenario rather than a
property of the model. On a red wine those routes are live and the conclusion must be re-derived,
which is asserted rather than left in prose.

### 5. The thing that got better while nobody was aiming at it

D-108 measured the unsulfited floor at **0.000 against Herzan's 2.7** and deliberately did not
patch it: *"inventing a constant to hit 2.7 buys nothing observable."* Nobody ever patched it. The
closure-oxygen axis closed most of it as a side effect, and the floor is now a function of the
closure (`probe2-output.txt`):

| closure | hermetic | screwcap | technical cork | natural cork | Nomacorc | SupremeCorq |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (0/0/0) mg/L | −7.9e-7 | 0.4668 | 0.7043 | 1.0131 | 1.4550 | **2.2591** |

Herzan's 2.7 now sits **just above the top of the menu** (0.837× at the most permeable closure)
rather than infinitely above a zero, with nothing fitted. The claim is the **span**, not any one
closure's number — quoting natural cork's 1.013 as "62 % closed" would be the §3 error again, one
number from a set standing in for the set. Hermetic stays at zero, which is the isolability check:
no oxygen, no source.

### 6. Why nothing was built

A post-dryness, SO₂-driven, lees-gated production term is a plausible mechanism and the paper
states it. It has **no magnitude anchor except Table 1 itself**, and calibrating against the table
the benchmark checks is a fit wearing a benchmark's name. It also could not run as written: the
model's viable biomass is 2.13e-4 g/L by the end of the tank phase, so a viable-yeast gate would
be firing on a wine that has no yeast — the gap is not one term but the absence of a lees /
young-wine phase between fermentation and bottle. The gap is therefore **measured, attributed and
pinned as `xfail(strict=True)`** so it cannot be closed silently — the D-142 idiom, and the reason
three tests here assert the published **direction** and never a published **magnitude**: a
magnitude in an xfail is a fit target handed to whoever closes it.

### 7. What was verified

8 tests, 5 passing and 3 `xfail(strict=True)`. The passing ones that earn their place:

- **The attribution is a test, not a paragraph** — `k_so2_oxidation` → 0 flips the sign and the
  lift stays under 5 % while the published lift exceeds 250 %. If someone later removes the
  competition and reports the tank column fixed, this fails.
- **The floor across the closure menu**, with hermetic pinned at zero, the whole menu pinned
  *below* the published 2.7, and the most permeable pinned *above* 0.8× of it — a two-sided pin,
  because a one-sided one would pass on a model that had drifted anywhere upward.
- **The flux is exactly zero from dryness at every sample point**, which is the missing-source
  half of the diagnosis pinned so it cannot rot.
- **The bridging substrate is zero**, so §4's confound stays disposed of.

**All three xfails were confirmed to fail on the MODEL assertion, not the published one**, under
`--runxfail`: `0.0964 > 0.3034`, `0.3034 > 1.0131`, `26.6037/26.2558 > 2.0`. A test asserting only
the published direction would xfail for the wrong reason forever and read as coverage —
[[feedback-grep-finds-claims-not-guards]] applied to an xfail, where the failure mode is quieter
because a red is expected.

**Two assertions failed first and both were wrong in a way worth recording.** The group comparison
"every sulfited-must variant beats every unsulfited one" is **false in the published data**:
(0/30/35) = 25.9 beats (60/0/35) = 17.2, because the tank column can out-do the must column. That
is the paper's own point and the first draft had asserted its negation. And a hard zero on the
hermetic floor failed at **−7.9e-7 mg/L** — solver residue from a 42 mg/L ferment peak driven back
down, so the pin is now the noise floor with the reason written beside it
([[feedback-pin-tolerance-vs-solver-tolerance]]; D-108's "a hard zero the chemistry cannot make",
one layer out).

### 8. Scope, stated rather than conceded

- **The model's aging axis has one phase, not two.** `ClosureOxygenIngress` runs from
  `begin_aging`, so the three tank months are metered at the *bottle's* closure rate. A stainless
  tank with weekly lees stirring takes up more oxygen than a corked bottle, so the tank phase here
  is oxygen-poor relative to the experiment. It does not rescue the sign: the competition probe
  removes the O₂ term's effect entirely and still leaves +1 %.
- **The interior timeline split is swept, not asserted.** The paper's components (ferment + three
  months tank + a bottle tail) do not sum to its stated 182 days. Traded off at a fixed 182-day
  total (tank 60 / 90 / 130 d, ferment 14 / 21 d), the sulfited-must rows move **26.25–26.99** and
  the unsulfited floor **0.622–1.211**. Every claim above survives the ambiguity.
- **One closure and one must composition.** 21 Brix, 200 mg/L YAN, 18 °C, natural cork for the
  ladder. Herzan's cultivar, pH and closure are not stated in what was read, so none is claimed.
- **The benchmark costs ~23 s** in a module-scoped fixture (14 integrations), which is the
  `--dist load` case `CLAUDE.md` describes: it must stay on one worker to be paid once.

### 9. Next

- **The tank column is the open item and it is now specified rather than vague**: a post-dryness
  acetaldehyde source under maintained free SO₂, gated on something the model does not have (a
  lees / young-wine phase with residual viable yeast). **It needs a source that measures the rate,
  not the endpoint** — Herzan's table is an endpoint and cannot size a rate without becoming a fit.
- **The 0-vs-2.7 floor is no longer a separate open item**; it is the closure menu's span and it
  is pinned. Remove it from the deferred tail.
- Unchanged: OTR(T) (D-136/D-187, blocked), the quinone branching (D-145, paywalled), the missing
  post-Fenton secondary O₂ draw (D-142, unsourced), the `add_copper`/`copper`-slot disconnect
  (D-149, refused pending a source), and the burst-axis pH question (D-150/D-186).
- Nothing here re-opens D-47 or D-48. Both are *confirmed working on the stage they were built
  for*; the finding is about a stage neither was scoped to.

### 10. Transferable lesson

**The correction map only records corrections somebody declared. A record's premise can be
silently demolished by unrelated work, and that leaves no trace at all.** D-108 named its own
blocker in plain words — closure O₂ ingress — and D-136 built it 28 records later without naming
D-108, because D-136 was about oxygen and not about acetaldehyde. No `Corrects:` marker was owed
and none was written, so D-108 grew no ⚠. The item then rode the copy-forward open lists **20 more
times after its blocker shipped** (30 mentions total in the archive, 20 of them after D-136),
right up to D-187's §8, still described as out of scope for a reason that had stopped being true.

The ⚠ machinery is built for the case where a later beat *disagrees* with an earlier one. It has
no edge for the case where a later beat *changes the world the earlier one was describing* — and
that case is more common, because it needs no disagreement and nobody involved is wrong at the
time. [[feedback-a-refusal-reads-like-a-gap]] is the sibling failure: there, a REFUSED item read
as open; here, a genuinely-blocked item stayed listed after its blocker was removed. Both are the
same structural hole — **an open list is a claim about the present, stored as prose written in the
past.**

The practical form, and it is cheap: when a beat is picked off an old open item, **the first probe
is not "how do I build this", it is "is the reason this was closed still true?"** — run it against
the code, not the record. One probe here (a sealed sulfited bottle, read at the end) reclassified
the whole beat from a build to a measurement before a line was written.

The secondary lesson is §3's and it is D-108's (v) with a mechanism: **a flat model checked against
a spread of published values will always produce one flattering ratio.** When the model's output is
near-constant across a treatment axis, per-cell ratios are drawn from a lottery whose prize is a
number that reads like agreement. Report the structure — what the model *varies with* — and let the
ratio be an illustration of it, never the headline.

### D-188 amendment — the harness had two dosing paths and only one was pinned, and the derived-count rule caught a number the beat had reasoned itself out of checking

Found in review immediately after D-188 shipped, and appended rather than edited in place (the
D-147/D-181/D-186/D-187 precedent). Suite **1656 → 1665** (`pytest --collect-only -q` on both
trees), so the record's opening 1664 and its §7 "8 tests, 5 passing and 3 xfail" are superseded by
**9 tests, 6 passing and 3 `xfail(strict=True)`**. The headline numbers are untouched — nothing
below moves a ladder value, an attribution or a floor.

**1. Two dosing paths in one experiment, and the finding is about a dosing contrast.** The must
dose runs through the scenario verb (`_verb_add_so2`); every tank top-up and the bottling dose
write `so2_total` directly, because "maintained" has to be computed from the state. That is a
harness assumption sitting exactly where the finding lives — *the must column behaves differently
from the later columns* — and §2 asserted the harness was faithful without measuring it. Now
pinned: `test_the_two_dosing_paths_are_the_same_mutation` compiles the verb and checks its
mutation is **byte-identical** to `so2_total += mg/L / 1000` on the same state, with no clamp, no
companion slot and no `param_update`. It passes, so the record's numbers stand — but it was an
assumption until it was an assertion, which is D-108's lesson (vi) and the reason the check is
worth its 20 lines. It is D-187's `seal_bottle` ≡ `add_oxygen` idiom, applied to the verb this
beat leaned on rather than the one it built.

**2. `ARCHITECTURE.md` said 72 test files and there are 73.** The beat reasoned — correctly on the
letter of `CLAUDE.md` — that no Process, slot, parameter file or package changed, so no structural
update was owed, and stopped there. But that file's counts are **derived**, and the rule is to
*re-run the snippet* rather than reason about whether one moved. Run, it disagreed on one line.
Fixed in this amendment's commit. **The general form is the same shape as this beat's own subject:
a rule that says "update it when X changes" invites you to check whether X changed, when what the
document actually promises is that every number in it is reproducible on demand.** The snippet
takes ten seconds and needs no judgement; the judgement call is what got it wrong.

**3. A magnitude pin was living inside the principle that forbids them.**
`test_removing_the_sulfite_oxygen_competition_flips_the_sign_but_not_the_size` asserts
`modelled_lift < 0.05`, in a **passing** test, while §6 says the pins here assert direction and
never magnitude "because a magnitude is a fit target handed to whoever closes it". Both are right
and the scoping was missing: §6's principle is about the **xfail block**, whose whole audience is
the person closing the gap. The 5 % is a bound on *today's* model, and it is what makes "the size
belongs elsewhere" falsifiable rather than rhetorical. Its docstring now says so, and says the
right response when a post-dryness source lands is to **delete** it, not widen it. A test whose
name promises an attribution and whose body enforces a threshold should say which it is.

**One number in the record is arithmetic, not a command, and it is the one the record's own
subject warns about.** The opening says the blocker had been built "51 records earlier" — that is
D-136 to D-187 counted by hand, unlike the *20 copy-forward mentions after D-136* in §10, which
came from a grep whose output is in the receipts. It is correct under the obvious reading. It is
recorded here rather than amended because the point is the asymmetry: in a record arguing that
prose numbers are unpinned by construction, the pinned one and the unpinned one sit two lines
apart, and only the provenance tells them apart.
