## D-194 — The sweet-wine aging scenarios were not aging a sweet wine, they were aging a must that is still fermenting: `_SWEET_BRIX` re-anchored from 70 to a real botrytis 38 °Brix, and the premise gets a guard because breaking it left the whole file green

**Corrects:** D-192 §9 — "they now age a wine at 1.4 % ABV instead of 19.8 %" describes the wrong failure. At the fixed day-30 `begin_aging` breakpoint the 70 °Brix arm is at **0.50 % ABV** and still fermenting (4.9 g/L of sugar over days 25-30), and it keeps fermenting through the entire 730-day aging tail. It is not a weak wine; it is a different phase of the process. Its "947 g/L raw" is also not the model's initial `S` at that brix, which is **880.7 g/L**.

Owner picked this beat by name from what D-193 left open (the sweet-wine re-anchor and pyruvate's
growth-linked excretion). Pyruvate is untouched here and stays open.

### 1. What was wrong, and why it was invisible

`tests/test_aging_scenario.py:920` set `_SWEET_BRIX = 70.0` with a comment reading *"botrytis-level
must → D-129 ceiling arrests it at ~20% ABV (E≈160 g/L) leaving ~540 g/L residual sugar"*. Both
halves had rotted, and they rotted differently:

- **The number.** 70 °Brix is 880.7 g/L in the model. Sauternes and TBA harvest at ~35-40 °Brix.
  Eleven tests whose names say *sweet wine* ran a must no botrytis ever produced.
- **The mechanism.** The comment credits the **D-129 ethanol ceiling** for arresting the ferment.
  That was true when written; D-192 wired `OsmoticSubstrateInhibition`, which brakes an 880 g/L must
  by ~76× at t=0, and the ferment now never reaches the ceiling at all. The comment is a live
  instance of the claim D-192 already corrected in the abstract ("D-129's *late, not stuck* is
  false") — sitting unfixed in the one place that depended on it.

The `_wine` helper carried a second copy of the same claim, which is why it survived: the assertion
existed twice and was checked nowhere.

### 2. The measurement that picked the value

The load-bearing constraint is one D-192 could not have seen, because it is not about the brake:
`_begin_aging(_FERMENT_DAYS)` fires at a **fixed** day 30. D-192 measured "at 32-40 °Brix the brake
changes the PATH, not the DESTINATION" on runs long enough to *arrive*. It says nothing about
arriving before a fixed breakpoint. If the ferment is still descending at day 30, aging begins on a
fermenting wine and the large residual sugar is **unfermented, not stuck**.

Probe 1, amino-acid-dosed sur-lie arm (`brix`, `S0`, `dS` over days 25-30, `E`/ABV at the day-30
breakpoint, and the state at day 760):

```
 Brix       S0     S@25d     S@30d  dS 25-30    E@30d  ABV@30d     S@end    E@end  ABV@end  verdict
   24    245.3      -0.0      -0.0    -0.000   116.16    14.71      -0.0   116.15    14.71  ARRIVED
   32    338.3       8.9       8.9    -0.000   157.09    19.90       8.9   157.07    19.90  ARRIVED
   34    362.6      29.7      29.7    -0.000   158.66    20.10      29.6   158.65    20.10  ARRIVED
   36    387.2      52.9      52.9     0.000   159.22    20.17      52.6   159.21    20.17  ARRIVED
   38    412.3      76.7      76.7     0.000   159.52    20.21      76.4   159.50    20.21  ARRIVED
   40    437.8     101.0     101.0     0.000   159.70    20.23     100.6   159.68    20.23  ARRIVED
   45    503.6     163.5     163.5     0.000   159.73    20.23     162.8   159.72    20.23  ARRIVED
   70    880.7     869.4     864.5     4.906     3.93     0.50     686.6    60.47     7.66  STILL FERMENTING
```

Everything in 32-45 arrives, and arrives with room to spare — `dS` over days 25-30 is 0.000 and `E`
moves under 0.03 g/L between day 30 and day 760. The brake **self-lifts** as `S` falls below its
300 g/L threshold, so the opening rate cut costs far less wall-clock than its t=0 magnitude
suggests. The risk was never the high end failing to arrive; it was the **low end failing the
existing `assert S > 50.0`**.

This does **not** contradict D-192's "genuinely STUCK": the bare arm converges to 757.3 g/L at day
760 against that record's 755.4 g/L at 20 years, so it is the same trajectory. The point is *when*.
Convergence happens long after the breakpoint, so the scenarios age across the **approach** to the
stuck state rather than at it.

### 3. Why 38, and the principle it turns on

| candidate | end residual | margin on `assert S > 50.0` | real-must fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 34 | 29.6 g/L | **FAILS** | Sauternes-low |
| 36 | 52.6 g/L | +5 % — fragile | in range |
| **38** | **76.4 g/L** | **+53 %** | **in range (Sauternes/TBA ~35-40)** |
| 40 | 100.6 g/L | +101 % | top of range |
| 45 | 162.8 g/L | +226 % | **above** real botrytis must |

45 °Brix is the tempting choice, because it is the one that reproduces real Sauternes' *residual
sugar* (120-150 g/L). It was rejected: it buys that only by inflating the must past what botrytis
must actually is, which is **tuning a scenario input to conceal a known model limit** — the modelled
ethanol ceiling is 20.2 % ABV against a real 13-14 %, a pre-existing `EthanolInactivation`
calibration limit that is orthogonal to this beat and is not fixed by hiding its consequence.

The rule that decides it: **`_SWEET_BRIX` is the must's Brix — an input the winemaker measures — so
it takes a real must's value, and the residual is left to be whatever the model predicts.** Anchor
the input; let the output be wrong where the model is wrong, visibly. 38.0 also sits inside D-192's
own measured 32-40 °Brix envelope, so the pick is not an extrapolation past that record.

### 4. The guard, and why this beat owes one where D-189 did not

The suite was run with the premise broken — which is not a thought experiment here, it is the state
this beat inherited. **All 98 tests in the file passed at 70 °Brix**, aging a must at 0.50 % ABV.
They also all pass at 38. So not one of the eleven `_SWEET_BRIX` tests can distinguish an arrested
sweet wine from a fermenting must.

The reason is that their sweetness assert is `assert float(sweet.series("S")[-1]) > 50.0`, and a
still-fermenting must has *more* sugar than a stuck one. The assert reads as "the wine is sweet";
what it actually witnessed was "the ferment has barely started". It passed **for the wrong reason**,
which is the failure mode a magnitude threshold on an unqualified pool always risks. The remaining
asserts are directional (`> 0.0`, `> 0.01`, `> 100× dry`) and are satisfied by either regime.

This is the mutate-the-premise discipline run for real, and it returned the opposite verdict to
D-189's: there the equivalent mutation went red on five existing asserts and no guard was owed;
here it came back green, so one is. `test_the_sweet_scenarios_age_an_ARRESTED_wine_not_a_still_fermenting_must`
asserts the two claims "sweet wine" actually makes, measured on the bare scenario:

| predicate | anchor (38) | retired (70) | threshold |
|---|---|---|---|
| **arrived** — `E` at the breakpoint | 156.05 g/L (19.77 % ABV) | **3.93** | `> 150.0` |
| **stuck** — relative `S` drift over the 730-day tail | **0.0028** | **0.1238** | `< 0.02` |

The 150.0 threshold sits ~4 % under the anchor and ~40× over the failure; the drift threshold has
7× headroom at the anchor and is exceeded 6× at the retired value.

The test carries its **mutation arm as a permanent positive control**: it re-runs 70.0 and asserts
the guard's own predicates *fail* there. A threshold that discriminates nothing reads exactly like
one that discriminates unless one arm is expected green and one red — and this also pins *why* the
value moved, so it cannot drift back silently.

### 5. What this beat did not do

The **20.2 % ABV ceiling is not touched.** A 38 °Brix must ferments to it, which is high for any
real botrytis wine; that is the `EthanolInactivation` calibration limit both the old and the new
comment name, and it is left visible rather than compensated. Re-anchoring a scenario input does not
license retuning physics, and the two failures are not the same failure.

**No physics changed.** `_SWEET_BRIX` lives in a test file; every parameter, Process and modifier is
byte-for-byte what D-193 left. What moved is which wine eleven scenarios are about.

## D-195 — Option B for pyruvate, measured and REFUSED: it really does restore the ~100s mg/L peak the literature describes, and it pays for it with the residual that binds SO2, taking the model outside Miao's measured buffering band

**Corrects:** D-49 — the pyruvate rate magnitudes were never "tuned so the pool peaks in the real ~100s mg/L range". The pool rises monotonically to **30.0 mg/L**, which is simultaneously its maximum and its residual, exactly as the same docstring says two paragraphs earlier when it records the peak-then-decline transient as dropped in v1. Only the "~10-40 mg/L finished-wine residual" half was true. Fixed in place.

Owner picked this beat by name, with the sweet-wine re-anchor (D-194) — the two items D-193 left
open. This closes **D-49's original option-B item**, which D-189 explicitly declined to close.

### 1. What was open, and why D-189 did not close it

D-189 measured option B (growth-linked excretion) on **α-ketobutyrate** and refused it: a
growth-linked source with the shipped flux-linked sink drains the pool it feeds, because growth
ends day 0.98 and dryness is day 2.04, so the sink clears `exp(-0.1 x 106.4)` ~ 2.4e-5 across that
window. That record states the arithmetic is general to all three pools, but deliberately left
pyruvate's item open, because **neither the motivation nor the cost transfers**: there is no
Crepin-equivalent measurement driving pyruvate, and its residual binds SO₂ (D-51) rather than
feeding a two-year aldol.

The generality claim rests on all three sinks sharing `k = 0.1`. That is prose, repeated in two
places, about a shared value — so it was **checked rather than trusted**: `keto_acids.yaml` gives
`k_pyruvate_reassimilation` = `k_alpha_kg_reassimilation` = `k_alpha_kb_reassimilation` = `1.0e-1`.
The premise holds.

### 2. Option B works. That is what makes the refusal worth recording

Crepin-ish must (24 Brix, 180 mg N/L, 1.0 g/L amino acids, 28 °C, 30 d, 50 mg/L SO₂ at day 29).
The re-anchor holding **total pyruvate production fixed** is computed on the run rather than
inherited: `INT(flux)/INT(growth)` = **49.6157**, against α-KB's 47.77 — it is a property of the
trajectory, not of the pool, and the two agreeing to ~4 % is a consistency check on both.

```
baseline     residual=  30.0 mg/L  peak=  30.0 mg/L  free_SO2= 33.1  bound_SO2= 16.9
option B     residual=   0.0 mg/L  peak= 122.5 mg/L  free_SO2= 42.8  bound_SO2=  7.2
restored     residual=  30.0 mg/L  peak=  30.0 mg/L  free_SO2= 33.1  bound_SO2= 16.9
```

Residual survival **4.17e-5**. The restore arm is bit-identical to baseline, so nothing below is a
silent restore failure confirming itself.

**The gain is real and visible here, unlike α-KB's.** D-189 could lean on the fact that its 2.62 %
share was inert on every output. This pool's option B genuinely produces the mid-ferment transient
the literature describes — a **122.5 mg/L peak**, squarely in the real ~100s mg/L range, against a
shipped pool that never peaks at all. The refusal therefore has to be earned on the cost.

### 3. The cost is a disagreement with measured wine, in the flattering direction

Pyruvate's residual is a bound-SO₂ sink; D-51 is built, and `acidbase.py` sums four carbonyls.
Draining the residual releases that SO₂: free SO₂ **33.1 → 42.8 mg/L (+29 %)**, bound
**16.9 → 7.2 mg/L (−57 %)**. The model would report a wine as substantially **better protected than
it is** — the direction that reads as good news, and so the dangerous one.

The shipped suite forbids it at **37 failures across 7 files** (1705 passed / 37 failed under the
mutation; 1742 passed under the control arm):

| file | failures | what they are |
|---|---|---|
| `test_oxidative_cascade_guards.py` | 16 | pinned trajectories: so2_total, A420, o2, acetaldehyde, methional, phenylacetaldehyde, faded_anthocyanin |
| `test_burst_oxidative_set.py` | 13 | the burst set's measured trajectory, and the direct set's invariance to it |
| `benchmarks/test_validation_danilewicz_so2_o2.py` | 3 | **sulfite buffering against Miao's real wines** |
| `test_keto_acids.py` | 3 | the closed form, the persistent residual, the pool-accumulates premise |
| `test_acetaldehyde.py` / `test_malolactic.py` | 2 | SO₂ stranding; SO₂ suppression of MLF |

**The decisive failure is Miao.** The sulfite-buffering secant falls to **1.1005**, outside his
measured band of **1.2526-1.9882**. Option B does not merely perturb internal pins — it takes the
model **out of agreement with real measured wine**, which α-KB's refusal never had to show.

Two honesty notes rather than hidden caveats. **Attribution — measured, see the amendment below:**
the re-anchor holds total production fixed on *this* must; other tests use other musts, where it is
held only approximately, so some share of the 37 is magnitude rather than pure shape. **A
magnitude-only control settles it: Miao's failure belongs to the RESIDUAL, not to the shape**, which
makes the refusal cleaner rather than weaker. **Not a probe artifact:**
`test_carbon_closes_on_a_compiled_run` fails on its *premise* assert ("the pool genuinely
accumulates", 3.5e-10 against > 10 mg/L), not on the carbon ledger. Carbon still closes.

### 4. The prose defect the probe exposed

Measuring the baseline peak to compare against option B's is what surfaced it: the shipped pool's
maximum **is** its residual, 30.0 mg/L. So the Tiers paragraph's claim that the magnitudes were
"tuned so the pool peaks in the real ~100s mg/L range" is false, and structurally impossible — the
same docstring, two paragraphs earlier, correctly says the pool rises monotonically to the
quasi-steady plateau and that the transient is dropped. It was crediting the shipped model with the
behaviour it elsewhere says it does not have, and the one shape that *would* deliver that peak is
the option B the same docstring defers.

Third beat running in which the wrong number was in **prose, not in a shipped value** (D-187,
D-192 §8, now this). The residual half of the sentence was true, which is what let the false half
ride: a claim with one checkable clause and one unchecked one reads as checked.

### 5. Verdict

**REFUSED for pyruvate.** D-49's option-B item is closed — measured, not deferred again.

**No guard was added and none is owed**, and this time it is not close: 37 asserts across 7 files
already forbid it, one of them against real data. That is the same conclusion D-189 reached for
α-KB and the *opposite* of D-194, where the equivalent mutation came back green on all 98 tests in
its file and a guard was therefore owed. The count of asserts *naming* a pool did not predict
either outcome — pyruvate has 27, α-KB had none, and both were refused without a new guard.

**α-ketoglutarate was NOT measured and is not claimed.** Its sink shares the same `k = 0.1` and its
residual binds SO₂ through the same D-51 equilibrium, so the same outcome is expected in kind and
smaller in size (its residual is ~20 mg/L against pyruvate's 30) — an inference, labelled as one.

### Amendment (same session) — the strongest sentence was the one unmeasured claim

The record above originally said the Miao failure was *"independent of"* the attribution caveat,
on the reasoning that "a secant outside a measured band is a data disagreement either way." That
is an **assertion about attribution dressed as a tautology**, and it was the only unmeasured claim
carrying weight in the verdict. Measured now.

**The control:** keep the **shipped flux-linked shape** and collapse the residual by exactly the
factor option B collapses it (survival 4.17e-5) — a same-sized move *without* the shape change
([[feedback-pair-the-red-with-an-ordering-preserving-baseline]]).

| arm | shape | Miao buffering secant | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | flux-linked | inside 1.2526-1.9882 | pass |
| **option B** | growth-linked | **1.100501** | outside |
| **magnitude-only** | **flux-linked (shipped)** | **1.100510** | outside |

The two failing arms agree to **six significant figures**, and the same three benchmark tests fail
in both. So the shape is not doing the work at all: **draining the residual by any route leaves
Miao's band.**

**This strengthens the refusal rather than qualifying it.** The original framing made the case
against option B's *shape*, which invited the obvious rescue — find a different growth-linked form
whose timing spares the residual. There is none to find: the objection attaches to the **residual
itself**, and option B necessarily drains it, since that is the structural arithmetic D-189
established (growth-linked source, flux-linked sink, `exp(-k INT flux)` across the gap). Any variant
that keeps the residual is not option B.

It also re-points the finding. §3 read as "option B disagrees with Miao"; the measured claim is
**"the pyruvate residual is load-bearing for the model's agreement with Miao's real wines"** — a
statement about the shipped model, not about a rejected variant, and one nothing in the archive
had established. The residual was introduced at D-49 as a thing that *exists to bind SO₂* (D-51);
this is the first measurement showing that binding is what keeps a real-data benchmark in band.

Receipts: `d195_optionb.py`, `D195_ARM=magnitude`.

## D-196 — The second oxygen the Fenton limb costs, built: the 1-hydroxyethyl radical takes an O₂ of its own, the "unsourced" label on it was refuted by a book already on disk, and the double-counting objection died on a hermetic O₂ pool being supply-limited rather than rate-limited

**Corrects:** D-188 — its open-list entry "post-Fenton secondary O₂ draw (D-142, **unsourced**)". The mechanism is printed outright in a source that has been in `_txt/` since before D-142.
**Corrects:** D-141 — two bookkeeping sentences it shipped in `oxidative_cascade.py`: `OxygenActivation`'s "the cascade's **sole** O2 consumer / every gram of O2 that leaves the pool leaves through here", and `PeroxideEthanolOxidation`'s "does **NOT** touch `o2` — that is OxygenActivation's alone". Both false as of this record. Gate 1 (D-137) is **not** breached — see §4.

### 1. The item was never blocked

Since D-142 the archive has carried "the missing post-Fenton secondary O₂ draw" on its open
lists — **twenty** copy-forward entries between D-142 and D-188 — and D-188's list
labelled it `(D-142, unsourced)`. It is not unsourced. Waterhouse, Sacks & Jeffery,
*Understanding Wine Chemistry* 2nd ed., §24.4.4.1, on disk in `_txt/`:

> "reaction with the next highest concentration component of wine, ethanol, generates the
> major detectable product of the Fenton reaction, the 1-hydroxyethyl radical. **This
> radical goes on to react with oxygen and produce acetaldehyde** unless it can be quenched
> by other processes, such as reaction with hydroxycinnamates."

So one acetaldehyde made on that limb costs **two** O₂ — one activated at the iron node,
one taken by the radical — and the cascade booked one. Twenty records carried the item forward and
none re-opened the source. [[feedback-check-the-blocker-is-still-blocking]]
[[feedback-re-read-the-source-you-already-mined]]

### 2. Why the stoichiometry is pinned per ACETALDEHYDE, not per H₂O₂

The quoted sentence names a competitor for the radical — hydroxycinnamate quenching — and
gives no rate for it. That would normally be an unquantified term the build has to invent.
It is not, because quenching removes the acetaldehyde and the second O₂ **together**: a
quenched radical yields neither. Pinning the draw at 1 mol O₂ per mol *acetaldehyde formed*
therefore absorbs the quench into an already-calibrated rate. Per mol H₂O₂ it would not,
and would need a quench ratio nobody has published.

`_O2_PER_ACETALDEHYDE = 1.0` is stoichiometry, not a YAML parameter — the `_SO2_PER_O2`
precedent, consistent with the four constants already in this module that are all 1.

### 3. THE BLOCKING OBJECTION, and why it died on a measurement rather than an argument

`k_o2_depletion_total` — the constant the cascade's activation floor rides on — is anchored
to observed O₂ **disappearance** ("a saturating O₂ charge is scavenged over weeks-to-months"),
and D-141 tuned the cascade so its **total O₂ budget reproduces the direct set's** (1.01×
unsulfited). If the second O₂ was already inside that calibration, this build double-counts
and the honest change is a re-baseline, not an addition. [[feedback-a-derived-yield-encodes-its-rate-law]]

Pre-registered verdict rule: if the unsulfited cascade/direct budget ratio lands ≥ 1.5×,
D-141's reproduction claim must be re-recorded. Measured, 60 d, 8 mg/L dose, hermetic:

| | budget ratio before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unsulfited red | 0.9614× | **1.0439×** |
| red, 60 mg/L SO₂ | 1.0015× | **1.0012×** |

**The prediction missed and the miss is the finding.** The *instantaneous* draw does double
(2.2902e-5 → 4.5804e-5 g/L/h unsulfited — exactly 2×, because with no bisulfite the ethanol
branch takes the whole H₂O₂ node). The *budget* does not, because over a hermetic dosed run
the O₂ pool is **supply-limited, not rate-limited**: a faster draw empties the same 8 mg/L
sooner rather than consuming more of it. D-141's reproduction claim survives untouched, and
nothing was double-counted. [[feedback-measure-which-side-before-building]]

Where the pool is *not* exhausted the change is large and real: beer's 120 d packaging arm
goes **71.3 % → 91.7 %** of its dose consumed (5.7062 → 7.3373 mg/L). Not a shipped number
— beer's default oxidative set is the direct one, and the shipped default wiring is
unchanged by this record in both media.

### 4. Gate 1 is not breached, and the two false sentences are corrected rather than reinterpreted

Gate 1 (D-137) is the finding that in wine O₂ reacts with essentially nothing but Fe(II),
which is why the cascade routes every O₂ through one activation node. A **carbon-centred
radical** reacting with O₂ at near-diffusion rate is not a counterexample: Gate 1's content
is about *ground-state* wine molecules — ethanol, bisulfite, phenols — and the radical step
is the next link of the same chain Gate 1's own source describes. What is no longer true is
the **bookkeeping**, so both sentences are struck in place with the reason, not quietly
reworded. `PeroxideEthanolOxidation.touches` gains `"o2"`.

### 5. The upper-bound half, named and NOT built

The radical's other product is the hydroperoxyl radical, which in principle returns to H₂O₂
via Fe(II) and hands an oxidising equivalent back — pushing the SO₂:O₂ ratio the **other
way**. Nothing read sources its fate in wine: Danilewicz 2007's radical chain is *bisulfite*
autoxidation, and he concludes it does **not** run in wine because polyphenols intercept it,
so it does not transfer. `_O2_PER_ACETALDEHYDE = 1.0` is therefore an **upper bound on the
net draw**, written as one in the code. Recorded so that a later recycling term cannot be
credited with a cancellation this record's omission created.
[[feedback-build-the-term-that-makes-agreement-worse-first]]

### 6. Attribution: the shape does work — and it took TWO controls to show it, because the first was a tautology

D-195, one commit earlier, refused a mechanism because a same-sized magnitude move
reproduced its whole effect to six significant figures. The same control was pre-registered
here.

**Control 1 (rate).** Scale `k_o2_depletion_total` by `(1 + s)`, no new term. It moves the
benchmark ratio **0.06 %** against the radical term's 2.23 %. But §3 had just shown the
budget is supply-limited, so a *rate* cannot move a ratio set by *stoichiometry* — passing
this control proves nothing. Reporting it as evidence would be exactly D-195's amendment
error: a tautology carrying a verdict. [[feedback-a-tautology-can-smuggle-an-attribution]]

**Control 2 (stoichiometric).** Charge the **same average** extra O₂ — `s̄ = 0.026699`, the
measured mean ethanol branch share at the operating point — as a **flat fraction of every
activation**, removing the state dependence and nothing else.

| arm | ratio, dose 80 | blocked @ 500 (tol 0.01) | ideal @ 500 (tol 0.02) |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped, share-weighted | 1.107886 | **0.995316 PASS** | **1.992643 PASS** |
| flat, same average cost | 1.105573 | **0.971712 FAIL** | **1.945532 FAIL** |

The two agree to **0.21 %** on the real-wine ratio — and the flat one **breaks both of
Danilewicz's asymptotes**, which `test_validation_danilewicz_so2_o2.py` calls the rebuild's
falsifiable content. The state-dependence is load-bearing *exactly* where the model's only
structural claim lives and nowhere else, because the ethanol branch's share goes to zero at
the limit dose precisely where the limits are asserted. **This is the opposite of D-195's
outcome, and only the second control could establish it.**

### 7. Effect on the benchmark, stated including what got worse

At the shared operating point the cascade reads **1.1338 → 1.1079**, still inside Miao's
1.0972-1.6621. The **dose-70 arm leaves his band** (1.1034 → 1.0728), so the straddle
`test_cascade_brackets_miaos_lower_bound_across_its_valid_dose_range` records narrows from
"in band from ~70 upward" to "in band only at 80". The test still passes — it asserts the
lowest dose is below the floor and the operating point is inside, and both remain true —
but the headroom D-142's amendment already called dose-contingent is now thinner. Recorded
rather than left for the next dose-grid change to discover.

The two asymptotes and the strict ordering are untouched (§6 table; 0.9547 < 1.1079 <
1.7871). Nothing here was fitted: the 2.3 % fall is `1/(1 + s)` with `s` a branch fraction
built from constants D-72/D-73 calibrated.

### 8. The copper re-fit a guard demanded, measured to be exactly nothing

The new draw is `share × activation_rate` and activation carries D-134's copper multiplier,
so it becomes a **second copper-multiplied O₂ draw by construction** and
`test_only_the_declared_o2_draw_responds_to_the_copper_multiplier[cascade]` went red —
predicted. That test's message says a new draw "needs a re-fit recorded, not this
expectation edited".

**Recorded: the re-fit is a no-op, exactly.** Ferreira's between-wine spread reads
**1.3245× on both arms, to four decimals**, while the absolute draw doubles. The reason is
structural rather than a coincidence of the scenario: `h2o2_branch_fraction` reads only the
ethanol and bisulfite weights, neither of which touches `copper`, so the new draw is a
copper-**independent** multiple of a draw copper already scales. Copper's *share* of total
uptake — the quantity D-134 fitted 600 L/g against — cannot move.

### 9. The suite stayed green, so a guard was owed

Full suite after the build: **1742 passed, 3 xfailed** — the same count as before, having
moved a benchmarked quantity 2.3 % and pushed one dose out of a measured band. That is
D-194's situation, and D-194's rule: the green mutation is what owes the guard.

Two added to `tests/test_oxidative_cascade_guards.py`:

* `test_the_fenton_limb_draws_one_o2_per_acetaldehyde` — the 1:1 stoichiometry at machine
  tolerance, on a real cascade state, plus the `touches` declaration.
* `test_the_radical_draw_is_bisulfite_dependent_not_a_flat_activation_surcharge` — forbids
  the §6 flat variant. **Its first draft asserted `h2o2_branch_fraction` directly and would
  have passed on the flat variant unchanged**, because the branch fraction is not what that
  variant changes; it measures the *realised* draw as a fraction of the activation draw
  instead, at two states whose free bisulfite differs. [[feedback-grep-finds-claims-not-guards]]

No benchmark-side mutation arm was added: the cheap guard forbids the same variant upstream
of the asymptote, and that file's own discipline rejects a second threshold on one quantity
as decoration.

Mutation arms (`d196_arms.py`) — `noop` **designed GREEN** and green, so the restore is
verified; `drop`, `half` and `flat` each red on both guards.
[[feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms]]

### Still open

The hydroperoxyl recycling limb (§5, unsourced). The activation node's missing pH term. The
quinone branching, still needing Nikolantonaki & Waterhouse 2012 or a third source. The
cascade remains **non-default**, so none of this reaches a shipped run.

### Amendment (same session) — a `Corrects` marker withdrawn, the acetaldehyde consequence measured, and a probe whose baseline had gone stale under it

Four corrections to the record above, none of which change what shipped.

#### A. The `**Corrects:** D-142` marker is WITHDRAWN, and the deleted line is the correction

The record as first written claimed D-142's "Next" sentence — *"the missing post-Fenton O₂ draw
is the cheaper structural candidate and would move `r` in the **right** direction on its own"* —
was falsified here. **It was not.** `r` is defined earlier in D-142 §3 as
`(H2O2 share to sulfite) + (quinone share to sulfite)`, i.e. SO₂ per O₂, and D-142's own
"Nor does it flip the bisulfite sign" paragraph says the missing draw "is also why the model
**cannot dip below 1** the way Miao's wine #1 does". So "the right direction" meant *downward* —
toward the sub-1 reach wine #1 (0.8443) demonstrates and the model could not attain.

This beat **confirms** that: the draw lowers the ratio, and the cascade's lowest valid dose now
reads 1.0330 against 1.0703. §7's finding is a **cost at the post-amendment operating point**,
not a falsification of D-142's mechanism claim, and the two are compatible — the same downward
move buys reach at the bottom and spends headroom at the top.

The marker line has therefore been **deleted** rather than left standing, on D-168's own rule:
"a ⚠ on D-77 would tell every future reader it contains an error it does not contain, and the
index cannot catch a semantically wrong marker — `tests/test_decisions_index.py` validates only
that a target exists and is earlier." Both other `Corrects` markers (D-188, D-141) stand and were
re-read. Recorded here because deleting it silently would be the same class of error.

#### B. The acetaldehyde consequence, which the first draft measured and then dropped

Probe 1 measured the final acetaldehyde pool falling **3.9×** in an unsulfited red where the
stoichiometry predicts 2×, and the record shipped without mentioning it — in a §7 titled
"including what got worse". Acetaldehyde is the *product of the limb this record modified*, a
sensory output and the model's strongest SO₂ binder, so the silence was the one bad option.

Measured now, by integrating the limb's own contribution rather than reading the pool. **The
identity holds:** production equals `mol O₂ consumed × share/(1 + share)` to **1.003×** (pre-D-196
arm) and **1.006×** (shipped), so the term is arithmetically right and nothing is hiding in it.

| unsulfited red, 60 d | pre-D-196 | shipped |
|---|---|---|
| ethanol limb produced | 1.0037e-2 g/L | 5.4642e-3 g/L (**1.84× less**) |
| final acetaldehyde pool | 2.6572e-3 g/L | 6.8345e-4 g/L (**3.89× less**) |
| retained fraction of production | 26.48 % | 12.51 % |

**The pool is a residual, and that is the whole of the discrepancy.** ~87 % of the acetaldehyde
this limb makes is consumed downstream — chiefly `acetaldehyde_reduction`, with
`acetaldehyde_bridged_condensation` and `tannin_ethyl_tannin_condensation` taking the rest — so
what survives to day 60 is a small remainder of a large throughput and moves by more than
production does. The residual amplification beyond the production change is **not further
attributed here**; the sinks are each first-order in acetaldehyde, so it is most likely the
earlier completion of the O₂ pulse leaving the pool longer to decay, and that is a conjecture,
labelled as one. It is the same shape D-195 found for pyruvate one commit earlier: the residual,
not the flux, is what an outside number reads.

**In a sulfited wine — the realistic case — none of this is visible:** at 60 mg/L SO₂ production
falls 3.6 % (3.2975e-4 → 3.1796e-4 g/L), the pool falls the same 3.6 %, and the retained fraction
is unchanged at 98.4 %. The dramatic figure belongs to the unsulfited arm alone.

#### C. A probe whose baseline went stale under it, caught only by the identity check

`probe1.py` captured `PeroxideEthanolOxidation.derivatives` **at import time** and toggled
between that capture and a patched version. That was correct when written — and stopped being
correct the moment the source was edited, because the capture then *was* the shipped D-196
function. Its "base" arm silently became the shipped code and its "+radical" arm stacked a
**second** draw on top.

Nothing went red. The only symptom was the identity reading **0.503** where it had to read 1.0,
and the first diagnosis of that was wrong too — a fine-grid re-run was tried on the theory that a
fast O₂ decay was under-resolved, and returned the identical 0.503061, which is what ruled the
numerical explanation out and pointed at the arms.

**No shipped number is affected** — probe 1 ran before the source edit, so its printed figures
are genuine, and probes 2-4 define their arms against the live attribute rather than a capture.
The lesson is the general one: **a mutation harness that captures a baseline is only valid until
the baseline moves, and it fails silently and green.** `probe5.py` defines the pre-D-196 arm as a
suppression of the shipped function instead, which cannot go stale the same way.

§1 said "**nineteen** copy-forward entries". Counted rather than estimated: **twenty** records
carry the item — D-150 through D-166 unbroken, then D-186, D-187, D-188 — one line each. §1 has
been corrected in place.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` needed no change, and that was **derived rather than reasoned**: its

### 1. The concession was 122 records old and had never been sized

D-75 shipped the oxidative Strecker route with an explicit concession, restated verbatim in
`aging.yaml`: mechanistically the O₂ is consumed at the phenol-oxidation step, making the
o-quinones that then do the Strecker deamination, so *"a separate `k_strecker` `[o2]` draw
formally **double-counts** that shared quinone step"*, and *"a two-stage (O₂ → quinone pool →
{pigment, aldehyde, acetaldehyde}) rework is deliberately **out of scope** (a larger structural
beat)"*.

That paragraph carries **two** claims, and only the second is a scope decision:

1. a **magnitude** claim — the double-charged draw is small (the `k_strecker` sentence above);
2. a **scope** decision — the rework is too big for v1.

Claim 2 is the owner's and stands: the two-stage rework *is* the oxidative cascade (D-141), which
exists, is isolable and stays non-default. Claim 1 is a measurable statement that no test, probe or
later record ever ran — it rode 122 records as prose in a record and a `notes:` field.
[[feedback-a-notes-field-is-unchecked-storage]] [[feedback-a-scope-note-can-carry-a-mechanism-claim]]

### 2. The partition is exactly kᵢ/Σkⱼ, and the code says so three times

Every O₂ sink in the default (direct) set is **first-order in `o2`** and `ProcessSet` sums them, so
the instantaneous partition does not depend on the O₂ level at all — a statement `aging.py` already
makes in three separate docstrings (*"ProcessSet sums the sinks, so o2 splits by kᵢ/Σk"*). Six
drawers plus one source. Classified against **this codebase's own other mechanism** rather than an
outside opinion — each "downstream" name has a cascade counterpart that consumes H₂O₂ or quinone and
(up to D-196's radical draw) no `o2` of its own:

| Process | role | cascade counterpart |
|---|---|---|
| `phenolic_browning` | **primary** — the phenol-autoxidation step | `OxygenActivation` |
| `sulfite_oxidation` | downstream | `PeroxideSulfiteOxidation` + `QuinoneSulfonation` |
| `anthocyanin_fading` | downstream | `QuinoneAnthocyaninFading` |
| `oxidative_acetaldehyde` | downstream (the D-73 lump) | `PeroxideEthanolOxidation` |
| `strecker_degradation` | downstream (the D-75 lump) | `QuinoneStreckerDegradation` |
| `ellagitannin_oxidation` | downstream | `QuinoneEllagitanninOxidation` |
| `closure_oxygen_ingress` | **source**, not a sink (D-136) | — |

### 3. D-75's number is right, and it is about the smallest of the five

Integrated over Carrascón's own saturation cycle (§4), share of the O₂ actually consumed:

| arm | browning | sulfite | anth. fade | ethanol | **Strecker** | ellag. | **downstream total** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unsulfited | 64.4 % | — | 30.4 % | 5.3 % | **0.033 %** | — | **35.6 %** |
| SO₂ 30 mg/L | 37.7 % | 41.2 % | 18.0 % | 3.0 % | **0.019 %** | — | **62.3 %** |
| SO₂ 60 mg/L | 23.9 % | 62.7 % | 11.5 % | 1.9 % | **0.012 %** | — | **76.1 %** |
| SO₂ 30 + oak 4 g/L | 37.7 % | 41.2 % | 18.0 % | 3.0 % | **0.019 %** | 0.15 % | **62.3 %** |

D-75's *"well under 1 % of the O₂"* holds with **two orders of magnitude to spare**, and its
*"~2 % of the always-on total"* is exact — `k_strecker`/`k_o2_depletion_total` = 1.0e-5/5.0e-4 =
2.0000 %, an identity between two constants rather than a property of any run.

**And the lump it defends is the majority of the budget.** `anthocyanin_fading` uses the *identical*
additive-on-top idiom, is never named in the concession, and takes **~1000× more O₂ than Strecker**
(30.4 % vs 0.033 % unsulfited). With SO₂ present the five downstream draws take **62–76 %**. So the
concession is not wrong about the term it names; it is a magnitude defence of a lump, conducted on
the lump's smallest member. **A true number, scoped to the wrong thing.**

The metric that does *not* discriminate, recorded so it cannot be quoted as if it did: Σ`k_eff` /
`k_o2_depletion_total` measures **9.04×** (unsulfited) / **25.05×** (SO₂ 60), but
`phenolic_browning`'s `k_eff` contains D-132's **sourced** phenolic boost, which is a legitimate
addition to the *primary* consumer. Confirmed and uninformative; downgraded in `PREREGISTER.md`
before probe1 ran rather than dropped after.

### 4. What the double charge is worth against measured oxygen uptake

The comparator is already on disk **and already transcribed into the suite**: `_CARRASCON_2018_REDS`
(Carrascón *et al.* 2018, *Food Chem.* 241:206-214, Tables 1+2) — eight commercial Spanish reds on
the repeated-air-saturation protocol D-132/D-133 are anchored on. Four comparability checks, run
**before** the model number existed:

- **Free SO₂ per wine** (Table 1): 2.6 / 10.5 / 14.8 / 14.4 / 24.7 / 33.7 / 13.3 / 10.1 mg/L — every
  wine carries free SO₂, so **the unsulfited arm is not the comparator**.
- **SO₂ consumed in the first saturation alone** (Table 2): 9.6–18.8 mg/L, i.e. *more* than the free
  SO₂ present, so SO₂ is being consumed throughout the averaging window rather than exhausted before
  it.
- **O₂ consumed per saturation**: 6.94–7.69 mg/L — the same operating point as the 8 mg/L dose used
  here, not a rescaling.
- **The cycle rule is reproducible on a trajectory** (§2.2): a cycle ends *"when the wine consumed
  90 % of the initial oxygen or after a week"*. The model's number is built to that definition
  instead of being compared against an instantaneous rate. In every arm the **7-day cap** binds.

Observed **average (steady) OCR: 0.88–1.25 mg O₂/L/day.** The *initial* OCR (1.95–6.83) is the burst
axis (D-133, non-default) and is not this set's comparator.

**AMENDED IN THE SAME SESSION — the 7-day cap flattered the model, and the honest deviation is
~4× bigger than this section first shipped.** Carrascón's rule has two limbs and I first reported
only the one the model wins on. Under the **7-day cap** the window closes while the model's rate is
still elevated and only 33–81 % of the charge is gone, where the eight reds reached ~85–91 %; under
the paper's **primary** limb (90 % consumed, no cap) the same arms read far lower. Both limbs, one
table — the primary limb is the comparator, the cap is the weaker one:

| arm | free SO₂ mg/L | comparable? | 7-day cap | **90 % rule (primary)** | vs floor 0.88 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped, unsulfited | 0.00 | no (no SO₂) | 0.5325 | 0.1769 | 0.20× |
| **shipped, SO₂ 30** | **16.84** | **yes** | 0.7485 | **0.3840** | **0.44× — 2.3× below** |
| shipped, SO₂ 60 | 40.24 | **no — above every wine** | 0.9284 | 0.6923 | 0.79× |
| naive de-duplication, SO₂ 30 | 16.84 | — | 0.3807 | **0.1085** | **0.12× — 8.1× below** |

**The SO₂ 60 arm lands in the band under the cap and must not be quoted**: its free SO₂ exceeds all
eight wines, and under the primary rule it is below the floor anyway. The honest reading is the
SO₂ 30 arm, and the cleanest statement of it avoids rate definitions entirely: **to consume the same
90 % of the same ~8 mg/L charge the model takes 18.6 days where the eight reds took ~7–8, so its
oxygen uptake is ~2.3× too slow.** That is a deviation this record records and does not tune: the
constants it would move are D-72/D-73/D-74/D-81 anchors with their own provenance, and the existing
pin on this axis (`test_burst_oxidation_plus_steady_lands_in_ferreira_initial_band`, 0.54–8.2
mg/L/day) is far too wide to have noticed. **Never quote the 15 %** the first draft of this section
carried — it is the cap limb, and it is the limb that flatters the model.
[[feedback-a-derived-yield-encodes-its-rate-law]]

**Comparability caveat, registered before the numbers existed:** eight commercial reds with their own
phenolics, iron and copper against the D-132 anchor red. This is a **band-membership** check, never a
per-wine fit, and a miss of either edge is a result rather than a licence to tune the arm until it
lands.

### 5. The naive de-duplication makes agreement WORSE — which is a reason D-75 never gave

Switching the five downstream draws off their `o2` debit, **re-baselining nothing**, takes the
modelled uptake — both arms on the **same** rule, the paper's primary one — from **0.3840 to
0.1085 mg/L/day**, i.e. **0.283×**, and from 2.3× below the observed floor to **8.1× below** it.
(Under the weaker cap limb the same comparison reads 0.7485 → 0.3807 = 0.509×, so the amendment in
§4 makes this finding **stronger**, not weaker: 3.5× rather than 2.0×.) The arm is deliberately named
`naive`, not "clean": deleting the draws is *not* what a two-stage rework does. The rework
re-baselines the primary draw, which is exactly why D-141 could verify the cascade **reproduces the
direct set's total budget** (0.96–1.04×, re-measured at D-196).
[[feedback-compute-the-clean-fix-before-adopting-it]]

**The naive arm reads 0.1085 at BOTH 30 and 60 mg/L SO₂, to four decimals** — the tell that what
survives the mutation is browning alone, which never reads SO₂. It is also the check that the arm
did what it claims: an SO₂-independent number is only possible once every SO₂-coupled draw is gone.

So the double charge is **load-bearing for agreement with measured oxygen uptake**: the model is
already 2.3× below the observed band *with* it, and de-duplicating it without a re-baseline would put
it 8.1× below. D-75 justified the out-of-scope call on effort ("a larger structural beat"); the
measurement supplies a second, stronger reason — the naive edit is not a partial improvement, it is
a regression. **Two mutation forms agree to four decimals** (`o2only` = drop the debit only,
`off` = zero the whole contribution), so the finding does not rest on which is used.

**This does NOT re-open** the refusal in `.claude/memory/prohibitions/oxidation-direct-and-burst.md`
against re-fixing the acetaldehyde/phenolic inversion inside the parallel frame. Nothing here is a
fix inside that frame; the O₂ bookkeeping is measured and left exactly as it was.

## D-198 — The hydroperoxyl recycling limb, refused on a measurement: three on-disk fates disagree, none is stated for the ethanol limb, the one three wine texts describe draws MORE O₂ rather than less, and the "documented no" D-197 expected turns out to be about a different reaction

**Corrects:** D-197 — its §8 prediction that a refusal would rest on *Understanding Wine Chemistry*'s "an attempt to detect this species was not successful". That sentence is about HO₂· as the intermediate of the **initiation** node `Fe(II) + O₂ → Fe(III) + HO₂·` (Fig. 24.9, index p. 327-328), not the **ethanol-limb co-product** D-196 §5 named (index p. 332). Same species, different reaction; a refusal resting on it would have been a misattribution.
**Corrects:** D-196 — the clause in §5 and in `_O2_PER_ACETALDEHYDE`'s comment calling `1.0` "an **UPPER BOUND** on the NET draw". For the fate three wine texts describe it is a *lower* bound: that route draws `A/(1−s)` against the shipped `A(1+s)`, an excess of `s²/(1−s)` at every `s > 0`. D-196 §5's *other* claim — that the limb pushes the SO₂:O₂ ratio the other way — is **confirmed**, and this record's own pre-registration predicted it false.

### 1. The item was open, and the reason it looked closed was a page-number collision

D-196 §5 named the limb and did not build it; D-197 §8 carried it forward and predicted the
outcome would be a documented refusal, on the strength of a failed detection reported in
*Understanding Wine Chemistry* §24.4.1. The two hydroperoxyl radicals in that chapter are
**different reactions with different index entries**: the undetected one is the one-electron
intermediate of the iron/oxygen initiation node, and the model already declines that route —
`_H2O2_PER_O2` implements the two-Fe(II) alternative UWC itself calls "more probable". The
species D-196 §5 named is the co-product of `CH₃·C(OH)H + O₂ → CH₃CHO + HO₂·`, four pages
later. Nothing was ever measured about *its* fate.

UWC's Figure 24.13 draws that step as `CH₃C·HOH  O₂ → CH₃CHO` with **no co-product at all**.
The source is silent, not negative. (Noted in passing: the body text says hydroxycinnamates
quench the 1-hydroxyethyl radical and points at Figure 24.14, whose caption says the captured
species is the **ethoxyl** radical. The source states it two ways.)
[[feedback-a-note-can-state-its-span-twice]]

### 2. The sweep, with its denominator printed

All 24 on-disk texts, every naming of the species, every hit classified and every skip counted:
**101 sentence-level hits across 17 of 24 files** — 32 biological, 7 lipid name-collisions, 4
lipid-chain, 6 initiation-limb, the rest fragments. **Zero** state the fate of the ethanol-limb
co-product. [[feedback-count-and-print-your-skips]]

What the corpus *does* hold is three fates for HO₂· in fermented beverages, all stated in other
contexts, and they disagree:

1. **→ H₂O₂**, reduced by Fe(II) or oxidising a catechol — Carrascón 2018, Marrufo 2018,
   Danilewicz 2007 scheme 8.
2. **Dismutation**, `2 HO₂· → H₂O₂ + O₂` — both beer texts.
3. **Haber-Weiss**, `O₂·⁻ + H₂O₂ → ·OH + OH⁻ + O₂` — *The Chemistry of Beer*.

### 3. Route 1 is a RATE-LAW change, not a stoichiometric one — which is why the bound is not a bound

H₂O₂ is quasi-steady-state in this module, so a limb that returns H₂O₂ feeds its own production
flux: `F = A + s·F`, i.e. `F = A/(1 − s)` with `s` the ethanol branch share. The closed forms
were checked against a turn-by-turn chain sum computed by a different method — **0 mismatches
at 1e-9** across six values of `s`.

| | O₂ uptake | SO₂:O₂ |
|---|---|---|
| shipped (D-196) | `A(1 + s)` | `(2 − s)/(1 + s)` |
| route 1 | `A/(1 − s)` | `2 − 1.5s` |
| route 2 | `A/(1 − 0.5s)` | `2 − 1.5s` |

`1/(1−s) − (1+s) = s²/(1−s) > 0`, so **route 1 draws more O₂ than the shipped constant at every
`s > 0`** — 0.07 % at the operating point, 426 % at `s = 0.9`. The activation node stops being
the rate-determining step, which is what `k_o2_depletion_total` is calibrated on.

The quinone term is what makes the ratio claim come out the way it does, and it is **derived
from this module's own rule** (`2 Fe(III) + o-diphenol → o-quinone`, so 0.5 quinone per Fe(III)
and per semiquinone), not assumed: `q = 0.5` puts the crossover at `s = (q+1)/(2−q) = 1.0`. The
first draft of this record set `q = 0` implicitly, got a crossover at `s = 0.5`, and was on its
way to recording D-196 §5's direction claim as false for low-SO₂ wine. **It is true everywhere**
— the gap is `1.5s(1−s)/(1+s) ≥ 0`, zero only at the two endpoints, 0 violations at 0.01
resolution. A wrong correction against a correct record, caught before it shipped.

### 4. Routes 1 and 2 give the IDENTICAL ratio, so the headline benchmark cannot separate them — and neither can anything else here

Both read `2 − 1.5s`. Only O₂ uptake distinguishes them analytically. Measured, it does not
distinguish them either: across route 1, route 2 and shipped the total O₂ consumed over the
hermetic run spans **0.078 %**, because D-196 §3 already established that pool is
supply-limited — a faster draw empties the same dose sooner. On the Miao ratio the two sourced
fates and shipped sit within **1.14 %**, against 2.34 % for the `preD196` edge.

**So even if a source pinned the fate tomorrow, this scenario could not tell which one it was.**
That is an independent fourth reason to refuse, and the most useful one for whoever picks the
item up. [[feedback-a-control-needs-mechanical-reach]]

### 5. Route 3 is not expressible, and the first version of that finding was a tautology

The pre-registration encoded Haber-Weiss as "the O₂ comes back, nothing else changes" —
byte-identical to the pre-D-196 tuple, so "route 3 reproduces pre-D-196" was true **by
construction** and was about to be reported as the control on the whole analytic frame. Derived
properly, Haber-Weiss *consumes* an H₂O₂ and regenerates the ·OH, making it a **third consumer
of the H₂O₂ node** rather than a modifier of the ethanol limb. `h2o2_branch_fraction` partitions
that node over exactly two weights; a third would be `k_HW·[HO₂·]`, a steady-state radical
concentration with no slot and no on-disk source. Blocked at the level of **structure**.
[[feedback-a-tautology-can-smuggle-an-attribution]]

The control became the brute-force chain sum, which reaches the closed forms by a different
method.

### 6. The pole is real, and the number the harness printed for it was an artefact

`s` reaches **exactly 1.000000** in unsulfited wine, measured — so route 1's series has a pole
there. The first run reported "dose 0, route 1: O₂ consumed 0.0000 mg/L". Both halves are
artefacts: varying the clamp I had put under the pole across six orders of magnitude moved the
answer over a **21.4 mg/L** range, and at the two tightest values the solver returned
`success: False — required step size is less than spacing between numbers`, truncating at
1199.8 h of 1440. The zero was a failed integration. **Recorded as undefined, not as a number.**

The chain terminator that would make the series converge is the hydroxycinnamate quench. D-196
§2 argued that quench needs no parameter, because it removes the acetaldehyde and the second O₂
together. **That argument does not extend here**: the quench also removes the returned H₂O₂, so
convergence depends on the quench ratio rather than on the already-calibrated acetaldehyde rate.
UWC cites Gislason et al. for it; a targeted sweep finds that name on disk **twice, both times
as a citation**.

### 7. The refusal is a green mutation, so it owes a guard — and the existing guard could not see the term

D-196's `test_the_fenton_limb_draws_one_o2_per_acetaldehyde` asserts a **ratio**, and every
recycling term scales O₂ and acetaldehyde by the same geometric factor. Measured rather than
argued, with a capped arm so the assertion actually executes instead of the fixture dying on the
pole:

| arm | 1:1 guard | flat-variant | **D-198 no-recycle** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `noop` | GREEN | GREEN | GREEN |
| `preD196` | RED | RED | GREEN |
| route 1 (uncapped) | RED* | RED* | RED |
| route 1, capped | **GREEN** | RED | RED |
| route 2 | RED | **GREEN** | RED |

\* red because the **fixture crashes** on the pole — a red that names nothing, and exactly the
distinction between a test going red and a test catching something.
[[feedback-pair-the-red-with-an-ordering-preserving-baseline]]

Each existing guard misses one fate. `test_the_fenton_limb_returns_no_h2o2_to_the_node_it_drew_from`
asserts the limb's acetaldehyde flux against `share × activation` — the identity that holds only
while the limb is a pure *consumer* of the H₂O₂ node — and catches all three while leaving
`preD196` green, which is the 1:1 guard's business rather than its own.
[[feedback-grep-finds-claims-not-guards]]

`noop` was **designed GREEN** and is green, reproducing D-196 §6's 1.107886 and its 1.1338
pre-value exactly, which is what verifies the restore between arms.
[[feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms]]

### 8. What shipped

One test, and **one struck comment**. `_O2_PER_ACETALDEHYDE` stays 1.0, the cascade stays
non-default, and **no shipped number moves** — the only source edit is the "UPPER BOUND" clause
in that constant's own comment, struck in place with the reason exactly as D-196 struck its two
false bookkeeping sentences, rather than quietly reworded.

**That edit was nearly missed, and the marker would have been the lie.** This record's first
version claimed `Corrects: D-196 — the clause in §5 **and in the comment**` while changing only
`DECISIONS.md` and the test file. `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that `Corrects` means the fix shipped
and `Flags` means the code still carries the old behaviour, so the marker was a `Flags` wearing
the other name — and `tests/test_decisions_index.py` validates only that a target exists and is
earlier, so it passed green **by construction**. D-196's own amendment §A had to withdraw a
semantically wrong marker for the same reason. The comment is now struck, which makes the marker
true; the alternative was to split it into `Corrects` + `Flags`.

Also derived rather than reasoned, on D-196 §D's precedent: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` needs no
change. Its own snippet re-run gives wine cascade 64 processes / 94 slots, beer cascade 28 / 57,
19 parameter files, 77 test files, 80 kinetics implementations — every count already in the
document. This beat adds no Process, slot, parameter file or test file; it adds one test
*function* to an existing file, which that document does not enumerate.

### Still open

The activation node's missing pH term (refused at D-150 — do not re-propose). The quinone
branching, still needing Nikolantonaki & Waterhouse 2012 or a third source. The recycling limb
is **no longer open as an unsourced item**: it is refused on four measured grounds — no source
for this limb's co-product, three incompatible sourced fates, a pole with no published

## D-199 — The quinone branching, re-opened and half-closed: the paper D-145 said had to be bought has had its key figure on disk since before D-141, it ranks two of the model's five quinone consumers, and the one taking 85 % of the node is not a nucleophile so no figure can ever rank it

**Corrects:** D-145 — its "the pull is Nikolantonaki & Waterhouse 2012" framing, and the three code sites carrying it (`k_quinone_polymerization`'s uncertainty note and provenance source in `aging.yaml`, and `QuinonePolymerization`'s docstring). That paper's Figure 24.12 is reprinted with permission, with its full caption, in *Understanding Wine Chemistry* 2nd ed. p. 331 — a book in the corpus since before D-141. The block was bibliographic in name only.
**Corrects:** D-141 — `QuinoneSulfonation`'s product identity. Its docstring said "bisulfite adds nucleophilically to the quinone ring"; UWC §24.4.3.2 gives that as the **minor** product at wine pH, with **>90 % reduced back to the o-diphenol**. Struck in place; `_SO2_PER_QUINONE` stays 1.0 because both routes consume one bisulfite per quinone.

### 1. The item, and why it looked bought rather than blocked

D-145 recorded `quinone`'s consumer split as **asserted, not measured**, and named the required
pull: Nikolantonaki & Waterhouse 2012, *"A method to quantify quinone reaction rates with wine
relevant nucleophiles"*. Roughly fifty records carried it forward. `aging.yaml` still said *"The
pull that would settle it is the same one the lifetime needs"*, and the prohibitions file said
only "Quinone branching **NOT settled**".

Nothing was re-swept. A single grep for quantitative quinone statements over the 24 on-disk texts
returned UWC §24.4.3, whose Figure 24.12 **is that paper's figure**, reprinted under ACS
permission. This is the third time a "blocked on external sourcing" item has turned out to be
sitting on disk (D-191, D-196, now this), and the second where the record named the source by
title. [[feedback-check-the-blocker-is-still-blocking]]

### 2. What the figure actually contains, and what it can never contain

First-order rate constants `k_Nu` for ten nucleophiles against 4-methyl-1,2-benzoquinone, in
model wine at 10 °C, with significance letters. The **letters are printed**; the values are a
log-scale plot read by eye to ±0.3 decades and are recorded as CONSTRUCTED, never quoted as
literals. [[feedback-pin-the-band-not-the-nominal]]

Of the model's five quinone consumers it ranks **two**:

| consumer | share of the node | ranked by Fig. 24.12? |
|---|---|---|
| `quinone_polymerization` | **84.78 %** | **no — and cannot be** |
| `quinone_sulfonation` | 15.21 % | yes (SO2, letter `e`) |
| `quinone_anthocyanin_fading` | 0.69 % red / 0 white | no |
| `quinone_strecker_degradation` | 0.0025 % | yes (Met, Phe, letter `a`) |
| `quinone_ellagitannin_oxidation` | 0 | no |

The dominant consumer is unrankable **in principle**, not by omission: `QuinonePolymerization` is
by construction *"the fate of quinone that NO nucleophile captured"*, first-order in the pool and
gated on no co-substrate. A table of nucleophile addition rates has no row for it.

Two further gaps compound this. Ascorbic acid and glutathione carry letter `e` **alongside SO2**
— the joint top group — and neither has a slot, a parameter or a Process anywhere in the model
(grepped: zero of each). UWC's own between-nucleophile argument runs through exactly those two.
And the figure's phloroglucinol entry is the **flavan-3-ol A-ring addition**, a co-substrate
reaction the model has no Process for at all: `tannin` never consumes `quinone`.

**The first draft of this analysis mapped phloroglucinol onto `quinone_polymerization`** and would
have reported a six-decade contradiction against the model's largest consumer. Both end in brown
pigment; they are different reactions. Caught by reading the Process rather than its name.
[[feedback-name-the-field-your-predicate-read]]

**So the status changes from "blocked on a pull" to "blocked on structure"** — and the note's own
sentence *"NOTHING IN HAND ADJUDICATES WHICH"*, of the two ways to close the fate gap, survives
the pull arriving. The correction must not overclaim in that direction either.

### 3. The branching IS the headline, measured by mutation

`k_quinone_polymerization` is a constant `QuinoneSulfonation`'s rate law never reads. Scaling it
walks the benchmark SO2:O2 ratio across and out of the entire measured range:

| `k_poly` × | bisulfite's share | SO2:O2 | vs Miao 1.0972-1.6621 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **10** (band high edge) | 1.86 % | **0.9738** | below the floor, and below the 1:1 limit |
| 3 | 5.86 % | 1.0144 | below |
| **1** (nominal) | 15.21 % | **1.1079** | in band |
| **0.1** (band low edge) | 59.69 % | **1.5172** | in band |
| 0.01 | 92.75 % | 1.7481 | above |
| 1e-4 | 99.90 % | 1.7866 | asymptote |

7 of 8 sample points at every setting; the skipped one is the instant the O2 dose lands, where
`[quinone]` is exactly 0. [[feedback-count-and-print-your-skips]]

**The 1.7481 is refused on the record.** At `×0.01` the model lands within 3 % of Danilewicz's
1.7 mode, which is the most seductive number in this beat. D-138 and D-141 both say **1.7 must
EMERGE from partial quinone capture and never be fitted**. Adopting it would fit one speculative
constant to one dataset's mode. Seen, declined, written down so it is not rediscovered as an
opportunity. Note also the asymptote is **1.7866, not 2.0**: bisulfite never wins the whole H2O2
node, and D-196's second O2 inflates the denominator.

### 4. The high edge of that constant's own band leaves every measured wine — a SECOND instance, not D-174's

`k_quinone_polymerization` is banded a full order each way. At the **high** edge the headline is
**0.9738**: below Miao's floor, below Danilewicz's range, and below the **1:1 blocked-quinone
limit** this file treats as the lower asymptote.

Scope, narrowly: the parameter is sampled whenever its Process is active, so this is live in a
**cascade ensemble** — but the cascade is non-default and **no shipped test runs a cascade
ensemble** (`simulate_ensemble` appears in 9 test files; the only one also mentioning the cascade
uses it in a band-edge probe). Reachable in a configuration nothing currently runs: weaker than a
live defect, stronger than hypothetical.

**Not D-174's instance.** That one is `k_o2_depletion_total`, high edge 1.0655. Two different
constants, each independently taking this ratio below Miao's floor. Do not merge them.

### 5. The product identity was wrong, and the error runs in fork D2's favour

UWC at wine pH: the sulfonate is minor, **>90 % is reduction back to the o-diphenol**.
`OxygenActivation` never debits the o-diphenol that becomes the quinone (fork D2, *"its carbon
comes from the untracked o-diphenol pool"*). Under reduction that pool is **regenerated**, so not
debiting it is *correct* for the major route — the source corroborates the fork rather than
breaking it. The residual sulfonate route is the part that genuinely removes a phenolic for good
and is not booked; recorded, not built, because no shipped pool is its substrate.

**Inert by construction**, which is why it is a docstring fix: either product debits `quinone`
and `so2_total` at exactly 1:1 and both products are off every ledger.

### 6. The one ordering the figure ranks is off by ~6.4 decades, and it does not matter

Concentration-weighted at the operating point, the model implies SO2 is **2.233 decades** faster
than the amino acids; the figure implies **8.597**. The model's Strecker law is first-order in
quinone with a depletion gate rather than bilinear in the amino acid, so that normalisation is an
**equivalence, not an identity** — and the printed content needs none of it (`a` vs `e`, plus
*"orders of magnitude slower than the reaction of GSH and SO2"*).

**Magnitude: inconsequential.** That route takes 0.0025 % of the node; correcting it would take it
to ~1e-9. The content is a mechanism statement — the quinone→Strecker route cannot run in a
well-sulfited wine, which is UWC's own regime caveat — and is deliberately not made a second
headline.

### 7. What shipped

Four struck claims (three "pending/would settle it" sites, one product identity), and **one
test**. No parameter value moves; the cascade stays non-default.

The guard asserts the branching's grip on the headline: monotone fall of the ratio in
`k_quinone_polymerization`, the nominal and low edge in Miao's band, the high edge below it. Its
band edges are **derived from the parameter store, never transcribed** from the note (the D-154
idiom), so re-banding in YAML moves the guard instead of leaving it pinned to stale numbers. It
discriminates in both directions on values already measured: re-anchoring the nominal one order
down makes the low edge 1.7481, above Miao's ceiling; one order up makes the nominal 0.9738,
failing the in-band assert. Its docstring says explicitly that a red means the sensitivity moved
and this record must be re-measured — not that the assertion should be relaxed.
[[feedback-a-threshold-cannot-separate-same-sign-regimes]]

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` needs no change, **derived rather than reasoned** on D-198's precedent —
the first draft of this record asserted it. Its own snippet re-run gives wine cascade 64 processes /
94 slots, beer cascade 28 / 57, 19 parameter files, 77 test files, 80 kinetics implementations: every
count already in the document. This beat adds no Process, slot, parameter file or test file — one test
*function* joins an existing file, which that document does not enumerate.

### Still open

The branching itself, now blocked on **structure** rather than on a pull: an absolute rate for the
no-nucleophile polymerisation fate, and slots for ascorbate and glutathione, which the figure puts
in the joint top group with SO2. The activation node's missing pH term stays refused (D-150).

## D-200 — Glutathione priced instead of built: at the level UWC's own Chapter 5 gives, it takes 0.32 % of the quinone node, so D-199's two-slot structural gap is really one slot — and the benchmark's in-band pass turns out to be held open by the absence of the other

**Corrects:** D-199 — its pairing of ascorbate and glutathione as a single two-member structural
gap ("two further gaps compound this … UWC's own between-nucleophile argument runs through
exactly those two", and the *Still open* line asking for "slots for ascorbate and glutathione").
The two are not symmetric and only one of them is a gap in the branching. Letter `e` is a
**model-wine, equal-concentration** statement; a flux is `k × [S]`, and at wine concentrations
glutathione is a **0.32 %** consumer of the node. Ascorbate, at the dose the same page prints, is
an **8.09 %** consumer. Asking for both slots overstates the structural deficit by a member that
cannot move the node.

### 1. Why this was priced before it was built

D-199 closed with the quinone branching "blocked on structure": Figure 24.12 puts ascorbate (AA)
and glutathione (GSH) in the joint top group with SO2, and the model has zero slots, zero
parameters and zero Processes for either. The obvious successor beat is to build them. It was
deliberately not taken as a build, for two reasons that were both stated before any code ran
(`PREREGISTER.md`).

First, **regime**. UWC is explicit that the GSH-quinone story is the *must* stage under
polyphenol oxidase — caftaric acid quinone plus GSH giving grape reaction product. The model's
cascade is the **non-enzymatic wine** node. Most must GSH is already spent as GRP before the wine
node exists, so the number that decides everything is the post-fermentation level, not the must
level. Pricing this on must GSH would have been the wrong regime, quietly.

Second, **the beat lands on the guard D-199 had just pinned**. A sixth quinone consumer moves the
SO2:O2 ratio by construction. That is fine when predicted and attributed, and a problem when it
arrives as a surprise red on an assertion whose own docstring says a red means D-199 must be
re-measured. Measuring first makes the movement a prediction rather than a discovery.

### 2. The concentration that decides it — and the book disagrees with itself by 10×

UWC §24.4.3.3 (p. 332) argues that SO2 out-competes GSH in real wine from the concentrations:
*"because of the higher concentration in wine of free SO2 (typically 30 mg/L, 0.5 mM) as compared
to GSH (**<30 mg/L, <0.1 mM**; Chapter 5), the former is expected to be of greater importance."*

Chapter 5 — the chapter that sentence cites — says: *"The concentration of GSH in wine is
**typically no more than a few mg/L**."*

The bound is **~10× loose against its own source**. Both statements support the conclusion UWC
draws, so the looseness is invisible inside UWC's own argument; it becomes visible the instant
the number is used quantitatively, which is what this beat does. Pricing GSH off the Chapter 24
bound gives 3.15 % of the node; pricing it off Chapter 5's actual level gives **0.32 %**. This is
the [[feedback-a-note-can-state-its-span-twice]] shape found in the *source* rather than in our
notes — and worth carrying, because D-199's receipts file transcribed the Chapter 24 bound in
good faith and it is the number a future reader would reach for. (No marker is owed for that: the
loose bound never entered the D-199 *record*, only its temp-directory transcription.)

Must-stage GSH, for completeness and as the regime that does **not** bind: 15-100 mg/L, mean 44
(UWC Ch. 5), and 14-102 mg/L (*Biology of Microorganisms on Grapes, in Must and in Wine*).

### 3. The measurement

A throwaway `Process` was injected into the compiled cascade: a competing nucleophile held at
**fixed** concentration — never depleting, so every share is an **upper bound** — reacting with
the quinone pool through the **same** bilinear law and the **same** `k_so2_oxidation` that
`QuinoneSulfonation` uses, scaled by the figure's relative rate. The shipped law takes its
nucleophile in g/L, so the effective molar constant is `k_so2_oxidation × M_SO2`; Figure 24.12
compares nucleophiles at equal *molar* concentration, and the bridge is applied explicitly. The
headline is read by calling the **shipped** `_run` with `compile_scenario` monkeypatched, never
re-derived (D-145's prohibition). Nothing in `src/` was touched.

| arm | added nucleophile's share | sulfonation | polymerisation | SO2:O2 | move |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | — | 15.2141 % | 84.7833 % | 1.107886 | — |
| null control, Process at C = 0 | 0.0000 % | 15.2141 % | 84.7833 % | 1.107886 | +0.0000 % |
| **GSH 3 mg/L** (Ch. 5's level) | **0.3168 %** | — | — | 1.107434 | −0.0409 % |
| GSH 5 mg/L | 0.5269 % | — | — | 1.107135 | −0.0678 % |
| GSH 20 mg/L (OIV-permitted dose) | 2.0745 % | 14.9147 % | 83.0083 % | 1.104925 | −0.2673 % |
| GSH 0.1 mM (Ch. 24's bound) | 3.1523 % | 14.7589 % | 82.0864 % | 1.103383 | −0.4065 % |
| GSH 0.1 mM, letter-faithful k = 1.0 | 2.5204 % | 14.8503 % | 82.6268 % | 1.104287 | −0.3249 % |
| GSH 102 mg/L (**must** ceiling) | 9.7442 % | 13.8022 % | 76.4513 % | 1.093904 | −1.2621 % |
| **ascorbate 60 mg/L** (UWC's dose) | **8.0915 %** | 14.0427 % | 77.8635 % | 1.096288 | −1.0469 % |

Shares are meaned over Miao's eight sample points; **7 of 8** carried positive quinone
consumption in **every** arm — the skipped one is the window-open sample, before the first O2
dose — so the arms are like-for-like [[feedback-count-and-print-your-skips]]. The **null control
is bitwise identical to the baseline**, which is the arm that proves the harness is not red by
construction [[feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms]].

**The non-depleting simplification is a tight bound, not a vacuous one.** Total quinone through
the whole node over the window is 0.4244 mmol/L; the injected arm captures 0.0132 (GSH at 0.1 mM)
and 0.0339 (AA), so a real pool would fall by **13.2 %** and **10.0 %**. The bound therefore
overstates a depleting pool's mean share by ~5-7 %, well inside the figure's own ±0.3-decade
uncertainty. **No verdict here turns on it.**

**And the verdict does not turn on the disputed concentration either.** It is unchanged across
the entire 10× span the two chapters disagree over: 3 mg/L → 0.32 %, 30 mg/L → 3.15 %. Both are
far too small to earn a slot, a parameter and a Process. Nor does it turn on the rate constant —
the letter-faithful `k_rel = 1.0` and the eye-read 1.26 differ by 25 % on a sub-1 % share. **No
further sourcing effort on the GSH level is warranted**, and that is the reason to stop rather
than an excuse for having stopped.

**Verdict 1: glutathione is MEASURED and NOT BUILT.** At the level its own book gives, it takes
0.32 % of one node — 1/48th of sulfonation's share and 1/268th of polymerisation's — and moves the
model's headline by 0.04 %. Even the OIV-permitted 20 mg/L *addition* reaches only 2.07 %.

### 4. The margin the benchmark was standing on, and what holds it open

Miao's band is (1.0972, 1.6621) and its floor is a **printed** table value, not a constructed
edge. The nominal clears that floor by **0.9646 %**. That margin had never been stated.

Both the ascorbate arm and the must-ceiling arm **consume the entire headroom**, landing a few
ten-thousandths below the floor. The word is deliberately *consume* and not *breach*: AA misses
by 0.0009, and the 10 % depletion correction above is larger than the miss, so which side of the
line it finally lands on is not resolved here and must not be asserted. What is resolved is that
**one unbuilt top-group nucleophile, at the concentration the book prints, is worth the whole
margin** [[feedback-pin-the-band-not-the-nominal]].

So the guard's in-band pass is not held open by anything the benchmark controls. It is held open
by the **absence of ascorbate from the quinone node**. That is a scope claim the file did not
make, and it is what shipped [[feedback-a-margin-is-a-claim-about-what-holds-it-open]].

### 5. Ascorbate: both limbs push the same way, and the first draft had it backwards

UWC p. 332 also records ascorbate's pro-oxidant flip: it *"does not rapidly consume H2O2, the
other major product of wine oxidation — it actually **reacts with oxygen and produces H2O2** — so
its use without SO2 can lead to enhanced browning."*

The first draft of this record reasoned that ascorbate's two limbs therefore **oppose** on the
headline — quinone capture starving sulfonation (down), peroxide production feeding bisulfite
(up) — and invoked [[feedback-build-the-term-that-makes-agreement-worse-first]] to argue the
capture limb must be built first so the other could not be credited with a cancellation. **That
was wrong, and it was caught by measuring the sign instead of arguing it.**

The benchmark already brackets it. `mode="blocked"` traps the quinone route and leaves bisulfite
only the **peroxide** equivalent — which *is* the per-O2 yield of an ascorbate→H2O2 channel,
because that reaction makes peroxide and **no quinone**. It reads **0.954696** SO2 per O2 against
the real mix's **1.107886**. Replacing a quinone-bearing O2 with a peroxide-only O2 therefore
*lowers* the ratio as well.

**Verdict 2: both ascorbate limbs push the headline down, so neither can pay for the other.** The
correct statement is stronger than the cancellation one it replaces: ascorbate cannot enter the
cascade at all without re-opening the band question. The D-181 lesson does not apply here — there
are not two terms of opposite sign, there are two terms of the same sign.

### 6. The branching denominator is not the whole test — and H2S is where that bites

Every share in this beat is a share of **quinone** consumption. That is the right denominator for
the branching question and the wrong one for "is this Process worth building": a consumer taking
a negligible share of quinone can still be a dominant sink for **its own** reactant. **Verdict 1
is therefore scoped — glutathione is not worth building *as a quinone consumer*** — and it is
safe at that scope precisely because no GSH slot exists, so there is no pool to deplete and no
downstream observable that could see it.

**H2S is not protected by that argument.** It is the fourth member of the figure's top group
(letter `e`, log k ~-0.9) and the only one whose slot the model **already has**; D-199's own
transcription records "no quinone-H2S Process exists". Arithmetic on this beat's measured
quantities — node throughput 0.4244 mmol/L, window-mean free bisulfite 0.589 mM, sulfonation's
15.2141 % — gives a quinone-H2S route **0.01512 %** of the node at a 10 µg/L fault level, which
is invisible, while removing **21.87 % of the sulfide pool** over a single oxidation challenge.
The pool fraction is **constant** in the pool size, because share and removal scale together.

That asymmetry is recorded, not acted on: it is an **estimate, not a measurement** (no such
Process exists to run), and it is a **separate beat**.

### 7. Pre-registration scorecard — and the hit that was two errors cancelling

`PREREGISTER.md` was written before any code ran. Five hits, two misses, one half-miss, one moot.

**P1 predicted GSH ≈ 0.47 % and the measurement is 0.32-0.53 %. The hit is worthless and the
reason is the finding.** The prediction was built from `sulfonation = 1.86 %` — which is the
**low edge** of `k_quinone_polymerization`'s band, not the **nominal 15.21 %**, an 8.2× error —
multiplied by a GSH concentration 10× too high. Two wrong inputs of opposite sign, cancelling to
within 1.5×. Either alone would have missed by an order of magnitude. The source of the first is
exact: the standing memory row prints the sensitivity as "1.86 % → 15.21 % → 59.69 %" and the
first number was read as the nominal. This is [[feedback-pin-the-band-not-the-nominal]] committed
against a record written to teach that very lesson, one beat later.

- **P2** (AA ≈ 1.3 %) — **MISS, 6.2×**; measured 8.09 %. Same low-edge anchor, uncompensated.
  Re-anchored it predicts 10.3 %, the residual being the denominator effect of adding a consumer.
- **P3** (the figure and UWC's prose cannot both be right) — **CONFIRMED, with the resolution
  found.** At equal rate constants ascorbate's 0.34 mM cannot out-flux bisulfite's 0.5 mM. UWC's
  "ascorbate appears to react faster than SO2" rests on ref [41]'s **real-wine observation**, not
  on Figure 24.12, which is a model-wine equal-concentration instrument.
- **P4** (GSH keeps the guard green) — **HIT**, −0.04 % against 0.96 % of headroom.
- **P5** (AA moves less than the band) — **HALF-MISS, on the wrong criterion.** AA moves less than
  the band's *width* (0.565) as predicted, but width is not what binds: the distance to the
  **nearest edge** is 0.96 %, and AA's −1.05 % is worth all of it. A margin is measured to the
  nearest edge, never to the span.
- **P6** (record, do not build, for GSH) — **HIT**.
- **P7** (polymerisation stays > 80 %) — **HIT** at every wine-realistic arm, 83.0-84.8 %. It
  falls to 76.5 % / 77.9 % only in the must-ceiling and ascorbate arms.
- **P8** (the real ascorbate blocker is the H2O2 side) — **HIT on the blocker, MISS on its sign**;
  see §5. The prediction found the right term and got its direction backwards.
- **P9** (products off every ledger) — **MOOT, and recorded as untested rather than as a hit.**
  Nothing shipped, so no conservation test ever ran against it
  [[feedback-conceded-caveats-are-not-coverage]].

### 8. What shipped

**One docstring.** No parameter, no slot, no Process, no new test. The D-199 guard now states the
margin it is standing on (0.9646 %), what was priced against it (GSH 0.32 %, AA 8.09 %), and that
what holds it open is the absence of ascorbate from the node rather than anything the file
controls.

**No guard is owed.** The movement this beat identified is *already* detected: the existing
`MIAO_BAND[0] <= nominal` assertion is precisely what would fire if a future beat added ascorbate.
A margin assertion on top of it would pin tighter than the band and go brittle against solver
noise, which is the failure [[feedback-pin-tolerance-vs-solver-tolerance]] and the standing
pin-the-band rule both warn about. What was missing was never detection — it was the *statement*
of what the detection depends on.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` needs no change, derived rather than reasoned on D-198/D-199's precedent:
this beat adds no Process, slot, parameter file or test file, and does not touch `src/`.

### 9. Still open

The branching, unmoved and still blocked on **structure**: an absolute rate for the
no-nucleophile polymerisation fate. What D-200 changes is the size of that structural gap —
