### 8. What this leaves open — unchanged, and still the owner's

**Nothing here resolves D-216 §11.** Beer's two speed anchors still conflict, the model still sits on the one that is an acceptance criterion rather than a measurement, and the choice is still the owner's. What changed is that the conflict is now known to be **robust to the one ambiguity that could have dissolved it**, and the escape route that might have made the choice unnecessary is **measured closed for want of a source** rather than left open as a hopeful "blocked pending literature". The corpus has been searched, the denominator is on the record, and it should not be searched again without a new text.

## D-218 — the published trial that adjudicates beer's two speed anchors finds the brief too slow at every reading, and the one reading that saves it is the one the archive itself calls anomalous: beer's uptake rate now turns on an unsourced per-cell dry mass this repo ships two values of, 5.6× apart

**Flags:** D-216 — §7 sizes the per-cell dry-mass discrepancy as *"~2× the textbook 40-60 pg"*. Against the repo's OWN wine conversion (18 pg/cell, `test_validation_varela2004.py`) it is 5.6×, and §4 below measures that this gap, not the literature, decides D-216 §11. Both values still ship.

Opened by the owner on D-216 §11 / D-217 §8, verbatim: *"which yardstick beer's speed should be calibrated against — the project brief's 5-7 day target, or the published trial. Nothing here decides it — search for more published data."* Authorised scope was a **search and an adjudication**. **No `src/` change, no parameter VALUE change, no recalibration, no change to §2.2's benchmark — four tests and one provenance repair.**

Working files: `M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d218-beer-speed-yardstick\` — `FINDINGS.md`, `probe_yardstick.py` … `probe_bracket.py`, `mutate_guards.py`, `kveik.xml` (Foster's full text via Europe PMC), `pdf/`.

### 1. The framing correction that came first: the two anchors are not the same kind of statement

They were never rivals to be chosen between. §2.2's anchor is **terminal** — one number, days to 1.010. Tyrell's is a **trajectory** — the fraction of fermentable extract gone on each of days 1-7. They also differ in gravity, temperature *and* pitch simultaneously. So a useful third source has to carry the whole tuple: gravity, temperature, pitch, early-limb fraction, days-to-terminal. A curve without a stated pitch is a fourth incomparable anchor, not an adjudication — which is why most of what a search returns is useless here.

Two free local checks ran before any search. The loose `applsci-11-01157-v2.pdf` in the temp tree **was** inside D-217's 26-file denominator and is a wine polyphenol review, not a missed beer source — closed. And **Tyrell's days 3 and 4 were already on disk**: D-215 §4 carries 0.800 / 0.900, which the shipped `TYRELL_FLUX_FRACTION` omits. With them the measured daily increments are .150 / .444 / .206 / .100 / .103 — peaking on day 2, then tailing. The model's are .086 / .126 / .163 / .185 / .168, peaking on **day 4**. [[feedback-re-read-the-source-you-already-mined]]

### 2. What the search found, and the ceilings inside it

Four sources, none previously in the archive.

| # | source | product | gravity | temp | pitch | what it gives |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | **Foster et al. 2022**, *Front. Microbiol.* 13:747546, doi:10.3389/fmicb.2022.747546 | three **Beer 1** clade commercial ale controls (Cali Ale, Vermont Ale, Kölsch) | **12.5 °P = 1.045** hopped all-malt | **22 and 12 °C** (+ six more) | **1.2 × 10⁷ cells/mL**, counted | *"reached SG < 1.01 after only 3 days"*; the 12 °C controls complete *"within 10 days"* |
| S2 | Reid et al. 2021, *Fermentation* 7(1) 13, **Table 2** — *their* fit to dataset 5, the industrial series of Speers et al. 2003 | Australian **lager**, 19 trials, 228 points | 14.1 °P | 10 °C **starting** temperature, profile not printed | not stated | a fitted 3-parameter logistic: `ADFe 0.8371, B 0.06372 h⁻¹, M 51.22 h` |
| S3 | Rodríguez-Guerrero et al. 2022, *Foods* 11:3602 | pilot beer, 17 L | 72-88 g/L sugar | 19, 19, 21, 28 °C | 0.529-0.705 g/L | four batches run **54, 72, 72, 96 h** |
| S4 | O'Brien et al. 2024, *Modelling* 5(1) 201 | 200 L pilot IPA, US-05 | not stated | 22 °C | not stated | *"primary fermentation for a typical IPA typically requires only 3-5 days"* |

**S1 is the one that adjudicates**, and it is a better fit to the question than anything hoped for: its wort is within 0.003 SG of §2.2's own, its pitch is counted rather than described, its two temperatures are the **same three strains** on the **same wort at the same pitch**, and its target gravity is **1.010** — taken from Parker 2008, so the one part of the brief that turns out to be independently sourced is the finish line, not the duration. St. Lucifer (Beer 2 clade) *"never reached an FG < 1.01, regardless of temperature"* and is correctly outside both statements, so the pair really is same-strain.

**Both of S1's numbers are ceilings, and reading them as durations is the trap this beat nearly fell into twice.** Figure 2's panels are **timepoints** — 12, 48, 72 and 120 h — with temperature on the x-axis. *"after only 3 days ... (Figure 2C)"* cites the **72 h panel**: the strains were below target when someone next looked. If they were still above at 48 h — which *"only"* implies but does not state — the true endpoint is somewhere in (48, 72] h. And *"within 10 days"* at 12 °C is the **incubation length** (*"Incubations were for 5 days, except for the 12°C fermentations (10 days)"*). Neither is a measured duration. This propagates into §3 and §4 and both say so.

**The withdrawn row.** An earlier draft ran the engine **isothermally at 10 °C** against S2 and reported 17.5 d and a 6.9× day-2 shortfall as the headline, concluding that the error tracks temperature and `E_a_uptake` is therefore the defect. Reid et al. write *"starting temperature of 10 °C"*, and Speers' own abstract turns on *"the **starting** temperature increased the fermentation rate"* — phrasing that only makes sense for a free-rising industrial lager. Running a start temperature as an isothermal set-point is **D-217 §3's failure mode one source over** (*"pitched at 15 °C"* read as *"ferments at 15 °C"*), caught before shipping rather than after. S2's normalised course survives — it does not depend on knowing the profile — but every model-vs-S2 comparison is void and none replaces it.

**S2 corroborates Tyrell's shape, weakly and with a caveat that must travel with it.** Converted from the printed logistic, S2 reads 0.150 / 0.449 / 0.790 / 0.945 / 0.988 on days 1-5 against Tyrell's 0.150 / 0.594 / 0.800 / 0.900 / 1.003. An industrial lager and a tube trial, different decades, countries, species and vessels, land within 0.045 of each other on days 3-5 and both are essentially finished by day 5. **But do not call this two independent measured courses.** A 3-parameter logistic is symmetric and peaks at its inflection *by construction* (M = 51.22 h ≈ day 2.1), so its "front-loaded then tailing" shape is the fitted form's, not the wort's — the more so because those same authors found the **asymmetric** 5-parameter form beat the symmetric one on 3 of 7 industrial datasets. And the day-1 agreement "to three decimals" is a coincidence between two figure-derived numbers, not corroboration; Tyrell's 0.150 is read off Fig. 4. [[feedback-a-derived-yield-encodes-its-rate-law]]

### 3. S1's temperature pair discriminates NOTHING — and the identity that looks structural is a crossing

S1 gives the archive its first same-yeast two-temperature pair, the exact shape D-217 §2 searched 26 files for and did not find. A within-source **ratio** is immune to both the per-cell-mass fork and any species confound, so it is the one confound-free test available. The model's ratio is **2.21** against a bound of ≤3.33, and an earlier draft of this record reported that as a pass.

**It is not a result, and §12's first guard exists to stop it being read as one.** The bound is cleared at *every* printed value of `E_a_uptake`:

| `E_a_uptake` | bare Arrhenius factor | model ratio @ 0.216 g/L | model ratio @ 1.2 g/L | vs the tightest bound (3.33) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30,000 (low edge) | 1.535 | 1.701 | 1.605 | clears |
| **55,100 (shipped)** | **2.198** | **2.224** | **2.217** | **clears** |
| 63,000 (high edge) | 2.460 | 2.429 | 2.456 | clears |
| 90,000 (out of band, 1.43×) | 3.619 | 3.334 | 3.534 | **fires** |

All on a **6-minute** grid, and that is not a detail. A duration read off a grid is quantised, so
a *ratio* of two durations carries a quantum of about `(1 + ratio) / (24 · per_hour · d_hot)` —
**~0.04 on an hourly grid at the heavy pitch**, which is larger than two of the three effects
below. [[feedback-read-a-fast-curve-on-a-fixed-grid]]

The first value that fires is **out of band**. D-216 §10 and D-217 §6 both record that an out-of-band mutation arm tests nothing; this is the same fact stated about the *literature*. And the bound is looser still than 3.33: by §2 both of S1's endpoints are ceilings, so an upper bound on `d12/d22` needs a **lower** bound on `d22`, which the paper does not give — take the open end of the sampling interval and the bound is 10/2 = 5.0. The 90,000 arm ships as the guard's **positive control**, because without it "everything clears" is indistinguishable from a broken predicate. [[feedback-a-null-result-needs-a-positive-control]]

**So D-217's `E_a_uptake` refusal needs no re-opening**, and the earlier draft's contrary claim — that the error is monotone in temperature and the activation energy is therefore the defect — is **refuted, not softened**. It rested entirely on the withdrawn row.

**The near-identity at the nominal is a crossing, not a law.** At the shipped value the ratio sits within ~1 % of the bare Arrhenius factor with no model in it, which reads as a structural fact: the ferment uptake-limited end to end, duration inversely proportional to rate. Sweeping shows otherwise. At **0.216 g/L** the residual `ratio / arrhenius` runs **1.108 → 1.012 → 0.987** across the printed band and crosses 1.0 at ≈58,000 J/mol, so the nominal sits short of a crossing rather than on a law. Pinning the identity would have pinned a coincidence — the same trap D-217 §2 named around −90,000 J/mol, one beat later and in the opposite direction.

**Which pitch that series is read on is load-bearing, and a first draft of this record got it wrong.** The crossing *moves with the pitch* — ≈58 kJ/mol at 0.216 g/L, ≈62 kJ/mol at 1.2 g/L — and at the heavy pitch it is **not resolvable at all**: the residual only reaches 0.9982 at the band's high edge, a margin of 0.0018 against a 6-minute quantum of 0.0044. A guard asserting the crossing there would have been reading the grid. The shipped guard therefore runs on the **light** pitch, where the same edge reads 0.9874 against a quantum of 0.0024, and it asserts the margins exceed the quantum before it asserts the crossing. The earlier draft quoted the light-pitch series beside a heavy-pitch guard; both halves were real numbers and the pairing was not.

**Pitch-invariance is local, and it is a defect signature rather than a pass.** Across the fork's full 5.6× pitch span the ratio moves 0.007 at the nominal and 0.10 at the low band edge. Real ferments do show a pitch-dependent temperature response; a model whose response is pitch-blind at its shipped value is agreeing with a bound for a reason the data does not have. **The apparent perfect invariance was the grid.** On the hourly grid the nominal spread reads −0.0002, which is below the 1/24 d quantum; on a 6-minute grid it reads +0.0070. The guard asserts the finer number. [[feedback-read-a-fast-curve-on-a-fixed-grid]]

### 4. The fork: §2.2's window survives in ONE of eight bracket cells, and it is the doubtful one

Everything above is preamble to this. S1 answers D-216 §11 on the brief's own terms — same target gravity, a wort within 0.003 SG — and the answer at every reading is **faster than the brief**. What stops that from being a verdict is that the engine needs S1's cells/mL as a g/L.

**The repo ships two conversions, 5.6× apart, and neither is sourced to a measurement.** `test_validation_varela2004.py` and `test_validation_palma2012.py` convert both wine pitches at *"the standard ~18 pg/cell S. cerevisiae dry-weight figure"*. `beer_generic.yaml`'s `mu_max` note records that `TYRELL_SCENARIO`'s 1.0 g/L against Tyrell's counted 9.96 × 10⁶ cells/mL implies **~100 pg/cell**. D-216 §7 called that *"~2× the textbook 40-60 pg"* — true of the textbook range, and it understates the repo's own internal disagreement by a factor of nearly three. That is what the `Flags:` marker is for.

Bisecting the `q_sugar_max` that puts the model on S1's endpoint, per reading and over both ends of S1's sampling interval:

| per-cell mass | pitch g/L | `q*` for d₂₂ = 3 d | §2.2 then reads | `q*` for d₂₂ = 2 d | §2.2 then reads |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **18 pg — the repo's own wine figure** | 0.216 | **1.500 = CEILING** | 2.58 d | **1.500 = CEILING** | 2.58 d |
| 40 pg — textbook low | 0.480 | 0.924 | 3.63 d | **1.500 = CEILING** | 2.58 d |
| 50 pg | 0.600 | 0.818 | 4.00 d | 1.462 | 2.63 d |
| 100 pg — implied by Tyrell | 1.200 | 0.560 | **5.50 d ✔** | 0.897 | 3.71 d |

**One cell of eight survives 5-7 d**, and it needs both of its coordinates to be the generous one: the per-cell mass the archive itself flags as anomalous, *and* S1's 72 h **sample** read as an exact duration. Move either and the window breaks. At 18 pg/cell it is not even reachable — 1.500 is the printed band's ceiling, a **saturation and not a crossing**, and at the ceiling the model still needs 3.04 d, missing by 1.4 %. Tabling 1.500 beside 0.924 as though both were fitted values would repeat D-177's error. [[feedback-a-cap-being-written-to-cannot-be-raised]]

Worth stating plainly because it is the beat's cleanest number: **at the archive's own 100 pg reading, with no knob touched at all, the shipped model reaches S1's endpoint in 3.33 d against a published ≤3.** An 11 % miss on a third-party trial, on a wort the benchmark was written for. The model is not badly wrong about beer's speed. The **brief** is.

### 5. What the new data does establish cleanly: the early limb, again

Not the rate scale, and not the temperature response.

1. The temperature response is untested by this literature (§3), so nothing licenses touching it.
2. The day-2 shortfall survives **every defensible pitch**. On Tyrell's wort the model's day-2 fraction runs 0.112 / 0.211 / 0.248 / 0.383 / 0.685 at pitches 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.2 / 2.0 / 4.0 against a measured 0.594; closing it needs ~2.7 g/L against Tyrell's counted 9.96 × 10⁶ cells/mL, i.e. ~270 pg/cell, **five times textbook**. It is not a pitch artefact.
3. It survives every rate that respects an endpoint. At `q` = 0.818 the course is 0.125 / 0.369 / 0.705 / 0.914 / 0.995 — still short of both measured day 2s and now finishing a day early against both tails. **A flat rate scale cannot buy the shape**, exactly as D-216 §4 found, and S1 does not change that.
4. Every measured or fitted course peaks on **day 1-2** and tails; the model peaks on **day 4**. The asymmetric 5-parameter logistic that S2's authors needed on 3 of 7 industrial datasets is a degree of freedom this engine does not have. That is the shape of the remaining defect, and it is a structural one.

* **Adopting 18 pg/cell is not a one-line change and this beat did not price it.** `TYRELL_SCENARIO`'s `pitch_gpl` would go 1.0 → 0.179, and D-211's `mu_max` was fitted at 1.0 by least squares on Tyrell's day-1/day-2 growth fraction. A beat that picks up the lighter conversion inherits a `mu_max` refit **and** a broken extract calibration, and should learn that here rather than rediscover it. [[feedback-pair-the-arm-with-its-baseline]]
* **No third-party day-by-day ale course at ~20 °C in numeric form was found.** S1's daily gravities are in Figure 2, S4's series is *"available from the corresponding author upon request"*, S2 is a fit. The two numeric trajectories in hand are still Tyrell and S2's fitted curve.
* **de Andrés-Toro's five isothermal runs (8/12/16/20/24 °C) were not obtained** — every open route 403s. D-217 refused that paper's *fitted coefficient* on rate-law grounds; its *data* is a separate asset and is still unmined.
* **MDPI blocks WebFetch and curl at the host but reads fine through the browser tool.** A blocked **transport**, not a paywall — recorded because the archive has been wrong about that distinction six times. [[feedback-paywalled-is-one-host]]
* **S1's Figure 2 holds six more temperatures for these same strains.** The prose pair has now been used and found non-discriminating; digitising the figure would give a *tighter* test, not close an open gap.

### 8. The recommendation, and what stays the owner's

**Prefer the published trials over the brief as the yardstick — and do not retire the 5-7 d window in this beat.**

The first half is now evidenced rather than argued. Every third-party endpoint found is at or faster than the fast edge of the brief's window: ≤3 d at 22 °C on a wort within 0.003 SG of §2.2's own; 54-96 h across four pilot batches at 19-28 °C; 3-5 d for IPA primary; and two courses both essentially finished by day 5. **Nothing found supports 5-7 days as a target.** It survives only as a loose upper bound, and `CLAUDE.md` already calls the brief *"reference, not gospel"*.

The second half is not deference, it is arithmetic. Retiring the window means moving `q_sugar_max`, and §4's own table shows what that buys: a rate satisfying S1 leaves the model finishing a day early against both measured tails while still missing both measured day 2s. D-216 §4 refused that trade and S1 does not overturn it. **Retiring an acceptance criterion the model currently passes, in order to adopt a rate that fits the data worse in shape, is not a fidelity gain.**

So the concrete next measurement, and it is now the only thing standing between this archive and an answer: **source the per-cell dry mass.** It is load-bearing in three places (D-216 §7, D-216 §8, §4 above), the repo ships two values 5.6× apart, and it is cheaper than anything else on the list. D-216 §11 is therefore **still open, but no longer open on the literature** — the literature has answered. It is open on a conversion factor.

**Corrects:** D-218 — §4's closing line, *"3.33 d against a published ≤3, an 11 % miss … the model is not badly wrong about beer's speed"*, was measured at the 100 pg reading this record retires. At the settled conversion the shipped model takes **4.84 d against the same ≤3, a 1.61× miss**, and also misses the 12 °C ceiling (10.74 d against ≤10). The other half of that line — *"the **brief** is"* wrong — survives intact.

It is load-bearing in three places, the repo ships two values 5.6× apart, and it is cheaper than anything else on the list."* Authorised scope was to **settle it and measure what it decides**. ### 1. The reframe: the two numbers were never rival estimates of one quantity

D-218 §4 framed this as a fork between two conversions 5.6× apart. That framing is what kept it open, because the two are not the same kind of claim.

* **18 pg** was an **asserted conversion** — *"the standard ~18 pg/cell S. cerevisiae dry-weight figure"* in `test_validation_varela2004.py` and `test_validation_palma2012.py`, sourced to nothing.
* **~100 pg** was **never chosen by anyone.** It is back-computed by dividing `TYRELL_SCENARIO`'s `pitch_gpl = 1.0` by Tyrell's counted 9.96 × 10⁶ cells/mL. So it is a **residual**: it absorbs the true cell mass *and* every error in the model's per-gram uptake rate *and* any non-cell mass in the pitch. That is why it came out at three times any defensible cell mass — it was never measuring a cell.

So "which of the two is right" has no answer, and hunting a third literature value would only have added a fourth incomparable number. The question that does have an answer is: **what gram is this engine's biomass state variable expressed in?**

### 2. The answer was already in the paper the wine core is fitted to

Coleman, Fish & Block 2007 — the source of wine's `Y_X/N` and its nitrogen regression, `k'_d`, `mu_max`, and the `X`/`X_A` split — Materials and Methods, *"Viable and total cell concentration procedures"*, VERBATIM (read off the ASM full text, `coleman_asm.html`, not a summary):

> *"Each cell count was converted to grams per liter of cell mass, assuming that each cell weighs 4 × 10⁻¹¹ g and that the 25 squares in the hemacytometer grid were covered with 10 μl."*

Coleman counted cells with a hemacytometer and weighed nothing. **Every gram in that paper is a count multiplied by 4 × 10⁻¹¹ g**, and therefore so is every wine biomass parameter this engine fits to it. A counted pitch converted at any other figure enters the model in a unit its own parameters do not use — which is exactly what the two wine benchmarks were doing.

That is the whole argument, and it is an identity rather than a preference. It also explains why no amount of searching would have settled this: the quantity is not a fact about yeast that the archive was missing, it is a **unit definition** the archive had on disk since D-13.

**The honest limit of the claim, stated so a later note cannot drift past it: Coleman writes "assuming".** Nothing in the chain is a weighing. The tier is `plausible`, not `validated`, and the `source:` field must not launder his assumption into a measurement.

### 3. What makes the unit physically honest, and the frame Coleman left open

Coleman says *"cell mass"* — never *"dry weight"* — so the frame needs settling independently, because this engine's `biomass_C_fraction` / `biomass_N_fraction` are declared **on dry cell weight** in both medium files and the conservation checks read them.

Invert his yield back to the quantity he actually measured, then price it with an elemental composition he had no hand in. His assumed 40 pg **cancels** out of the measurement and re-enters only as the thing being checked:

| step | value |
|---|---|
| `Y_X/N` at 330 mg N/L, from his own Fig. 4 regression | 10.06 g cell / g N |
| ÷ 4×10⁻¹¹ g ⇒ **cells per g N — what the hemacytometer measured** | 2.515 × 10¹¹ |
| dry mass per g N, from Roels `CH₁.₈O₀.₅N₀.₂` (`biomass_N_fraction` = 0.114) | 8.77 g |
| ⇒ **dry mass per cell** | **34.87 pg** |

34.87 against an assumed 40 is a **13 % agreement between a counting-chamber convention and an elemental formula**, and it settles the frame: read as a WET mass, 4×10⁻¹¹ g would make yeast **33 % nitrogen on a dry basis** against a real 7-12 %. It is a dry mass. A geometric cross-check agrees on magnitude and is recorded as a cross-check only, never as the shipped source: a 100-150 fL wine/ale cell at ρ ≈ 1.11 g/mL and ~30 % dry matter is 30-57 pg.

**Band: 28-50 pg**, which is what the elemental route gives across `biomass_N_fraction`'s own printed 0.08-0.14 uncertainty. The test derives it live rather than asserting it, so it moves if that parameter's provenance does.

**Both retired readings sit OUTSIDE that band**, and neither is a near miss: 18 pg implies a ~50 fL cell — a small lab haploid, not the diploid EC1118 those very benchmarks run — and ~100 pg implies a ~300 fL cell, which no *S. cerevisiae* is.

### 4. What was rejected, and why the obvious sources are traps

* **Tyrell 2013 prints no pitch by weight.** Yeast was propagated, harvested at *"Hochkräusen"* and pitched by count (MEBAK III 10.4.3). So ~100 pg could never have been read off the source — checked before searching, per the standing lesson. Foster 2022 measures a DCW but never pairs it with a count.
* **The Handbook of Enology's dosing statements are NOT a band.** p.95 gives 10⁶ cells/mL ↔ 10-20 g/hL of active dry yeast (⇒ 100-200 pg); p.334 gives 10-25 g/hL ↔ 2-10 × 10⁶ cells/mL (⇒ 25-50 pg). The same book, mutually inconsistent, and both are **product-dosing conventions** whose gram carries moisture, carrier and dead cells. Crossing them would have produced a "band" whose whole spread *is* the convention's looseness — D-209's error exactly. Recorded as the losing readings, with the reason.
* **The commercial dry-yeast convention (~10¹⁰ cells per gram of product ⇒ ~100 pg) is a frame error, not a rival.** It is a mass of *product*, not of cell. Worth noting because it is the most plausible origin of a `pitch_gpl` of 1.0: one gram of dried yeast per litre is very close to Tyrell's counted 10⁷ cells/mL — in the product frame. This is offered as a hypothesis about provenance, not as a finding.
* **Varela 2004 cannot close it.** They count with a Neubauer chamber *and* weigh gravimetrically, which looks ideal, but no figure or table pairs the two at a timepoint, and their biomass numbers are **final**, where the repo needs a pitch. A final-biomass ratio used to set an initial pitch is a frame gap, not a value.

### 5. What it does — measured, in three places, with nothing recalibrated

**(a) The wine call sites — repaired, inside every printed band, and NOT inert.** Both go 0.018 → **0.0400 g/L** (10⁶ cells/mL, through the new boundary function). All six of Varela's assertions hold unchanged across the 2.22× pitch change — but that is a statement about the *asserts*, not about the quantity they characterise, and that file's own docstring says a change which *"silently narrows OR widens"* its gap must be caught. **It widened, at both nitrogen levels:**

| | 0.018 g/L | 0.0400 g/L | Varela |
|---|---|---|---|
| N=300 hours to dryness | 89 (1.910×) | **84 (2.024×)** | 170 |
| N=50 hours to dryness | 313 (2.236×) | **289 (2.422×)** | 700 |
| D-57's N50/N300 duration ratio | 3.517 | **3.440** | 4.118 |
| biomass g/L, N=300 / N=50 | 3.382 / 1.400 | 3.404 / 1.422 | 5.8 / 1.5 |

Every number moves 5-8 % and nothing fires, because a research-lab inoculum is swamped by growth. But the direction is uniformly **faster**, which is the direction the model was already wrong in, so D-57's characterised shortfall gets marginally worse rather than staying put. **No band is widened to absorb it** — D-219 is named as the reason it moved, which is what that docstring asks for. Reporting this as "inert" would have been the Palma mistake below, made silently on the arm where the asserts happened to survive.

**One band did move, and the direction is a COST.** Palma's nitrogen-limited LF arm at 144 h goes 41.0 → **28.6 g/L** against Palma's measured ~80, so the N-sensitivity shortfall goes from ~2× to ~2.8×: **further from the measurement, not nearer.** Re-banded [35, 48] → [24, 33] with D-219 named. It has leverage there and nowhere else because at 90 mg N/L the ferment is nitrogen-starved and final biomass is inoculum-dominated. The old 41 was flattered by an inoculum 2.22× too light. Two other Palma pins (CF 138 → 128 h against a 125 floor; gap 1.917 → 1.778 against a 1.7 floor) are now near their floors and were deliberately **not** re-centred — a band moved to re-centre a passing number is a band fitted to the model.

**(b) The beer scenario — measured, NOT corrected.** Tyrell's counted pitch is **0.3984 g/L**, so `TYRELL_SCENARIO` carries **2.51×** the biomass Tyrell pitched. At the counted pitch:

| | shipped 1.0 g/L | counted 0.3984 g/L |
|---|---|---|
| day-2 extract fraction (Tyrell measured 0.594) | 0.2117 | **0.0903** |
| day-2 shortfall | 2.81× | **6.58×** |
| nitrogen drawn by 24 h (Tyrell's spread 0.234-0.448) | 0.360 | **0.145 — outside** |

The pitch is **not** corrected here for the reason D-218 §7 already priced: `mu_max` was fitted at 1.0 g/L against Tyrell's growth fraction, so moving the pitch inherits a `mu_max` refit **and** a broken extract calibration in one beat. What ships is the measurement.

**2.51× and D-215's "~2.8× too slowly" are NOT two routes agreeing, and must not be read as one.** D-215's factor was measured *at pitch 1.0*, i.e. with the excess already in place. They **compound** — 6.58 ≈ 2.51 × 2.62 — which is why the shortfall at the counted pitch is 6.58× and not 2.8×.

**(c) The verdict on the brief's window: §2.2's 5-7 days does NOT survive.** D-218 §4's bracket had the window surviving in exactly one of eight cells, at the 100 pg reading. That reading is now retired, and the settled one is a different row of the same table: the `q_sugar_max` reaching Foster's published endpoint (0.9242) takes §2.2's benchmark to **3.63 d**, verified live. And with no knob touched at all, at Foster's counted pitch of 0.48 g/L, the shipped model takes **4.84 d against a published ≤3** and **10.74 d against a ≤10 ceiling** at 12 °C.

So D-218 §8's recommendation stands and is now unconditional on a conversion — *nothing found supports 5-7 days* — but its consolation does not: the model is **~1.6× slow** against a third-party trial, not nearly right. Both halves are corrected above.

**The window is still not retired in code, and that is arithmetic rather than deference.** Retiring it means moving `q_sugar_max`, and D-216 §4 priced that: a rate satisfying Foster leaves the model finishing a day early against both measured tails while still missing both measured day 2s. Fitting an acceptance criterion the model passes today to a rate that fits the data worse in SHAPE is not a fidelity gain.

### 6. What ships, and what each guard's RED names

The constant lives in `fermentation/units/convert.py` as `cells_per_ml_to_pitch_gpl`, **not** in a parameter YAML. The discriminator is not directive #2 against D-3 in the abstract, it is that **nothing in `core` or `runtime` resolves it**: `pitch_gpl` goes straight into `X` at the compile seam, and no `Process` reads a cell count. It is a literature→canonical boundary conversion, which is that module's stated remit; a YAML entry would have forced either a new organism-level parameter file or a third duplication across wine and beer for a value no `Process` ever sees.

Four guards in `tests/test_units.py` (arithmetic, ~1 s) and three in `tests/test_organic_acids.py` §13 (~10 s):

* **`test_the_pitch_conversion_is_colemans_own_biomass_unit_not_an_estimate`** — asserted EXACTLY, not to a tolerance, because an identity has no tolerance. A RED names the unit drifting away from the parameters fitted in it.
* **`test_the_elemental_route_corroborates_colemans_assumption`** — §3, computed live from the shipped `Y_X/N` regression and `biomass_N_fraction`. **Its positive control is the WET reading**, which the predicate must reject; without it "the routes agree" is indistinguishable from a predicate that cannot disagree.
* **`test_both_readings_the_archive_shipped_are_outside_the_settled_band`** — the band is derived from `biomass_N_fraction`'s own uncertainty, not asserted. A RED on either retired reading means the band has widened enough to re-admit one, which would re-open D-216 §11.
* **`test_the_published_pitches_convert_to_the_recorded_values`** — Tyrell 0.3984, wine 0.0400, Foster 0.4800.
* **`test_the_beer_scenario_carries_two_and_a_half_times_tyrells_counted_biomass`** — §5(b), and it is where the refusal to move the pitch lives. It carries a **designed contrast**: the shipped pitch must land INSIDE Tyrell's nitrogen spread while the counted one falls outside, so "outside" cannot be confused with a predicate that never fires.
* **`test_the_handoff_window_does_not_survive_the_settled_conversion`** — §5(c). Its last assert is that every surviving corner belongs to a RETIRED reading, plus a non-vacuity check that at least one corner survives at all. A RED is a change to the ANSWER of D-216 §11.
* **`test_at_the_settled_conversion_the_shipped_model_is_slow_against_foster`** — the numbers replacing D-218 §4's 11 %. A RED on the 12 °C arm would mean the slowness is not uniform across temperature, which would license re-opening D-217.

**Falsified before shipping — four arms, all in band, with a designed GREEN and the restore verified between every one:**

| arm | `test_units.py` | §13 |
|---|---|---|
| conversion → 18 pg (the retired wine assertion) | **RED** | **RED** |
| conversion → 100 pg (the retired beer residual) | **RED** | **RED** |
| `biomass_N_fraction` → 0.10 (in band; the elemental route's own input) | **RED** | green |
| `biomass_C_fraction` → 0.46 (in band; read by NO guard — **designed GREEN**) | green | green |

The third arm is the one worth reading: it reddens the arithmetic guards while leaving the engine guards alone, which is what shows the corroboration check has real reach into the parameters rather than being a restatement of the constant. The fourth is the harness check — a silent restore failure would have made every arm above confirm itself.

### 7. Scope not entered, and what a later beat inherits

* **`TYRELL_SCENARIO`'s pitch is still 1.0 g/L against a counted 0.3984.** Correcting it is a real beat and it inherits, together: a `mu_max` refit (D-211 fitted it at 1.0 by least squares on Tyrell's day-1/day-2 growth fraction), a day-2 extract shortfall that grows to 6.58×, and beer's pH agreement dropping from 7 of 8 days inside to 6 (D-216 §8). None of that is a reason the pitch is right; it is the price list.
* **Coleman's 4×10⁻¹¹ g is still an assumption, and Cramer et al. 2002 — the paper his model came from — was not obtained** (Wiley, not checked across hosts). If Cramer *measured* it, the tier rises from `plausible`; if Cramer assumed it too, the unit identity is unaffected but nothing in the chain is a weighing and that should be said once, plainly, rather than re-discovered.
* **Nobody has yet paired a count with a gravimetric dry weight in one wine or beer fermentation at one timepoint.** That is the measurement that would make this `validated`. Varela counts and weighs but never pairs them; Foster measures DCW but for a trehalose denominator.
* **The wine biomass gap is now a cell-mass question too.** Varela's gravimetric 5.8 g/L at 300 mg N/L is 19.3 g dry per g N — against Coleman's 10.1 and the elemental 8.77 — so the long-standing ~42 % `Y_X/N` cross-study gap (D-56 finding 3) is *either* a cell-number difference *or* a cell-mass one, and no data in hand separates them. The elemental route forbids resolving it on mass alone: 68 pg/cell would reconcile the two but implies yeast at 5.2 % nitrogen.
* **§2.2's 5-7 d window is now refuted rather than merely unsupported.** Retiring it is a live, owner-facing decision, and D-216 §4's shape refusal is what stands between the verdict and a rate change.

**Corrects:** D-218 — §4's *"Every third-party endpoint is at or faster than 5-7 d's fast edge"* and its verdict that the brief's duration is unsupported. Both were read off Figure 2's timepoint panels, which are dominated by the moderate and high temperatures. Foster's own course puts all three Beer 1 controls INSIDE 5-7 d at 15 °C. The window's DURATION is corroborated; it is the duration paired with §2.2's 20 °C that is refuted.
**Corrects:** D-219 — §5(c)'s *"D-218 §8's recommendation stands and is now unconditional on a conversion — nothing found supports 5-7 days"*. It is conditional on a temperature, which the timepoint reading could not see. Its arithmetic is untouched: at 20 °C the window is still refuted, and the model is still slow.

Peak time moves with temperature: 24 h at 30 °C, 24-36 h at 22 °C, 48-72 h at 15 °C, and no peak at all inside 120 h at 12 °C. The defect it names survives, for a different reason — see §4.
**Corrects:** D-216 — its scope note *"There is no second measured beer extract course on disk"* is now false, and with it the framing of §11's open question as a choice between *"an acceptance criterion from the handoff brief"* and *"a published trial"*: the brief's DURATION turns out to be corroborated by a published trial too, at 15 °C. **Its refusal to move `q_sugar_max` is untouched** — that rests on §2.2's benchmark and on the shape objection in its §4, neither of which this record spends.

Opened by the owner, who chose *"chase more data"* from a menu of four after D-219: try the browser route for the five-temperature study, mine the temperature figure already on disk, and pull the missing cell-mass paper. Authorised scope was the pulls and whatever they measure. **No parameter value moved, no knob touched**: one transcribed literature table, five guards, three corrections.

Working files: `M:\claud_projects\temp\ferment\d220-second-beer-course\` — `PREREGISTER.md`, `FINDINGS.md`, `extract_s1.py`, `extract_s1b.py`, `analyse.py`, `endpoint.py`, `probe_model.py`, `probe_model2.py`, `probe_repo_helper.py`, `mutate.py`, `foster_s1.json`/`.csv` (the full 720-point recovery), `supp.zip`.

### 1. The pull: the course was inside the paper the archive had already mined twice

D-218 and D-219 both read Foster et al. 2022 through main-text **Figure 2**, which is the same experiment collapsed to four timepoint panels with temperature on the x-axis. Every duration the archive took from it was therefore a **ceiling read off a sample**, and D-218 said so explicitly. What neither beat opened is the paper's own sentence pointing at the rest: *"We monitored the specific gravities of small-scale wort fermentations at eight different temperatures (**Supplementary Figure 1**)"*.

Supplementary Figure S1 is the **course** — 10 strains × 8 temperatures (12, 15, 22, 30, 35, 37, 40, 42 °C) × 9 timepoints from 0 to 120 h. It arrived in the Europe PMC supplementary bundle (`PMC8966892/supplementaryFiles`, HTTP 200, 11.2 MB), which nobody had requested. This is [[feedback-re-read-the-source-you-already-mined]] for the second time, one beat after D-219 mined the same paper's Methods.

**Until this beat the archive had exactly ONE measured beer extract course on disk** (Tyrell's), which is what D-216's scope note recorded and what made every shape argument since unfalsifiable.

### 2. The values are a transcription, not a plot reading

The supplementary figure is **vector** — `pdfimages -list` finds no raster — so every point is a path vertex, mapped through the axis tick labels' own coordinates. [[feedback-read-a-fast-curve-on-a-fixed-grid]] does not bite: there is no grid, only exact geometry.

The layout was **established from the geometry rather than assumed**. The connecting polyline is drawn undodged at the true x (so its vertices are the means) while the error bars are dodged per series (so their cap spans give ± SD). Eight colours × 300 segments each is the eight-level viridis palette.

**Two checks the recovery had to pass and was not told about:**

* Foster ran one wort per temperature, so the t=0 gravity must agree across all ten strain panels of a temperature — and it does, to four decimals (12 °C→1.0430, 15 °C→1.0429, 22 °C→1.0420, 30 °C→1.0420, 35 °C→1.0448, 37 °C→1.0435, 40 °C→1.0435, 42 °C→1.0448). Each panel's axis was fitted independently, so a calibration fault could not reproduce that.
* The colour→temperature map is pinned by the **stall at 40-42 °C**, which is the paper's own headline: the commercial ale controls barely ferment there while the kveik do. 12-30 °C alone are monotone and cannot tell an ascending palette from a rescaled one, which is why the shipped table carries a 42 °C column it otherwise has no use for.

All 80 series recovered complete at all 9 timepoints; 720 points.

### 3. §2.2's window is not refuted. It is mis-temperatured, and only the PAIR is wrong

§2.2's benchmark asserts two things at once: a **1.048 wort at 20 °C**, and **1.010 in 5-7 days**. Foster's wort is 1.045 and his runs bracket 20 °C. Days to the same 1.010 target — which both sources take from Parker 2008:

| strain | 12 °C | 15 °C | 22 °C | 30 °C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cali Ale | 6.54* | **5.39*** | 3.33 | 2.89 |
| Vermont Ale | 7.53* | **5.91*** | 3.76 | 3.10 |
| Kölsch | 8.73* | **5.04*** | 2.91 | 2.26 |

\* extrapolated past the 120 h end of the run, on a **decelerating** tail (Cali at 15 °C falls 3.43 SG-points/h over 72-96 h and 1.67 over 96-120 h). So the true crossings are **later**, never earlier, and every claim here is written to be strengthened by that rather than weakened. Foster's 1.045 against §2.2's 1.048 pushes the same way. At 15 °C the extrapolation is also short — Kölsch sits at 0.2378 extract fraction against a 0.2331 target at the last measured point.

**At 15 °C all three land inside 5-7 d.** The brief's duration is a real brewing figure. What cannot be true is that duration *at 20 °C*: the same strains take 2.91-3.76 d at 22 °C, so 20 °C cannot take 5-7.

**Stated as a bracket, deliberately, and not as the interpolation that was available.** An Arrhenius interpolation of the endpoint rate gives 3.40-4.27 d at 20 °C, but its cold input is itself an extrapolation and its activation energy is fitted from two points — a soft number wearing a hard claim. The bracket makes the same point and cannot be attacked. The interpolated figures are recorded here and asserted nowhere.

So D-218 §8's recommendation survives in its verdict and dies in its reasoning: *nothing supports 5-7 d* was too strong, and the honest statement is that **§2.2 pairs a real duration with a temperature that contradicts it**. Retiring it is still the owner's call, and D-216 §4's shape refusal still stands between the verdict and a rate change.

### 4. What the course actually convicts: the engine is ~1.5× slow, and it is a LEVEL error

D-218 had ceilings, so it could compare at one reading of one temperature. With the course, the engine runs at Foster's own wort and Foster's counted pitch (0.48 g/L through D-219's boundary conversion) at four temperatures, through §12's own helper so the numbers stay commensurable with everything §12 and §13 pin:

| | 12 °C | 15 °C | 22 °C | 30 °C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| model, days | 10.742 | 8.379 | 4.838 | 2.717 |
| measured mean | 7.60 | 5.45 | 3.34 | 2.75 |
| **ratio** | **1.41×** | **1.54×** | **1.45×** | **0.99×** |

**The slowness is a level error, not a temperature-response error** — near-constant from 12 to 22 °C. That is a positive result for D-217, which refused to re-source `E_a_uptake`, and it reaches the same place by different evidence: the lever that would close this is a rate SCALE, which is exactly the `q_sugar_max` D-216 measured, priced and refused on §2.2's benchmark. The refusal's premise is what this beat moves, not its arithmetic.

**§2.2's window is what hides the slowness.** The model passes 5-7 d at 20 °C at 6.08 d, and it passes because a criterion calibrated to a cooler ferment certifies a model that is half again too slow. Two errors of opposite sign, one certifying the other. [[feedback-a-margin-can-be-borrowed-from-a-defect]]

### 5. The 30 °C agreement is a crossing and must never be cited as a validation

The model lands inside the measured spread at 30 °C, and that is the section's designed contrast rather than a success. Real ale yeast **saturates** above ~22 °C: the apparent activation energy of Foster's measured endpoint collapses from **49.5 to 17.9 kJ/mol** across the 22→30 °C step, while the model holds **55.5 then 53.7**. The model runs down a straight line while the data flattens, and 30 °C is where the two cross. [[feedback-a-hit-can-be-two-errors-cancelling]]

That apparent activation energy is a **lumped coefficient of the whole course**, not a reading of `E_a_uptake`, and is recorded here only because the model/measured *divergence* is the finding. Taking it for the parameter would be D-183's error and the exact one D-217 refused de Andrés-Toro's −97 kJ/mol for. It is also 45.5-55.5 kJ/mol, inside the printed band, so it discriminates nothing even if one tried. **D-218's rule — never cite Foster's temperatures as a test of this model's temperature response — therefore stands, but for a new reason: it was written when both endpoints were ceilings, and it survives now that they are measurements.**

### 6. The shape claim, corrected in its generality and confirmed in its substance

D-218 generalised *"every measured or fitted course peaks on day 1-2"* into a structural verdict, from Tyrell plus fitted logistic curves. Foster says peak time moves with temperature: the plateau of steepest fall ends at 24 h at 30 °C, 24-36 h at 22 °C, **48-72 h at 15 °C**, and at 12 °C the ferment has not peaked inside the 120 h run.

Reported as a **plateau, not an argmax** — at 15 °C Cali's 36-48, 48-72 and 72-96 h intervals run 3.53 / 3.45 / 3.43 SG-points/h, and picking a winner from those is reading noise.

**This does not rescue the model, and the first draft of this record wrongly said it did.** That draft compared the engine's day-4 peak — measured at Tyrell's wort, pitch and temperature — against Foster's course at a different wort, pitch and strain, which is the cross-frame error the archive keeps catching. Run at Foster's *own* conditions the engine peaks later still at every temperature. So the defect D-218 named survives; what dies is the reason it gave, and the correction is that the model is uniformly slow rather than uniquely late-peaking.

### 1. What the edit is, and why it is a temperature and not a duration

§2.2 asserts two things at once: **a 1.048 wort at 20 °C**, and **1.010 apparent in 5-7 days**. D-220 recovered Foster et al. 2022's Supplementary Figure S1 — the archive's second measured beer course — and found the duration real and the pairing impossible: the same three commercial ale controls take 5.06-6.26 d at 15 °C and 2.91-3.77 d at 22 °C.

This beat re-derived those 15 °C crossings from D-220's own 720-point recovery rather than citing them, because D-220's figures are extrapolated past the 120 h end of the run on a decelerating tail. A **geometric-deceleration** extrapolation — continuing the ratio by which consecutive interval slopes shrink — reproduces D-220's linear numbers exactly before diverging, and pushes all three later:

| strain | D-220, linear | conservative | inside 5-7? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kölsch | 5.042 | 5.055 | yes |
| Cali Ale | 5.390 | 5.527 | yes |
| Vermont Ale | 5.910 | 6.263 | yes |

**Foster's own band sits INSIDE the handoff's window**, so keeping 5-7 and moving only the temperature is the edit generous to the model. The window is the brief's own number and is untouched; only `conditions` moved.

### 2. What the pass was worth

At 20 °C the criterion passed at 6.05 d. At 15 °C the engine takes **9.000 d**, missing the window's high edge by 2.00 d and Foster's own conservative slow strain by **2.74 d**. This is D-220 §4's *"~1.5× too slow at every temperature below 30 °C"* seen through the acceptance criterion: a criterion calibrated to a cooler ferment was certifying a model half again too slow, two errors of opposite sign with one hiding the other. [[feedback-a-margin-can-be-borrowed-from-a-defect]]

**The reading is not a grid artefact, and it is the more stable of the two.** Across 1, 2, 4 and 8 output points per hour the 15 °C duration spreads **0.0052 d**; the retired 20 °C frame spreads 0.0365 d. The criterion moved to the quieter temperature. [[feedback-read-a-fast-curve-on-a-fixed-grid]]

### 3. The conflict inverts in DIRECTION, and that is the beat's centre

`q_sugar_max` bisected against the criterion in both frames. D-216's *"the window is already violated at q ≈ 0.6"* reproduces at 0.6214.

| frame | admissible `q_sugar_max` for 5-7 d | shipped 0.5 | D-216's Tyrell-matching 1.397 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 °C (retired) | 0.4250 – 0.6214 | 6.05 d **PASS** | 2.69 d |
| 15 °C (live) | 0.6670 – 1.0165 | 9.00 d **FAIL** | 3.99 d |

At 20 °C the criterion sat just above the shipped rate and **forbade a faster engine**. At 15 °C the shipped rate falls below the band and the criterion **demands one**. So beer's two speed anchors no longer disagree about the sign of the correction — both want the engine faster — and disagree only on magnitude, by ~1.37× (the criterion tops out at 1.017, Tyrell wants 1.397). D-216 §11's open question is now about a magnitude rather than about a direction.

**D-216's refusal survives its own premise being spent, and this was the beat's blocking check.** The refusal rested partly on the criterion forbidding 1.397. The criterion no longer forbids faster rates in general, but it still forbids that one, and not marginally: 1.397 stays outside across the **entire** printed `E_a_uptake` band (30,000 → 3.58 d, 63,000 → 4.17 d), reaching 5-7 d only at ~120,000 J/mol, 1.9× the printed high edge. Nothing here licenses a rate change.

### 4. The claim that dies outright: `E_a_uptake` is no longer inert at §2.2

D-216 §6 named `E_a_uptake` as the only lever that decouples beer's two speed anchors, on the grounds that the benchmark ran at exactly `T_ref` = 20 °C so its Arrhenius factor was 1.0 by construction. D-217 §1 asserted that across the whole band and well outside it, on both signs, and measured **0.0000 d**.

| frame | span of days-to-target across the printed 30,000-63,000 J/mol band |
|---|---|
| 20 °C (retired) | **0.0000 d** — exact, by construction |
| 15 °C (live) | **1.75 d** — against a window only 2.0 d wide |

**There is no magnitude argument to retreat to.** The parameter went from the criterion's most inert to one of its strongest levers in a single frame change. The reason is structural rather than numerical: **Tyrell's trial is 15.0 °C and the criterion is now 15.0 °C**, so one Arrhenius factor enters both anchors and the parameter cannot move either alone. The decoupling was never a fact about yeast; it was an artefact of a criterion asserted at a temperature the literature contradicts, and removing it is a correction rather than a loss.

D-217's refusal to re-source `E_a_uptake` rests on the corpus having nothing and is untouched. The low band edge does not rescue the criterion either — 30,000 J/mol gives 7.69 d, still outside.

`E_a_growth` carried the same 20 °C inertness claim in its own note and loses it the same way, much more weakly: 0.0000 → **0.2917 d**, a sixth of uptake's, consistent with the file header's statement that growth is the weaker lever on attenuation. Both notes are corrected and both numbers are now asserted, so they cannot drift apart from each other.

D-218 §12's fork table asks what §2.2 reads when the engine is re-rated to Foster's 72 h endpoint, at four readings of the per-cell dry mass. Re-scored in both frames:

| per-cell mass | `q_sugar_max` | §2.2 at 15 °C | §2.2 at 20 °C |
|---|---|---|---|

**The survivor moves from the retired reading to the settled one.** At 20 °C exactly one row sat inside the window and it was the 100 pg conversion D-219 retired — the survivor was the reading known to be wrong. At 15 °C the survivors are the settled 40 pg row and its neighbour, and the retired row is the one that fails. D-218 §3's central caveat inverts with it: the survival there held only while Foster's 3 d was read as exact, and the open end of the sampling interval took the row to 3.71 d and broke the window in all eight bracket cells. **None of this says the model passes.** All four rows are re-rated engines. The shipped rate takes the criterion to 9.00 d, which is §2's xfail. What inverts is which *literature* anchors can be satisfied together. Tyrell's extract schedule remains incompatible with both.

### 2. The extent agreement was the pitch excess, and no rate can give it back

Beer's growth here is nitrogen-limited, so the absolute gain is fixed by the wort: `dX = YAN / biomass_N_fraction` ≈ **1.75 g/L at either pitch** (1.7344 measured at 1.0, 1.7470 at 0.3984). Dividing that same gain by a lighter inoculum is the whole story:

| | pitch 1.0 (retired) | pitch 0.3984, rate unmoved | pitch 0.3984 + refit (SHIPS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| multiplication | 2.734× | 5.354× | **5.385×** |
| against Tyrell's measured 2.92-3.48× | 6 % below | 1.54× above | **1.546× above** |

**`mu_max` sets WHEN the ceiling is reached, not WHERE it is**, and that is run rather than asserted: across the entire re-constructed band the fold moves **0.010** (5.3817 at 0.053, 5.3921 at 0.075) while the day-1 growth fraction moves 0.263 → 0.442. A new guard integrates both edges and reads the fold off each; its RED would mean growth has stopped being nitrogen-limited, which would re-open D-211 §1's identity — the thing that makes a cell-count panel a nitrogen curve at all. [[feedback-run-the-mutation-the-claim-names]]

So D-211 §5's *"the extent was right and only the rate was wrong"* inverts into *"the rate is refit and the extent is now visibly wrong"*. **That is a repair, not a regression**: the agreement it retires was an artefact of an inoculum 2.51× too heavy, and the model's error is the same size either way — it was being scored against a scenario that hid it.

**Stated as a quantity rather than a mood, and NOT entered.** Tyrell's counted growth is (29.06-34.69) − 9.96 = 19.1-24.7 ×10⁶ cells/mL = 0.76-0.99 g/L at 40 pg, so only **87-113 mg/L** of nitrogen reached suspended biomass against the **200 mg/L** the scenario assumes. Tyrell prints no FAN at all (the wort is a dilution of Bavarian Pilsener malt extract; the strains' amino-acid profile is *"data not shown"*), so nothing sources a repair. The other candidate is the model's own assumption that one lumped nitrogen pool goes wholly into suspended biomass. Whichever it is, it is an extent question and this beat is a pitch and a rate.

### 3. The price list, measured three ways — and D-219's was measured without the refit it named

D-219 §7 and D-221 §8 both carried the pitch forward as *"uncorrected, here is the price list"*. The list is what this beat had to clear. Column B is D-219's list re-measured; column C is what ships.

| | A: shipped (1.0, 0.034) | B: pitch only (0.3984, 0.034) | C: pitch + refit (SHIPS) | Tyrell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nitrogen drawn by 24 h | 0.360 | **0.145 — outside** | **0.298 — inside** | 0.234-0.448 |
| pH days inside the envelope | 7 of 8 | **5 of 8** | **7 of 8** | — |
| day-1 pH miss, above the envelope | +0.070 | +0.426 | **+0.172** | alkaline side |
| day-2 extract shortfall | 2.81× | 6.58× | **4.21×** | 0.594 measured |
| day-7 attenuation of fermentable extract | 0.931 | 0.701 | **0.782** | 0.997 |
| §2.2's criterion at its own 15 °C | 9.00 d | 9.00 d | **8.50 d** | 5-7 d window |
| time to peak biomass | 59.1 h | 94.6 h | **55.7 h** | — |

**Two of D-219's three named prices are bought back by the refit, and it never ran the refit.** The nitrogen attribution returns inside Tyrell's own spread and the pH course returns to 7 of 8. That is not a lucky cancellation: an inoculum 2.51× lighter reaches the same nitrogen-limited ceiling 1.6× later, and a rate refit on the same curve puts the timing back where the curve says it is.

**The prices that are NOT bought back now ship as visible rather than hidden.** The day-2 extract shortfall goes 2.81× → 4.21×, day 7 attenuates 0.782 against a measured 0.997 — so the engine is slow against Tyrell's ENDPOINT too and not only its early limb, which the excess pitch was concealing — and D-211's pinned day-1 pH miss goes +0.070 → +0.180, still on the alkaline side. **None of these is a new defect.** Every one is the same engine measured against the trial's own inoculum instead of against 2.51× of it.

**D-219's 6-of-8 was borrowed from a third pitch.** It cited D-216 §8, which measured 6 of 8 at **0.5 g/L** — a figure D-219 itself retired when it settled the per-cell mass. At the actual counted 0.3984 g/L the unrefit course is **5 of 8**. A price list is a measurement and inherits the frame of whatever produced it. [[feedback-a-notes-field-is-unchecked-storage]]

### 4. The knob that closes Tyrell's schedule has left its own band — a NEW reason, not a louder one

D-216 §3's first tier was explicit: *"`q_sugar_max` = 1.397 reproduces Tyrell's day 2 and is INSIDE the printed 0.3-1.5 band — so 'the value is out of band' is NOT the reason."* The whole point was that the refusal could not be discharged cheaply.

Re-bisected at the counted pitch on the same hourly grid:

| | retired frame | corrected frame |
|---|---|---|
| model's day-2 fraction at the shipped rate | 0.212 | **0.141** (measured 0.594) |
| `q_sugar_max` reproducing day 2 | 1.397 | **2.3226** |
| against the printed high edge 1.5 | 0.93× — inside | **1.548× — OUTSIDE** |
| §2.2's criterion at that rate, 15 °C | 3.99 d | **2.38 d** |
| across the printed `E_a_uptake` band | 3.58-4.17 d | **2.13-2.50 d** |

The retired 1.397 now books only 0.343 of the wort by day 2. So the first tier of D-216's refusal is spent and **replaced by a stronger one of a different kind**: the knob is inadmissible on its own printed band, before the second anchor is consulted at all. It is asserted against the shipped parameter file rather than written into a comment, so that a band edit turns it red. [[feedback-grep-finds-claims-not-guards]]

**The second tier moves the same way.** Removing `K_repression` entirely — the unbounded limit, not a candidate value — closed **79 %** of the day-2 gap at the retired pitch and closes **46 %** at the counted one, taking the benchmark from 3.42 d to 4.54 d. The term did not shrink; the gap grew. D-216's *"not even the unbounded limit of the term that owns most of it"* is therefore true by a wider margin than when it was written.

### 6. One guard was LOOSENED, and it is a mesh statement

`test_seeding_the_oxygen_is_a_solver_MESH_artifact_and_not_a_coupling`'s sanity ceiling went **1e-4 → 1e-3 g/L**. Repo etiquette forbids weakening a test to get green, so this is named here rather than left in a comment.

The worst slot at the shipped tolerance is `S`, and it moved 1.4e-5 → **1.3e-4 g/L** — 1.6e-6 of an 82 g/L sugar charge. The cause is not a new coupling: a faster ferment has steeper gradients, so the same adaptive mesh straddles more per step. **The ceiling was never the discriminator.** The decisive assertion is the one below it — two decades of `rtol` must buy at least one decade of agreement — and it is untouched and still passes. A genuine oxygen→acid coupling would flatten out instead of converging, and D-212 priced the day-1 acetic requirement at 6-14 mg/L, an order above even the loosened ceiling. [[feedback-separate-mesh-from-coupling-by-convergence]]
