* across the regression's **own printed 5-95 % credible regions** (`a0` 3.31-3.70, `a1` −4.35e-3 to −2.93e-3), corner-swept: **1.32-4.03×**. This is an over-wide rectangle on a correlated pair, so it **bounds** the spread rather than measuring it, and is recorded as a bound.
* against the Fig-4 eye read `wine_generic.yaml` already records as corroboration (`Y_X/N` ~ 9-10 g/g): 1.82-2.62×.
* across D-230's sourced malt-wort envelope (189-194 mg N/L): 1.92-2.55× — barely moves.
* on the **wrong** convention, counting Tyrell's total crop rather than the new cells the nitrogen built: 1.45-1.73×. Scored rather than left unexamined; the finding survives it.

**The sign survives everywhere.** The low edge of the widest range is 1.32; nothing in any band reaches 1.0.

**What this relocates.** The residue is not a defect in beer's growth Process and not a beer-side modelling choice. It is a ~2× disagreement about a ratio that was **counted**, and the engine inherits it because it takes its gram from one trial and is scored against another.

### 5. The third branch — and the half of it that is refused here

Wine yeast in Chardonnay must at 330 mg N/L and ale yeast in wort at ~190 are not the same organism in the same medium. This is a reading D-230 did not name, and it does not close either branch — it **dissolves** the two-way choice by supplying a cause that needs neither heavier cells nor a settled crop. D-230's guard demands that a beat closing the extent gap say which branch it closed; **this record closes none and adds one**, which is stated here so the correction map is not read as a narrowing.

Its two halves do not fare alike:

* **Different nitrogen level: REFUSED, and it goes the wrong way.** Coleman's own text says the yield *"was about two times greater at lower initial nitrogen concentrations"*, and the regression puts `Y_X/N` at Tyrell's 200 mg N/L at **16.09 g/g** = 4.02 × 10¹¹ cells per g N. Correcting for the nitrogen difference therefore takes the disagreement from 2.03-2.63× to **3.25-4.21×** — deeper, not shallower. This is **D-230 §7's harmonisation fence arriving independently from the count side**: that fence priced the same move at 5.40× → ~9× on the extent, and it holds here on a quantity it was not derived from.
* **Different organism / medium: untouched, unsourced, and now the residue.**

### 6. Sourcing: empty, with the scope of the negative stated

D-219 checked Coleman, Tyrell, Foster, Varela and the Handbook of Enology; D-230 grepped the five beer texts **only for flocculation rates**. This beat grepped them for a count-to-dry-weight pairing.

**Patterns run, stated so the negative has a scope** — an unscoped negative is how D-230's own candidate sat on disk unsummed for eight records: `dry (cell )?weight`, `dry matter`, `g dry`, `per cell`, `cells per g`, `cells/g`, `pg`, `10^1[0-2] cells`, `pitching rate`, `million cells`, `cells/mL`, `g/hL`. Run over all five beer texts **and** over Peyer's 243-page thesis in full.

**Nothing.** What the corpus does print is the **product-dosing convention D-219 already rejected**: *Concepts in Wine Chemistry* — *"about 20 g/hL … contains about one million cells/cc"* ⇒ **200 pg/cell**, a gram of *product* carrying moisture, carrier and dead cells. That is a **third** instance of the rejected frame alongside the Handbook of Enology's two mutually inconsistent pages (100-200 and 25-50 pg). The frame keeps turning up because it is the only thing the literature routinely prints; it is not a rival reading and must not be re-proposed as one.

So branch 1 stays an inference. Turning it into a measurement needs an ale strain's count paired with its own dry weight, and **no text in this corpus prints one**.

### 7. Guards

* `test_the_per_day_settled_share_cannot_discriminate_the_two_branches` (NEW) — runs both `mu_max` band edges and asserts the day-1-vs-day-3 comparison **reverses sign** between them, plus the contrast that day 3 is inert (< 0.02) while day 1 is not (> 0.15). Pinned so the next beat does not re-invent the test; a RED means the edges have stopped disagreeing and the discriminator has become usable.
* `test_the_ph_clock_measures_the_known_day_one_ph_miss_and_not_settling` (NEW) — pins the +0.162 day-1 miss, converts it to 0.148 in nitrogen fraction by inverting both values through the same map, and asserts it exceeds 60 % of Tyrell's own day-1 count envelope. A RED when the buffer-removal half is built, which is the one condition under which the clock discriminates.
* `test_the_engines_wine_yield_read_as_a_count_disagrees_twofold_with_the_beer_trial` (NEW) — pins 2.03-2.63× central, the 1.32-4.03× credible-region bound, the 1.45-1.73× wrong-convention sensitivity, and the 3.25-4.21× nitrogen-corrected deepening. Two structural asserts carry the claims the prose makes: that the gram used **is Coleman's own 4 × 10⁻¹¹** and not merely the engine's (they coincide today only because D-219 adopted his, and a divergence would corrupt the Coleman side with no symptom), and that `f_N` **cancels** — re-derived through the per-cell-mass form at all three of its band values and required to reproduce the count route to machine precision. Without the second, the model-free claim would rest on a formula that simply omits `f_N`, which proves nothing about whether omitting it was legitimate.

### 8. Falsification

Arm A doubled the engine's gram (4e-11 → 8e-11); arm B was the restored baseline, designed GREEN. **The restore was verified by SHA-256** and arm B passed 20/20.

Arm A predicted four REDs and produced **ten**. The four predicted are the three new guards plus D-230's two extent tests (`..._cannot_be_a_nitrogen_budget_error`, `..._two_way_frame_ambiguity...`). The six unpredicted are every rate and timing test in the file, plus `..._measured_multiplication_is_not_reproduced...`. **The reason is structural and is the same one D-230 §6 found for wort nitrogen**: the pitch enters through this conversion, `mu_max` is fitted at that pitch, and the growth fraction is normalised on the nitrogen-limited peak — so the gram is not isolable from the rate fit either. Named rather than absorbed by widening the prediction.

### 9. The correction's second half, found by asking what else that number feeds

Reclassifying `Y_X/N` = 10.06 from "his" to "ours" is only a label until you ask what depends on it. `tests/test_units.py`'s `_elemental_pg_per_cell` derives D-219's **28-50 pg** band live — but it sweeps `biomass_N_fraction` across 0.08-0.14 while taking `Y_X/N` as **one number**. That number is the repo fit, and its printed 5-95 % credible regions move it **6.52-15.38 g/g**, a factor of 2.4. Propagating both inputs gives **18.6-76.7 pg**.

**D-219's conclusion survives and is strengthened**: both retired readings sit outside the *wider* band too (18 below 18.6, 100 above 76.7), so the exclusion never depended on the narrower one — which is a better result than the record claimed, because it did not know it had the margin. **One characterisation does not survive**: 18 pg misses by **0.6 pg, about 3 %**, and D-219 calls the two *"not near misses"* and prices 18 pg as a ~50 fL lab haploid. Against the honest width it is a near miss.

**Nothing is re-banded.** `SETTLED_BAND_PG` keeps its edges and its meaning; a new guard pins the propagated width alongside it, asserts the exclusion holds there, and asserts the near-miss. The point is that the narrowness is a **choice about what to propagate**, so the next beat asking "is 20 pg admissible?" gets the honest answer rather than the point-estimate one. Whether the shipped band should widen is D-219's settlement to re-open, not this record's.

### 10. Not covered

The extent gap is **not closed**, and this record does not narrow D-230's ambiguity — it widens it from two branches to three while removing two ways of deciding between them. The missing settling Process stays missing and stays rate-blocked. The buffer-removal half of D-209 §8 stays unbuilt, and is now also the gate on the pH clock. `mu_max`'s timing residue, `E_a_fusels`, wine's two calibration frames and `k_ester_volatil`'s sourcing are all where D-227/D-228/D-230 left them. Wine's own nitrogen budget still has not been audited the way beer's was.


## D-233 — The peptide capacity/pKa pair is the SMALL half of a defect the archive never named: the pH anchor is back-solved at compile from the NOMINAL pKa map and never re-solved for a sampled member, so every off-nominal ensemble member in BOTH media starts at a pH the scenario never asked for — the anchor half is BUILT, the capacity half stays measured and guarded

**Corrects:** D-24 — its scope bullet *"`y0` is held fixed"* was stated unconditionally and is now conditional. The axis D-24 meant to exclude (scenario inputs: Brix, YAN) is unchanged; what the bullet also froze, silently, was the part of `y0` a **parameter derives**. `cation_charge` is back-solved from `initial_ph` **through the pKa map**, and every `pKa_*` is in the sampled set — so holding it fixed did not hold an initial condition, it broke `initial_ph`'s own contract.

Opened by the owner as D-214's parked item — *"the peptide PAIR is incoherent off-nominal — MEASURED, RECORDED, NOT FIXED … it needs its OWN beat"*. Scope authorised as **fix beer's protein-buffer inconsistency**. What the measurement found underneath it was larger, and the owner then authorised the anchor repair with the numbers in hand. One production change, six new guards, three mutation arms, one correction, one number of my own retracted mid-beat.

### 1. The item as opened is real, and it is confirmed rather than inherited

`peptide_buffer_capacity_beer` is back-solved OFFLINE against Peyer's published wort BC = 1.18 at the **nominal** `pKa_peptide_buffer` = 4.25, then shipped as a compile-time constant. That pKa is read at **runtime** and is drawn. So a member carries a wort whose buffering capacity is not the one the constant exists to reproduce.

The back-solve was re-implemented (Peyer's own fast-BC protocol, the titration already written inside `test_the_peptide_capacity_still_reproduces_peyers_published_wort_bc`) and rooted over the capacity. **Control: at pKa 4.25 it returns 1.5480662315921658 against the shipped 1.5480662315921656 — 2.22e-16 g/L, one ULP.**

| pKa | coherent capacity g/L | mM | BC at the SHIPPED capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.86 | 1.617633297044 | 10.9946 | **1.116059** |
| 4.25 | 1.548066231592 | 10.5218 | 1.180000 |
| 4.50 | 1.573902153671 | 10.6974 | **1.145594** |

The mM triple matches the note in `pKa_peptide_buffer` (10.99 / 10.52 / 10.70), so that triple is current, not stale. **D-214's "1.1161-1.180" is confirmed as a SPAN — and it is a span, not a direction**: BC is maximal AT the nominal by construction and falls off on **both** sides, so the low edge is the worst point but the high edge is wrong too. That ordering is now asserted, because a one-sided reading of the same span would be wrong.

### 2. Three arms separate the capacity half from the anchor half

Tyrell's wort, 15 °C, 14 d, degassed pH, all deterministic — no ensemble, so none of D-166's `only=`/`exclude=` RNG-pairing hazards apply.

* **COH(p)** — pKa = p everywhere AND the capacity back-solved at p. What a coherent member is.
* **MID(p)** — pKa = p everywhere, capacity left nominal. Isolates the capacity half.
* **ENS(p)** — MID's parameter map with the NOMINAL `y0`. What the sampler actually ships.

The only `y0` slot the pKa moves is **`cation_charge`**, established by diffing `y0` rather than assumed.

| pKa | day | ENS−COH (whole defect) | MID−COH (capacity half) | ENS−MID (anchor half) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3.86 | 0 | −0.1387 | +0.0000 | −0.1387 |
| 3.86 | 7 | −0.0482 | −0.0100 | −0.0382 |
| 3.86 | 14 | −0.0479 | −0.0100 | −0.0378 |
| 4.50 | 0 | +0.1185 | −0.0000 | +0.1185 |
| 4.50 | 14 | +0.0334 | −0.0048 | +0.0382 |

**D-214's +0.0099 pH is CONFIRMED — measured here as 0.0100** at day 7/14 on the low-pKa arm. It is also **21 %** of that arm's total defect at day 14 and **7 %** at t=0. The parked item was real and was the minor half; nothing in D-214 is wrong, but the beat it asked for could not have been scoped from it.

### 3. The anchor half is a CONTRACT violation, and t=0 is where it is airtight

`cation_charge` is back-solved at COMPILE from `initial_ph` using the pKa map (`_beer_cation`, and the wine twin at D-18), and the pH is solved at RUNTIME from the member's own sampled pKas. `initial_ph`'s documented contract is *"reproduce this pH at t=0"* (D-179/D-180; D-18 for wine). Off-nominal members did not.

**t=0 is asserted rather than the band, and the reason is structural, not stylistic.** At t=0 the state IS `y0`, and the anchor was solved so the pH function returns `initial_ph`. So **any** nonzero t=0 spread is 100 % artefact — there is no legitimate component to net out, unlike at day 14 where most of the spread is real physics. Measured on a 32-member LHS ensemble over all **83** sampled parameters:

| | t=0 degassed pH | spread | worst miss vs the anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped | 5.5062 .. 5.7778 | **0.2716** | **0.1438** |
| anchor re-solved per member | 5.6500 .. 5.6500 | 0.0000 | **2.30e-11** |

### 4. A number this beat produced and then RETRACTED, recorded rather than quietly dropped

The first draft of this measurement said *"the reported beer pH band is ~29 % wider at day 14"*, off a **1.287×** ratio. **That figure is wrong as a statement about the band, and it is retracted.** It came from sweeping `pKa_peptide_buffer` alone with all 82 other parameters held nominal, so it is that one parameter's own contribution. Run over every sampled parameter the band barely moves:

| day-14 degassed pH | range | spread |
|---|---|---|
| shipped | 4.1807 .. 4.7825 | 0.6018 |
| anchor re-solved | 4.1881 .. 4.7850 | 0.5969 |

**Band inflation 1.008× — 0.8 %, not 29 %.** The other parameters dominate the day-14 spread and the anchor error largely washes out across members. Worst PER-MEMBER day-14 shift is 0.0346 pH.

So the defect is a **per-member trajectory error, not a band-width error**, and the case for repairing it rests on the t=0 contract and on per-member correctness — **never on the reported spread**. The 1.287× must not be quoted as a property of the band. This is [[feedback-a-magnitude-defence-can-be-scoped-to-the-smallest-member]] run in reverse: a single-parameter sweep generalised to a registry it was never measured over. It is recorded because the archive has carried inherited numbers before, and a retraction that leaves no trace is how a wrong number gets re-derived later.

### 5. It is not beer-only, and it is not the peptide buffer's fault

`pKa_peptide_buffer` reaches the sampled set through `acetaldehyde_reduction`'s `reads`, which declares the SO₂/pH parameters read inside `ph_of_state` — D-160 added them **precisely because `reads` scopes the ensemble sampler**. So the whole `pKa_*` registry is drawn **iff a pH-reading Process is active**, and the defect is absent otherwise. That bounds the claim.

**WINE has the same defect**, and it was measured rather than inferred: a 24 °Brix must anchored at pH 3.50, 32 members, **21** sampled `pKa_*` parameters — t=0 pH **3.4208 .. 3.5780**, spread 0.1572, worst miss **0.0792 pH**.

This is the same structural class as D-206's `must_aa_fraction_methionine` ([[feedback-a-parameter-can-be-pinned-and-drawn]]): read at compile AND runtime, only the runtime half sampled. D-206 was the second instance; this is a **registry**, in both media.

### 6. What was built

`simulate_ensemble` takes an optional `y0_for_member` builder. Omitted ⇒ the fixed array, so **every existing direct caller is byte-identical**. `CompiledScenario.run_ensemble` supplies one via the new `CompiledScenario.reanchor_for_member()`, which returns `None` when there is nothing parameter-derived to rebuild (no `cation_charge` slot, or no `initial_ph`).

The repair itself is one call: `acidbase.cation_charge_for_ph(y0, schema, member_values, initial_ph)`. **That function already existed** — D-186 built it for `set_ph` — and at t=0, with `Byp` 0 and no evolved CO₂, it reduces **term for term** to the compile seam's own `solve_cation_charge`. So it re-derives the compiled anchor rather than competing with it, which is what makes the nominal draw an exact control rather than a tolerance.

**It re-anchors that one slot and nothing else.** A full re-run of the initial builder was considered and declined: it would move seeds this beat never measured (the nitrogen-dependent yield, the hop boil calc, every dosed inert slot), and shipping unmeasured movement to fix a measured one is the trap. The nominal run keeps the compiled `y0` by construction, so D-24's byte-for-byte reproducibility claim for the nominal is untouched.

**A builder that cannot solve a member's draw is a member FAILURE**, recorded in `failures` beside the solver failures — never a silent fall back to the nominal `y0`, which would put an unanchored member inside the reported spread while every survivorship count still read clean.

### 7. Six guards, and all three mutation arms hit their predicted outcome

* `test_every_sampled_member_starts_at_the_ph_the_scenario_anchored[beer|wine]` — the headline. **RED before this beat.**
* `test_the_reanchor_reproduces_the_compiled_slot_at_the_nominal_draw[beer|wine]` — the control [[feedback-the-setting-where-a-change-is-exact-is-the-control]]. It also asserts no slot **other** than `cation_charge` moved.
* `test_an_unanchored_scenario_gets_no_reanchor_builder` — pins the `None` branch that keeps every un-anchored ensemble in the repo byte-identical.
* `test_simulate_ensemble_without_the_hook_is_unchanged` — the low-level compatibility contract.
* `test_a_member_whose_anchor_cannot_be_solved_is_a_failure_not_a_fallback` — pins the no-silent-fallback rule above.

Falsified before shipping [[feedback-mutate-the-premise-before-building-the-guard]], with the outcome **predicted in advance each time** and the restore verified green between arms [[feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms]]:

* **Arm A — unwire the hook.** Predicted 2 RED / 5 GREEN. Got exactly that, and the RED **names the anchor**: *"wine: the worst sampled member starts 7.5238e-02 pH from the anchored 3.5"* (0.0752 at 16 members against the 0.0792 measured at 32 — the same defect, not a new one).
* **Arm B — re-anchor to `initial_ph + 0.05`.** Predicted 4 RED / 3 GREEN. Got exactly that. This is the arm that matters: it separates *re-derived correctly* from *re-derived consistently wrong*, which the headline guard **cannot** see alone, because it scores each member against the anchor through the same path the builder used.
* **Arm C — move the shipped capacity +1 %.** Predicted both BC guards RED. Got exactly that, proving the BC guards read what ships rather than a copied constant.

### 8. The capacity half is NOT repaired, and that is a decision with a reason

Repairing it means running the BC back-solve **per member**, which means moving the root-find into `src`. That was declined: `test_the_peptide_capacity_still_reproduces_peyers_published_wort_bc` is the guard that **forced the D-180 and D-181 re-anchors by going RED when the acid table moved**, and deriving the root in-process would make it compare the root-finder against itself — trading a guard that can fail for one that cannot. The full-precision literal is also load-bearing on purpose (the D-154 "663 vs 662.802522" lesson).

So `test_a_drawn_peptide_pka_carries_a_wort_that_is_not_peyers_1_18` **pins a defect on purpose**, and its docstring says so in terms a later reader cannot mistake: **a RED means the pair was made COHERENT — do not revert that beat, delete this guard and say so in the record.** A guard pinning a known-wrong value with no such note is how a later fix gets reverted as a regression.

### 9. Why this is not a licence to sample scenario inputs

D-24 excluded an axis, and that exclusion **stands**: Brix, YAN and every other recipe input stay fixed across members, and this beat adds no way to vary them. The distinction it draws is between what a recipe **states** and what this engine **computes** from what the recipe states. `initial_ph` is stated; `cation_charge` is computed from it *through parameters that are sampled*. Re-deriving the second is sampling parameter uncertainty correctly — which is the axis D-24 is **for** — rather than widening it. A future beat that wants to vary a stated input still needs its own decision.

### 11. The day-14 shift is CONVERGED, so "per-member trajectory error" is measured and not asserted

§4's t=0 result needs no convergence check — `cation_charge_for_ph` is exact, so 2.30e-11 is `solve_ph`'s own closed-form residual. The **day-14** per-member shift does: it is a trajectory difference under BDF at `rtol=1e-6`, and this repo's own rule is that no threshold separates a small coupling from the adaptive mesh [[feedback-separate-mesh-from-coupling-by-convergence]].

Both arms run the SHIPPED path (`run_ensemble` uses `kwargs.setdefault`, so an explicit `y0_for_member=None` reproduces the pre-D-233 behaviour exactly), 16 members, same seed and hypercube:

| rtol | worst day-14 shift | median shift | t=0 miss, fixed → anchored |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1e-6 | 0.032809 | 0.007881 | 0.1476 → 2.18e-11 |
| 1e-8 | 0.032809 | 0.007881 | 0.1476 → 2.18e-11 |
| 1e-9 | 0.032809 | 0.007881 | 0.1476 → 2.18e-11 |

**Identical to six decimal places across three orders of magnitude of solver tolerance.** It HOLDS rather than converging toward zero, so the shift is a real correction to each member's trajectory and not mesh noise. (0.032809 here against §4's 0.0346 is 16 members vs 32 — a different worst member, not a different result.) §4's number is therefore safe for a later beat to cite as physics.

### 10. Not covered

The capacity half stands, measured and guarded (§8). The wider census this implies — **every** parameter read at compile time that is also in the sampled set — is **not** run here and is its own beat; D-206's `must_aa_fraction_methionine` and this anchor are two known members of a set nobody has enumerated, and `reanchor_for_member` deliberately repairs only the anchor, so any other member of that set is still live. Whether `pKa_peptide_buffer`'s band should be re-derived now that the anchor moves with it is untouched. Everything D-232 left open is where it left it: the three-way growth-extent residue, the missing settling Process, the buffer-removal half of D-209 §8, and wine's un-audited nitrogen budget.

## D-234 — The compile-read-AND-sampled census is 32 names, 21 of them invisible to a grep, and it lands on a configuration the archive already forbade: `set_ph` still anchors only the nominal member, so since D-233 the two pH anchors disagree exactly as D-186's own docstring said they must not — and `copper_typical`'s entire share of the reported band is a broken cancellation whose coherent half moves nothing at all

**Flags:** D-233 — it repaired the t=0 anchor and left `set_ph`'s, producing the exact configuration D-186's own docstring forbids (*"Do not 'fix' this one anchor alone"*). Identified and measured here; the code still carries the half-repair, and the fix is priced rather than shipped. **D-186 is NOT flagged: its instruction is the live one and this record upholds it.**

Opened by the owner as D-233 §10's parked item — *"the wider census this implies — **every** parameter read at compile time that is also in the sampled set — is **not** run here and is its own beat"*. No production change. One test module, twelve guards, four mutation arms, one of my own pre-registered numbers wrong by 12 and published as wrong.

### 1. The predicate, stated before the instrument

A parameter is a **census member** iff (1) it is read during `compile_scenario` — through `ParameterSet.__getitem__`/`.value`, or off the `dict` that `.resolve()` returns — and (2) it is in the set `simulate_ensemble` would draw for that same compiled scenario, `_resolve_sample_names(process_set, parameters, None, None, events)`.

Such a parameter is **half** sampled. An ensemble re-draws the parameter map but compiles `y0` and `events` once, at the nominal, so the compile-time role stays pinned while the runtime role moves. Where the two roles were designed to cancel, sampling breaks the cancellation in one direction only, and the surviving term can carry the wrong sign — the shape D-206 found and `feedback-a-parameter-can-be-pinned-and-drawn` records.

**This is not D-153/D-156/D-157/D-159's drawability surface, and the distinction is pinned rather than asserted.** That audit asks whether a banded parameter is reachable by the sampler *at all*; its answer for the compile-consumed class (`otr_*`, the oak yields, `bottling_burst_*`) is *never drawn*. This one asks the opposite overlap: the names the sampler **does** reach and whose compile-time half it **cannot** move. The two sets are disjoint by construction, and `test_the_census_and_the_drawability_surface_are_disjoint` says so, because a reader who conflates them would read "compile-consumed" as "already audited".

### 2. A grep cannot answer it, which is why the set stayed unenumerated

The obvious instrument is a search for `parameters["…"]` over `scenario/compile.py`. It finds **26** names. It misses **21** — the 19 `pKa_*` and both `nitrogen_uptake_charge_*` — because the pH anchor reads them off `parameters.resolve()`, inside `acidbase.build_pka_map`'s generator expression and inside `nitrogen_charge_from_gpl`. So the block that contains the whole of D-233's defect is precisely the block source-matching cannot see (`feedback-grep-finds-claims-not-guards`).

**I pre-registered 12-20 names off that grep, and the answer is 32.** The prediction is wrong by more than the census is large, and it is wrong for the same reason the census was owed: I estimated the size of a set using the instrument that had already failed to find two of its members.

The instrument that does work records actual reads — `ParameterSet.__getitem__`/`.value` patched at **class** level (the seam builds four derived ParameterSets: `_apply_nitrogen_dependent_yield`, both `_override_*`, `_inject_temperature_ramp_rate`, and a wrapper around the loaded one stops recording at the first of them), plus a `resolve()` that returns a recording `dict` so keys read *off the map* are caught rather than the whole map being logged as read.

**The recorder has its own control**, because a blinded recorder reports an empty census and every membership test then passes vacuously — D-155's decoration in a fourth costume. `test_the_recorder_sees_a_read_no_grep_can` asserts it sees `pKa_tartaric_1` (resolve-mediated), `must_aa_fraction_methionine` (subscript), and **fewer than half** of all parameter names (a recorder that logged `resolve()`'s return rather than its reads would call all ~280 of them members).

### 3. The census — 32 names over the battery, five verdicts

Battery: one wine exercising every verb the medium admits, one beer likewise, one wine taking the two scenario-override knobs no other member reaches. Per scenario: wine 51 compile reads / **29** members, beer 33 / **20**, wine-with-overrides 38 / **30**; union **32**.

| # | member(s) | compile-time role | runtime role | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | `pKa_*` (the whole map) | t=0 anchor back-solve, `_wine_initial` / `_beer_cation` | every pH-reading Process (D-160) | **REPAIRED** — `reanchor_for_member` (D-233) |
| — | the same 19 | **`_verb_set_ph`'s event**, which closes over the compile-time resolved map | as above | **LIVE** — §4 |
| 2 | `nitrogen_uptake_charge_wine` / `_beer` | inside the same anchor solve, via `nitrogen_charge_from_gpl` | the charge balance | **REPAIRED** — `cation_charge_for_ph` reads them from the member's own map |
| 8 | `must_aa_fraction_*` | splits the must dose into eight pools | scales each depletion gate | **CLOSED at D-206** — §6 |
| 1 | `copper_typical` | seeds the `copper` state slot | mean-centres `PhenolicBrowning`'s `f(Cu)` | **LIVE** — §5 |
| 2 | `biomass_carrying_capacity`, `k_autolysis` | a scenario override replaces the reference value | their own rate laws | **BY DESIGN** — §7 |

The count is deliberately **not** pinned. Freezing a total is the vacuity D-159 refused and would go red on every new parameter. What is pinned is that **every member carries a verdict**: `test_every_census_member_is_classified` fails by name on a new one. `test_no_classified_member_has_gone_stale` pins the other direction, so the registry cannot rot into a description of a tree that no longer exists.

### 4. Finding 1 — `set_ph` anchors the nominal member only, and D-186 named this state as wrong in advance

`_verb_set_ph` captures `parameters.resolve()` at compile and its `mutate` closure re-solves the cation from **that** map. `simulate_scheduled` holds `events` fixed across members, so every member re-anchors with somebody else's pKa set. D-186 measured this (0.1292 pH over 24 members), declined to repair it, and gave the reason in its own docstring:

> **Do not "fix" this one anchor alone** — the two would then disagree about what a member's pH means, and the state-level one would be the odd anchor out.

D-233 then fixed the other one. Its §9 checked that it was not licensing a *scenario input* to be sampled, which is the objection it went looking for; it did not check whether the anchor it repaired had a sibling. So the configuration D-186 forbade is the one that ships, and it was reached by a beat that repaired the half in front of it.

Measured on **one** ensemble so the two numbers are a comparison and not two records' figures — wine, `initial_ph` 3.5, `set_ph` to 3.4 at day 12, probed 0.05 h after the event:

| | anchor | worst member miss | member spread |
|---|---|---|---|
| t=0 (`initial_ph`) | 3.5 | **2.03e-11** | **2.03e-11** |
| after `set_ph` | 3.4 | **0.07896** | **0.13202** |

24 members; at 12 the same scenario gives 0.05822 / 0.11128, at 8 0.04203 / 0.05667, and the miss grows with how far the ferment has dragged pH from the anchor before the verb fires (day 6 → 0.0147, day 10 → 0.0420, day 12 → 0.0582 at 12 members) — because that drift is what gives the drawn pKas leverage. **The nominal run is exact at both anchors**, which is precisely why nothing else in the suite sees it.

**The repair, priced and not shipped.** `StateMutation` is `Callable[[StateSchema, FloatArray], FloatArray]`, and `simulate_scheduled` already holds the member's running map (`current_params`) at the line where it applies the mutation — so the fix is to widen that signature by one argument and pass it. Blast radius measured, not guessed: **13** `def mutate` in `src`, **13** `mutate=` sites, **1** in `tests`, **3** `StateMutation` references. Only `_verb_set_ph` would change behaviour; the other twelve verbs ignore the argument and stay byte-identical, which is also the claim a shipping beat would have to prove. It is a runtime-type change and it belongs to its own beat, for the same reason D-233 declined the full `y0` rebuild: it moves a seam this beat did not measure.

### 5. Finding 2 — `copper_typical`'s coherent channel is exactly silent, so all of its band contribution is artefact

`copper_typical` seeds the `copper` state slot at compile (for a wine that does not name `copper_gpl`) and is the mean-centring reference in `PhenolicBrowning`'s multiplier `f(Cu) = 1 + k·(copper − copper_typical)`. D-134 made the two numerically identical on purpose, so an un-overridden wine sits at `f == 1` **exactly**, not merely close. A member moves the reference and not the seed, so that invariant holds at the nominal draw and nowhere else.

Two arms at the band top (0.00068 g/L against a nominal 0.00026), wine aged 4 d after a 5 mg/L O₂ dose, aged browning `A420` at the horizon:

| arm | what moves | `A420` vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| **control** — recompile, both roles move | seed **and** reference | **0.000000 %**, bit-identical |
| **sampler** — patch the map, what an ensemble does | reference only | **−14.04 %** |

The honest channel is not merely small, it is **exactly zero**: mean-centring makes a coherent copper level unable to change browning at all, by construction. So `copper_typical`'s entire share of the reported spread is the broken cancellation, and its sign is the one the parameter's name argues against — a wine whose *typical* copper is drawn higher browns *less*, because the wine it is compared against did not move. It is the D-206 shape on a second, independently found member, and there it was 13.4 % against 0.06 %; here it is 14.0 % against 0.0.

**The equality is a null and it has a positive control** (`feedback-a-null-result-needs-a-positive-control`): `k_browning_phenolic`, read only at runtime, moves `A420` by ~51 % and both arms move it **identically** — so the recompile path and the patch path agree wherever there is no compile-time role to pin, and the copper zero is a fact about copper rather than about the harness.

**The repair is not obvious, which is why it is not here.** Re-seeding `copper` per member is the same mechanism as D-233's anchor, but it must apply only when the scenario did **not** name `copper_gpl`: when it did, the reference and the wine's copper are genuinely independent quantities and drawing the reference alone is correct. So the fix is conditional on a compile-time branch, and it grows `y0_for_member` into the general seed rebuild D-233 explicitly declined. Owner's call.

### 6. The eight `must_aa_fraction_*` are closed by D-206 — verified, not trusted

D-206 enumerated all eight from `AMINO_ACID_SPECS` rather than arguing from methionine, and reported the gate each takes under a drawn fraction. Bands move between beats, so the census's job is to check that the record which closed the class still describes what ships (`feedback-reproduce-a-published-number-before-trusting-the-new-column`, turned on the repo's own archive). Closed form, no integration: the pool is seeded `dose·f_i/Σf` at compile, the gate is `aa_i/(K·f_i + aa_i)` at runtime, so `f_i` cancels exactly when both halves move.

Reproduced to the digit at D-206's own dose: every gate **0.888889** at nominal; `must_aa_fraction_methionine` **0.952381 → 0.833333** (D-206: 0.9524 → 0.8333), `must_aa_fraction_phenylalanine` **0.892430 → 0.885375** (D-206: 0.8924 → 0.8854); methionine widest, phenylalanine narrowest, ordering unchanged. **Nothing is owed here and nothing is to be re-run** — the class is measured, the worst case is named, and the honest channel was 0.06 % five years out.

(The absolute gate depends on the dose — at `amino_acids_gpl` = 1.0 the nominal is 0.909091, not 0.888889. That is the scenario's dose, not drift.)

### 7. The two override knobs are BY DESIGN, and D-24's surviving exclusion is intact

`carrying_capacity_gpl` and `autolysis_rate_per_h` are scenario inputs read at compile, and the parameters they override are sampled — the predicate matches. But `_override_carrying_capacity` / `_override_autolysis_rate` build a Parameter whose **value** is the scenario's number and whose **uncertainty** is the YAML reference's band, and the sampler draws `triangular(low, value, high)`. Measured, 24 members at `carrying_capacity_gpl` = 4.0 against a 2.5 reference on [2.0, 5.0]: drawn mean **3.8296**, median 3.8826, against the triangular expectation with the override as mode (3.6667) and with the YAML value as mode (3.1667). The stated operating point is the **mode**, not a number the sampler discards.

So this is not a defect and must not be filed as one: what is sampled is the parameter the input moved, carrying the YAML's uncertainty about it, which is what an ensemble is for. D-164's in-band bound exists for exactly this reason — an override outside the band would make `triangular(low, value, high)` ill-formed — and both YAML notes say so already. **D-24's surviving exclusion (scenario inputs are never sampled) is not breached**, and D-233 §9's warning against reading its correction as licence still stands.

### 8. Guards, and the four arms that falsified them

Twelve tests in `tests/test_compile_sampled_census.py`: three on the instrument, four on the census itself, two pinning the LIVE defects **on purpose** in D-233's idiom (**a RED there means the defect was repaired — delete the guard and say so in the record, never revert the repair**), one positive control, two measuring the CLOSED and BY-DESIGN verdicts.

Falsified before shipping with the outcome **predicted in advance each time**, and the file re-run green between arms (`feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms`):

* **Arm A — unwire D-233's re-anchor** (`y0_for_member` → `None`). Predicted 1 RED / 11 GREEN, failing on the *t=0* half. Got exactly that, and the RED names the baseline: worst t=0 miss **0.0801** at 12 members, against D-233's 0.0792 at 32 — the same defect, not a new one.
* **Arm B — a new unclassified compile read** (`parameters["mu_max"]` in `_wine_initial`). Predicted 2 RED / 10 GREEN — both wine parametrizations, beer green because the builder is wine-only. Got exactly that, and the RED names `mu_max`.
* **Arm C — blind the recorder** (`resolve()` returns the plain dict). Predicted 2 RED / 10 GREEN: the instrument's own control, and the staleness test. Got exactly that. **The RED fired wider than the prediction's reasoning**, and the extra names are the finding (`feedback-a-red-set-firing-wider-is-a-finding`): I predicted the 19 `pKa_*` would drop out and **21** did, the two `nitrogen_uptake_charge_*` with them — so the blind spot is *every* resolve-mediated read, not `build_pka_map`'s alone. `test_every_census_member_is_classified` stays GREEN under this arm, which is the reason it cannot be the only guard: a blinded recorder sees **fewer** members.
* **Arm D — remove the copper channel** (`f_copper` forced to 1.0 in `PhenolicBrowning`). Predicted 1 RED / 11 GREEN, failing on the *sampler* assertion with the control assertion still green — because a coherent move was already inert. Got exactly that.

### 9. Not covered

Both LIVE rows stand, measured and guarded: `set_ph`'s per-member anchor (§4, blast radius priced) and `copper_typical`'s seed (§5, conditional on `copper_gpl` and therefore on the `y0` generalisation D-233 declined). Whether `pKa_peptide_buffer`'s band should be re-derived now that the anchor moves with it is still untouched, as D-233 left it. The census is scored over the shipped **direct** oxidative wiring; the cascade sinks declare `copper_typical` too, so the `oxidative="cascade"`/`"direct_burst"` sets are an unmeasured third battery member — expected to widen §5's number rather than change its sign, since copper multiplies the whole of that set's O₂ uptake, but that is an expectation and not a measurement. Everything D-232 left open is where it left it: the three-way growth-extent residue, the missing settling Process, the buffer-removal half of D-209 §8, and wine's un-audited nitrogen budget.

## D-235 — Both pH anchors are per-member again: `set_ph`'s mutation reads the RUNNING parameter map, which closes the configuration D-186's own docstring forbade and D-234 measured — and the same one-line widening exposed a THIRD half-pinned read, in `add_dap`, worth 0.0108 pH that nobody had priced

**Corrects:** D-234 — its first LIVE row is repaired, and two of the figures it priced for this repair are wrong: the blast radius was counted at *definitions* and missed 28 test **call** sites, and "only `_verb_set_ph` would change behaviour" is false, because `_verb_add_dap` reads the map too.
**Corrects:** D-186 — its declined repair ships. Its *instruction* is upheld rather than reverted: it forbade fixing one anchor alone, and both anchors are fixed here.

Asked for by the owner together with the copper repair; this is the pH half, and copper is its own record.

### 1. What changed, in one line

`StateMutation` was `(schema, state) -> state` and is now `(schema, state, params) -> state`, where `params` is the **running** parameter map `simulate_scheduled` already held at the line that applies the mutation (`current_params` — the member's own draw under an ensemble, with every earlier `param_update` merged). `_verb_set_ph`'s mutation reads that instead of the `parameters.resolve()` it closed over at compile.

The ordering is now stated rather than left to a reader: the mutation is applied **before** this event's own `param_update` is merged, because an update takes effect from `time_h` *forward*. No shipped verb carries both; now one can.

### 2. The number the repair was for

Wine, `initial_ph` 3.5, `set_ph` to 3.4 at day 12, seed 0 — the same scenario D-234 §4 measured, so this is a before/after of one setting and not two records' figures.

| | worst member miss | member spread |
|---|---|---|
| after `set_ph` — before (D-234, probed 0.05 h past the event) | 0.07896 | 0.13202 |
| after `set_ph` — **now, AT the event** | **1.9836e-11** | **2.1265e-11** |
| t=0 anchor (D-233), same run | 2.0280e-11 | 2.3136e-11 |

24 members; at 12 the event reads 5.21e-12 / 6.64e-12. The second anchor is now in the first's class, which is the whole claim — D-186's objection was never the magnitude but that the two anchors would disagree about what a member's pH *means*.

**The probe moved, and that is a correction to how the defect is read, not a softening of it.** D-234 probed 0.05 h *after* the event. The driver emits every breakpoint post-mutation, so the grid point AT the event time is the anchored state, and the 0.05 h offset carries three minutes of ferment on top of it. Measured now at that offset: 7.04e-07 worst (24 members). That residual is drift and always was; it is four orders below the defect, so it changed nothing about D-234's reading — but a repaired anchor has to be scored where the anchor is.

### 3. The finding — a THIRD half-pinned read, in `add_dap`

Widening the signature made every verb's access to the running map explicit, which is how `_verb_add_dap` turned up. Its mutation calls `acidbase.remix_nitrogen_charge_excess`, which reads `nitrogen_uptake_charge_<medium>` — the medium's mean nitrogen charge z̄, the reference an excess is measured *relative to* — and it read it off a `parameters.resolve()` captured at compile. D-234 §3 filed that parameter REPAIRED, correctly, for its *other* compile role (`cation_charge_for_ph` takes it from the member's map). It has a second one, exactly as the pKa map did, and nobody looked.

The consequence is not "a number is slightly off". The slot stores a charge **excess**, and the charge balance reads the member's own z̄ back at every later step — so a nominal z̄ here stores the pool's excess against one reference and has it read against another. Wine, 250 mg/L YAN, 0.4 g/L DAP at day 2, 24 members, seed 0:

| quantity | worst member | mean |
|---|---|---|
| `nitrogen_charge_excess` slot | **0.0903** | 0.0400 |
| pH at the dose | **0.0108** | 0.0053 |

The slot's worst miss equals the worst |Δz̄| (0.09031) to five figures, and that is not a coincidence: by day 2 the assimilable-nitrogen pool is nearly exhausted, so the dose sets the excess outright and the member inherits the *whole* of its z̄ draw as error. This is near the worst case for the shape rather than a lucky reading of it.

Repaired in the same commit: the call takes the running map. `dosed_charge` deliberately does **not** move — `dap_nitrogen_charge` is a property of the compound, reaches no Process's `reads`, and so has no member value at all; it sits on the drawability surface's never-drawn side, not in this census.

0.0108 pH is ~7× smaller than `set_ph`'s 0.079. Shipping it anyway is `feedback-closer-to-reality-decides`: there is no threshold below which storing a value against the wrong reference becomes correct, and leaving it would have made D-234's "the other twelve verbs stay byte-identical" true by *choice* while reading as true by *construction*.

### 4. The blast radius was priced at the wrong end

D-234 priced this repair as 13 `def mutate` in `src`, 13 `mutate=` sites, 1 in `tests`, 3 `StateMutation` references. The first three are right. The fourth is **2**, not 3. And the count that actually cost the work is one it never took: **28 direct `event.mutate(schema, y)` call sites across six test files** — `test_aging_scenario.py` (16), `test_interventions.py` (5), `test_closure_ingress.py` (4), `test_fined_sulfur_destination.py` (2), `test_drawability_surface.py` (1), `benchmarks/test_validation_herzan_acetaldehyde.py` (1) — each a test applying one verb's jump in isolation, and each a hard failure under the new arity. `mypy` found them; the grep could not have.

That is D-234's own §2 failure one level down. There, a search for `parameters["…"]` missed 21 members because it matched the *read-site* pattern while the reads happened elsewhere. Here, a search for `def mutate` / `mutate=` missed 28 sites because it matched the *definition* pattern while the calls happened elsewhere. Both times the instrument was chosen for the thing being changed rather than for the thing that would break.

Each of the 28 now passes the compiled scenario's own `param_values` — the map that verb would really see — rather than an empty dict, so a site stays honest if its verb later starts reading it.

### 5. Guards

In `tests/test_compile_sampled_census.py`, where the defect was pinned:

* `test_set_ph_anchors_only_the_nominal_member` **went RED and was deleted**, per its own instruction and D-233's idiom. Replaced by `test_set_ph_reproduces_its_target_for_every_member`: the positive form, measured at the event, pinned as a **ceiling of 1e-9** — three orders below the defect it replaces and six above the root finder's own residual, so it is a band and not the digits. It keeps the t=0 assertion as the baseline that says what "per-member" costs here, and keeps both nominal-exactness assertions, which are what say the widening moved nothing that was already right.
* `test_exactly_two_verbs_read_the_running_parameter_map` is new and pins §3's claim rather than asserting it: each compiled mutation is handed a **recording** map and reports which names it looked up, so the reader set is `{set_ph, add_dap}` by measurement. A numerical diff under a perturbed map was rejected for D-234 §2's reason — it would call a verb a non-reader wherever the read happens not to move anything, and would call `dosed_charge` a non-read on the same logic.
* The registry rows for the 19 `pKa_*` and both `nitrogen_uptake_charge_*` change verdict. `test_no_classified_member_has_gone_stale` is unaffected by design: a repaired member is still compile-read and still sampled, only its verdict moves.

Full suite green at **1893 passed, 5 xfailed**.

### 6. Not covered

`copper_typical`, D-234's second LIVE row, is untouched here — it is a `y0` seed and not a mutation, so nothing in this beat reaches it; it is the next record. `pKa_peptide_buffer`'s band re-derivation is still where D-233 and D-234 both left it. The cascade-wiring battery member D-234 §9 named is still unmeasured. Everything D-232 left open is where it left it: the three-way growth-extent residue, the missing settling Process, the buffer-removal half of D-209 §8, and wine's un-audited nitrogen budget.

## D-236 — The `copper` seed moves with the member, so `f(Cu) == 1` is a design invariant again rather than a nominal-draw coincidence: aged browning's 16.65 % spread from `copper_typical` was 100 % artefact and is now bit-identical — and the guard that pinned the defect stayed GREEN through the repair, which is the part worth reading

**Corrects:** D-234 — its second LIVE row is repaired. Its measurement stands unchanged; what it called "not obvious, therefore not here" turned out to be one conditional rule, and the condition is the whole of the difficulty.
**Corrects:** D-233 — a SCOPE supersession, not an error. Nothing it measured or decided is wrong, but two of its statements no longer describe the code: the method it introduced is renamed `reanchor_for_member` → `y0_for_member`, and its "**It re-anchors and nothing else** … the rest of `y0` is untouched" now covers two slots. Marked so a reader who greps straight to D-233 gets the ⚠ instead of a symbol that no longer exists — which is the whole job of the correction map.

The copper half of the pair of repairs the owner asked for; the pH half is D-235.

### 1. The defect, restated in the frame that matters

`copper_typical` seeds wine's `copper` state slot at compile (for a wine that does not name `copper_gpl`) *and* is the mean-centring reference in `PhenolicBrowning`'s multiplier `f(Cu) = 1 + k·(copper − copper_typical)`. D-134 made the two numerically identical **on purpose**, so an un-overridden wine sits at `f == 1` exactly rather than nearly. An ensemble re-draws the parameter map but compiles `y0` once, so a member moved the reference and not the seed: the invariant held at the nominal draw and nowhere else.

D-234 §5 measured the two channels with a hand-wired `simulate_scheduled` — coherent move **exactly 0.000000 %**, patched-map move **−14.04 %** — and concluded that *all* of this parameter's share of the reported band is the broken cancellation. Measured here in the frame the band is actually reported in, an ensemble with `only=["copper_typical"]`, 12 members, aged 4 d after a 5 mg/L O₂ dose:

| | seed values across members | aged `A420` vs nominal |
|---|---|---|
| **before** | 1 unique (0.00026, the nominal) | up to **16.65 %** |
| **after** | 12 unique, each the member's own draw | **0.0000 %**, bit-identical |

Bit-identical rather than small: with one name drawn and both of its roles moving together, every member integrates the identical right-hand side as the nominal run. That is what makes the guard an exact-equality assertion instead of a tolerance — a tolerance would pass on a repair that merely shrank the artefact.

### 2. The repair, and why the condition is the hard part

`CompiledScenario.reanchor_for_member` becomes `CompiledScenario.y0_for_member`: a list of **rules**, one per slot whose compile-time value is a sampled parameter, applied to a copy of the compiled `y0`. Rule 1 is D-233's pH anchor, unchanged. Rule 2 re-seeds `copper` from the member's draw. It is still not the general seed rebuild D-233 declined and D-234 expected — nothing runs the initial builder again, and a slot with no rule is the compiled number.

The rename is not cosmetic: "re-anchor" stopped describing what the method does, and a name that lies is how a claim gets lost across a rename (D-231). The two tests that carried the old claim moved with it, and one of them **strengthened**: the nominal-draw control asserted "the re-anchor touched no slot but `cation_charge`" and now asserts that the whole rebuilt array equals the compiled one, so every present and future rule is covered without editing it.

**The condition.** The rule fires only for a wine that did **not** name `copper_gpl`. When a scenario states its copper, the wine's copper is a scenario INPUT and the reference `f(Cu)` is centred on is a separate sourced quantity; drawing the reference alone is then *correct* physics, not an artefact — a wine at 0.5 mg/L compared against a lower typical really does brown faster. Re-seeding there would overwrite an input with a parameter draw, which is exactly what D-24 excludes and what D-234 §7 went out of its way to certify intact. Measured on the same scenario with `copper_gpl` = 5.0e-4: the seed stays at the stated value for all 12 members and aged `A420` still spreads **14.34 %**, which is the honest channel and must survive.

The condition is checked twice over — on the scenario key *and* on the compiled slot still holding the nominal `copper_typical` — so a future seam that stops deriving this slot silently stops the rule rather than silently overwriting whatever replaced it.

### 3. The guard that stayed green, which is the finding

`test_copper_typical_reaches_the_run_only_through_the_broken_cancellation` was written at D-234 in D-233's idiom: *a RED here means the defect was repaired; delete it and say so in the record.* **It did not go red.** Its arms drive `simulate_scheduled` directly on `compiled.y0` with a patched parameter map, so they never touch `y0_for_member` — the hook the repair is made of. Patching a map after compile still moves the reference and not the seed, exactly as it always did.

Two ways to get this wrong, and both were live:

* read the green as *the repair was inert*. It is not — the ensemble measurement in §1 is what moved, and a hand-wired caller is simply a different path.
* delete it anyway, on the strength of the instruction. Its mechanism claim is still true and still load-bearing, and deleting it would leave the coherent-channel null (`f(Cu)` moves nothing when both roles move) with no guard at all.

So it is **re-scoped and renamed** — `test_a_hand_wired_run_on_a_patched_map_still_breaks_the_f_cu_cancellation` — pinning the mechanism, while `test_the_copper_seed_moves_with_the_member` pins the repair. Its sampler-arm assertion now reads as *a RED means the mechanism became unobservable*, which is a different failure from the one it used to name. **A defect pin that keeps passing across its own repair is a statement about which path it drives, not about the repair**; the idiom "a RED means it was fixed" only holds for a pin whose arms reach the thing being fixed. Recorded as `feedback-a-defect-pin-can-outlive-its-defect-by-driving-another-path`.

### 4. Guards and the two arms

Two new tests in `tests/test_compile_sampled_census.py`, plus the re-scoped one. Both arms were run with the outcome **predicted in advance**, and the file re-run green between them (`feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms`):

* **Arm E — unwire the copper rule.** Predicted 1 RED / 14 GREEN, failing on `test_the_copper_seed_moves_with_the_member`. Got exactly that, and the RED names the seed: `0.00026` against a drawn `0.00040114`. The named-copper arm stays GREEN under it, which is the point — its seed is pinned by the scenario either way, so it cannot substitute for the repaired test.
* **Arm F — fire the rule unconditionally** (drop the `copper_gpl` branch). Predicted 1 RED / 14 GREEN, failing on `test_a_scenario_that_names_its_copper_is_not_re_seeded`. Got exactly that, and the RED names the breach: the stated `0.0005` replaced by the draw. This is the arm the branch owes, because the repaired-side assertions would *all still pass* if the rule fired unconditionally — the condition is invisible from that side.

The registry row for `copper_typical` changes verdict, and with it the census has **no LIVE rows left**.

Full suite green at **1895 passed, 5 xfailed**, which is D-235's 1893 plus this beat's two new tests exactly — the `test_ensemble.py` un-anchored guard was rewritten, not split, so an unaccounted delta would itself have been a finding.

### 5. Not covered

The `oxidative="cascade"` / `"direct_burst"` sinks also declare `copper_typical`, and D-234 §9 named them as an unmeasured third battery member expected to widen §1's number. They are not measured here either — but the repair reaches them for free, because it moves the *seed*, and `copper − copper_typical` is now zero for every member under any wiring that mean-centres on the same reference. That is a mechanical argument, not a measurement, and it is stated as one.

`pKa_peptide_buffer`'s band re-derivation is still untouched, as D-233, D-234 and D-235 all left it. The `peptide_buffer_capacity_beer` back-solve remains offline at the nominal, measured and guarded, for the reason D-233 gave: moving it into `src` would make its Peyer reproduction test compare the root-finder against itself. Everything D-232 left open is where it left it: the three-way growth-extent residue, the missing settling Process, the buffer-removal half of D-209 §8, and wine's un-audited nitrogen budget.

## D-237 — The alternate oxidative wirings are measured, and D-234's expectation was wrong in DIRECTION: the cascade is the MILDEST of the three, not the widest — the copper repair does reach all of them bit-identically, and widening the census to them turned up a 50× band under `direct_burst` that the ensemble can never draw

**Corrects:** D-234 — its §9 expected the `oxidative="cascade"` / `"direct_burst"` sets "to widen §5's number rather than change its sign". The sign is right; the direction is not. Measured, the cascade moves aged `A420` by **15.38 %** against the direct wiring's 16.65 % — it is the mildest arm, not the widest.
**Corrects:** D-236 — a SCOPE completion, not an error. Its §5 stated the repair reaches the other wirings as "a mechanical argument, not a measurement, and it is stated as one". It is now a measurement, and the argument holds exactly.

The item the owner opened as *"the alternate oxidation wiring is still unmeasured — though the copper fix reaches it mechanically, which the record states as an argument rather than a measurement"*. No production change: this beat is instrument and guards.

### 1. The measurement, in the frame the band is reported in

`WINE_BROWNING` (D-236's own scenario), 12 members, `only=["copper_typical"]`, aged 4 d after a
5 mg/L O₂ dose. The PRE arm is the shipped pre-repair path rather than a re-implementation of it —
`run_ensemble` uses `kwargs.setdefault`, so an explicit `y0_for_member=None` reproduces it exactly.

| wiring | nominal aged `A420` | PRE-repair worst vs nominal | POST |
|---|---|---|---|
| `direct` (D-236's number, reproduced) | 1.337247e-02 | **16.6509 %** | **0.0000 %**, bit-identical |
| `cascade` | 1.110819e-02 | **15.3814 %** | **0.0000 %**, bit-identical |
| `direct_burst` | 1.116781e-02 | **16.7300 %** | **0.0000 %**, bit-identical |

D-236 §5's argument is confirmed with nothing left over: under every wiring `copper_typical`
reaches the run *only* inside a difference mean-centred on itself — `PhenolicBrowning`'s `f(Cu)`
under the direct sets, `activation_rate`'s re-homed copy of the same D-134 term under the cascade
(where `PhenolicBrowning` is absent entirely and `A420` comes from `QuinonePolymerization`). Move
the seed and the difference is zero for every member, so every member integrates the nominal's
right-hand side.

The **named-copper** arm — the honest channel that must survive — survives under all three, and
its PRE and POST numbers are *identical* to every digit, because the rule correctly does not fire:
direct **14.3368 %** (D-236 recorded 14.34), cascade **13.0549 %**, direct_burst **14.4185 %**.

### 2. Why the cascade is milder, measured rather than reasoned backwards

D-234's expectation was not careless — it followed D-141, where moving `f(Cu)` from browning to the
activation node made copper multiply *the whole* O₂ total including bisulfite instead of ~60 % of
one rate. That reasoning is about the **O₂ channel**, and on the O₂ channel it is right. The band
is reported on **browning**, and there it inverts:

| wiring | PRE-repair `o2` endpoint spread | PRE-repair `A420` spread |
|---|---|---|
| `direct` | 1.578e-04 | **2.7941e-03** |
| `cascade` | **3.430e-04** | 2.1350e-03 |
| `direct_burst` | 1.109e-04 | 2.3452e-03 |

The cascade moves **more than twice** as much O₂ and **less** browning. Under the direct sets
`f(Cu)` multiplies browning's own rate, so it changes browning's *share* of a fixed O₂ dose
directly. Under the cascade it multiplies the one shared activation gate, and every sink
downstream splits whatever that gate passes — so copper changes *when* the dose is consumed far
more than it changes how much of it ends up as pigment.

**The lesson is about the observable, not the size.** An expectation derived on one channel was
carried over to a number reported on another, and it survived two records unmeasured because both
channels are "oxidation". Recorded as
`feedback-an-expectation-transfers-with-the-channel-not-with-the-subject`.

### 3. The census is wiring-invariant, which is the widest reading of the item

D-234's 32-name census was scored over the **direct** wiring only, and said so. Re-run with the
recorder against all three wirings on all four battery members: **identical, in both directions,
everywhere** — wine 29, beer 20, wine-with-overrides 30, browning 9, unchanged. So the census is a
statement about the engine, not about one of its three wirings.

The structural reason, stated because it is what a future beat would break: the three sets differ
in which **Processes** are wired, and a Process is a *runtime* consumer. Compile-time reads come
from the seam's seeding and the verbs, and neither branches on the oxidative set. A wiring that
ever seeds its own state from a parameter would land in the census.

**Beer is not a third number.** `_OXIDATIVE_BURST_BEER == _OXIDATIVE_DIRECT_BEER` — the burst
Process is wine-only — so a beer `direct_burst` arm reports the same run twice. Asserted rather
than assumed, and it is also the one exemption in §4's non-vacuity check, named rather than hidden.

### 4. What the widening found that nobody was looking for — the census COMPLEMENT

`burst_antioxidant_initial` seeds the `burst_antioxidant` pool at compile, its band is
**0.0005 – 0.0033 – 0.025 g/L, a 50× span**, and **no Process declares it in `reads`** —
`AntioxidantBurstOxidation` reads its rate constants, never its seed. So the sampler cannot reach
it, and under `direct_burst`, the one wiring where that pool is the entire substrate, its
uncertainty is absent from every reported band.

This is a **third cell** nothing guarded, and naming it against its two neighbours is the point:

* the **census** is compile-read AND sampled — half-pinned, the surviving half can carry a wrong sign;
* the **drawability surface** (D-153…D-159) is banded AND drawn but unable to move the run;
* this is banded, **able** to move the run, and **never drawn**.

It is **pinned, not repaired**. Wiring a seed into a Process's `reads` changes what every burst
ensemble reports, and shipping unmeasured movement to close a gap found in passing is exactly the
trap D-233 §6 declined. The guard carries the D-233 idiom in terms a later reader cannot mistake:
a RED means it was fixed — delete it and say so in the record.

### 5. Ten guards, one mutation arm, and a prediction that was wrong in a useful way

Ten new tests in `tests/test_compile_sampled_census.py` (15 → 25). Nine of nine registered
predictions HIT; the tenth is §2.

**Arm J — replace the cascade's mean-centring reference with a bare `0.0`.** Predicted 1 RED / 24
GREEN. **Got 2 RED / 23 GREEN**, and the extra RED is the arm being right rather than the
prediction: killing the reference removes `copper_typical` from the cascade *altogether*, so the
**honest** channel collapses to exactly 0.0 too and the named-copper arm fires. The prediction was
under-specified — it reasoned about the repaired side only.

**The RED that matters is on the CONTROL, not on the equality.** Under Arm J the bit-identity
assertion would still have passed — a channel that moves nothing is bit-identical for the wrong
reason — and the only thing standing between that and a green suite is the PRE-repair arm asserting
>10 % movement first. A null result whose positive control is optional is not a null result.

**Two non-vacuity checks were added because the first version of one of them was itself vacuous.**
The census-invariance test compares the three wirings' Process sets to prove they really differ;
written the obvious way against `process_set.active` it **passed on all four scenarios while
comparing nothing**, because every oxidative Process is disabled until `begin_aging` and the
active sets at compile time are identical by construction. It compares membership now. That is
[[feedback-grep-finds-claims-not-guards]] arriving inside a guard written *for* non-vacuity.

### 6. Not covered

No production code changed here, so nothing D-236 left open moved. The `burst_antioxidant_initial`
gap of §4 is identified and pinned, not repaired, and it implies a census of its own — **every**
banded parameter read at compile that no Process declares — which is not run here. The
`peptide_buffer_capacity_beer` back-solve is the owner's other open item and is the next record.
`pKa_peptide_buffer`'s band re-derivation is still untouched, as D-233, D-234, D-235 and D-236 all
left it. Everything D-232 left open is where it left it: the three-way growth-extent residue, the
missing settling Process, the buffer-removal half of D-209 §8, and wine's un-audited nitrogen
budget.

## D-238 — The peptide capacity/pKa pair is coherent per member: D-233's reason for declining it was aimed at DERIVING THE SHIPPED CONSTANT, and re-rooting the SEED is a different act that leaves the round-trip guard's teeth exactly where they were — and the defect pin it was supposed to turn red stayed green for the second time in three records

**Corrects:** D-233 — §8's decision, on a scope distinction it did not draw. Its objection ("moving the root-find into `src` would make the round-trip test compare the root-finder against itself") is sound *about the shipped constant*, which is untouched here. It also reported the back-solve one ULP from the shipped literal (`…658` vs `…656`); that was a looser root-find, not a floor — at `xtol=1e-15` it is bit-identical, measured.
**Corrects:** D-214 — its parked item is now closed rather than measured-and-left. Nothing it measured is wrong; its 0.0099 pH stands, re-measured here at 0.0094-0.0095 and converged.

The owner's other open item, opened as *"the beer buffer-capacity constant is still solved offline
at the average (fixing it would make its own validation test check the solver against itself)"*.
The parenthesis is the archive's own reason, and taking it seriously rather than around it is what
this record is.

### 1. The objection, dissected — it is about one act, and the repair is a different one

`test_the_peptide_capacity_still_reproduces_peyers_published_wort_bc` has teeth because it holds
**two literals** against each other: the shipped `peptide_buffer_capacity_beer` from YAML, and
Peyer's published 1.18. It is what forced the D-180 and D-181 re-anchors, going red when the acid
table moved under it. Those teeth would be pulled by **deriving the shipped constant** — then the
test would ask whether a root satisfies the equation it was rooted on, which is a tautology.

Re-rooting the per-member **seed** is not that act. The YAML literal is unchanged, still scored
against Peyer's number by a titration neither the solver nor the constant produces. Both failure
modes the guard exists for still fire: move the acid table and the shipped literal stops giving
1.18 *and* the runtime solver stops reproducing the literal.

The distinction is worth naming because the archive nearly lost a repair to it for two records:
**an objection to a method is not an objection to every use of the method.** Recorded as
`feedback-a-circularity-objection-names-an-act-not-a-tool`.

### 2. What was built

`fermentation.core.acidbase` gains two pure functions — `peyer_fast_bc` (his §5.3.4 protocol on
this engine's charge balance) and `peptide_capacity_for_wort_bc` (the same back-solve, rooted on a
member's own map). `brentq` was already imported in that module, so no dependency moved.

`CompiledScenario.y0_for_member` gains **rule 3**, and it runs **first** — before D-233's anchor —
because `peptide_buffer` is an acid slot the t=0 cation back-solve reads. Rule 1 now reads the
array under construction rather than the compiled one.

`wort_buffering_capacity_peyer` = 1.18 is a **new provenanced parameter** (prime directive 2): the
target was prose inside the capacity's own block until the code needed to read it. Pinned
zero-width, and for a reason worth stating — Peyer's 0.94 / 1.18 / 1.21 / 1.24 / 1.34 series is
five *different worts* across the mash-and-boil process, not an error bar on the control wort, and
banding it off that series would be the transcription error
[[feedback-a-series-of-conditions-is-not-an-error-bar]].

**The control is exact, and that is the whole argument for the shape of this fix.** Run on the
compiled beer `y0` at the nominal pKa, the runtime solver returns the shipped literal **bit for
bit** — it re-derives the offline root rather than competing with it, exactly as
`cation_charge_for_ph` reduces term for term to the compile seam's own `solve_cation_charge`
(D-233 §6). D-233 §1's table reproduces to the digit at state level: 1.617633297044 / 1.548066231592
/ 1.573902153671 g/L, carrying BC 1.116059 / 1.180000 / 1.145594 at the shipped capacity.

### 3. The whole running map feeds the root, and the alternative was priced before it was refused

The tempting narrower rule is to re-root on the member's **peptide pKa only**, holding every other
pKa at the nominal. It was measured rather than argued: worst member **0.40 %** of the capacity
across 12 members, spreads 0.84 % (pKa-only) against 0.93 % (full map). It does not collapse a
channel; it barely moves one. **That 0.40 % is a FLOOR, not a bound** — one scenario, one seed,
twelve members — and it is written as one in the YAML note a later beat will actually read, because
this archive has quoted a single-configuration number as a general one before (D-233 §4's retracted
1.287×).

It was refused on two grounds, the second decisive:

* the back-solve is against a **measurement**. Peyer's 1.18 is a fact about a real wort, so every
  model constant entering the computed BC should feed the fit. The eight `*_typical_wort` acid
  LEVELS are not in the sampled set at all (measured: **0 of 8**), so this is the other acids'
  *pKas* and nothing else.
* a rule that reads the member's map and deliberately uses **one name** from it is a *new*
  half-pinned read — shipped inside the fix for half-pinning, in the exact defect class D-234's
  census exists to hunt. The next census sweep would land on it and be right to.

### 4. The cost, converged — and it is the OPPOSITE shape to the anchor half

D-233 §2's own arms (MID = pKa moved, capacity nominal; COH = both moved), both driven through the
public `peptide_buffer_gpl` seam so neither re-implements the rule under test:

| rtol | pKa 3.86 day 0 / 7 / 14 | pKa 4.50 day 0 / 7 / 14 |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-6 | 0.000000 / −0.009440 / −0.009529 | −0.000000 / −0.004512 / −0.004554 |
| 1e-8 | 0.000000 / −0.009440 / −0.009529 | −0.000000 / −0.004512 / −0.004554 |
| 1e-9 | 0.000000 / −0.009440 / −0.009529 | −0.000000 / −0.004512 / −0.004554 |

**Identical to six decimals across three orders of magnitude of solver tolerance**, so this is a
real per-member trajectory correction and not mesh noise — the check this repo requires of any
small coupling [[feedback-separate-mesh-from-coupling-by-convergence]]. D-233 §2's −0.0100 and
D-214's +0.0099 are both confirmed.

**Day 0 is exactly zero, and that is the finding, not a null.** The anchor half was 100 % artefact
*at t=0* and washed out later; the capacity half is invisible at t=0 and grows with the ferment.
The reason is that the t=0 cation back-solve **absorbs** a capacity change completely — a bigger
peptide pool is answered by a bigger back-solved cation, and the anchored pH is unmoved. So the two
halves of one defect are exactly out of phase, and a beat that had measured either one alone at its
own best moment would have concluded the other did not exist.

### 5. The defect pin stayed green again — predicted this time, which is the difference

`test_a_drawn_peptide_pka_carries_a_wort_that_is_not_peyers_1_18` was written at D-233 in the idiom
*"a RED means it was FIXED — delete this guard and say so in the record"*. **It did not go red**,
and unlike D-236 §3 that was predicted before the repair was built: every number in it is the
shipped CONSTANT scored through the test file's own titration, and the repair moves the per-member
SEED on a path those arms never drive.

Re-scoped and renamed to `test_holding_the_capacity_fixed_while_the_pka_moves_costs_peyers_1_18`,
pinning the mechanism that argues for rule 3. Its docstring's stated *reason* was rewritten, not
just its scope — it asserted that a per-member root-find would compare the root-finder against
itself, which §1 shows is false, and a guard carrying a false reason is how a correct beat gets
reverted as a regression.

Two records apart, the same idiom has now failed twice in the same way. **"A RED means it was
fixed" is only sound for a pin whose arms reach the seam the fix will land on**; for one that
scores a constant, or drives a hand-wired path, the repair is invisible and the instruction reads
as evidence of inertness. The pin still has to be re-read, not obeyed.

### 6. Guards and three arms, each with its outcome predicted in advance

Four new tests in `tests/test_organic_acids.py`, plus the re-scoped pin. Full suite green at
**1909 passed, 5 xfailed** — D-236's 1895, plus D-237's ten and this beat's four exactly, with the
rename accounted for as a rename [[feedback-an-unaccounted-test-count-delta-is-itself-a-finding]].

* `test_the_runtime_solver_reproduces_the_shipped_capacity_at_the_nominal` — the exact control,
  **and** the cross-check that the state-built and parameter-built worts are one composition.
* `test_every_sampled_member_carries_peyers_wort_bc` — the repair. Reads the member's **seeded
  slot**; the parameter still holds the nominal by design, so a guard reading the parameter would
  have passed identically before and after.
* `test_the_nominal_member_keeps_the_compiled_capacity_exactly` — the exact-nominal skip.
* `test_a_scenario_that_names_its_peptide_buffer_is_not_re_capacitated` — the branch, with the
  positive control that a stated pool's members genuinely do leave Peyer's target.

Restore verified green between arms [[feedback-verify-the-restore-between-mutation-arms]]:

* **Arm K — unwire rule 3.** Predicted 1 RED. Got it, naming the seed pinned at the shipped literal.
* **Arm L — fire rule 3 but leave rule 1 reading the compiled array** (the ordering). Predicted RED
  on `test_every_sampled_member_starts_at_the_ph_the_scenario_anchored[beer]` with wine — which has
  no peptide slot — green as the free control. Got exactly that, **and the miss is 0.1534 pH against
  the original defect's 0.1438**: a wrong order is worse than no repair at all. D-233's own headline
  guard catches the ordering for free, so it needed no new guard, only the prediction.
* **Arm M — fire rule 3 unconditionally.** Predicted 1 RED. Got it, naming the breach (the stated
  1.4 replaced by a back-solved 1.548). The condition is checked **twice over** — the scenario key
  *and* the compiled slot — and either check alone blocks the breach, so this arm had to drop both.

### 7. Two docs that would have started lying, fixed in this commit

`peptide_buffer_capacity_beer`'s YAML block said *"its uncertainty is carried by that pKa's band
instead of duplicated here"* and *"do not restore a band here without also making the pair sample
jointly"*. The pair now **does** sample jointly, through a seam rather than a band, and the seed's

pre-anchor seam as the right place to model less buffering protein; rule 3 now writes that slot

### 8. Not covered

`pKa_peptide_buffer`'s band re-derivation is **still** untouched, as D-233 through D-237 all left
it — and it is now more clearly owed than before, because both of its compile-time roles move with
the member and the band was drawn when neither did. The 0.40 % second channel of §3 is measured and

Everything D-232 left open is where it left it: the three-way growth-extent residue, the missing

## D-239 — Beer's wort carries three free amino-acid side chains that buffer and then leave with the yeast: the sentence saying so has been quoted in this repo since D-179 as the reason the peptide lump is peptides, the lump silently absorbed their share at the back-solve, and splitting the two fates apart costs day 7 the last of its envelope margin

**Corrects:** D-209 — its §8 scope line, which called the omitted buffer half a **same-sign** acidification that "can only make the acidification larger, never smaller". Measured against a coherently unwired arm, the early sign is the OTHER one: **+0.0023 pH at day 1**, because only 0.298 of the wort's nitrogen is drawn by 24 h, so the pool is still 70 % present and buffering while the lump's share of it has already gone. The claim is right from day 2 onward (−0.0140), not before. Everything else in that section stands, including the drift it measured and this term reproduces.
**Corrects:** D-179 — its reading of Peyer §5.5. The passage says free aspartate, glutamate and histidine "account for ca. 10 % of the total BC", and it was read as licence to model the buffer as peptides ALONE. It is equally a statement that a wort carries 10 % of its buffering in three species this model did not have, and the back-solve had nowhere to put that share except the permanent lump.

The owner's chosen beat: D-209 §8's unbuilt **buffer-removal half** — assimilation removes the
nitrogen pool's charge but not its *buffering* — the one item D-232 §10 still listed open after
D-214 refused both of its named rivals.

### 1. The cheap check first, and it refused the refusal

D-178 killed malt phosphate on geometry: pKa 2.15/7.20 sits either side of beer's window, so its
charge is ~0.99 **flat** across pH 4.0-4.6 and an inverse anchor absorbs it outright — "a near
no-op, not a weak buffer". Free amino acids look like the same case: α-COOH ~2.0-2.4 and α-NH₃⁺
~8.8-9.9 are both outside the window. If that closed the term, no trajectory run was needed.

It does not. Computed from Peyer Table 16's own composition — the table D-209's `z̄` was derived
from — the pool's local buffer capacity is **0.179 mEq/L/pH at wort pH against the model's own
2.073, i.e. 8.6 %**, and 4.2-6.4 % across the rest of the window. Three species carry effectively
all of it: histidine 0.135 of the 0.179 at pH 5.65, aspartate and glutamate taking over as the
beer acidifies (0.176 and 0.154 of 0.459 at pH 4.40).

**8.6 % reconciles with a published ~10 % that was already in this repo's own files**, and that
is the part worth reading twice. `acidbase.yaml`'s header has quoted Peyer §5.5 since D-179:

> *"because of the very low or very high pKa values of the α-carboxylic acid group (range 1.7-2.2)
> or α-amino group (range 8.8-10.6), respectively, most amino acids contribute only poorly to the
> BC in the relevant pH range … Little contribution to the wort buffer system is made by aspartate
> (pKa 3.86), glutamic acid (pKa 4.25) and histidine (pKa 6.04), which account for ca. 10% of the
> total BC at a wort pH of 5.5."*

The first half of that sentence is D-178's own geometry argument in the source's words; the second
half names the three exceptions and sizes them. The archive kept the first half and used the
second as a reason the lump is peptides. **The sentence was on file, quoted in code, and read as a
licence to omit** [[feedback-re-read-the-source-you-already-mined]].

### 2. The defect is not a wrong constant — it is one lump with two fates

`peptide_buffer_capacity_beer` is back-solved so the model's wort reproduces Peyer's published
BC = 1.18. Until now that back-solve ran on eight organic acids and the lump and **nothing else**,
so every bit of a real wort's amino-acid buffering was attributed to the lump. The lump is
permanent. The amino acids are eaten. **So beer's wort buffered correctly at t=0 and went on
buffering like a wort for the rest of the ferment.**

That framing matters for what shipped. The lump is a lump and is entitled to stand for anything
non-organic-acid; nothing about 1.5481 g/L was *wrong*. What was wrong is that it conflated two
pools with different fates, and the fix is a re-partition at constant total, not a re-fit:
