## D-249 — the assimilable-nitrogen exhaustion timing miss is ATTRIBUTED and the repair REFUSED: the nitrogen channel is SLOWER than the fermentation containing it at every pitch, no transport capacity can reach the miss, and what the beat does identify is a time-free rate-law shape defect that survives both the clock and a 6.25× pitch change

**Corrects:** D-248 — §5 and §12 left the exhaustion timing "open and unattributed" and read it as ~1.5× fast. It is attributed here, and the reading was framed on the wrong denominator: the whole run is faster than Crépin's than the nitrogen channel is, so the miss is the clock, not the nitrogen.
**Flags:** D-246, D-248 — the shared Crépin fixture pitches at 0.25 g/L, the wine benchmark's default. Crépin states no inoculum at all; the only sourced value for this medium is her sibling paper's 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ = 0.04 g/L, **6.25× smaller**, and moving onto it takes the exhaustion time to 29.9 h against her 28 h while breaking D-248's own Coleman-yield guard. Identified and priced, code unchanged — it is a trade and the owner's call.

D-248 §12 left three things open and named two as the owner's call. The owner picked the timing. It ends in a refusal, and the measurement that makes the refusal load-bearing turns out to name a different defect than the one the beat went looking for.

### 1. The load-bearing comparison is pitch-invariant, and it is the whole refusal

The miss was read against Crépin's `N_T` alone. Read instead against the fermentation the nitrogen sits inside — same trajectory, only the observable differing:

| | pitch 0.25 (shipped) | pitch 0.04 (sourced, §3) |
|---|---|---|
| hours to dryness (`S ≤ 2 g/L`) | 78.2 | 97.2 |
| whole-run gap vs her EF of 150 h | **1.92× fast** | **1.54× fast** |
| 90 % of the assimilable N consumed | 17.6 h | 29.9 h |
| nitrogen gap vs her `N_T` of 28 h | **1.59× fast** | **0.94×** |

At **both** pitches the nitrogen channel is slower than the run containing it. A channel that lags its own fermentation cannot be what makes that fermentation fast, and the conclusion does not depend on an inoculum nobody has sourced.

**With the clock divided out it is stronger still.** Crépin exhausts at 28 h of a 150 h fermentation — 18.7 % of the way in. The model is at **22.5 %** (shipped) and **30.8 %** (sourced). Relative to its own run the model is nitrogen-**late**, not early, and that survives multiplying either time axis by any constant.

**The temperature confound points the other way.** `commensurate_scenario` ramps 28 → 18 °C over its 14 days; Crépin held 28 °C. Corrected to isothermal the model is *faster*: 78.2 → 73.0 h and 97.2 → 89.2 h. The finding is fast **despite** a confound pushing at it.

### 2. Varela is corroboration only, and the pitch match is what makes it a comparison at all

`tests/benchmarks/test_validation_varela2004.py` already pins this engine at **1.6–2.2× fast** against Varela 2004 at the same 28 °C, and attributes it there to a cross-study Coleman-vs-Varela difference rather than a model defect (D-56/D-57) — Coleman's own reference model gives ~84.5 h for those inputs and the engine matches it line-for-line.

That band is measured at `_PITCH_GPL_RESEARCH = cells_per_ml_to_pitch_gpl(1.0e6)` = **0.04 g/L**. So reading the shipped fixture's 1.92× as "inside the band" would compare runs pitched **6.25× apart** — an artifact, and this record does not make that claim. Reconstructed at Crépin's stated temperature *and* the sourced pitch the gap reads **1.68×**, inside the band: a different must at a different nitrogen level landing where the same engine already lands. §1 does not rest on this and stands without it.

**The nearest counter-example is named rather than left for a reader to find.** `tests/test_organic_acids.py::test_the_model_ferments_tyrells_wort_on_tyrells_schedule` is a live xfail saying the model ferments Tyrell's **wort** ~3.2× too *slowly* — the opposite direction to everything above. The two coexist: different medium, different sugar spectrum, and a beer clock calibrated through its own lineage (D-215/D-222/D-223) rather than through Coleman. Nothing here claims a clock direction for beer, and "the model's clock runs fast" is a **wine** attribution only. Reconciling the two is neither attempted nor implied by this record.

### 3. The fixture's pitch is unsourced, and moving it is a TRADE rather than a repair

Crépin never states an inoculum — `grep -c inocul` over the full PMC text is **0**. Minebois — the same Bely, Sablayrolles & Barre 1990 medium and the same lab lineage — states 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, converted through the engine's own D-219 crossing to **0.0400 g/L**. The fixture carries **0.25**, inherited from the wine benchmark's default rather than chosen for these papers.

| | 0.25 (shipped) | 0.04 (sourced from the sibling) | Crépin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 90 % of N consumed | 17.6 h | **29.9 h** | **28 h** |
| peak biomass | 3.418 | 3.213 | **3.39** at EF |
| Coleman `Y_X/N × N_init` ratio | **0.984** | **0.925** | — |
| assimilable N residual | 0.00622 | 0.00623 | 0.0021 |

**It buys the timing and sells the anchor.** 0.925 sits outside the 0.984 ± 0.02 that `test_biomass_now_reaches_the_coleman_yield_the_compile_seam_installs` asserts, so this *breaks* a shipped guard rather than moving a number, and peak biomass goes from +0.8 % to −5.2 % against her measured 3.39. And 0.04 is a transfer from a related paper, not Crépin's number. Not changed here; flagged, priced, and left to the owner.

### 4. No transport capacity can reach the miss — which is why it is refused, not deferred

D-248 §5 pinned the *extent* as insensitive to `amino_acid_uptake_capacity_ratio` across a 200× sweep and was careful to say the timing was a separate matter that misses. It is also **unreachable**:

| `r` | 1 | 5 | 20 | 100 | **1000** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 90 % consumed | 17.61 h | 16.71 | 16.49 | 16.40 | **16.38** |
| nitrogen gap | 1.59× | 1.68 | 1.70 | 1.71 | **1.71** |
| the run's own gap | 1.92× | 1.93 | 1.94 | 1.94 | **1.94** |

Across **three orders of magnitude** the exhaustion time saturates at ~16.4 h and never overtakes the run. The reason is the rate law itself: `ρ_N ∝ X` makes uptake a slave to the biomass performing it, so however large the capacity, nitrogen cannot be consumed faster than cells accumulate. A knob that cannot reach the quantity it would be fitted to is not a deferred repair.

### 5. The residue the beat DOES identify is time-free, and it is a functional-form defect

Crépin's Data Set S1 panel B gives dry weight at all four landmarks: **0.83, 1.39, 3.36, 3.39 g/L** at 16, 20, 28 and 150 h. Against the fraction of nitrogen gone at each:

| at this fraction of N consumed | measured `X`/final | model `X`/peak (0.25) | model (0.04) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 % | **0.245** | 0.543 | 0.513 |
| 75 % | **0.410** | 0.777 | 0.762 |
| 100 % | 0.991 | 0.917 | 0.910 |

Biomass-against-nitrogen contains no time, so no clock rescaling can move it — and the two model columns, 6.25× apart in inoculum, show it is not a pitch artifact either. Real yeast strip half the must holding a quarter of their final biomass; this model needs over half of its peak.

**Localised to uptake rather than growth.** At the sourced pitch the *biomass* landmarks are off by 1.29× and 1.21× while the *nitrogen* landmarks are off by 1.59× and 1.42×: growth timing is roughly right there and uptake lags further. That places the defect in the uptake rate law and keeps it clear of `mu_max`, which D-230 §7 warns against re-opening on a second growth limitation.

**This is NOT D-248 §10 re-opened, and §10 stays refused.** §10 designed and refused a storage-quota / nitrogen-catabolite-repression **cap** — a brake on uptake once the cells' quota fills. That is the opposite sign: a late brake cannot *raise* the biomass share at 50 % nitrogen consumed, so it would be inert on exactly this measurement, which is what §10 said of it. Its three grounds are untouched. What is identified here is that **`ρ_N ∝ X` is the wrong functional form early** — an object §10 never considered and never priced.

**Refused for now, on the D-120 / D-189 / D-195 / D-247 pattern.** A replacement form needs either a sourced per-cell transport capacity (a `V_max` per gram of cell with its own saturation constant) or an explicit intracellular storage compartment that uptake fills and growth draws from. Neither is in hand, and inventing one would make the model reproduce this table by construction — the D-98 trap. Measured and priced.

### 6. A source note, recorded and not resolved

Crépin prints her four landmarks **twice and differently**: the Results section gives "16, 20, 40, and 110 h", Methods gives "(16 h, 20 h, 28 h, and 150 h)". `CREPIN_EXHAUSTION_H = 28.0` follows Methods, the operational statement of when the samples were actually drawn. Nothing above turns on the choice — 40 h makes the nitrogen miss larger and 110 h makes the clock gap smaller, and neither rescues the model. Re-deriving the constant is a separate beat.

### 7. What is pinned

New file `tests/test_nitrogen_timing_attribution.py` (7 tests, ~10 s, **no `src/` change**): the pitch-invariant direction claim at both pitches; the 1000× capacity saturation; the time-free landmark share; the temperature confound's sign; the matched-pitch Varela corroboration; the time-free front-loading at both pitches; and a declared-fact guard on the fixture's unsourced pitch, so moving it has to be deliberate.

**The direction guard is verified non-vacuous by its opposite arm.** Scaling `q_sugar_max` to 0.6 slows the run to 144.1 h while leaving the nitrogen at 17.59 h untouched, and the guard goes **RED** — so a future change that fixed the clock without touching nitrogen would be caught, which is exactly the case in which this record's attribution reverses.
## D-250 — the D-248 uptake surplus was booked as EXTRACELLULAR ammonium, so nitrogen already inside the yeast went on titrating the must: it is moved to an intracellular slot in no charge balance, worth up to +0.215 pH mid-run, and the same move CLOSES the bacterial-nitrogen residue as not-a-defect

**Corrects:** D-248 — on two counts. (1) Its surplus nitrogen was refunded to `N`, which the acid-base charge balance reads (D-209); that is an addition of differently-charged nitrogen to `N`, which `nitrogen_charge_excess`'s own docstring (D-210) records as the one thing that cannot happen without a re-mix. Mass always closed; charge did not. (2) Its `Flags: D-100` residue ("MLF/Brett cannot read the `N` slot uptake fills, so the model over-states yeast/bacteria nitrogen competition") rested on reading that slot as extracellular — under the corrected booking the bacteria are blind to an *intracellular* store, which is right, and the residue closes without a repair.

The owner picked the bacterial-nitrogen residue. Measuring it turned up a larger defect sitting underneath it, and the two turned out to be one repair with a fork — the owner took the fork, and the residue closed as a consequence rather than as work.

### 1. What the assigned residue actually measures

`MalolacticGrowth` and `BrettGrowth` draw nitrogen from the identity-agnostic pair only (`amino_acids` = arginine, `amino_acids_generic` = glutamine). D-248's uptake strips that pair to ~0.6 % of initial. Shipped tree, wine + 2 g/L dosed amino acids, uptake on vs the same run with it disabled, fresh compile per arm:

| | uptake ON (shipped) | uptake OFF (control) |
|---|---|---|
| co-inoculated MLF, `X_mlf` end | 0.09560 (1.912×) | 0.11595 (2.319×) |
| ...malate remaining at day 3 | **0.5526** | **0.6478** |
| Brett 40 d, `X_brett` end | 0.30747 (**1.025×**) | 0.49028 (1.634×) |
| ...4-ethylphenol end | 0.034837 | 0.046710 |

Brett loses **96 %** of its growth increment. But MLF is **not attributable on malate**: the starved arm converts *more*. That is two errors in one observable, and finding the second one is §2.

### 2. The larger defect: the surplus was booked where it still titrates the must

`N` runs **300 → 436.8 mg N/L** on that must — above its own starting ammonium share, never above the must's declared total. Nitrogen is conserved to `rtol=1e-8` in every arm; **the defect is charge, not mass**. `acidbase.NITROGEN_KEY` is `"N"` and the pool carries the medium's mean charge per mole N (D-209), so pH runs **3.030 → 3.216** where the control holds at 3.030.

Dose-scaled, and exactly zero where D-248 promised it would be:

| must | `N` peak / start | max pH gap vs the no-uptake arm |
|---|---|---|
| undosed wine | 1.000× | **0.0000** (Process disabled at the compile seam — D-248's isolability claim holds) |
| + 0.5 g/L amino acids | 1.062× | 0.0449 |
| + 2.0 g/L amino acids | 1.456× | **0.2147** |

It is a **mid-run transient** — `N` still reaches ~0 by day 2 — so Crépin's endpoint residual and every endpoint-scored benchmark were blind to it, and no wine test scores pH mid-run on a dosed must. **The artefact was invisible to every shipped guard**, which is why the owner's call to pin it is what makes this beat non-vacuous. (This is not the recorded day-1 pH miss: that one is beer, where the amino-acid ledger returns zero by construction.)

### 3. The dose decomposition separates the two errors, and reverses one reading

The pH artefact scales with the dose; pool stripping is near-total at both. So running both doses is the decomposition.

| dose | `X_mlf` increment ON/OFF | malic left at d3, ON/OFF | `X_brett` increment ON/OFF | 4-EP ON/OFF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 g/L | 0.537 | **4.000** | **0.146** | 0.939 |
| 2.0 g/L | 0.691 | 0.853 | **0.039** | 0.746 |

**Starvation owns the bacterial catalyst at both doses, and is worse at the LOW dose** where the pH artefact is small — a 0.045 pH shift through an SO₂ gate cannot produce an 85 % loss. **The malate sign flip is a 2 g/L artefact**: at 0.5 g/L the starved arm leaves 4× more malate, which is starvation showing through cleanly; at 2 g/L the 0.215 excursion lifts MLF's own pH logistic enough to over-compensate and reverse the reading. Brett's confound points the *other* way — its gate partitions molecular SO₂ at the solved pH, so a higher pH means *less* inhibition — which is why its 96 % loss is attributable despite a tailwind.

### 4. The fork, and why the two are one repair

- **A: `N` is extracellular ammonium**, as the code said. Then bacteria should read it, the blindness is the defect, and the pH artefact stays.
- **B: `N` after uptake stands in for intracellular storage** — which D-248's own docstring concedes when it lists "booked as extracellular ammonium rather than an intracellular reserve" among the reasons its tier is speculative. Then bacteria are *correctly* blind, the assigned residue closes, and the booking is the real repair.

Fixing the booking closes the residue for free; teaching bacteria to read `N` commits to A and keeps the artefact. **They cannot both ship.** Owner took B. Same shape as D-248's own `yan_mgl` two meanings: one repair, two frames.

### 5. What was built

`stored_nitrogen` — wine-only, `g N/L`, weight 1.0 on `total_nitrogen`, in **no** charge balance. Uptake parks its nitrogen there and no longer touches `N` at all. Growth's Monod **and** its `f_N·dX` draw read `N` and the store together, split **in proportion to what each holds**; the D-32 swap refunds that draw on the *same* split, through one shared helper.

- **The split is proportional rather than store-first on purpose.** A preferential draw puts a C⁰ kink exactly where the store empties, and the BDF Jacobian probe straddles that kind of gate.
- **The swap's split is a correctness coupling, not tidiness.** Growth's `N` draw is now a *fraction* of `f_N·base_dx` while the swap's refund is the whole of `ψ·gate·f_N·base_dx`; booked wholly to `N` it makes net `dN/dt` **positive** and the artefact returns with the uptake Process innocent. Driven and guarded.
- **The two cellular nitrogen gates read the sum**, and this was forced rather than chosen. Uptake *inflated* `N`, so the Ehrlich fusel gate `n/(K_n+n)` has been running high and the H₂S de-repression gate `K/(K+n)` suppressed ever since D-248 — the state in which D-248's four fusel xfails closed. Gates on `N` alone would collapse both.
- **`Process.touches_where_present`** — a medium-conditional declared touch, for a Process wired into both media that writes a slot only one carries. Growth is the case: declaring the store in `touches` outright makes every beer ProcessSet raise on an unknown variable; declaring it nowhere makes every wine ProcessSet raise on a leak. It is not a relaxation — an undeclared slot still fails strict mode, and the guard pins that with its own leaky-Process arm.

### 6. The prediction was pre-registered, and it is also the verification

`N` and the store have the same source and the same sinks; only the split differs. So the **sum** must follow the shipped `N` trajectory, and *everything except pH must be bit-identical*. Measured across trees, one process per tree:

- **Beer: bit-identical, 0.00e+00 on every observable.**
- **Wine, everything except pH: ≤1.9e-7** (biomass, sugar, ethanol, all eight pools, three fusels, H₂S, the skeleton park).
- **Wine pH: 3.13776 → 3.03030** peak on the dosed must — 3.0303 against the no-uptake arm's 3.0301. `N` peak 1.456× → **1.004×**.

The residual 1e-7 is the schema, not the physics, and that is **falsified rather than asserted**: the *undosed* wine — where uptake is disabled at compile and cannot contribute — moves 1.17e-7 on biomass too. 98 → 99 slots changes `solve_ivp`'s RMS-weighted BDF error norm and therefore step selection; this is the third recorded instance.

### 6b. The repair UN-MASKS the physical signal, which §3's table only sets up

"Wine moves nowhere except pH" is true of the thirteen observables diffed in §6 — and the thing *downstream* of pH is the malate reading §3 is about. Re-run on the repaired tree, same probe:

| malate left at day 3, uptake ON / OFF | pre-D-250 | post-D-250 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.5 g/L must | 4.000 | **4.655** |
| 2.0 g/L must | **0.853** | **1.181** |

The starved arm now leaves more malate at **both** doses. The defect §3 identifies is not the ratio at either point — it is that the ratio's **sign depended on the dose**; that is what is fixed. Nothing in the repo exercised a co-inoculated MLF with uptake live (every shipped MLF and Brett test isolates the competitor in both arms), which is exactly why it could ride, and it is now pinned at both doses.

**The extracellular reading of §7, exact and interpolated the way D-249 crosses:** 90 % consumed at **16.411 h** outside the cells against **17.608 h** on the model total, i.e. **1.7062×** and **1.5902×** against Crépin's 28 h, with the run at 78.189 h for **1.9184×**. The store peaks at **32.753 mg N/L**, 16.3 % of the must's assimilable nitrogen. Reading the crossing at the sample index instead of interpolating puts it 0.5 h late and returns 1.66 — incomparable with the 1.59 it is scored against, so the guard uses D-249's own `_cross` idiom.

### 7. What is NOT repaired, so a later beat does not re-find it

**Bacteria stay blind, and Brett still loses 96 % of its growth increment.** That is the model being *right*: real yeast take essentially all the assimilable nitrogen (Crépin's 0.2 %), so a co-inoculated bacterium really is out-competed. The gap is a **bacterial nitrogen source this model lacks — peptides, which yeast do not take** — not blindness to the yeast's own store. Pinned so it cannot be "fixed" back.

**The store is not tied to living biomass**, so it does not drain on cell death or autolyse. Conservation still closes; it is a fidelity note, and it was equally true of D-248's parking in `N`.

**A reading that D-250 makes separable for the first time.** Crépin sampled the *medium*. `_assimilable_n_mgl` keeps counting the store — that is what D-248's "40.8 % → 0.62 % residual" meant, and dropping it would redefine the number rather than migrate it — but the narrower extracellular quantity is now readable and exhausts sooner (D-249's nitrogen gap reads 1.71× rather than 1.59×). **D-249's verdict survives it**: the channel is still slower than the 1.92× run containing it, and still exhausts later in the run than Crépin's 0.187. Re-deriving D-249's headline on the narrower quantity is a separate beat, not taken here.

### 8. What is pinned

New file `tests/test_nitrogen_stored_intracellularly.py` (14 tests, ~47 s). The ammonium inflation at both doses against a no-uptake control; the pH excursion, with D-248's 0.2147 and 0.108 quoted so the guard is about a known magnitude; nitrogen conservation in both arms; **the store's absence from the charge balance asserted structurally** — loading it must not move solved pH by one bit, with a non-vacuity arm loading `N` instead, so the test cannot pass in a build where the balance stopped reading nitrogen at all; the swap's split, driven at a state where the store holds 95 % of the reachable nitrogen; the helper's conservation and proportionality; growth on a full store and an empty must; the bacteria's deliberate blindness; and `touches_where_present`'s scope, with a leaky Process that must still raise. Plus the corrected malate sign at **both** doses — the one case nothing else in the repo runs — the store's own `assert_nonnegative` (it inherited none), and §6b's 1.71 pinned rather than merely stated.

**Three mutation arms verified RED**, restored from an on-disk snapshot and byte-checked between arms: uptake parking back in `N` (5 tests red), the swap refunding wholly to `N`, and growth's Monod reading `N` alone.

Suite **2036 + 6 xfail**, measured off a green full run.

## D-251 — D-249's front-loading residue was measured in a frame Crépin never sampled: two fifths of it is the frame, the rest is REACHABLE by the shipped capacity knob inside its own declared band, and what stops the calibration being taken is the cell-nitrogen it costs

**Corrects:** D-249 — §5's attribution, narrowly. Its "`ρ_N ∝ X` is the wrong functional form early" rests on a biomass-versus-nitrogen table computed through `_assimilable_n_mgl`, which counts D-250's intracellular store as unconsumed; Crépin sampled the *medium*. In her frame the gap is 1.68× rather than 2.22×, and the observable §4's capacity sweep was scored on is **flat in `r`** in the total frame — which is why that sweep saw nothing. §5's *measurements* stand; the functional-form verdict does not. Whether the form is adequate is now **pitch-conditional and unresolved**, not settled either way.
**Flags:** D-250 — `assert_nonnegative`'s 1e-9 default sits below the store's own solver-noise excursion on Crépin's must at **shipped** parameters (−2.3e-9). Identified and measured; no guard tolerance changed here.

The owner picked D-249's time-free shape residue. It ends without a build, and the reason is not the one D-249 predicted: the residue is smaller than recorded, the existing knob reaches what is left, and the thing that stops the beat is a price nobody had computed.

### 1. The frame: Crépin sampled the medium, the model counted the cells too

`_assimilable_n_mgl` counts the `N` slot, the eight pools **and** D-250's `stored_nitrogen`. That is deliberate and D-250 §7 defends it — D-248's "40.8 % → 0.62 % residual" was measured while the surplus sat in `N`, so dropping the store would redefine the number rather than migrate it. But it makes the model's nitrogen clock run late against a paper that sampled the must. Both readings below come off the **same trajectory**; only the observable differs.

| shipped run, `r = 1`, pitch 0.25 | model, total frame | model, Crépin's frame | Crépin |
|---|---|---|---|
| biomass share at **half** the N gone | 0.543 | **0.412** | **0.245** |
| ...at **three-quarters** gone | 0.777 | **0.626** | **0.410** |
| the gap D-249 reported | 2.22× / 1.90× | **1.68× / 1.53×** | — |

**Two fifths of the front-loading gap is the frame**, with nothing in `src/` changed.

### 2. The rest is reachable, and the reason D-249's own sweep could not see it

D-249 §4 swept `amino_acid_uptake_capacity_ratio` across 1000× and found the exhaustion *time* saturating at ~16.4 h. True, and it is why the timing miss stays refused. It was never scored on the **shape**. Scored now, in both frames, at the fixture's pitch:

| `r` | 1 | 2 | 3.9 | 5 | 1000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| half-N biomass share, **total** frame | 0.543 | 0.542 | 0.542 | 0.542 | **0.542** |
| half-N biomass share, **Crépin's** frame | 0.412 | 0.327 | **0.245** | 0.218 | **0.091** |

**The total frame is blind to this knob by construction** — the knob moves nitrogen from the medium into the store and that frame counts both sides. Across three orders of magnitude it moves in the third decimal. In the frame the paper is written in, the same knob walks the share through Crépin's 0.245 and crosses it at **`r ≈ 3.9`**, inside the `[0.5, 10]` uncertainty the parameter already declares. No new parameter, no widened band, no new rate law.

### 3. Two landmarks and their ratio — which is what keeps this from being the D-98 trap

Fitting one number to one number is construction. Crépin's three-quarters landmark is **not free** once the half is matched, and the ratio between them is a statement about the shape of her nitrogen-versus-biomass curve that one knob cannot tune independently.

| at the landing capacity | half | three-quarters | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crépin | 0.245 | 0.410 | **1.673** |
| model, pitch 0.25, `r = 3.9` | 0.245 | 0.404 | **1.648** |
| model, pitch 0.04, `r = 2.65` | 0.242 | 0.412 | **1.701** |

**Her third landmark discriminates nothing and is labelled so.** At N_T she holds 99.1 % of final biomass; so does this model, at `r = 1` and `r = 1000` alike (0.991–0.994 across the whole grid). Near-complete consumption and near-peak biomass are the same event in a nitrogen-limited run. It is one landmark of agreement that was always going to agree, and counting it as a third would be an overclaim.

### 4. The price, and it is the whole reason the calibration is not taken here

Nitrogen taken up ahead of anabolic need has to sit somewhere. `biomass_N_fraction`'s shipped 0.114 g N/g dry weight is the canonical N-**replete** yeast elemental reference (Roels 1983 / Heijnen, CH₁.₈O₀.₅N₀.₂) — *total* cell nitrogen, band [0.08, 0.14]. The wine seam overrides it downward per Coleman's `Y_X/N(N_init)`, to **0.0624** on this must, so what a stored pool may occupy is the headroom below the ceiling.

| | store peak, as share of the must's N | stored N per g cell | **total cell N** |
|---|---|---|---|
| shipped `r = 1` | 16.3 % | 0.0209 | **0.0833** (below the reference) |
| pitch 0.25, `r = 3.9` | 41.4 % | 0.0767 | **0.1391** |
| pitch 0.04, `r = 2.65` | 35.3 % | 0.0747 | **0.1371** |

Landing Crépin's landmarks makes the cells carry **0.137–0.139 g N/g DW** — past the reference value by 20 % and within 0.001–0.003 of the band's own top edge, at **both** pitches. It is admissible on the letter of the band and it spends essentially all of it. **And the landing capacity is not pitch-invariant** (3.9 against 2.65 across a 6.25× inoculum change), so a calibration taken today inherits the unsourced pitch D-249 flagged. Two reasons the trade is the owner's, not a beat's.

### 5. The cost is measured at the capacity actually recommended, and the first pricing got the failure CLASS wrong

Full suite with the shipped value mutated to **3.9** — the capacity §3 lands on — then snapshot-restored and byte-checked (`9ac5289f8cac61e21d60daba04eee0b4`): **2 failed, 2041 passed, 6 xfailed**. No fusel guard, no Coleman-yield guard, no propanol floor, no Minebois share and no benchmark moves — consistent with D-248's insensitivity finding, which was about *extent*. **Both** failures are `r = 1` values pinned by the last two records: D-249's nitrogen gap 1.59 → 1.67 (`test_the_nitrogen_channel_is_SLOWER_than_the_run_containing_it_at_both_pitches`) and D-250's extracellular gap 1.71 → 1.84 (`test_the_extracellular_reading_is_now_separable_and_d249s_verdict_survives_it`). The calibration costs **two re-pins**, not a repair.

**The first draft of this section priced a capacity nobody recommends, and mis-classed what failed.** It ran the suite at `r = 3.5` — mutated before the landing capacity had been measured — read **3 failed / 2033 passed** (2036 collected: that run predates this record's own seven tests), and called all three re-pins. The third was not a re-pin: it was `assert_nonnegative` tripping on the `stored_nitrogen` dip of §6, a solver-noise excursion sitting a factor of two from a 1e-9 boundary, and it does **not** fire at 3.9. A tolerance crossing is not a price. Both runs are kept here because the difference between them is the point: **a cost table is only a cost table at the value being recommended, and a failure count is not a price until every entry in it has been classed.**

### 6. The store's nonnegativity dip is solver noise, and it is already there at the shipped capacity

The `r = 3.5` run of §5 tripped `stored_nitrogen went negative: -1.910e-09` at t = 53.1 h; the `r = 3.9` run does not trip it at all. Growth's draw is split between `N` and the store in proportion to what each holds, so the store's share of the draw vanishes as the store empties and no over-draw is possible by construction. The falsifiable consequence is that the dip must scale with **solver tolerance** and not with capacity. Measured on Crépin's must:

| | `rtol` 1e-6 | 1e-8 | 1e-10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `r = 1` (**shipped**) | **−2.34e-9** | −5.3e-13 | −4.0e-20 |
| `r = 3.5` | −1.59e-9 | −2.4e-12 | −1.8e-15 |

Eleven orders for four of tolerance, and **the shipped capacity's dip is the larger of the two** — while at the recommended 3.9 the guard does not fire at all, which is the clearest statement available that the excursion tracks the integrator rather than the knob. So this is not a property of the calibration at all: `assert_nonnegative`'s 1e-9 default is already within a factor of two of firing on shipped parameters, and no shipped test happens to integrate a trajectory where it does. A tolerance calibration, recorded rather than changed — the guard's atol is not this beat's to move.

### 7. What is NOT settled, so a later beat does not read this as more than it is

**The form is not vindicated; it is un-convicted.** What is shown is that the observable D-249 convicted it on cannot convict it, and that the shipped knob reaches the target inside its declared band. A capacity that lands the landmarks only by loading cells to the top of the elemental band is evidence *for* a form change as much as against one — the difference is that the case now has a price attached and a frame that matches the paper.

**D-248 §10 stays refused and is NOT re-opened.** A Droop-style quota needs the store's contents to feed back into the uptake *rate*, and that feedback is precisely the brake §10 refused and D-249 §5 called inert on this observable. D-250 built a compartment uptake fills and growth draws from; it did **not** make the rate read it. Re-opening §10 is the owner's call, and this record does not make it.

**The calibration itself is the owner's trade**, priced above: `r` 1.0 → ~3.9 (or ~2.65 at the sourced pitch), two re-pinned numbers, cells at the top of the elemental band, and a value that inherits an inoculum nobody published.

### 8. What is pinned

New file `tests/test_nitrogen_uptake_shape_frame.py` (7 tests, ~30 s, **no `src/` change**): the frame correction with D-249's own totals re-derived rather than quoted, and a non-vacuity arm requiring the store to be non-empty; the total frame's blindness to the knob **paired with** the medium frame's 0.412 → 0.091 response, so flatness cannot be read as a dead knob; the crossing, with monotonicity, a bracketing arm and the declared band's edges as literals; both discriminating landmarks and the ratio; the third landmark's non-discrimination across the whole grid; the cell-nitrogen price with the shipped capacity as its control and both edges of the ceiling asserted; and the dip's tolerance scaling with its own "if this does not collapse, it is an over-draw and a different finding" arm.

D-249's shape test keeps its numbers and gains the frame label it never had — that unlabelled frame is what produced this beat.

**Two mutation arms verified RED**, restored from an on-disk snapshot and byte-checked: collapsing the medium frame onto the total one (5 of 7 red) and returning the landing capacity to the shipped 1.0 (3 red).

Suite **2043 + 6 xfail**, measured off a green full run.
## D-252 — both prices standing against the fixture's unsourced pitch are void: the Coleman anchor is structurally insensitive to the inoculum and D-249 charged a hardcoded literal for it, and D-251 priced a transient nitrogen store against an end-state band Crépin's own data fall below — while her data cannot settle the inoculum, and the gain says why

**Corrects:** D-249 — §3's price. "It buys the timing and sells the anchor" measured the Coleman-yield guard going 0.984 → 0.925 at the sourced pitch. That guard predicted against `0.25 + initial/f_N` with the fixture's pitch as a *literal*, so at 0.04 it subtracted an inoculum the run did not have. Against the run's own pitch the anchor reads **0.9848**, inside its own ±0.02. The move sells the anchor nothing. §3's *other* half — peak biomass +0.8 % → −5.2 % against her measured 3.39 — stands untouched.
**Corrects:** D-251 — §4's price. "Landing Crépin's landmarks makes the cells carry 0.137–0.139 g N/g DW against a sourced 0.114, band top 0.14" compared the model's own transient *maximum*, at a moment Crépin never sampled, against a band that describes *end-state elemental composition*. Her own end state falls **below the entire band**. At the one moment she did sample, the landing capacity carries **less** nitrogen per gram than her numbers imply. The calibration is not shown to be affordable — it is shown not to have been priced.

D-251 closed by handing the owner a trade with a price on it. Both halves of that price — the anchor D-249 charged and the cell nitrogen D-251 charged — turn out to be artifacts of how they were measured. Nothing here moves the fixture's pitch, and nothing here recommends taking the calibration.

### 1. The anchor was never a quantity an inoculum change could sell

`test_biomass_now_reaches_the_coleman_yield_the_compile_seam_installs` compares peak biomass against Coleman's `Y_X/N × N_init`, formed as `predicted = 0.25 + initial / f_N`. The `0.25` is the fixture's pitch, written in.

`_apply_nitrogen_dependent_yield` computes `f_N` from the declared `N_init` **alone** — asserted, not assumed, in the new file — so `f_N` is bit-identical at both pitches (0.06241), the biomass increment is pitch-independent, and both terms of the ratio shift by the same `X₀`:

| | pitch 0.25 (fixture) | pitch 0.04 (sourced) |
|---|---|---|
| `f_N` compiled | 0.06241 | 0.06241 |
| peak biomass | 3.4181 | 3.2126 |
| ratio, against the guard's **literal** 0.25 | 0.9844 | **0.9252** |
| ratio, against the run's **own** pitch | 0.9844 | **0.9848** |

**"Structurally insensitive", not invariant.** `(X₀ + ΔX)/(X₀ + N₀/f_N)` does not cancel `X₀` — both terms shift additively and the ratio drifts toward 1 as `X₀` grows. The drift is measured, at **0.0004** across a 6.25× change, and pinned, so the word can never be quoted as an identity.

The guard is **correct at the pitch it runs at**; the literal is brittle, not wrong, and its verdict at the shipped pitch is unchanged. It now derives `X₀` from the trajectory, matching the repo's own idiom at `tests/test_wine_nitrogen_budget.py:304` and `:494` — the only place that diverged was this one line.

### 2. Her data cap the cell-nitrogen fraction below the WHOLE declared band, in both frames

On the model's own accounting convention — `_apply_nitrogen_dependent_yield`: *"every assimilated gram of nitrogen enters biomass, so Y_X/N = 1/f_N identically"* — Crépin's must and her measured final dry weight fix the whole-run yield up to the inoculum: `f_N = YAN/(X_final − X₀)`. Her first sampled dry weight is **0.83 g/L** and the curve rises (0.83 → 1.39 → 3.36 → 3.39), so `X₀ < 0.83` and `f_N` is capped:

| | model frame (201.11 mg N/L) | papers' frame (179.91) |
|---|---|---|
| `f_N` cap from `X₀ < 0.83` | **0.0786** | **0.0703** |
| `biomass_N_fraction` band low edge | 0.08 | 0.08 |

**The cap is below the band's own low edge, in both frames.** So `[0.08, 0.14]` — a canonical N-replete elemental composition (Roels/Heijnen) — is not a ceiling on anything in this ferment: Crépin's yeast average less nitrogen per gram over the whole run than the band's *poorest* cell. A band whose low edge sits above the measured whole-run value cannot price a transient store, which is what D-251 §4 used it for.

### 3. At the moment she DID sample, the landing capacity undershoots her

D-251 §4's 0.1391 is the model's transient maximum. Located: it falls at **20.5 %** of the nitrogen gone (landing capacity, fixture pitch) and **10.6 %** (sourced pitch) — both before Crépin's first landmark at 50 %. It is compared to no measurement at all.

Read at her landmark instead, on the same total-cell basis with the inoculum's own nitrogen credited:

| | at her 50 %-nitrogen landmark |
|---|---|
| Crépin implies (both frames × three inocula × two inoculum credits) | **0.108 – 0.156** |
| model, landing capacity, pitch 0.25 | **0.0920** |
| model, landing capacity, pitch 0.04 | **0.0971** |
| model, shipped capacity (control) | 0.0761 |

The calibration does not overload the cells against the source. It still **under**-loads them, and the shipped capacity under-loads them further — which is the control that stops the undershoot reading as a property of an inert observable.

**Two conditionals, stated rather than absorbed.** (1) This is an *internal-consistency* argument on the model's own convention. Consumed is not the same as in-cells if yeast excrete nitrogen, and nothing here sources that either way — it is **not** an independent source-side observation of storage, and must not be quoted as one. (2) The moments are named rather than matched, which is the whole content of the paragraph above.

### 4. What her data CANNOT do: settle the inoculum

`X₀ = X_final − YAN/f_N` is exact and useless. The inoculum is a few per cent of the final biomass at either candidate, so the whole candidate range barely moves the implied yield:

| assumed `X₀` (g/L) | 0.00 | 0.04 | 0.25 |
|---|---|---|---|
| implied `f_N`, model frame | 0.05933 | 0.06003 | 0.06405 |

**8.0 %** across the whole range; separating the sourced 0.04 from the fixture's 0.25 needs `f_N` known to **6.7 %**, where its own declared band spans a factor of **1.75**. The gain is off by more than an order of magnitude.

The point estimate is frame-dependent as well, and the two frames straddle the fixture's pitch: **0.168 g/L** (model frame) against **0.507** (papers'). The archive records no assay frame for Coleman's own YAN — the provenance gives Table A2 + Fig 4 and no method for the nitrogen axis — so the pairing of a model-frame `N₀` with a Coleman-fitted `f_N` is unresolved and neither end is usable. D-248 §8's "the two frames cancel exactly" is about the seam's *internal* carve-out and release; it does not reach this external pairing.

### 5. What the owner's trade actually is now

Unchanged as a decision, and it is still theirs. What has changed is what is on each side of it:

- **Moving the pitch to 0.04** buys the exhaustion timing (29.9 h against her 28 h, from 17.6 h) and costs peak biomass (+0.8 % → −5.2 % against her measured 3.39). It costs the Coleman anchor **nothing** — that line of the D-249 price list is deleted.
- **Taking the front-loading calibration** (`amino_acid_uptake_capacity_ratio` 1.0 → ~3.9) buys Crépin's two discriminating landmarks and their ratio for **two re-pinned numbers** (D-251 §5 as corrected). The cell-nitrogen objection is void; what remains is that the landing capacity is not pitch-invariant, so it still inherits an inoculum nobody published.
- **The inoculum cannot be resolved from Crépin's biomass data.** It is not a matter of a better reading — the required precision is an order of magnitude beyond what the parameter is known to.

Neither move is made here.

### 6. What is pinned

New file `tests/test_inoculum_and_cell_nitrogen.py` (6 tests, ~10 s, **no `src/` change**): the anchor read both ways with the 0.925 kept as a literal-produced number and the 0.0004 drift pinned so "insensitive" cannot be read as "constant"; `f_N`'s identity across the two pitches, since the whole argument rests on the seam reading `N_init` alone; the cap below the band's low edge in both frames with the band's edges as load-bearing literals; the null on the inoculum pinned as a *gain* (8.0 %, 6.7 %, factor 1.75) rather than as a conclusion, with an arm that reopens it if the band ever narrows far enough to discriminate; her landmark against the model's, with the shipped capacity as the control; and the location of the model's peak, with an arm that fires if it ever moves onto a moment she sampled.

Two green-but-false prose repairs in the same commit (the D-247 §6 discipline): the hardcoded pitch at `tests/test_assimilable_nitrogen_uptake.py`, and `test_the_fixtures_pitch_is_unsourced_and_the_only_sourced_value_is_6_25x_smaller`'s docstring, which still published "0.984 to 0.925 — outside the band".

## D-253 — both owner's calls are TAKEN: the fixture pitches the sourced inoculum, which closes the nitrogen clock, and the uptake capacity is landed on Crépin's biomass-versus-nitrogen shape at 2.6 — the extent stays un-fitted, Minebois does not regress, and D-251's solver-noise brittleness fired for real

**Corrects:** D-251 — §5's "neither move is made here" and the two-point grid behind its `LANDING_R`. Both moves are made. Re-measured on a bracketing grid at the pitch that now ships, the landing capacity is **2.6**, not the 2.65 spot-checked off `(1.0, 2.65)`.
**Corrects:** D-248 — §5's "the model strips 90 % of the assimilable nitrogen by 18.6 h against Crépin's 28 h, ~1.5× fast". That was measured at a pitch neither paper published. The *attribution* D-249 built on it (the nitrogen channel is slower than the run containing it) is untouched and still holds at both pitches.
**Corrects:** D-248 — `wine_generic.yaml`'s standing claim that the timing "is not repairable by moving r without giving up the saturated regime that makes the extent unfitted". The clause was right that `r` is not the timing's repair — it was wrong about what taking a level would cost.

D-252 voided both prices standing against the pitch move and explicitly declined to make it. The owner called both. This record is what taking them measured.

### 1. Order matters, and it is not cosmetic

The landing capacity is **not pitch-invariant**: 3.9 at the house 0.25 g/L, 2.6 at the sourced 0.04. Landing `r` first would have fitted a shipped parameter to an inoculum nobody published. So the pitch moves first, on its own commit, with the suite green in between; then `r` is re-measured against the fixture the engine actually runs.

### 2. The pitch, and the half nobody had priced

`commensurate_scenario` pitched 0.25 g/L, the wine benchmark's house default. Minebois §Materials and Methods states 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ for the same Bely, Sablayrolles & Barre 1990 medium out of the same lab lineage; through the D-219 crossing that is 0.04 g/L. So the value is **directly sourced for the Minebois fixture** and inherited by lineage for Crépin, who states no inoculum at all.

| | house 0.25 | sourced 0.04 | Crépin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 90 % of assimilable N gone, total frame | 17.6 h | **29.9 h** | 28 h |
| same, extracellular frame (D-250) | 16.4 h | **28.6 h** | 28 h |
| peak biomass | 3.418 g/L | **3.213 g/L** | 3.39 g/L |
| Coleman anchor, run's own pitch | 0.9844 | **0.9848** | — |

**D-252 priced this move on Crépin alone.** `commensurate_scenario` pitches *both* musts, and D-248's strongest external result — Minebois's two in-study fusel shares going 1.73×/1.68× to ~1.0× — rides on the same fixture. Measured: **1.009×/0.977× → 1.014×/0.982×**, inside the pin either way, and flat in `r` across 0.5–10. Propanol's de-novo share holds at 0.8777 (pin [0.870, 0.886]) and the low band at 0.1223 (pin [0.114, 0.130]); neither needed re-pinning. The unpriced half is not a cost.

Three re-pins, no `src/` change: the Coleman anchor's `r = 0` arm 0.616 → **0.591** (that arm is the pre-D-248 frozen path, where growth stops with the nitrogen standing, so its peak *is* inoculum-set — the two arms moving differently is the same separation D-248 rests on); the exhaustion-time guard, which asserted "still misses, ~1.5× fast"; and the extracellular gap 1.71× → **0.98×**.

### 3. The capacity, landed on the shape

D-251 established that the level was identifiable for the first time on the extracellular frame D-250 split out. At the pitch that now ships, on a bracketing grid:

| `r` | 1.0 | 2.0 | 2.5 | **2.6** | 2.7 | 3.0 | 5.0 | Crépin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| biomass share at N½ | 0.370 | 0.281 | 0.250 | **0.2449** | 0.240 | 0.226 | 0.164 | **0.2448** |
| biomass share at N¾ | 0.595 | 0.470 | 0.420 | **0.4150** | 0.410 | 0.396 | 0.326 | **0.4100** |

**The anti-fitting defence is the second landmark and the ratio, not the tier.** One knob sets three columns; the ¾ landmark and the landmark ratio are not free once the half is matched, and both come along uninvited.
